# Part I — Target architecture: executive synthesis

> **TARGET ARCHITECTURE / RESEARCH — NOT CURRENT PRODUCT STATE.** Parts I–XX
> describe the intended system, alternatives, and build program. A present-tense
> sentence here is not implementation or deployment evidence. Part 0 controls every
> current-state, launch, primitive-count, and token-savings claim.

## 1. The product in one sentence

Taedri is a verified capability-reuse and decision layer that helps humans and software agents find, compose, materialize, execute, and independently verify existing software capabilities before spending model context and engineering effort recreating them.

The product is not a vector database, package mirror, graph database, LLM proxy, code generator, tool catalog, or workflow engine by itself. It coordinates all of these behind stable contracts so that the cheapest proof-acceptable path can satisfy a real request.

``` text
human demand
  -> typed request and acceptance contract
  -> exact/replay/retrieval/graph/model mechanism portfolio
  -> smallest sufficient route or architecture plan
  -> deterministic binding and policy checks
  -> post-selection artifact resolution
  -> authorized execution
  -> independent verification
  -> immutable outcome, usage, provenance, and decision receipt
  -> cheaper future replay or improved routing evidence
```

The economic unit is not a primitive record or token avoided. It is:

``` text
one independently accepted, policy-compliant software outcome
```

## 2. Why the system should exist

Coding agents repeatedly pay to rediscover facts already encoded in packages, tests, schemas, integration catalogs, repositories, templates, prior successful routes, and the organization’s own code. They then often rewrite a partial equivalent, omit failure behavior, assume compatibility from similarity, or lose the successful result when the session ends.

Taedri converts that repeated probabilistic work into reusable assets:

- code entities and capability capsules;
- typed ports and compatibility assertions;
- body-free search cards;
- implementation and artifact handles;
- route and architecture plans;
- tests, oracles, counterexamples, and negative knowledge;
- exact provenance, version, environment, and effect receipts;
- learned routing evidence based on independently accepted outcomes.

The compounding loop is:

``` text
more real demands
  -> better demand taxonomy
  -> better retrieval and route evidence
  -> more verified reusable assets
  -> fewer unnecessary model calls and rewrites
  -> more accepted outcomes per dollar
  -> more demand and verification evidence
```

## 3. Product and project boundaries

The current naming and responsibility map is:

| Name                            | Primary responsibility                                                                                    |
|---------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **AI Done Right**               | parent product/company umbrella                                                                           |
| **AIDevObserver**               | customer-facing observation, reuse, guidance, and outcome-assurance experience for coding sessions        |
| **AIDevObserver Benchmark Lab** | internal and external evaluation environment; legacy repository naming may include `aidevexplorer`        |
| **TaedriCodeGraph**             | language-neutral code-entity, descriptor, edge, compatibility, evidence, and package-processing substrate |
| **Teleon**                      | demand-to-capability route compiler and deterministic plan/binding layer                                  |
| **RouterMesh**                  | six-plane mechanism, model, provider, endpoint, harness, and verification-triggered routing control plane |
| **Baltor**                      | verified-context, disclosure, and trust-governance layer                                                  |
| **OpenHubForAI**                | registry and distribution substrate for capability, capsule, route, model, tool, and evidence records     |

These may deploy together as a modular monolith initially. Logical contracts must not be confused with a requirement for separate microservices or repositories.

## 4. Historical source-era evidence narrative and its limits

Earlier supplied source material described selected maintenance experiments in which
exact Taedri primitives and baseline model outputs passed the same executable oracles.
It also described a local mixed-origin route involving private tenant candidates and
an external PyPI reference. Those five maintenance primitives, their source tree, the
mixed-origin script, and its cited receipt are absent from this checkout, so this
paragraph is preserved as historical input and is not current empirical evidence.

These results establish feasibility for those exact tasks, artifacts, environments, and receipts. They do not establish a universal token-savings rate, customer savings, energy savings, broad coding performance, or production authorization. The combined program therefore keeps observed evidence, estimates, simulations, and goals explicitly separate.

## 5. The recommended first vertical slice

The canonical first slice is:

``` text
schema-validated RequestEnvelope
  -> exact handle / verified replay / solution pack checks
  -> parallel lexical + identifier + history + graph retrieval
  -> request-local typed graph
  -> topology-appropriate route solver
  -> adaptive contrastive route cards at 1/2/4/8 alternatives
  -> deterministic / local ranker / local SLM / cheap hosted / strong fallback
  -> lazy trust-checked artifact resolution
  -> existing execution runtime
  -> claim-specific independent verification
  -> operational trace + provenance + outcome receipt
```

A future implementation may reconstruct that mixed-origin route from source and then
carry it through real package/thin-pack materialization, digest validation, local
execution, verification, rollback, and replay-condition recording. The route must not
be called existing until those artifacts are present and reproducible.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Part II — Canonical invariants and semantic kernel

## 6. Non-negotiable invariants

1.  **Search before coding.** A new helper requires evidence that eligible standard, package, internal, or previously verified capabilities were considered first.
2.  **Reuse is a preference, not an unconditional command.** Privacy, policy, portability, licensing, latency, determinism, maintenance, ownership, or assurance may make a new implementation preferable.
3.  **Native source names remain unchanged.** Collision-resistant identity belongs in a sidecar identity lattice, not source-code renaming.
4.  **Candidate is not truth.** `candidate`, `tested`, `verified`, `authorized`, `released`, `revoked`, and `serves_truth` remain separate states.
5.  **Similarity retrieves; contracts compose; evidence decides.** An embedding or LSH match never proves compatibility.
6.  **Every important fact is an assertion.** Assertions retain source, producer, scope, time, evidence, confidence, version, and counterexamples.
7.  **Every representation is versioned and append-only.** A new description, embedding, hash, label, or model output does not overwrite earlier alternatives.
8.  **Implementation bodies are resolved after selection.** Common search and planning contexts use body-free cards, ports, decisive edges, examples, and evidence.
9.  **A model proposes; a compiler binds.** Models may interpret, rank, decompose, or propose plans, but cannot declare their own result compatible, authorized, executed, or verified.
10. **Effects are explicit.** File, network, database, message, subprocess, secret, model, human, and external-service effects require authority and receipts.
11. **Independent verification gates claims.** A response from the same model or implementation is not an independent oracle.
12. **Negative knowledge is retained.** Failed routes, incompatible pairs, version breakpoints, counterexamples, and rejected claims become searchable assets.
13. **Hard gates precede preferences.** No weighted score may override authority, compatibility, environment, license, evidence, or safety constraints.
14. **All physical attempts are recorded.** Retries, provider failover, semantic fallback, repairs, tool calls, costs, tokens, failures, and committed effects remain visible.
15. **Mechanisms remain replaceable.** Databases, indexes, models, harnesses, providers, workflow engines, and deployment topologies must compete through conformance and measured outcomes.
16. **Store broadly; disclose narrowly.** Corpus scale is not a justification for injecting more context into each call.
17. **Benchmark answers stay sealed.** Task and oracle metadata may be useful; protected solutions and hidden tests do not enter ordinary retrieval or training partitions.
18. **A production claim names its exact scope.** Version, artifact digest, build, runtime, platform, environment, policy epoch, tenant scope, and verifier matter.

## 7. Subject universe

Taedri describes more than functions. Its open `SubjectKindRegistry` must support:

- repository, release, distribution, wheel, sdist, binary, image, layer, build, lockfile, and SBOM;
- source file, notebook, cell, module, namespace, package, import, export, and generated file;
- token, occurrence, literal, expression, statement, block, syntax node, macro, annotation, and decorator;
- symbol, variable, binding, parameter, return, yield, exception, event, callback, field, slot, and runtime value;
- function, lambda, generator, coroutine, handler, method, constructor, property, descriptor, and operator;
- class, record, enum, protocol, interface, trait, mixin, generic, specialization, and metaclass;
- type, schema, tensor, dataframe, message, endpoint, RPC, CLI command, configuration, query, and external resource;
- test, fixture, property, assertion, oracle, benchmark, counterexample, failure mode, and mutation;
- edge assertion, n-ary relation, motif, code group, subsystem, capsule, route, workflow, architecture, deployment, and migration;
- primitive, adapter, validator, renderer, controller, worker, generator, policy, model, tool, agent, human step, and verification arm;
- demand, decision, attempt, effect, artifact, receipt, release, revocation, incident, and observed outcome.

Adding a new subject kind must not require a schema migration across every existing record. It registers applicability, canonicalization, allowed relations, validation, indexing, and projection behavior.

## 8. Identity lattice

One identifier cannot safely serve source navigation, logical capability identity, artifact identity, and runtime observations. Preserve a lattice:

``` text
ArtifactIdentity
  exact bytes, digest, source, release, build, platform

OccurrenceIdentity
  artifact + file + span/syntax path

SymbolIdentity
  language-aware semantic symbol and declaration family

ContractIdentity
  normalized inputs, outputs, effects, errors, state, environment

CapabilityIdentity
  stable logical outcome independent of one implementation

ImplementationRevisionIdentity
  immutable body/config/dependency/environment realization

RuntimeObservationIdentity
  one exact attempt over exact inputs and environment

RouteIdentity
  topology plus bindings, policy, revisions, and verifier requirements
```

Taedri’s canonical entity identifier should be a sidecar identifier derived from a typed namespace and stable facts. Native fully qualified names remain searchable aliases. Package URLs, VCS revisions, OCI digests, SPDX identifiers, SCIP symbols, Kythe VNames, language-server locations, and analyzer-specific IDs remain external identities connected through `IDENTIFIES_SAME_SUBJECT_AS` assertions with stated scope.

## 9. Universal assertion envelope

Every descriptor, label, edge, compatibility claim, observation, or score is an assertion:

``` yaml
assertion:
  assertion_id: taedri://assertion/<digest>
  subject_id: taedri://subject/...
  predicate_or_facet: ...
  object_or_value: ...
  scope:
    artifact: ...
    version_range: ...
    environment: ...
    tenant: ...
    valid_time: ...
    transaction_time: ...
  producer:
    kind: [parser, analyzer, test, model, human, imported_standard]
    identity: ...
    version: ...
    configuration_digest: ...
  evidence_refs: []
  derivation: [declared, extracted, inferred, observed, verified, contradicted]
  confidence: null
  lifecycle: [candidate, tested, verified, authorized, released, revoked]
  serves_truth: false
  counterexamples: []
  invalidation_dependencies: []
  created_at: ...
```

The bitemporal split matters. A claim may have been valid for release `v1.4` while being imported into Taedri later; correcting the import history must not erase the historical product fact.

## 10. DescriptionPortfolio

There is no single universal description, vector, hash, label, or score. Each subject owns a versioned `DescriptionPortfolio` whose unit is:

``` text
descriptor = (
  subject,
  facet,
  production_event,
  representation,
  scope,
  evidence,
  lineage,
  validity,
  cost
)
```

The portfolio may contain:

- exact names, aliases, locators, signatures, source and canonical structural forms;
- multiple black-box summaries for user intent, mechanism, inputs, outputs, effects, errors, state, performance, examples, and failure boundaries;
- preferred, alternate, hidden, misspelled, acronym, domain, and multilingual labels;
- fielded lexical views, token/character microfeatures, sparse vectors, BM25 fields, SPLADE-like expansions, and negative terms;
- exact digests, normalization-specific hashes, winnowing, MinHash, weighted MinHash, SimHash, fuzzy digests, AST/CFG/DFG fingerprints, Weisfeiler–Lehman features, motifs, paths, and runtime/test sketches;
- many independent embeddings for names, purposes, source, signatures, schemas, ports, behavior, failures, examples, tests, graph role, history, domain, and routes;
- graph neighborhoods, centrality, communities, typed paths, hyperedges, route roles, and temporal evolution;
- declared, inferred, observed, contradicted, verified, deprecated, and revoked evidence.

Preferred views are scoped materialized projections for a retrieval, solver, execution, or verification role. They never destroy the underlying variants.

## 11. CapabilityCapsule and CodeCapsule

A capsule is a registry-native, versioned collection of selectively resolvable roles:

``` yaml
capability_capsule:
  logical_handle: taedri://capability/...
  revision: ...
  contract_refs: []
  implementation_refs: []
  role_digests:
    search_card: ...
    source: ...
    types: ...
    graph: ...
    docs: ...
    examples: ...
    tests: ...
    runtime: ...
    evidence: ...
    provenance: ...
  compatibility_signatures: []
  effects: []
  errors: []
  environment_constraints: []
  lifecycle: candidate
  serves_truth: false
```

Capsules are not separate Git repositories or packages. One package may yield thousands of capsules; one logical capability may point to multiple implementations; one implementation may support several contract variants.

## 12. Body-free search card

The normal search result should preserve decision-changing facts without source bodies:

``` yaml
handle: taedri://capability/text/normalize-unicode
revision_hint: verified-2026-07
name: normalize Unicode text
contract: (text:string, form:enum[NFC,NFD,NFKC,NFKD]) -> string
effects: []
errors: [invalid_form]
properties: [deterministic, idempotent_for_fixed_form, potentially_lossy_under_compatibility_forms]
summary: Normalize Unicode code-point sequences into a selected canonical or compatibility form.
evidence: [standard_reference, cross_implementation_tests]
authorization: eligible
expansion_handles: [contract, decisive_edges, examples, tests, source]
```

Cards are generated at multiple detail levels. The context optimizer chooses the smallest view expected to preserve the route decision.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Part III — First-class edges, compatibility, and route mathematics

## 13. Relation identity and evidence

Separate the semantic relation, its assertions, and its searchable projections:

``` text
RelationIdentity
  stable subject–predicate–object or n-ary relation identity

EdgeAssertion
  one producer's scoped claim with evidence and lifecycle

EdgeFeatureBundle
  lexical, sparse, fingerprint, embedding, graph, history, and numeric views
```

This prevents two analyzers from overwriting each other and permits a relation to be simultaneously declared, inferred, contradicted, and later verified under different scopes.

## 14. Pairwise edges and hyperedges

Pairwise edges cover ordinary facts such as `CALLS`, `RETURNS`, `IMPORTS`, `OVERRIDES`, `READS`, or `VERIFIED_BY`. N-ary relations are necessary for facts whose meaning would be lost if decomposed, including:

- call occurrence + caller + callee + positional/keyword bindings;
- function + parameter port + supplied value + conversion;
- route step + incoming ports + outgoing ports + policy guard;
- controller + desired state + observed state + emitted actions + status;
- benchmark task + candidate + environment + oracle + score;
- model attempt + provider + endpoint + prompt program + tool set + verifier result.

Every hyperedge can expose pairwise projections for cheap adjacency while preserving its canonical n-ary identity.

## 15. CompatibilitySignature

Compatibility is directional and purpose-specific. A signature should cover:

- value and schema types;
- required/optional fields and nullability;
- cardinality, shape, rank, units, encoding, locale and time zone;
- sync/async, batch/stream, eager/lazy, finite/unbounded and seekable/non-seekable behavior;
- state, ordering, determinism, idempotence, monotonicity and delivery semantics;
- errors, warnings, backpressure, retry, timeout, cancellation and compensation;
- file, database, network, message, secret, subprocess, GPU and human effects;
- platform, architecture, runtime, dependency, accelerator and version constraints;
- license, authorization, tenant, privacy and data-egress constraints;
- latency, memory, throughput, token and verification budgets;
- evidence strength and invalidation conditions.

The verdict vocabulary should include:

``` text
exact
compatible
compatible_with_adapter
compatible_with_loss
conditionally_compatible
incompatible
unknown
conflicted
revoked
```

## 16. Compatibility solving rather than similarity scoring

For producer port `p` and consumer port `q`, compatibility is a conjunction of hard predicates plus optional adapters:

``` text
eligible(p -> q) =
    type_assignable(p.output, q.input)
  AND shape_satisfies(p, q)
  AND effects_allowed(p, q, policy)
  AND environment_intersection_nonempty(p, q)
  AND version_constraints_satisfiable(p, q)
  AND evidence_floor_met(p, q)
  AND authority_valid(p, q)
```

If direct eligibility fails, adapter search is bounded by adapter classes, information-loss budget, effect budget, path length, and proof requirements. The solver returns a witness explaining each satisfied constraint or the first minimal conflict set.

## 17. Avoiding all-pairs explosion

At 100 million entities, global pair enumeration is impossible. Candidate generation is query-time and block-based:

1.  lifecycle, tenant, authorization, environment and artifact gates;
2.  exact contract, type, schema, protocol and port-family blocks;
3.  identifier, alias, history, dependency and verified-route neighbors;
4.  lexical/sparse fields and structured facets;
5.  MinHash/weighted MinHash/SimHash/clone and graph-fingerprint buckets;
6.  selected facet embeddings and late interaction;
7.  bounded typed graph expansion;
8.  deterministic directional compatibility checks;
9.  adapter/path search only over the request-local graph;
10. evidence-aware ranking and context-slice selection.

Blocking quality is measured by pair recall, reduction ratio, downstream route recall, latency, memory, and false compatibility—not by ANN recall alone.

## 18. Route and architecture representations

Use the smallest representation that preserves topology and constraints:

| Resolution             | Suitable output                                                             |
|------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| exact selection        | one opaque handle or `NONE`                                                 |
| linear composition     | `A>B>C`                                                                     |
| independent chains     | `A>B;C>D`                                                                   |
| typed route            | nodes, ports, bindings, adapters, guards and verifiers                      |
| workflow               | branches, loops, events, queues, state, retry and compensation              |
| component architecture | responsibilities, boundaries, contracts and quality attributes              |
| deployment             | placement, resources, trust zones, scaling and recovery                     |
| change plan            | current graph, target graph, migrations, compatibility windows and rollback |
| executable delta       | exact files, patches, commands, manifests and tests                         |

Simple compact grammar currently proven in the implementation:

``` text
NONE | CHAIN (';' CHAIN)*
CHAIN := HANDLE ('>' HANDLE)*
HANDLE := [A-Z]+
```

Richer forms remain proposals until a versioned parser and deterministic compiler support their semantics. Prose must never silently fill missing branches, effects, retries, or compensation.

## 19. Context-slice optimization

Context selection is a constrained optimization problem:

``` text
minimize    disclosure_cost(slice) + token_cost(slice) + latency(slice)
subject to  P(correct_route | demand, slice) >= quality_floor
            every hard constraint and decisive contrast is represented
            no unauthorized body or tenant fact is disclosed
```

Practical experiments should vary:

- 1, 2, 4, and 8 route alternatives;
- handle-only, compact, standard, detailed, and evidence-rich cards;
- positive candidates alone versus contrastive candidates plus hard negatives;
- graph neighborhood radius and port-edge budgets;
- examples, failures, tests, counterexamples and source-body disclosure;
- local ranker, local SLM, cheap model and strong-model selectors.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Part IV — Request-to-outcome control loop

## 20. DemandIR and RequestEnvelope

The user prompt is not the request contract. Normalize current input, multi-turn state, workspace, explicit memory, authority, environment and acceptance criteria into a versioned envelope:

``` yaml
request_envelope:
  request_id: ...
  tenant_id: ...
  actor: ...
  raw_inputs: []
  conversation_state_ref: ...
  workspace_snapshot: ...
  demanded_outcomes: []
  input_ports: []
  output_ports: []
  hard_constraints: []
  soft_preferences: []
  allowed_effects: []
  forbidden_effects: []
  authority: []
  privacy_and_egress: []
  environment: []
  budgets: {}
  acceptance_oracles: []
  unresolved_questions: []
```

Cheap deterministic parsing and templates should populate obvious fields. Local NLP and SLM stages handle bounded ambiguity. Strong models see only the unresolved delta when possible.

## 21. Retrieval and composition waterfall

The waterfall is configurable rather than globally fixed:

1.  hard policy and lifecycle gates;
2.  explicit handle resolution;
3.  verified result/route replay;
4.  known solution packs and repository-local conventions;
5.  deterministic request templates;
6.  exact names, aliases, identifiers, signatures and contracts;
7.  history, usage and negative-memory lookup;
8.  fielded lexical/BM25 and sparse retrieval;
9.  typed graph expansion and bidirectional route solving;
10. LSH, clone, schema, behavior and graph fingerprints;
11. selected embedding and late-interaction lanes;
12. local non-generative ranker or cross-encoder;
13. local SLM handle/route selection;
14. cheap hosted specialist;
15. strong model over finalists and unresolved facts;
16. bounded panel, clarification, review or safe abstention.

Stages may race, fuse, repeat, or be disabled under a versioned policy. Every stage returns an accepted route, abstention with missing facts, or escalation with a bounded unresolved delta and spend ceiling.

## 22. Deterministic binding and PlanLock

Before materialization, the compiler checks:

- every handle belongs to the supplied candidate snapshot;
- exact implementation revisions exist and are not revoked;
- port and control-flow bindings are valid;
- adapters are explicit and within the loss budget;
- mutation preconditions hold;
- effect ordering is safe;
- licenses, authorization and tenant policies pass;
- runtime, dependency and platform constraints are satisfiable;
- proof/evidence floors are met;
- verification and rollback/compensation plans exist where required;
- budgets remain feasible.

The resulting `PlanLock` binds demand, candidate snapshot, route IR, exact revisions, environment, policy epoch, artifacts and verifier requirements by digest.

## 23. Selective materialization

After selection and authorization:

1.  resolve only required capsule roles;
2.  fetch exact content-addressed artifacts;
3.  verify digest, signature, provenance and policy;
4.  construct a locked environment;
5.  install or unpack without unintended network access;
6.  revalidate contract and dependency assumptions;
7.  execute under declared limits and effects;
8.  retain all logs, traces, outputs and side effects;
9.  run an independent oracle;
10. accept, repair, replan, compensate, quarantine, or abstain.

## 24. Verification waterfall

Verification should escalate by claim type:

``` text
exact digest and schema checks
  -> static contract and policy checks
  -> declared tests
  -> property and metamorphic tests
  -> differential implementation checks
  -> mutation testing and adversarial negatives
  -> sandboxed execution over held-out fixtures
  -> specialized verifier or calibrated small model
  -> strong independent model judge
  -> human adjudication sample
```

The candidate implementation cannot be its own decisive verifier. Model-judge identity, prompt, input transformation, calibration, uncertainty and known blind spots belong in the receipt.

## 25. Exact receipts and replay

``` yaml
route_use_receipt:
  demand_digest: ...
  request_envelope_digest: ...
  candidate_snapshot_digest: ...
  selected_handles_and_revisions: []
  route_ir_and_plan_lock_digest: ...
  graph_policy_environment_epochs: []
  materialized_artifact_digests: []
  physical_model_provider_endpoint_attempts: []
  tool_and_harness_attempts: []
  inputs_outputs_effects: []
  verifier_and_oracle_results: []
  outcome_disposition: ...
  tokens_latency_resources_and_cost: ...
  failures_repairs_and_exclusions: []
  safe_replay_conditions: []
```

Replay is allowed only after input, environment, authority, policy, artifact, dependency and oracle conditions are revalidated. A prior success is evidence, not timeless truth.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Part V — RouterMesh: six separate control planes

## 26. Why routing must be decomposed

“Choose a cheaper LLM” conflates at least six decisions with different inputs, failure semantics, and learning targets. RouterMesh preserves them as separate planes:

1.  **Deterministic bypass.** Decide whether no generative model is required because an exact handle, verified replay, template, solver, package call, deterministic tool, or cached accepted result can satisfy the request.
2.  **Semantic model selection.** Choose the reasoning capability/model family appropriate to the unresolved task.
3.  **Provider routing.** Choose an eligible provider or local runtime for the selected semantic model or equivalent capability.
4.  **Endpoint scheduling.** Choose region, GPU, replica, queue, batch, cache affinity, concurrency slot, and admission time.
5.  **Harness/agent routing.** Choose the prompt program, tool bundle, context assembler, coding harness, workflow, agent topology, or human-in-the-loop pattern.
6.  **Verification-triggered control.** Decide whether to accept, repair, retry, fail over, escalate, replan, compensate, quarantine, seek authority, or abstain based on independent evidence.

Task-to-model selection must remain separate from provider/GPU routing. A provider outage should not silently change the semantic model; a semantic-model change is a different reasoning arm and requires a new decision record.

## 27. MechanismArm registry

Every selectable implementation, retrieval strategy, model, provider deployment, harness, verifier, human queue, or nested workflow is a mechanism arm:

``` yaml
mechanism_arm:
  arm_id: ...
  plane: ...
  logical_capability_contracts: []
  implementation_identity: ...
  supported_task_cells: []
  required_context_and_tools: []
  input_output_limits: []
  authority_policy_license_requirements: []
  privacy_and_egress: []
  effects: []
  determinism_and_seed_behavior: ...
  latency_cost_resource_models: []
  quality_calibration_evidence: []
  retry_failover_cancellation_semantics: ...
  health_capacity_and_rate_limits: ...
  version_and_invalidation: ...
```

The registry supports deterministic functions, exact caches, lexical/graph/vector retrievers, rankers, local models, hosted models, package calls, MCP tools, A2A agents, workflow engines, human review, and ensembles without pretending they are interchangeable.

## 28. Hard eligibility and constrained selection

First compute the eligible set:

``` text
E(x) = {
  a : capability_match(a,x)
      ∧ authority_pass(a,x)
      ∧ policy_pass(a,x)
      ∧ environment_feasible(a,x)
      ∧ privacy_egress_pass(a,x)
      ∧ evidence_floor(a,x)
      ∧ resource_feasible(a,x)
}
```

Then choose over the eligible Pareto frontier. One useful risk-constrained objective is:

``` text
a* = argmin_a E[
       monetary_cost
     + λ1 * latency
     + λ2 * disclosed_context
     + λ3 * verification_cost
     + λ4 * repair_cost
     + λ5 * operational_burden
     + λ6 * maintenance_and_lock_in
     | x, a]

subject to:
  P(independently_accepted_outcome | x,a) >= τ(x)
  CVaR_q(harm_or_failure | x,a) <= R(x)
  a ∈ E(x)
```

Weights and floors are tenant-, workload-, and risk-profile-specific. A Pareto set should be retained when one scalar score would hide meaningful tradeoffs.

## 29. Verification-aware escalation and value of information

Escalate only when the next action is expected to change a decision or reduce consequential uncertainty enough to justify its cost:

``` text
EVSI(next | state)
  = E[max_a U(a | state + observation_next)]
    - max_a E[U(a | state)]

invoke next when:
  EVSI(next | state) > expected_total_cost(next)
```

The state includes unresolved demand fields, candidate margins, compatibility conflicts, evidence strength, verifier disagreement, prior failures, budgets and committed effects. This makes “use a frontier model last” a decision policy rather than a slogan.

## 30. Failure transitions are not one fallback list

Maintain distinct transitions for:

- transient retry of the same physical attempt;
- endpoint or region failover for the same model/runtime contract;
- provider failover for the same semantic model;
- semantic model escalation or substitution;
- structured-output repair without repeating semantic reasoning;
- context expansion because decisive evidence was absent;
- verifier-triggered candidate repair;
- route or architecture replan;
- authorization request or human clarification;
- compensation after an external effect;
- safe degradation or abstention.

After user-visible streaming begins, a different semantic model must not be silently spliced into the response. After an external effect commits, a retry requires a proven idempotency key, transactional boundary, or compensation path.

## 31. Current router and orchestration ecosystem placement

| System or standard                                                                     | Useful role in Taedri                                                                         | Boundary                                                                                              |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [RouteLLM](https://github.com/lm-sys/RouteLLM)                                         | preference-trained strong/weak semantic model routing and threshold calibration               | primarily a two-model semantic selector; not the full six-plane control system                        |
| [LiteLLM routing](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/routing)                                | provider abstraction, deployment load balancing, cooldowns, rate limits, retries and failover | provider/endpoint plane; should not own capability truth or verification                              |
| [semantic-router](https://github.com/aurelio-labs/semantic-router)                     | low-latency intent and route classification, including local encoders                         | candidate mechanism for deterministic/semantic pre-routing, not proof of task completion              |
| TensorZero                                                                             | inference gateway, experiments, observability and optimization feedback                       | useful adapter and evaluation surface; Taedri retains logical arm and receipt identity                |
| Portkey, Helicone, Langfuse and OpenLLMetry                                            | gateway/observability/evaluation components                                                   | telemetry and provider policy do not replace semantic routing or independent outcome oracles          |
| LangGraph, Semantic Kernel, Haystack, LlamaIndex, PydanticAI and DSPy                  | harness, graph, prompt-program and agent execution arms                                       | register exact topology, tools, prompts and versions as arms rather than making one harness canonical |
| Temporal, Dagster, Prefect, Argo and Tekton                                            | durable workflow and worker execution                                                         | appropriate for long-running/retryable effects; not ordinary model selection                          |
| [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/latest)                            | host/client/server discovery and invocation of resources, prompts and tools                   | expose a compact Taedri meta-tool surface; tool descriptions remain untrusted assertions              |
| [A2A](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/)                                  | agent discovery, skills, tasks, messages, artifacts, streaming and lifecycle                  | agent-to-agent interoperability; Taedri adds capability/evidence and outcome receipts                 |
| [AG-UI](https://docs.ag-ui.com/concepts/architecture)                                  | event-based agent/user-interface integration                                                  | presentation and interaction events, not capability compatibility                                     |
| [OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) | normalized physical attempt, model, token, tool and agent telemetry                           | telemetry evidence must be joined to Taedri demand, route, effect and oracle identity                 |

## 32. Harness integration pattern

Expose a small logical surface rather than millions of tools:

``` text
taedri.describe_request
taedri.search_capabilities
taedri.expand_candidates
taedri.solve_route
taedri.resolve_artifacts
taedri.execute_plan
taedri.verify_outcome
taedri.inspect_receipt
taedri.report_negative_evidence
```

Each tool supports progressive disclosure. Harness files such as `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, skills, hooks, plugins, MCP servers and agent cards may configure behavior, but they enter through registered, versioned contracts with explicit authority and context budgets.

## 33. Learning without self-deception

Router learning data must be based on external or independent outcome labels, not model confidence or clicks alone. Required controls include:

- frozen development, calibration and sealed evaluation partitions;
- propensities for every selected arm;
- controlled exploration subject to risk limits;
- inverse-propensity or doubly robust offline evaluation;
- task-cell, tenant, model, provider and environment stratification;
- drift and out-of-distribution detection;
- uncertainty and abstention calibration;
- delayed outcome reconciliation;
- negative controls and deliberately bad arms;
- counterfactual replay where outputs for multiple arms can be obtained safely;
- exact policy and feature epochs in every decision receipt.

Optimize failure-inclusive cost per independently accepted outcome, not apparent win rate among completed or self-selected calls.

## 34. Router falsification experiments

1.  **Six-plane ablation.** Compare a monolithic router with separated semantic/provider/endpoint decisions under outages, price changes and GPU saturation.
2.  **Deterministic-bypass tournament.** Measure exact, history, template, graph and model lanes over a preregistered task population.
3.  **Selective escalation.** Compare fixed waterfalls, confidence thresholds, conformal abstention, contextual bandits and EVSI policies.
4.  **Quality-floor calibration.** Test whether a promised accepted-outcome floor holds by task cell, not only globally.
5.  **Provider-equivalence test.** Verify whether “same model” deployments actually match tokenizer, prompt adapter, tool schema, structured output and sampling semantics.
6.  **Failure-transition test.** Inject transport errors, rate limits, invalid JSON, semantic failures, verifier disagreement and committed effects; verify the correct transition.
7.  **1/2/4/8 finalist test.** Vary number and detail of route cards per selector model and measure accepted outcomes, tokens, latency and unsupported claims.
8.  **Local-to-frontier cascade.** Compare deterministic, local ranker, local Gemma/SLM, cheap hosted and strong-model arms over the same frozen tasks.
9.  **Learning-bias audit.** Demonstrate the difference between naïve logged win rates and propensity-corrected evaluation.
10. **Model-router drift.** Change model versions and task mix; measure calibration decay and automatic invalidation behavior.

### 34.1 Expanded plane-by-plane mechanism portfolio

#### Deterministic bypass and replay

- [Open Policy Agent](https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/latest/) and [Common Expression Language](https://cel.dev/) for hard eligibility and request-template rules;
- exact demand, state, artifact, policy and oracle replay keys;
- verified route/history lookup;
- GPTCache and RedisVL semantic-cache arms as provisional candidates only;
- local intent routes from semantic-router;
- prompt caching as model-call economics, not a no-model bypass.

A safe replay key binds normalized DemandIR, policy, acceptance contract, primitive/tool versions, relevant external state, authority, freshness, corpus snapshot, schema and verifier requirements. Effectful work normally reuses the plan and evidence; it does not blindly repeat the committed effect.

#### Semantic model selection

- [RouteLLM](https://github.com/lm-sys/RouteLLM) for preference-trained strong/weak routing;
- [FrugalGPT](https://github.com/stanford-futuredata/FrugalGPT) for budget-constrained cascades;
- local rules, logistic regression, GBDT, cross-encoder and SLM selectors;
- managed prompt routers from AWS, Azure and OpenRouter as opaque competing arms;
- Router-R1, MixLLM and contextual-bandit research arms under shadow evaluation;
- strong-model planning only over unresolved deltas and a locked model catalog.

Managed routers never become Taedri truth. Capture the actually selected semantic model and re-evaluate against application-specific independent outcomes.

#### Provider routing

- LiteLLM, Envoy AI Gateway, Portkey, OpenRouter provider selection, Cloudflare AI Gateway and Kong AI Gateway;
- health, price, residency, retention, feature support, rate limit and failover constraints;
- explicit equivalence tests for tokenizer, model revision, prompt adapters, tool calling, structured output, refusals, sampling, streaming and data policy.

If two providers expose materially different behavior under the same model name, they are separate semantic arms, not interchangeable deployments.

#### Endpoint scheduling

- [Kubernetes Gateway API Inference Extension](https://gateway-api-inference-extension.sigs.k8s.io/);
- [llm-d Router](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router);
- [NVIDIA Dynamo](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo);
- SGLang Model Gateway and vLLM production serving;
- KV/prefix-cache locality, adapter locality, prefill/decode topology, queue, memory, deadline and priority features.

Endpoint scheduling holds semantic model and provider contract fixed. Cache affinity must never trap a task on an inadequate model.

#### Harness, tool and agent routing

- deterministic conditional graphs in Haystack and ordinary workflow engines;
- LangGraph and LangChain middleware;
- LlamaIndex query-engine routing;
- AutoGen, Semantic Kernel and other multi-agent patterns;
- DSPy compilation for bounded prompt programs;
- MCP tool/resource/prompt servers and A2A Agent Cards/skills/tasks;
- hierarchical disclosure: server/agent → capability → interface → selected body.

Register an arm per behavior. `litellm.same_model_failover`, `langgraph.tool_router`, and `openrouter.auto_model` are more useful identities than one coarse vendor label.

#### Verification-triggered control

- compiler, type, schema, unit, integration, property, metamorphic and state/effect oracles;
- AutoMix-style answer-first escalation;
- semantic entropy and self-confidence as auxiliary uncertainty features;
- Guardrails/Instructor/Outlines-style format controls as interface verifiers, not semantic proof;
- conformal or selective abstention research arms;
- calibrated local and strong independent judges;
- human review and abstention for unresolved high-risk cells.

### 34.2 Failure-inclusive routing mathematics

Core metric:

``` text
CPAO = all realized routing, execution, repair and verification cost
       / independently accepted outcomes
```

Select a stronger arm `s` over weak arm `w` when:

``` text
V(x) * (p_accept(s,x) - p_accept(w,x))
  > incremental_model_cost
  + incremental_verification_cost
  + incremental_repair_cost
  + latency_penalty
  + risk_penalty
```

Panel alternatives should add failure diversity, not merely top individual scores. For candidate set `A`:

``` text
maximize  Σ utility(a) + γ log det(K_A + εI)
```

where `K_A` captures residual-error diversity. This can reject four highly correlated frontier models in favor of a smaller, cheaper, complementary set.

### 34.3 RouterMesh record set

Required records:

- `CallEnvelope` and `RouteSession`;
- `MechanismArm` and `ArmCapabilityClaim`;
- `RouterPolicy` and `EligibilityDecision`;
- `FallbackTransition` with retry/effect/streaming semantics;
- `ModelCatalogEntry`, `ProviderDeployment`, `EndpointSnapshot` and `HarnessTopology`;
- `CalibrationRecord`, `DriftRecord` and `ExplorationRecord`;
- `DecisionReceipt`, `PhysicalAttempt`, `VerificationDisposition` and `OutcomeReceipt`.

Every decision receipt retains selected and actual identities, candidates excluded with reason codes, feature and policy digests, predicted acceptance and uncertainty, propensity, selector overhead, model/provider/endpoint/harness facts, all attempts, committed effects and final independent outcome.

Required typed transitions include:

``` text
transport_retry_same_endpoint
provider_failover_same_semantic_model
endpoint_reschedule_same_attempt
semantic_model_escalation
format_repair
context_retrieval
tool_reselection
agent_handoff
plan_repair
plan_rebuild
effect_reconcile
compensate
clarify
abstain
```

### 34.4 Evaluation suite

Use complementary frozen suites rather than one router benchmark:

- [RouterBench](https://github.com/withmartian/routerbench) for model outcome/cost routing records;
- LLMRouterBench, RouterEval, TwinRouterBench and RouteJudge/ORBIT for broader and agentic routing;
- MMR-Bench and VL-RouterBench for multimodal selection;
- BFCL for function/tool calls;
- LiveMCPBench for large MCP tool discovery;
- ToolSandbox and `tau2-bench` for stateful tool interaction;
- SWE-bench and repository tasks for end-to-end coding economics;
- Taedri’s own real design-partner and maintenance tasks with hidden independent oracles.

Freeze model catalog, provider revisions, prices, prompt/harness variants, benchmark partitions and verifier versions. Report selector overhead, failed attempts, tool calls, repairs, human work, latency and delayed failures.

### 34.5 Safe adaptation sequence

1.  exact observability and identity;
2.  deterministic/rule baselines;
3.  local lexical, embedding and GBDT selectors;
4.  shadow comparisons of RouteLLM, local SLM and managed routers;
5.  provider and endpoint separation with model held fixed;
6.  MCP/A2A capability compilation and harness experiments;
7.  verification-driven typed control;
8.  doubly robust offline policy evaluation;
9.  conservative contextual bandit in reversible low-risk cells;
10. bounded exploration, per-cell calibration, drift detection and automatic rollback.

# Part VI — New research: a federated universal code-intelligence layer

## 35. Do not create a lossy universal AST

The right standardization boundary is not one syntax tree or one analyzer that pretends every language has identical semantics. Taedri should normalize identity, assertions, evidence, contracts, ports, relations, descriptor production and receipts while preserving analyzer-native facts.

``` text
language/package/build analyzers
  -> native fact bundles
  -> evidence-preserving adapter mappings
  -> Taedri subject and relation identities
  -> descriptor and compatibility portfolios
  -> retrieval/solver projections
```

When two analyzers disagree, retain both assertions and their scopes. A reconciliation rule may prefer one for a particular view, but it does not erase the disagreement.

## 36. Code-intelligence standards and their roles

| Source                                                                                             | Native strength                                                                                                         | Taedri ingestion role                                                                                        | Important limitation                                                                                       |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [SCIP](https://github.com/scip-code/scip)                                                          | language-agnostic index format for occurrences, symbols, documentation, relationships and navigation                    | primary import/export format for precise symbol and occurrence facts across supported indexers               | navigation graph is not a full behavioral or compatibility model                                           |
| [LSP](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.18/specification/) | interactive definitions, references, call/type hierarchy, symbols, semantic tokens, diagnostics, edits and capabilities | runtime analyzer adapter and workspace observation source                                                    | responses depend on workspace/build state and are not an immutable index unless snapshotted                |
| LSIF                                                                                               | persisted language-server index for navigation                                                                          | legacy/import compatibility where existing producers remain useful                                           | SCIP is generally the stronger new-index target; retain original version and producer                      |
| [Kythe schema](https://kythe.io/docs/schema/)                                                      | language-neutral VNames, semantic nodes, anchors and a rich edge vocabulary                                             | ontology and verifier precedent for definitions, references, aliases, types, calls, overrides and generation | VName stability and language rules vary; map rather than replace Taedri identity                           |
| [Glean](https://github.com/facebookincubator/Glean)                                                | typed, versioned fact predicates and derived facts over large codebases                                                 | precedent or optional engine for analyzer fact ingestion, derivation and cross-language querying             | Glean predicates remain source-specific evidence, not Taedri’s only storage model                          |
| [Tree-sitter](https://tree-sitter.github.io/tree-sitter/)                                          | incremental concrete syntax trees and broad grammar ecosystem                                                           | cheap exhaustive syntax pass, exact spans, error nodes and language grammar coverage                         | syntax alone cannot resolve types, dynamic dispatch or runtime behavior                                    |
| compiler frontends and typed ASTs                                                                  | language-specific name/type resolution and semantic facts                                                               | highest-fidelity symbols, overloads, generics, imports and compile diagnostics                               | version/toolchain/build flags materially affect output                                                     |
| [CodeQL](https://codeql.github.com/docs/)                                                          | relational code database with control/data/taint flow libraries                                                         | security, flow and semantic relation assertions plus query-based oracles                                     | query results are analyzer- and configuration-scoped; licensing/deployment terms need exact classification |
| [Joern CPG](https://docs.joern.io/code-property-graph/)                                            | merged AST, control-flow and dependence-style code property graphs over multiple languages                              | flow/motif/taint/path assertions and graph fingerprints                                                      | CPG schemas and frontend coverage differ; graph presence is not proof of runtime feasibility               |
| Universal Ctags                                                                                    | fast symbol/tag extraction across many languages and file types                                                         | cheap fallback discovery and alias/blocking keys                                                             | low semantic precision relative to compiler/indexer output                                                 |
| SemanticDB/TASTy, rust-analyzer data, Go export data, TypeScript program graphs, Roslyn symbols    | ecosystem-native semantic indexes                                                                                       | high-fidelity language plugins and exact external identities                                                 | not portable across ecosystems without mapped contracts                                                    |
| [LLVM IR](https://llvm.org/docs/LangRef.html), MLIR and bytecode/IL                                | normalized compiled operations, control flow, types and optimization boundaries                                         | source-to-build linkage, compiled behavior, language-crossing motifs and binary evidence                     | optimization may erase source structure; debug/provenance mapping is required                              |
| DWARF, PDB, source maps and debug metadata                                                         | source↔compiled location, type and inlining maps                                                                        | connect artifact/runtime observations back to occurrences and symbols                                        | missing or stripped metadata creates explicit coverage gaps                                                |
| Ghidra, Binary Ninja-style IR and disassembly analyzers                                            | binary functions, calls, symbols, data and control flow                                                                 | artifact verification and dependency/body discovery when source is absent                                    | inferred symbols/types require lower evidence status                                                       |

The adapter registry records which native facts are losslessly mapped, approximately mapped, unsupported, or contradictory.

## 37. AnalyzerFactBundle

``` yaml
analyzer_fact_bundle:
  bundle_id: taedri://analyzer-bundle/<digest>
  artifact_digest: ...
  workspace_and_build_snapshot: ...
  producer:
    analyzer: ...
    version: ...
    configuration: ...
    language_and_toolchain: ...
  native_schema: ...
  native_fact_count: ...
  native_payload_ref: ...
  mapped_assertions: []
  mapping_manifest: ...
  diagnostics: []
  coverage_ledger: ...
  nondeterminism_and_environment: ...
```

Retain the native payload by digest so a future mapper can reprocess it without rerunning an expensive compiler. Mapped assertions link back to exact native fact coordinates.

## 38. LanguagePlugin contract

Every language or artifact analyzer implements only the supported capabilities:

``` text
detect_artifacts
inventory_files_and_generated_regions
parse_syntax
resolve_symbols_and_occurrences
resolve_types_and_overloads
extract_import_export_dependency_edges
extract_calls_control_and_data_flow
extract_effects_errors_state_and_resources
extract_tests_fixtures_examples_and_oracles
extract_build_runtime_and_package_metadata
emit_native_fact_bundle
map_native_facts_to_taedri
report_coverage_and_unknowns
```

Capability negotiation is explicit. A Tree-sitter plugin may provide excellent syntax and no type resolution; a compiler plugin may require a successful build; an LSP adapter may provide partial results over a broken workspace. The absence of an assertion is never silently treated as a negative fact.

## 39. Package, build and supply-chain identity

Connect code entities to exact package and artifact records using:

- Package URL (`purl`) and ecosystem-native coordinates;
- VCS URL, commit, tree and subdirectory;
- PyPI/npm/Maven/Cargo/NuGet/Go/OCI metadata;
- source archive, wheel, binary, container and layer digests;
- lockfile and dependency-resolution graph;
- build recipe, toolchain, flags, platform and environment;
- [SPDX 3.0](https://spdx.github.io/spdx-spec/v3.0.1/) and CycloneDX SBOM records;
- [SLSA provenance](https://slsa.dev/spec/v1.2/provenance), in-toto attestations and Sigstore bundles;
- OSV vulnerability ranges, VEX status and OpenSSF project signals;
- license expressions, notices and per-artifact rights.

Package reputation is a routing feature, not a truth gate by itself. A popular package may be ineligible for a specific version, platform, license, policy, behavior, or maintenance requirement.

## 40. Processing an existing package end to end

``` text
resolve source and exact release
  -> acquire archives without execution
  -> hash, identify, license/SBOM/provenance scan
  -> exhaustive file and entity inventory
  -> cheap syntax and metadata pass
  -> semantic index/compiler/LSP passes
  -> framework/domain/plugin analyzers
  -> tests/examples/issues/changelog extraction
  -> optional isolated build and runtime observation
  -> identity reconciliation
  -> assertion and descriptor production
  -> compatibility signature generation
  -> index projections and body-free cards
  -> independent verification and immutable epoch publication
```

Analysis profiles should be progressive:

- **metadata-only** for initial discovery and rights gating;
- **syntax-complete** for exhaustive entity inventory;
- **semantic** for symbols, types and high-confidence edges;
- **framework-aware** for registries, schemas, decorators and domain contracts;
- **build-aware** for generated code, compiled artifacts and dependency realization;
- **runtime-observed** for effects, errors, performance, state and actual call paths;
- **verified** for claim-specific independent testing.

## 41. Cross-analyzer reconciliation

For each candidate fact, reconciliation considers:

- exact artifact/build/workspace equality;
- referent alignment through occurrence and symbol identities;
- analyzer capability and known failure modes;
- direct versus inferred fact status;
- language-specific semantic authority;
- configuration and version scope;
- test/runtime corroboration;
- contradictions and negative cases.

Do not create a majority-vote “truth” when three cheap parsers agree against one compiler. Evidence type and referent precision matter more than raw producer count.

## 42. New code-intelligence experiments

1.  **SCIP–Kythe–LSP triangle.** Index the same repositories and measure entity alignment, edge coverage, contradictions, stability and cost.
2.  **Syntax versus semantic recovery.** Compare Tree-sitter, ctags, compiler, SCIP and LSP facts over valid, partially broken and generated projects.
3.  **Source-to-binary lineage.** Link source symbols through compiler IR/debug data to binary functions and runtime traces.
4.  **Dynamic-language resolution.** Combine static Python/JavaScript facts with import tracing, coverage, monkey-patch observation and type/runtime evidence.
5.  **Generated-code identity.** Test protobuf/OpenAPI/ORM/UI generators across regeneration, formatting, reordered inputs and template upgrades.
6.  **Fact round trip.** Export a Taedri projection to SCIP/Kythe-like forms and reimport it; quantify lost and invented semantics.
7.  **Analyzer disagreement corpus.** Intentionally construct overload, aliasing, reflection, metaprogramming, conditional-import and build-flag cases.
8.  **Incremental update benchmark.** Change one symbol, dependency, generator input or build flag and measure exact invalidation fan-out.
9.  **Language-plugin conformance.** Require every plugin to pass identity, span, unresolved-reference, error-node, versioning and coverage tests.
10. **Black-box descriptor utility.** Measure whether descriptions derived from precise semantic/flow facts improve retrieval and route success over docstrings alone.

### 42.1. Add a build-context plane, not just a source plane

Source identity is insufficient for semantic identity. The same file may resolve to different symbols, types, generated sources, binaries and effects under another dependency lock, feature set, compiler, target or build flag. `BuildContext` therefore becomes a first-class subject with its own immutable digest.

Minimum sources are:

- [Clang compilation databases](https://clang.llvm.org/docs/JSONCompilationDatabase.html), including the exact working directory, arguments, input and output for each translation unit;
- [Build Server Protocol](https://build-server-protocol.github.io/docs/specification) targets, sources, dependencies, capabilities, compiler options, generated-source flags and task ancestry;
- [Bazel Build Event Protocol](https://bazel.build/remote/bep) events and named-set/artifact relationships;
- Maven/Gradle task graphs, Cargo metadata and features, Go module/workspace graphs, npm lockfiles and TypeScript project references;
- Python build-system requirements, wheel tags, environment markers, optional dependencies and generated extension metadata;
- compiler/runtime/container identity, platform, architecture, environment and any semantic-affecting configuration.

Build-context equality is exact only when the canonicalized inputs are equal. Similar configurations may form a candidate lineage or compatibility claim but never an identity merge.

``` yaml
build_context:
  context_id: taedri://build-context/<digest>
  source_snapshot_id: ...
  build_system: {name: ..., version: ...}
  targets: [...]
  toolchains: [...]
  dependency_solution_digest: ...
  feature_and_flag_digest: ...
  generated_input_digest: ...
  platform_contract: ...
  environment_allowlist: ...
  captured_by: ...
  replay_recipe_ref: ...
  completeness: ...
```

### 42.2. Use an explicit artifact and lineage lattice

Different identifiers answer different questions:

| Layer                | Recommended identifiers                                              | What it establishes                     |
|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| ecosystem coordinate | Package URL plus registry-native coordinate                          | package/release naming                  |
| source snapshot      | VCS commit/tree plus repository/subdirectory                         | immutable source observation            |
| archived source      | Software Heritage persistent ID where available                      | durable content/archive identity        |
| produced artifact    | digest, OCI digest, build ID and OmniBOR artifact ID where available | immutable distributable/binary identity |
| build                | `BuildContext` digest plus provenance statement                      | exact configured production event       |
| entity revision      | artifact/build + native symbol + file digest + anchor                | one extracted code-entity observation   |
| logical entity       | registry ID connected by evidence-bearing lineage claims             | cross-release continuity hypothesis     |
| runtime entity       | image/build ID plus address/token/debug coordinate                   | one deployed executable referent        |

Source maps, DWARF, Portable PDB, JVM/.NET metadata and compiler-origin records then create evidence-bearing `SOURCE_MAPPED_TO`, `COMPILED_TO`, `GENERATED_FROM` and `OBSERVED_AS` edges. In particular, [ECMA-426](https://tc39.es/ecma426/) should be treated as a source-map evidence format, not as proof that two source-level objects are behaviorally identical.

### 42.3. Treat interface artifacts as high-confidence ports

The [WebAssembly Component Model’s WIT](https://component-model.bytecodealliance.org/design/wit.html) is especially close to the desired port abstraction because it describes functions, types, resources, interfaces and worlds independently of implementation. Equivalent contract sources include:

- OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, Smithy and GraphQL schemas;
- Protocol Buffer descriptors and gRPC service descriptors;
- JSON Schema, Avro, Parquet and Arrow schemas;
- Python stubs and protocols, TypeScript declarations, Rust traits, Go interfaces, JVM/.NET metadata and Swift SymbolGraph;
- CLI help/manpage/specification schemas, environment contracts and file-format descriptors;
- MCP tool schemas, A2A agent cards and event/webhook contracts.

Each imported port must retain the difference between **declared**, **statically inferred**, **runtime observed** and **independently verified**. Generated clients link back to one canonical interface root so the graph can collapse equivalent generated families without erasing language-specific implementations.

### 42.4. Make package metadata an independent evidence stream

[Python Core Metadata 2.5](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/core-metadata/) adds `Import-Name` and `Import-Namespace`, improving distribution-to-import mapping, while fields such as `Requires-Python`, `Requires-Dist`, extras, SPDX license expression and wheel tags constrain compatibility. These are artifact/release claims; they must not be silently generalized to every source checkout or differently built wheel.

For every ecosystem, ingest independently:

- registry metadata and yanks/deprecations;
- source-distribution and binary-distribution metadata;
- import/module namespace declarations;
- public typing/stub distribution rules;
- entry points, plugins, extras/features and platform selectors;
- ownership, maintenance, release cadence and deprecation notices;
- documentation inventories, examples, changelogs, migration guides and issue references.

Conflicts between source, stubs, docs, package metadata, compiler facts and runtime observations become explicit contradiction records. They are useful signals for verification and routing, not dirty data to overwrite.

### 42.5. Attach a supply-chain evidence graph

Ingest [SPDX 3.0.1](https://spdx.github.io/spdx-spec/v3.0.1/), [CycloneDX](https://cyclonedx.org/specification/overview/), [SLSA provenance](https://slsa.dev/spec/v1.2/provenance), in-toto attestations, DSSE envelopes, OSV, CSAF, SARIF, VEX and [GUAC](https://docs.guac.sh/) projections. Preserve their native records and project scoped claims onto immutable artifacts before propagating any risk to contained entities.

This permits deterministic constraints such as:

``` text
license_expression in tenant.allowlist
AND provenance_level >= required_level
AND artifact_digest not in affected_OSV_range
AND VEX_status != affected
AND build_platform satisfies deployment_platform
```

An SBOM generally proves neither that a named vulnerable method is reachable nor that an unaffected method is safe. Reachability, exploitability and remediation remain separate evidence layers.

### 42.6. P0 package ladder and exit gates

The first corpus should maximize semantic variety, not download count. Index three materially different releases of each family:

| Package family                                         | Why it is valuable                 | Stress cases                                                            |
|--------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `requests`/HTTP stack                                  | familiar functional baseline       | layered dependencies, exceptions, transport adapters                    |
| `pydantic`                                             | model/schema/metaprogramming       | v1→v2 migration, generated validation, decorators, typing               |
| `pytest` + `pluggy`                                    | plugin/hook architecture           | discovery, fixtures, hook specifications, dynamic registration          |
| SQLAlchemy                                             | rich class/descriptor/query system | declarative metaprogramming, sync/async, dialect plugins                |
| pandas                                                 | extremely broad object API         | generated docs, overload-like dispatch, extension types, C-backed paths |
| NumPy plus `orjson` or another extension-heavy package | native/binary boundary             | stubs, ufuncs, ABI/platform wheels, compiled implementation             |

P0 is not complete until the following are measured on a frozen conformance corpus:

1.  at least 99.9% deterministic entity-revision IDs across identical reruns;
2.  zero silent cross-artifact or cross-build identity merges;
3.  fewer than 0.5% false merges in sampled cross-release lineage candidates;
4.  every promoted assertion traceable to exact artifact, extractor version, native fact and source/build coordinate;
5.  unknown/unsupported analyzer coverage is explicitly reported;
6.  package, module, class, callable, method, attribute, parameter, local and generated-entity cases are represented;
7.  exact, lexical, structural, graph and semantic retrieval can each be ablated;
8.  1/2/4/8 alternative route-card tests show whether added diversity improves independently accepted outcomes per token;
9.  post-selection body resolution is proven to reduce disclosed bytes/tokens without lowering accepted-task success beyond the preregistered margin;
10. all results are reproducible from immutable inputs and an exact receipt.

# Part VII — Source acquisition and primitive mining program

## 43. Acquisition objective

Popularity alone produces a redundant corpus. Select sources for marginal verified capability and edge yield:

``` text
gain(source) =
    w1 * novel_verified_capabilities
  + w2 * novel_typed_edges
  + w3 * independent_oracles
  + w4 * cross_backend_equivalences
  + w5 * negative_constraints
  + w6 * task_demand_coverage
  + w7 * version_drift_information
  - w8 * extraction_cost
  - w9 * execution_cost
  - w10 * rights_risk
  - w11 * contamination_risk
  - w12 * duplicate_saturation
```

Use submodular coverage or log-determinant diversity so the scheduler does not repeatedly select near-duplicate libraries from one domain.

## 44. Required source partitions

| Partition                                  | What it teaches                                             | Retrieval/training status                       |
|--------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| package artifacts and public APIs          | what capabilities exist and how they are invoked            | ordinary candidate ingestion subject to rights  |
| specifications and schemas                 | ports, protocols, constraints and compatibility             | preferred machine-readable evidence             |
| tests, fixtures and conformance suites     | behavior, boundaries, failures and oracles                  | evidence plane; test rights recorded separately |
| examples and integration catalogs          | successful compositions and usage motifs                    | candidate composition evidence                  |
| issues, patches and changelogs             | negative knowledge, version breakpoints and failure history | history/negative-memory indexes                 |
| repositories and dependency graphs         | actual adoption, architecture and supply chain              | provenance and ecosystem features               |
| competitions and public task corpora       | real demand archetypes and metric structures                | task plane with contamination labels            |
| sealed benchmarks and hidden tests         | independent evaluation                                      | inaccessible to ordinary retrieval/training     |
| runtime observations and customer receipts | what worked in exact environments                           | tenant-scoped evidence and learning data        |

## 45. High-yield machine-readable ecosystems

Prioritize sources that already encode ports or composition:

- OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, JSON Schema, Protocol Buffers, Smithy, GraphQL and gRPC descriptors;
- Apache Camel components and Kamelets;
- Airflow providers, Singer/Meltano connectors, dbt adapters and OpenLineage;
- n8n, Pipedream, Zapier, Make and IFTTT templates where rights and APIs permit;
- Postman collections, public API hubs and SDK generators;
- Kubernetes CRDs, Tekton Catalog, Argo examples, Helm values schemas, Kustomize, Crossplane and KRM functions;
- Storybook CSF, design-token registries and UI component manifests;
- FFmpeg filter/codec registries, GStreamer plugin/caps registries, OpenImageIO/OpenColorIO and OpenTimelineIO;
- dataframe portability suites such as Narwhals/Ibis and query transpilers such as SQLGlot;
- workflow descriptions, policy catalogs, conformance suites and reference architectures.

These often yield more typed edges per extraction hour than raw repository crawling.

## 46. PyPI portfolio strategy

Build a stratified portfolio across:

- packaging, environment and version semantics;
- types, schemas, validation and serialization;
- HTTP, async, protocols, state machines and retries;
- routing, dependency injection and plugin systems;
- databases, transactions, migrations and query compilation;
- arrays, tables, tensors, estimators and file formats;
- testing, property generation, fuzzing and differential oracles;
- cloud SDKs and machine-readable service models;
- parsers, formatters, refactoring and static analysis;
- authentication, cryptography, policy and redaction;
- ML, agents, tool protocols and model serving;
- graphs, search, sketches, optimization and algorithms;
- data cleansing, entity resolution, strings, JSON and telemetry;
- image, video, audio, charts, timelines and multimodal processing;
- scientific, geospatial, medical, financial, legal and industry-specific niches.

Correct download popularity for dependency centrality, generated clients, namespace families, platform artifacts, abandoned projects, extras, duplicate implementations and domain saturation.

## 47. Esoteric Capability Worker Pack

Eight source-specific workers share one publication contract:

1.  **Data contract and cleansing compiler** — Pandera, Frictionless, TDDA, cuallee, CleverCSV, PyJanitor, Cleanlab and tests.
2.  **Cross-engine semantic compiler** — Narwhals, Ibis, SQLGlot, Arrow/DataFusion and backend conformance matrices.
3.  **JSON, logging and telemetry compiler** — JSON Schema/query languages, structlog, OpenTelemetry conventions and Collector components.
4.  **Visual/media capability harvester** — FFmpeg, GStreamer, libvips, OpenImageIO/OpenColorIO, Vega-Lite and OpenTimelineIO.
5.  **Kubernetes/template compiler** — Jobs, Helm, Kustomize, Tekton, Argo, Crossplane, CUE/KCL/KRM, KEDA and KubeRay.
6.  **Generator and architecture compiler** — Backstage, Copier/Cookiecutter, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI generators, Storybook and reference applications.
7.  **Task/oracle and contamination compiler** — package tests plus approved task/benchmark development partitions.
8.  **Conformance and receipt runner** — disposable environments, post-selection body resolution, execution, independent verification and counterexample minimization.

Shared worker stages:

``` text
discover
  -> fingerprint and rights gate
  -> extract machine-readable surface
  -> static symbol/schema graph
  -> candidate capsule generation
  -> evidence attachment
  -> cheap validation
  -> isolated execution
  -> independent verification
  -> counterexample minimization
  -> immutable versioned publication
```

## 48. Candidate-generation scale without truth inflation

Taedri may generate millions of candidate ideas, including NAICS-specific, human-action, CRUD, migration, transformation, reporting, data, media and infrastructure variations. High-volume lanes—including local models and approved high-throughput endpoints—must preserve:

- `candidate=true` and `serves_truth=false` by default;
- exact producer/model/prompt/configuration lineage;
- quota and cost receipts;
- deduplication and novelty estimates;
- task/domain/template ancestry;
- no automatic promotion from volume or model confidence;
- deterministic verification gates and evidence-linked promotion.

Candidate diversity is useful for coverage and hard-negative generation. It is not proof of capability inventory quality.

## 49. Three ingestion waves

### Wave A — deterministic and schema-rich

- schema/validation/string/JSON packages;
- SCIP/Kythe/Tree-sitter and package metadata;
- Narwhals/Ibis/SQLGlot/Arrow/DataFusion;
- OpenTelemetry, Vega-Lite, FFmpeg/GStreamer registries;
- Kubernetes schemas, Helm/Kustomize, Tekton/Argo examples;
- OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/Protobuf generators and conformance suites.

### Wave B — stateful and cross-engine

- entity resolution, online ML, drift and repair libraries;
- Hamilton, dlt, Dagster, Prefect, dbt/SQLMesh and OpenLineage;
- image/video quality, subtitle and audio tools;
- KEDA/KubeRay/Kueue/Crossplane/policy catalogs;
- Backstage/Copier/Storybook/reference architecture motifs;
- development partitions of task and benchmark corpora.

### Wave C — expensive, ambiguous or judge-dependent

- learned visual/media quality and semantic edit verification;
- multimodal GUI and interactive-agent environments;
- distributed controller failure mining;
- human-preference and strong-model description generation;
- incomplete-rights or weak-oracle sources.

## 50. Adaptive acquisition scheduler

Each worker writes an `AcquisitionReceipt` containing discovered entities, candidate capsules, novel edges, verified claims, contradictions, execution cost, source health, rights state and task-demand coverage. A scheduler allocates the next budget using measured marginal yield rather than a static package list.

Periodically reserve exploration budget for:

- new ecosystems and languages;
- underrepresented subject and capability families;
- packages with unusual schemas or conformance suites;
- low-popularity sources with high edge diversity;
- negative sources and known incompatibility corpora;
- version history and breaking-change mining;
- sources proposed by real failed requests.
