# Part VIII — Target architecture: production SaaS and 5M → 50M → 100M

## 51. Target production-architecture decision

Build Taedri as a canonical registry with independently rebuildable projections:

1.  **PostgreSQL** is authoritative for identities, versions, manifests, evidence metadata, tenancy, authorization anchors, policy/configuration epochs, outbox events and projection watermarks.
2.  **S3-compatible content-addressed storage** holds packages, source bodies, analyzer payloads, capsule roles, receipts, model outputs, snapshots and large evidence.
3.  **Hybrid search** serves exact terms, fielded BM25, filters, sparse features and initially dense vectors. OpenSearch is a practical first production engine; Vespa is a strong ranking-centric alternative.
4.  **Bidirectional compact adjacency** serves bounded typed route solving. Begin in partitioned PostgreSQL; split to a wide-column/KV projection only at a measured limit.
5.  **Temporal or an equivalent durable workflow engine** coordinates acquisition, analysis, enrichment, reindexing, verification, retries and recovery.
6.  **Redis/Valkey** is an ephemeral cache, rate-limit and short-lived coordination layer—not durable truth.
7.  **ClickHouse** holds high-volume usage, search-quality, router, audit, cost and experiment analytics when volume justifies it.
8.  **Sandbox execution** is physically separated from control/query services and runs one untrusted job per microVM, hardened pod, or capability-restricted WASI instance.

Do not begin with a general-purpose graph database. The hot graph workload is exact adjacency plus shallow, typed, bounded path solving. Add a graph engine only after production query traces demonstrate deep or unconstrained traversals it materially improves.

`Vector*` remains inside the hybrid search engine initially. Split it only when ANN indexing, filtered recall, model-family isolation or memory pressure requires independent scaling.

## 54. Canonical versus projection data

Every durable mutation lands in PostgreSQL and a transactional outbox in the same transaction. Projectors consume events idempotently and update search, vector, adjacency, analytics and caches.

Do not dual-write the canonical store and indexes directly from request handlers.

Large content remains in CAS and is referenced by digest. Every serving projection is reproducible from canonical metadata, immutable artifacts and versioned projection recipes.

Support three read consistency modes:

- `eventual` — fastest serving projection;
- `read_your_write` — index result merged with recent authorized canonical rows;
- `wait_for_projection` — block until a named projection watermark reaches the required version.

## 55. Public catalog plus tenant overlays

Do not copy the public PyPI/npm/code catalog for every customer. Maintain:

``` text
global_public
organization_shared
tenant_private
project_private
```

Tenant overlays can add private code, descriptions, aliases, embeddings, trust decisions, deprecations, compatibility evidence, route history and edges to public entities. Queries merge global and authorized overlay candidates before ranking.

Public and private neighbor blocks should remain separable. Do not read unauthorized mixed adjacency and filter after graph expansion.

## 56. Compact adjacency and route serving

Canonical edge records retain conditions, evidence and history. Online adjacency stores a compact projection:

``` text
(scope_bucket, node_id, edge_type_bucket, adjacency_shard)
  -> [target_id, edge_type_id, predicate_bitmap,
      cost_bucket, confidence_bucket, edge_version]...
```

Materialize forward and reverse projections. Chunk high-degree nodes to avoid one hot row. Route solving enforces:

- maximum hops;
- maximum expanded nodes;
- maximum neighbors sampled/read per hub;
- allowed edge-sequence automaton;
- per-edge and total cost/loss/risk budgets;
- authorization on every expansion;
- timeout and alternative limits.

Use typed bidirectional BFS for unweighted paths, Dijkstra/A\* for costed paths, and constrained finite-state solving for allowed edge sequences.

## 57. Scale progression

| Concern               | ~5M entities                           | 20M–50M entities                                   | 100M stress target                                           |
|-----------------------|----------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| canonical store       | HA PostgreSQL                          | larger HA PostgreSQL, replicas and partitions      | sharded PostgreSQL/Citus/distributed option only if measured |
| lexical/hybrid search | one managed cluster                    | multi-node cluster, index families and routing     | clusters by public/tenant or ecosystem/entity family         |
| dense retrieval       | search-engine vectors or pgvector      | retain if healthy; otherwise dedicated vector tier | quantized, model-family collections and dedicated shards     |
| adjacency             | partitioned forward/reverse PostgreSQL | remain until p99/write amplification fails SLO     | materialized KV neighbor blocks and hub chunking             |
| object bodies         | S3-compatible CAS                      | lifecycle tiers and cross-region copy              | same; primarily an object-storage problem                    |
| workflow              | managed/HA Temporal                    | task queues and worker pools by family             | regional fleets and replayable workflows                     |
| analytics             | optional managed ClickHouse            | recommended                                        | dedicated/serverless organization with tiered retention      |
| graph analytics       | offline/columnar exports               | evaluate actual demand                             | secondary graph projection only if justified                 |

Specialized infrastructure is added at a measured boundary, not because 100M appears in a slide.

## 58. Storage planning formulas

Capacity must be calculated from the real corpus:

``` text
canonical_bytes
  = entity_count * compressed_core_row
  + assertion_count * compressed_assertion
  + indexes + MVCC + replicas + temporary_maintenance_space

vector_bytes
  = entity_count * online_vectors_per_entity
    * dimensions * bytes_per_dimension
    * ANN_and_replication_multiplier

edge_bytes
  = directed_edge_count * compact_edge_bytes
    + canonical_evidence_and_condition_bytes
```

Approximate raw vector examples:

| Representation | Bytes/entity |      5M |     50M |    100M |
|----------------|-------------:|--------:|--------:|--------:|
| 384d float16   |         ~768 | ~3.8 GB |  ~38 GB |  ~76 GB |
| 768d float16   |       ~1,536 | ~7.7 GB |  ~77 GB | ~154 GB |
| 768d float32   |       ~3,072 |  ~15 GB | ~154 GB | ~307 GB |
| 384d int8      |         ~384 | ~1.9 GB |  ~19 GB |  ~38 GB |

ANN graphs, segments, payloads, replicas, merges and headroom may multiply raw vector storage by several times. Experimental embeddings should remain in CAS or cold analytical storage until a benchmark demonstrates marginal utility. The schema supports unlimited variants; the online index is a promoted view.

## 59. Search-stack alternatives

### Recommended modular profile

PostgreSQL + OpenSearch + CAS + Temporal, adding Qdrant and ClickHouse at measured boundaries.

### Lean PostgreSQL-first profile

PostgreSQL FTS/trigram + pgvector + adjacency tables + CAS + Temporal. Credible for the first millions at moderate QPS, but split before transactional writes, heavy FTS, ANN, route expansion and analytics interfere.

### Ranking-centric Vespa profile

PostgreSQL + [Vespa](https://docs.vespa.ai/en/ranking/phased-ranking.html) + CAS + Temporal. Vespa unifies lexical, sparse, tensor, ANN, filtering and multi-phase ranking, but imposes greater operational and ranking-model complexity.

### Managed-cloud profiles

- AWS: Aurora PostgreSQL, OpenSearch, S3, DynamoDB adjacency when needed, ECS/EKS, Temporal Cloud and ClickHouse Cloud.
- GCP: AlloyDB, GCS, Cloud Run/GKE, managed search/vector, Temporal Cloud and ClickHouse Cloud.
- Distributed SQL becomes relevant only for proven active-active writes, regional survival or strict data-locality requirements.

## 60. Fly.io assessment

[Fly Machines](https://fly.io/docs/machines/) are well matched to:

- stateless API/query replicas near users;
- burst ingestion and descriptor workers;
- disposable per-job verification Machines;
- regional caches and read-oriented services;
- workers placed near artifact or model endpoints.

Recommended early Fly shape:

- one canonical write home region;
- stateless APIs in selected regions;
- local caches but no accidental active-active canonical writes;
- worker groups separated by process/application;
- Machines API for burst sandboxes;
- managed external search, vector, workflow and analytics as scale grows.

Fly Volumes are host/region-local and not automatically replicated; use them for caches or rebuildable state, not the only canonical or index copy. Tigris or another S3-compatible store can serve the CAS with an independent backup/versioning plan. Fly remains a viable stateless/worker platform at large corpus scale even when stateful clusters move elsewhere.

## 61. Authentication, authorization and tenant isolation

Use an OIDC provider with organizations, service identities and enterprise SSO. WorkOS, Auth0, Clerk and Keycloak are viable mechanism choices.

Enforce scope in every physical plane:

- PostgreSQL rows and row-level policies;
- search filters and index routing;
- vector payloads/collections/shards;
- cache keys;
- workflow/task payloads;
- adjacency blocks;
- CAS prefixes and scoped credentials;
- usage, audit and telemetry records.

[PostgreSQL row security](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-rowsecurity.html) should be forced for tenant tables, with no ordinary application role holding `BYPASSRLS`. The server derives scope; a client-supplied tenant filter is never the authorization boundary.

Isolation tiers:

- pooled long-tail tenants;
- dedicated search/vector shards for large tenants;
- dedicated database/index/key/region for regulated tenants;
- separate immutable global public catalog.

## 62. Sandboxed processing and verification

Use escalating trust zones:

1.  static parsing without import or execution;
2.  isolated build/import verification;
3.  stricter user-requested execution with explicit effects;
4.  WASI/component execution for pure transforms where feasible.

Each untrusted job receives default-deny network, read-only root, ephemeral scratch space, scoped artifact credentials, CPU/RAM/PID/file/disk/output/time limits, no host mounts or metadata service, capped/sanitized logs, and destruction after receipt publication.

Mechanism alternatives include Firecracker microVMs, gVisor, Kata Containers, hardened Kubernetes RuntimeClasses and Wasmtime/WASI. Compatibility and isolation properties are benchmarked per workload rather than assumed.

## 63. Workflow and task-queue design

Suggested durable task queues:

- fetch/quarantine/unpack;
- package metadata/SBOM/provenance;
- syntax by language family;
- semantic/compiler/build analysis;
- documentation/tests/examples;
- descriptors and local SLM;
- embeddings by CPU/GPU/model family;
- compatibility inference;
- isolated runtime verification;
- search/vector/adjacency projection;
- release diff and invalidation;
- backfill/reindex;
- deletion/revocation/retention;
- billing and meter export.

Use workflow-engine task queues before adding an independent broker. Add Kafka, Redpanda, NATS JetStream or a cloud event bus when independent streaming consumers, throughput, retention or replay requirements clearly exceed workflow semantics.

## 64. Observability and learning telemetry

Instrument every service and worker with OpenTelemetry. Join physical traces to Taedri identities:

- tenant/scope hash;
- demand and RequestEnvelope version;
- query and RouterMesh arms;
- projection watermarks;
- candidate counts per stage;
- ANN/LSH/graph parameters;
- route expansion and alternative count;
- cache status;
- descriptor, embedding, ranker and model versions;
- tokens, latency, compute and monetary cost;
- verifier result and receipt digest.

Core dashboards include query latency, ingest acceptance latency, projection lag, queue age, retrieval recall, zero-result rate, route success, graph expansions, verifier disagreement, sandbox failure, per-tenant spend and restore/reindex time.

High-cardinality entity and tenant detail belongs in traces/logs, not metric labels.

## 65. Usage metering and commercial events

Retain an append-only ledger:

``` text
event_id, tenant_id, feature, quantity, unit,
occurred_at, source_receipt, price_version, workflow_id
```

Candidate billable dimensions include active stored entities, CAS bytes/egress, promoted indexed vectors, edges, ingestion CPU/GPU seconds, sandbox compute, route/query tier, model tokens, verification jobs, retention and seats. Pricing should emphasize organizational control, reuse and accepted outcomes rather than reward primitive fragmentation or unnecessary tokens.

OpenMeter and Stripe are possible aggregation/invoice mechanisms. Taedri’s internal ledger remains authoritative and the billing provider is not a synchronous query dependency.

## 66. Disaster recovery and reproducibility

| Data                               | Authority                 | Recovery                                                                             |
|------------------------------------|---------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| identity/version/evidence metadata | PostgreSQL                | HA, WAL archive, PITR and cross-region backup                                        |
| bodies/artifacts                   | CAS                       | versioning/object lock where needed, cross-region/provider copy, digest verification |
| search/vector indexes              | projection                | snapshots for RTO plus deterministic replay                                          |
| adjacency                          | projection                | snapshots and replay from canonical edges                                            |
| usage ledger                       | PostgreSQL/analytics copy | durable ledger, reconciliation and exports                                           |
| cache                              | none                      | discard and refill                                                                   |

Automate restore smoke tests, sampled CAS digest verification, projection rebuilds, region recovery and provider-exit exercises. A backup is not proven until a clean environment successfully restores and verifies it.

## 67. Scale and failure experiments

### Corpus and traffic

- ingest a real 5M-entity corpus;
- generate 20M/50M/100M variants preserving language, package, tenant and degree distributions;
- include Zipf package popularity, whale tenants and 10,000+ degree hubs;
- test realistic exact/fielded/semantic query mixtures and burst patterns.

### Retrieval and routes

- compare PostgreSQL+pgvector, OpenSearch-only, OpenSearch+Qdrant and Vespa on one frozen relevance set;
- test tenant/language/kind/version/compatibility filters and filtered-ANN recall;
- solve 2/4/6-hop routes with 1/2/4/8 alternatives;
- inject hubs, cycles, missing reverse edges and conditional incompatibilities;
- verify deterministic route receipts across projection rebuilds.

### Indexing and consistency

- reindex under live query load and perform blue/green alias swaps;
- delay each projector and test all consistency modes;
- duplicate, reorder and omit outbox events;
- corrupt a projection, rebuild it and compare digests;
- migrate embedding models using shadow and dual indexes.

### Failures

- fail the PostgreSQL primary, search node, vector shard, worker fleet, object store and entire region;
- terminate workflows and sandboxes at every boundary;
- introduce a 10× backlog and verify budget-aware admission;
- restore from PITR and measure full service RPO/RTO;
- verify read-only/degraded modes and exact user-visible status.

### Isolation and metering

- fuzz every query, cache, adjacency, export and billing path for cross-tenant leakage;
- retry/reorder/duplicate usage events and reconcile receipts to invoices;
- test quota cutoffs under concurrent requests;
- prove revoked access and stale cache behavior.

### Sandbox

- archive/path/symlink bombs;
- fork, memory, disk, file-count and output bombs;
- dependency confusion and malicious build hooks;
- metadata/network/credential exfiltration attempts;
- terminal/log injection;
- destruction and receipt integrity after all failures.

# Part IX — Product, business model and adoption system

## 68. Product wedge

Taedri’s first commercial wedge should be narrower than “a universal graph of all code,” while preserving that architecture underneath:

> Turn an existing package or repository into a verified, agent-ready capability map that lets coding systems retrieve and use the right code with fewer tokens, fewer model escalations and fewer incorrect implementations.

The first product ingests a Python package or repository, generates stable entity identities, searchable descriptions, compatibility edges, provenance, executable examples and verification evidence, then exposes them through a CLI, SDK, API, MCP server and coding-agent integrations.

The immediate customer outcome is not “we built a graph.” It is:

- agents stop rereading entire libraries;
- package capabilities become discoverable by intent, type, constraint and compatibility;
- eligible existing functions are reused instead of rewritten;
- context contains compact route cards rather than source-tree dumps;
- expensive models are invoked only when cheaper retrieval, routing or models are insufficient;
- every selected capability remains traceable to exact source, version, evidence and verification.

A strong demonstration uses a difficult, heavily used package with several releases—such as SQLAlchemy, pandas, Pydantic or pytest—and realistic integration tasks. The comparison is against repository-wide RAG, ordinary code search and direct frontier-model baselines, with all indexing, routing, verification and failure costs included.

TaedriCodeGraph is the substrate. Teleon compiles capability routes. RouterMesh chooses models, providers, endpoints, harnesses and verification. Baltor manages verified context. AIDevObserver can become the customer-facing reuse and measurement surface. They share identities and receipts but remain separately understandable products.

## 69. Initial users and jobs to be done

### AI developer-tool teams

These teams build coding assistants, repository agents, internal copilots or autonomous software-engineering systems. They need to add dependable code intelligence without creating every indexer, reduce inference spend, improve API/tool selection, ground changes in exact versions, explain decisions and evaluate routing changes against accepted outcomes. They are likely the strongest first buyers because cost, latency and task success already have economic owners.

### Platform and developer-productivity teams

These teams operate large internal codebases, approved dependency catalogs, paved roads and reusable components. They want to make libraries discoverable across organizational boundaries, prevent duplicate implementations, guide agents toward supported APIs, expose approved capabilities safely and detect compatibility or migration risk. Their graph combines a public package catalog with private tenant overlays.

### Package maintainers and commercial SDK vendors

They want a complex library to be easier for humans and agents to use, entity-level release comparisons, machine-readable migration data, executable examples, documentation-drift detection and insight into unsuccessfully searched capabilities. Taedri can become an agent-readiness layer published beside normal documentation.

### Regulated and high-assurance engineering organizations

They need traceability to exact evidence, approved-version enforcement, retention of retrieval/execution receipts, residency/provider controls and proof that selected routes met constraints. They are later customers because tenancy, audit and deployment requirements are higher, but potential contract value is also higher.

## 70. Product packaging and pricing hypotheses

Pricing remains a design-partner hypothesis until actual usage distributions are measured.

### Community edition

An open local workflow indexes a small repository or package, inspects cards, runs deterministic retrieval and exports the interoperable graph schema. It seeds integrations and makes the standard credible. A continuously maintained package catalog, historical release intelligence, distributed indexing, fleet routing, organization controls and hosted benchmarks remain managed-product advantages.

### Developer cloud

A free or low-cost hosted tier can limit repositories, snapshots, graph queries and refreshes. A plausible paid hypothesis is **$99–$<!-- -->499/month**, varying with repository count, refresh frequency, storage and compute, and including API, CLI, MCP, route receipts and basic analytics.

### Team and platform

A team hypothesis is **$1,000–$<!-- -->5,000/month** for private overlays, shared policies, role controls, evaluation dashboards, frequent indexing and higher query volume. A platform hypothesis is **$5,000–$<!-- -->20,000/month plus usage** for larger catalogs, custom workers, continuous monitoring, capacity and service commitments.

### Enterprise

An initial annual-contract hypothesis is **$60,000–$<!-- -->300,000+**, driven by deployment model, source volume, retention, support, languages, residency and throughput. These are research ranges, not validated willingness-to-pay evidence.

### Metering principles

Internally meter source bytes/entities, extraction/embedding compute, retained graph/artifacts, query families, model tokens, sandbox compute and refresh frequency. Externally bundle these into understandable allowances such as indexed repositories, maintained package versions, capability queries and verification compute. Outcome pricing may become viable later, but accepted-outcome definitions are initially customer-specific and gameable.

## 71. Cost and return model

The economic claim is measured against the customer’s actual workflow:

``` text
C_baseline =
    model inference
  + retrieval infrastructure
  + failed attempts and retries
  + developer review/rework
  + latency or queue cost

C_taedri =
    amortized ingestion and maintenance
  + deterministic/lexical/graph retrieval
  + selected model inference
  + execution and verification
  + residual failure/rework
  + Taedri subscription

Net value = C_baseline - C_taedri
ROI = Net value / Taedri total cost
CPAO = total workflow cost / independently accepted outcomes
```

CPAO is the primary optimization metric. Token reduction matters only when independently accepted outcomes stay equal or improve. Report retrieval, selection, escalation, execution, verification and failure costs separately, and report median/p75/p95 by task family rather than a concealing global percentage.

A credible proof answers:

- how many input, cached and completion tokens were avoided;
- how often a strong model was no longer required;
- whether route cards improved first-attempt success;
- whether verification cost less than the failures it prevented;
- how indexing cost amortized across reuse;
- whether developers spent less time locating, understanding or reimplementing code.

## 72. Defensibility and data flywheel

The moat is not embeddings, a graph database or one parser. Those are replaceable. The compounding asset is the versioned relationship among code, intent, compatibility, routes, evidence, execution and independently verified outcomes.

Each completed task can improve:

- descriptors and blockers that retrieve an entity;
- edges that predict actual compatibility;
- the minimum route-card detail needed for a task;
- model/harness/verifier choices by task cell;
- executable versus merely plausible examples;
- failed package combinations and negative certificates;
- which graph regions deserve further enrichment.

``` text
more indexed evidence
  -> better candidates and routes
  -> more executions and receipts
  -> better compatibility/routing estimates
  -> lower cost per accepted outcome
  -> adoption and more evidence
```

Usage-derived claims remain candidates until promoted. Tenant code and behavior never leak into the public catalog. Cross-tenant learning uses explicit opt-in, publishable facts or privacy-preserving aggregates. Open schemas can strengthen adoption while the managed historical catalog, verification corpus, compatibility evidence and operating quality remain difficult to reproduce.

## 73. Adoption path

1.  **Observe only.** Index one package/repository and compare retrieval with the incumbent system.
2.  **Shadow route.** Produce route cards and model decisions without affecting production.
3.  **Assist.** Let developers or agents inspect and choose Taedri candidates.
4.  **Bounded execution.** Enable low-risk task cells with mandatory verification.
5.  **Policy-controlled autonomy.** Expand only where risk, cost and acceptance thresholds hold.
6.  **Organization capability layer.** Add private services, templates, receipts and solution packs.

Every phase has rollback, an unchanged counterfactual baseline and an exact receipt. Begin with interfaces customers already use: CLI, Python/TypeScript SDK, HTTP, MCP, repository checks and popular agent harnesses.

## 74. Design-partner program

Recruit six to ten partners across coding-agent companies, platform-engineering teams and complex package/SDK maintainers. Use a six-to-eight-week engagement:

- Week 1: freeze task corpus, packages, releases, baselines and acceptance oracles.
- Weeks 2–3: index and validate identity; measure retrieval recall.
- Weeks 3–4: shadow route cards and 1/2/4/8 selector/detail experiments.
- Weeks 5–6: bounded execution with independent verification.
- Weeks 7–8: quantify economics, burden, failure modes and willingness to pay.

The program succeeds only when several partners demonstrate lower CPAO on a material task family, no meaningful accepted-outcome regression, reproducible receipts, repeated post-study use and a named budget owner. Exchange discounts for structured feedback, reusable benchmark access and permission to publish anonymized evidence; avoid custom consulting that produces no reusable worker, schema, evaluation or integration.

## 75. Proof metrics, gates and failure modes

### Core metrics

- independently accepted outcome rate and CPAO;
- time to first accepted outcome;
- input/output/cached/avoided tokens and strong-model escalation rate;
- retrieval recall at fixed candidate budgets;
- route-card precision and failure diversity;
- identity stability and exact source/version traceability;
- compatibility false-positive and false-negative rates;
- verifier disagreement and execution failure;
- reuse frequency, freshness and incremental-update latency;
- ingestion cost per useful entity;
- customer activation, retained weekly use, expansion and willingness to pay.

### Commercial stop/continue gates

| Failure                                        | Required response                                                                             |
|------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| impressive graph, no workflow improvement      | gate enrichment on accepted outcomes and observed reuse                                       |
| indexing costs exceed avoided inference/rework | incremental extraction, demand-prioritized packages and hot-region enrichment                 |
| inferred compatibility appears authoritative   | preserve evidence state, contradiction, scope and verification                                |
| cold-start packages lack evidence              | serve deterministic facts, expose uncertainty and schedule by expected information value      |
| verification erases routing gains              | tier verifiers by risk and measure marginal caught-error value                                |
| stale/version-confused results                 | bind every result to artifact, build context, anchors and validity intervals                  |
| privacy blocks adoption                        | local indexing, tenant overlays, retention controls and dedicated deployment                  |
| product names confuse buyers                   | sell one outcome-oriented wedge; reveal internal architecture only as useful                  |
| open source commoditizes components            | compete on maintained catalog, evidence, reliability, routing and integrations                |
| outcome metric is gamed                        | independent oracles, stratification, human sampling and immutable receipts                    |
| scope outruns wedge                            | no new language/back end/marketplace before CPAO, retention and willingness-to-pay gates pass |

The business earns expansion only where verified reuse produces more accepted software outcomes per dollar, minute and unit of human attention.

# Part X — Executable 90-day implementation program

## 76. Program outcome and delivery principles

The first 90 days prove one complete measurable loop:

> acquire an existing package release → assign stable identities → extract entities, ports, descriptions, assertions and edges → retrieve compatible candidates → compose route alternatives → resolve selected bodies → execute safely → verify independently → emit an exact receipt.

The objective is not to ingest all of PyPI immediately. It is to show that Taedri can represent difficult packages accurately, retrieve and compose their capabilities more cheaply than whole-repository prompting, and scale without corrupting identity or provenance.

Delivery rules:

1.  freeze evidence and identity contracts before optimizing retrieval;
2.  keep claims append-only and promote candidates through explicit policy/verification;
3.  version every extractor, schema, normalizer, descriptor, embedding and model output;
4.  preserve raw artifacts and native extractor results for deterministic rebuilding;
5.  begin with PostgreSQL, CAS and a conventional search index, not a mandatory graph database;
6.  establish deterministic and lexical baselines before embeddings or LLM routing;
7.  resolve bodies only after selection;
8.  evaluate accepted outcomes per total token, dollar and elapsed time;
9.  use public benchmarks as supplements—sealed package-specific fixtures are the release gate;
10. never silently merge artifacts, entity revisions or lineage hypotheses.

## 77. Workstreams

| ID  | Workstream   | P0 deliverable                                                     |
|-----|--------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
| W0  | contracts    | versioned schemas, migrations and conformance suite                |
| W1  | acquisition  | reproducible PyPI/source/wheel/CAS manifest                        |
| W2  | extraction   | Python entity revisions and exact anchors                          |
| W3  | enrichment   | versioned descriptions, keywords, fingerprints, embeddings and LSH |
| W4  | graph        | typed assertions, ports, hyperedges, lineage and compatibility     |
| W5  | retrieval    | exact/history/identifier/BM25/graph candidates with explanations   |
| W6  | planning     | DemandIR, compatibility solver and 1/2/4/8 route cards             |
| W7  | resolution   | minimal post-selection body/dependency manifests                   |
| W8  | execution    | sandboxed package tasks and deterministic tool adapters            |
| W9  | verification | independent oracles, counterexamples and exact receipts            |
| W10 | RouterMesh   | deterministic, ranker, local-SLM and hosted selector arms          |
| W11 | platform     | API, workers, observability and tenant-ready boundaries            |
| W12 | evaluation   | gold sets, regressions, load tests and economics dashboard         |

Every workstream exposes a deterministic command, machine-readable output, fixtures, metrics and an owner.

## 79. P0, P1 and P2 boundaries

### P0 — close the loop

- Python source distributions and wheels;
- exact entity revisions and probabilistic logical lineage;
- modules, functions, methods, classes, variables, parameters, attributes, imports, decorators, exceptions and call/reference edges;
- exact/history, identifier, fielded BM25 and typed graph retrieval;
- deterministic compatibility solving;
- route cards at 1/2/4/8 alternatives and multiple detail levels;
- post-selection source resolution;
- sandbox execution, independent verification and receipts;
- deterministic, local ranker, local SLM and one strong-model fallback.

### P1 — generalize and improve

- embedding ensembles, LSH families and learned fusion;
- runtime traces and native-extension/binary evidence;
- release-diff intelligence, tenant overlays and caches;
- contextual-bandit routing in shadow;
- JavaScript/TypeScript as the second language;
- MCP projection and WIT-inspired ports;
- five-million-entity operational load test.

### P2 — platform scale

- 20M–50M catalog and stress tests toward 100M;
- additional language indexers;
- distributed adjacency, marketplace ingestion and billing;
- public catalog plus private overlays;
- learned acquisition scheduling and multi-region recovery.

## 80. Time-boxed delivery plan

### Days 0–14 — contracts, fixtures and deterministic substrate

- Ratify identity, assertion, anchor, edge, descriptor, compatibility, route and receipt schemas.
- Implement canonical serialization, content digests, migrations and producer versions.
- Scaffold PostgreSQL, CAS, API, CLI and background worker.
- Acquire three releases each of `requests`, `pydantic` and `pytest`.
- Create micro-fixtures for aliases, re-exports, decorators, nested scopes, generated members, monkey patching, namespace packages and colliding names.
- Extract modules, classes, functions, methods, variables, parameters, signatures, docstrings, imports, definitions, references and anchors.
- Implement exact/qualified-name lookup, release filtering and raw-evidence inspection.
- Establish golden snapshots and reproducibility tests.

**Day-14 gate:** identical reruns produce stable revision IDs for at least 99.9% of records; all residual nondeterminism is classified; no silent cross-artifact merge exists; every served assertion traces to immutable evidence and producer.

### Days 15–30 — retrieval and route construction

- Add `pluggy`, SQLAlchemy, pandas, NumPy and `orjson`, with three releases each.
- Add fielded BM25 over names, aliases, docs, signatures, types, examples, exceptions and metadata.
- Add history retrieval and typed bidirectional expansion.
- Implement deterministic RequestEnvelope→DemandIR parsing with local fallback.
- Implement compatibility signatures, hard constraints, negative evidence and route solving.
- Produce 1/2/4/8 cards at multiple detail levels.
- Add minimal post-selection resolution.
- Define accepted-outcome, cost, latency and token ledgers.

**Day-30 gate:** Recall@20 ≥ 0.90 on the curated capability set; exact fixtures are 100%; fewer than 1% of returned P0 routes contain a known typed incompatibility; every route exposes origins, score components, satisfied constraints and rejection reasons.

### Days 31–60 — enrichment, execution, verification and routing

- Add MinHash/SimHash, configurable embeddings, per-facet vectors and fused ranking.
- Retain every descriptor as a portfolio entry.
- Add network-deny sandboxes with bounded CPU, memory, files, output and time.
- Build exact-value, schema, invariant, metamorphic, differential, exception and upstream-test oracles.
- Implement deterministic, statistical ranker, local SLM, cheap hosted and strong selector arms.
- Instrument the full request-to-outcome trace.
- Run alternative-count, detail, duplicate, primitive-count and model-tier experiments.
- Add release-lineage candidates and contradiction records without auto-promotion.

**Day-60 gate:** every execution has a complete receipt; negative fixtures have zero false acceptance; sealed deterministic fixtures replay successfully ≥99%; a Taedri policy improves independently accepted outcomes per token by a preregistered target (initial research target: 25%) over the full-card strong-model baseline after verification cost.

### Days 61–90 — incremental operation and scale proof

- Implement incremental releases, exact invalidation, reindexing, lineage review and rollback.
- Add public/private overlay boundaries and row-level authorization tests.
- Cache exact requests, candidate sets, solution packs, descriptor bundles and verified routes independently.
- Load at least 5M entity revisions and 25M edges; stress against a 20M-entity synthetic profile.
- Publish OpenAPI, Python SDK, CLI, dashboards, restore runbooks and schema-extension guidance.
- Fault-test worker death, duplicate delivery, stale embeddings, index lag, object-store outage, model outage and verifier disagreement.
- Produce measured go/no-go decisions for specialized graph storage, Vespa/OpenSearch consolidation and Rust hot paths.

**Day-90 gate:** filtered warm candidate search p95 \<300 ms and route construction p95 \<1 second at the 5M profile; ingestion is idempotent/resumable; restore and isolation suites pass; no P0 service depends on an unversioned model output.

These thresholds are initial engineering hypotheses and should be amended by an ADR when workload evidence shows they are too lax or unrealistically strict.

## 81. MVP schema and API

Required records:

- `PackageCoordinate`, `PackageRelease`, `DistributionArtifact`, `SourceSnapshot`;
- `BuildContext`, `FileRevision`, `SourceAnchor`;
- `CodeEntityRevision`, `LogicalCodeEntity`, `SymbolProjection`;
- `AssertionEnvelope`, `EvidenceRef`, `Contradiction`;
- `EdgeAssertion`, `Hyperedge`, `Port`, `CompatibilitySignature`;
- `DescriptionPortfolioEntry`, `Fingerprint`, `EmbeddingRef`;
- `PrimitiveCard`, `RequestEnvelope`, `DemandIR`;
- `CandidateSet`, `RouteCard`, `ResolutionManifest`;
- `ExecutionReceipt`, `VerificationReceipt`, `OutcomeReceipt`.

Every derived record includes producer, producer version, schema version, evidence, confidence, validity interval, `candidate` and `serves_truth`.

``` text
POST /v1/packages:ingest
GET  /v1/entities/{revision_id}
POST /v1/entities:search
POST /v1/graph:expand
POST /v1/compatibility:check
POST /v1/demands:compile
POST /v1/routes:solve
POST /v1/routes/{id}:resolve
POST /v1/executions
POST /v1/verifications
GET  /v1/receipts/{id}
GET  /v1/evidence/{id}
```

Every response carries schema version, trace ID, evidence handles and deterministic pagination tokens.

## 82. Fixtures and benchmark matrix

| Fixture class | Purpose                                                                                                        |
|---------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| micro         | exact expected language entities, anchors and edges                                                            |
| real package  | three releases of each P0 package, including sdist, wheels, tests, examples and metadata                       |
| adversarial   | collisions, re-exports, vendoring, generated code, dynamic attributes, malicious archives and corrupt metadata |
| scale         | realistic degree skew, hubs, long routes, overlays and version histories                                       |

Benchmark extraction against gold anchors and selected SCIP/Kythe-style expectations. Benchmark retrieval with internal capability questions plus appropriately licensed public retrieval sets. Benchmark tool/planning behavior with package-specific tasks, BFCL/ToolSandbox-style function selection and repository tasks. Public scores never substitute for exact internal receipts.

Primary metrics are identity stability, anchor precision, entity/edge recall, Recall@k, MRR, valid-route rate, verifier acceptance, false acceptance, latency, memory, ingestion throughput, tokens and dollars per accepted outcome, and replay success.

## 83. Risk register

| Risk                     | Tripwire                                            | Response                                                          |
|--------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
| false identity merge     | unrelated artifacts share a served logical identity | quarantine lineage; require evidence-weighted promotion           |
| schema explosion         | one package requires incompatible core fields       | small core envelope plus namespaced extensions                    |
| dynamic Python gaps      | gold recall below target                            | add type/runtime evidence and expose unknowns                     |
| descriptor cost growth   | enrichment breaches budget                          | demand-gate, cache, batch and retain only promoted online indexes |
| premature graph database | core semantics depend on vendor behavior            | portable edge tables and adjacency exports                        |
| benchmark leakage        | public score rises without sealed-task gains        | release-gate on held-out package tasks                            |
| sandbox escape           | host/network policy violation                       | halt execution workstream and rotate environment                  |
| tenant leakage           | any cross-tenant result                             | block multi-tenant launch                                         |
| provenance volume        | evidence exceeds planned ratio                      | tier raw, normalized and compact receipt retention                |
| provider/model drift     | policy regresses after revision change              | pin/catalog exact revisions and run shadow evals                  |

## 84. Decision gates

- **Day 14:** approve or revise identity/evidence kernel; do not expand retrieval while unexplained false merges remain.
- **Day 30:** deterministic-plus-lexical retrieval must clear recall; every embedding arm must beat or complement that baseline.
- **Day 60:** continue model routing only when accepted-outcome economics improve after verifier cost.
- **Day 90:** choose PostgreSQL-plus-search, Vespa consolidation or specialized adjacency using measured workload data. Approve the second language only after Python P0 gates pass.

# Part XI — Frontier research hypotheses

## 86. Research rule

These hypotheses extend Taedri from code search into an evidence-directed compiler for reusable software capability. None is a required production dependency. Each enters the system as a versioned arm and survives only if it beats a simpler baseline on a frozen task population after all storage, control, execution and verification costs.

## 87. Compatibility-basis retrieval

**Thesis.** One entity embedding entangles behavior, shape, effect, operational constraints, examples, provenance and failure semantics. Retrieve both demand and capability over an approximately independent compatibility basis.

**Mechanism.** Maintain sparse lexical features plus separate dense or learned-sparse representations per facet. Decompose DemandIR into the same basis, retrieve independently, apply hard typed constraints and combine finalists using late interaction in the spirit of [ColBERT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.12832). Preserve an explicit residual: demand dimensions that no candidate explains.

**Experiment.** Compare one-vector, concatenated-vector, independent-facet and basis-plus-late-interaction retrieval on the same package-composition tasks.

**Initial falsification gate.** Reject if it fails to improve Recall@50 by 10% at comparable latency, or if additional index cost exceeds the downstream token/failure savings.

## 88. Algebraic evidence and route solving

**Thesis.** Reachability, cost, confidence, risk and provenance are multiple algebras over one graph rather than entirely separate engines.

**Mechanism.** Use configurable semirings: Boolean for reachability, min-plus for cost, max-min for weakest-link confidence, set operations for provenance and Pareto/lexicographic products for constraints. [GraphBLAS](https://graphblas.org/) supplies a useful generalized sparse-graph precedent. Retain SMT/CSP fallback for nonlocal constraints.

**Experiment.** Express four route objectives over one adjacency representation and compare bespoke solvers for correctness, performance and code complexity.

**Initial falsification gate.** Reject if generalized solving is more than 2× slower without a material reduction in implementation/verification burden, or cannot express decisive nonlocal constraints.

## 89. Local-to-global compatibility residuals

**Thesis.** Many failures occur because individually plausible edges cannot be made globally consistent.

**Mechanism.** Associate primitives with local assignments—types, units, schemas, effects, environments and versions—and edges with mappings over overlaps. Approximate consistency with a factor graph/message passing; escalate unresolved cases to SMT. The residual inconsistency becomes an explicit route-risk feature. This is sheaf-like reasoning without requiring the product vocabulary to expose category theory.

**Experiment.** Seed unit, nullability, async/sync, schema, effect and version conflicts into multi-library routes.

**Falsification.** Reject if residuals do not predict execution failure better than independent edge scores, or solving costs more than the failed executions it avoids.

## 90. Query-adaptive descriptor portfolios

**Thesis.** The best description is query-dependent. The right context is the smallest diverse evidence-backed subset that resolves the current decision.

**Mechanism.** Treat descriptor disclosure as rate-distortion-constrained subset selection. Estimate information gain from held-out outcomes, subtract token/latency cost and penalize redundancy with maximal marginal relevance or a [determinantal point process](https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.6083). Keep each descriptor addressable and cacheable.

**Experiment.** Compare full cards, one fixed summary, learned knapsack and diversity-aware portfolios at 1K/2K/4K token budgets.

**Initial falsification gate.** Reject if adaptive disclosure does not improve accepted outcomes per token by 15% over the best fixed summary.

## 91. Active graph exploration by expected value of information

**Thesis.** A fixed waterfall wastes work because the best next action depends on which uncertainty blocks the current decision.

**Mechanism.** Maintain beliefs over candidate suitability and missing constraints. Choose the next exact lookup, extractor, test, graph query, embedding search, package inspection or model call by expected reduction in decision loss per dollar and millisecond. Stop when the best remaining action has nonpositive expected value.

**Experiment.** Replay tasks with hidden accepted routes and compare the controller to fixed cascades.

**Falsification.** Reject if control overhead exceeds 5% or cost falls less than 10% at equal acceptance.

## 92. Scoped negative capability certificates

**Thesis.** Absence is not negative evidence. Taedri needs bounded knowledge of what a capability cannot do.

**Mechanism.** Store `INCOMPATIBLE_WITH`, `DOES_NOT_ACCEPT`, `CANNOT_GUARANTEE` and failed-route assertions with evidence, version, environment and validity. Issue closed-world completeness certificates only for enumerable scopes such as one release’s exports. Use compact filters, including binary fuse filters where appropriate, as cheap rejection indexes.

**Experiment.** Compare candidate volume and harmful suppression over incompatibility-heavy workloads and release drift.

**Falsification.** Reject any negative cache whose incorrect or stale scope suppresses more than 0.1% of valid routes.

## 93. Multi-sketch blocking

**Thesis.** No one LSH family captures functional relatedness; a demand-conditioned sketch ensemble can reduce a 100M corpus without surrendering oracle recall.

**Mechanism.** Combine exact interface keys, token/AST MinHash, description SimHash, type-signature hashes, graphlet/Weisfeiler–Lehman sketches, input/output example fingerprints and dependency-neighborhood hashes. DemandIR selects unions/intersections; the final compatibility solver remains authoritative.

**Experiment.** Test sketches separately and jointly over duplicates, forks, wrappers, behavioral substitutes and misleading lexical neighbors.

**Initial falsification gate.** Reject if the ensemble cannot retain 99% oracle recall while reducing candidates by at least three orders of magnitude on the target distribution.

## 94. Hierarchical routing with delayed verified reward

**Thesis.** RouterMesh should learn from independently accepted outcomes, not preferences or self-confidence alone.

**Mechanism.** Use a constrained contextual bandit separately at each plane. Context includes task facets, candidate entropy, tools, route depth, policy, health and remaining budget. Reward arrives after verification and charges all retries/tools/verifiers. Run conservative off-policy evaluation and shadowing before bounded low-risk exploration; [MixLLM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.18482) is one relevant model-routing precedent.

**Experiment.** Shadow-route historical traffic, compare with static task-cell policies, then permit small reversible exploration.

**Falsification.** Reject when offline confidence bounds fail to predict shadow truth or regret stays above the static router after sufficient support.

## 95. Counterexample-guided route repair

**Thesis.** A verification failure should repair only the invalid plan region and permanently improve future constraints.

**Mechanism.** Adapt counterexample-guided inductive synthesis: propose route, obtain a minimal independent counterexample, turn it into a scoped constraint/negative edge, and re-solve the smallest affected subgraph. Every counterexample becomes a regression fixture.

**Experiment.** Inject type, schema, effect, environment and semantic failures into three-to-eight-node routes.

**Falsification.** Reject if repair loops routinely cost more than full replanning or fail to prevent the same scoped recurrence.

## 96. Temporal package graphs and semantic impact cones

**Thesis.** A package is a temporal graph. Enrichment should be delta-computed and changes propagated only over relation families capable of carrying their impact.

**Mechanism.** Match exact revisions first, then propose structural/behavioral lineage. Classify signature, contract, implementation, ABI, dependency and observed-behavior changes. Propagate impact along relevant dependency edges rather than every downstream reference. Work such as [Sembid](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.00393) supports the broader point that signature-only compatibility misses behavioral breaking changes.

**Experiment.** Index three releases of six packages and predict downstream test failures.

**Falsification.** Reject probabilistic lineage if false merges exceed 0.5%; reject impact cones if they do not beat changed-file and signature-diff baselines.

## 97. Execution-conditioned multi-view representation

**Thesis.** Static representations should dominate cheap retrieval; runtime evidence should be acquired only for finalists whose ambiguity justifies it.

**Mechanism.** Begin with names, text, signatures, syntax, CFG/data-flow and dependencies. For uncertain finalists add traces, coverage, dynamic slices, resources, exceptions and I/O behavior. Align views while retaining independent evidence. Multi-view code research such as [CODE-MVP](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.02029) is useful precedent, not proof of this production policy.

**Experiment.** Compare static-only, always-dynamic and uncertainty-triggered dynamic enrichment.

**Initial falsification gate.** Reject if triggered execution cannot recover 90% of always-dynamic accuracy at no more than 25% of its cost.

## 98. Proof-carrying semantic caches

**Thesis.** Semantic similarity is not safe reuse. A hit requires an explicit equivalence envelope.

**Mechanism.** Cache exact results, candidate sets, graph slices, routes, adapters, verifier results and solution packs separately. A semantic hit is usable only when its certificate covers normalized intent, artifacts, schemas, environment, effects, policy, oracle class and validity. Learn thresholds by task cell, never globally.

**Experiment.** Compare exact-only, distance-threshold and certificate-gated caches under package, environment and policy drift.

**Falsification.** Reject if certificates destroy more than 80% of correct hits or allow more than 0.1% unsound reuse; effectful replay should target zero false acceptance in the safety suite.

## 99. Demand-driven corpus enrichment

**Thesis.** The next extraction job should maximize expected future avoided cost, not give every entity equal enrichment.

**Mechanism.** Score package/entity/extractor jobs by demand, uncertainty, route centrality, staleness, cost and expected reuse. Reserve exploration capacity so the popular head cannot permanently starve the long tail.

**Experiment.** Replay a six-month demand trace under equal-priority, popularity-only, uncertainty-only and value-aware scheduling.

**Initial falsification gate.** Reject if value-aware scheduling fails to improve verified reuse coverage per extraction dollar by 20%.

## 100. Verified primitive Darwinism

**Thesis.** Promote, specialize, merge or retire reusable capabilities by verified utility, not author reputation or raw downloads.

**Mechanism.** Track accepted-route frequency, marginal contribution, environments survived, verifier strength, failure clusters, substitutability and maintenance burden. Promote stable compositions into solution packs; split environment-dependent behavior; demote drifted or dominated choices. Preserve lineage and alternatives.

**Experiment.** Replay historical task streams under alternative promotion policies and evaluate on future tasks/releases.

**Falsification.** Reject policies that merely concentrate the catalog, fail to improve CPAO or create brittle packs under drift.

## 101. Prioritized frontier experiment portfolio

| Priority | Experiment                         | Initial scope                        | Initial success gate                         |
|---------:|------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|
|        1 | multi-sketch blocking              | 1M entities; five similarity classes | ≥99% oracle recall and ≥1,000× reduction     |
|        2 | compatibility-basis retrieval      | six packages; 500 demands            | ≥10% Recall@50 gain at comparable latency    |
|        3 | descriptor rate-distortion         | 1K/2K/4K budgets                     | ≥15% accepted-outcomes/token gain            |
|        4 | scoped negative certificates       | versioned incompatibility corpus     | \<0.1% harmful suppression                   |
|        5 | proof-carrying route cache         | drifted package/environment matrix   | \<0.1% unsound hits with useful hit rate     |
|        6 | temporal lineage/impact cones      | three releases × six packages        | \<0.5% false merges; beats diff baseline     |
|        7 | execution-triggered enrichment     | 300 ambiguous pairs                  | ≥90% dynamic accuracy at ≤25% cost           |
|        8 | global compatibility residual      | 500 seeded conflicts                 | meaningful failure lift over edge-only score |
|        9 | semiring solver kernel             | four objectives                      | comparable speed and less solver duplication |
|       10 | active information-value waterfall | 1,000 replayable tasks               | ≥10% cost reduction at equal acceptance      |
|       11 | counterexample-guided repair       | 200 failing routes                   | fewer tokens/executions than full replan     |
|       12 | verified-reward bandit             | shadow, then low-risk traffic        | beats static CPAO within risk bound          |

The first six can be evaluated without trusting a frontier model. The final six become credible only after receipts, independent verification and temporal identity are reliable. All numeric gates are preregistration defaults, not facts; adjust them before the run, never after seeing results.

# Part XII — Consolidated operating mandate and immediate build sequence

## 102. Canonical build sequence

The recommended sequence resolves the recurring architecture question “what should be built first?”

1.  **Identity/evidence kernel.** Canonical bytes, immutable artifact/build/entity IDs, sidecar lineage and assertion envelopes.
2.  **Package acquisition.** Quarantined sdist/wheel fetch, hashes, package metadata, manifests, CAS and exact receipts.
3.  **Python structural extractor.** Exhaustive source anchors and entity inventory without importing the package.
4.  **Semantic evidence adapters.** Native typing/compiler/SCIP/LSP and package-specific facts, each with coverage and diagnostics.
5.  **DescriptionPortfolio and cards.** Independent versioned text, keywords, sparse features, sketches and embeddings; compact body-free view.
6.  **Typed edge/port graph.** Evidence-bearing bidirectional relations, hyperedges, negative facts and compatibility signatures.
7.  **Deterministic retrieval.** Exact, history, identifier, fielded BM25 and typed expansion, with stage explanations.
8.  **Demand and solver.** RequestEnvelope, DemandIR, request-local graph, hard compatibility and route alternatives.
9.  **Selective materialization.** PlanLock, authorization and minimal role/digest resolution only after selection.
10. **Execution and verification.** Bounded sandbox, independent oracles, typed repair/escalation/abstention.
11. **Receipts and economics.** Join source, decision, attempts, effects, verification, token/latency/cost and downstream outcome.
12. **Router laboratory.** Deterministic/local/SLM/hosted arms and 1/2/4/8 detail experiments in replay/shadow.
13. **Incremental temporal graph.** Release deltas, lineage review, invalidation, negative certificates and replay eligibility.
14. **Scale/tenancy.** 5M proof, then measured 20M–50M expansion and 100M stress; public catalog plus isolated overlays.

Do not reorder expensive descriptor/model work ahead of the evidence kernel and deterministic baselines. Do not block the first slice on the final distributed graph, every language, or learned routing.

## 103. Definition of done for one package-derived primitive

A primitive or code entity is not complete because it has a generated summary. P0 definition of done requires:

- immutable package release, distribution artifact and source/build identity;
- collision-safe entity revision ID and exact native/source coordinates;
- original source name preserved;
- entity kind plus namespaced analyzer-native projections;
- signature, parameters, outputs/yields/errors/effects and relevant state/resources;
- declared, inferred, observed and verified contracts kept distinct;
- DescriptionPortfolio with producer, input digest, facet, scope and validity;
- exact, lexical, structural/LSH and optional semantic retrieval keys;
- typed incoming/outgoing relation assertions and reverse-search projection;
- compatibility signature, preconditions, environmental constraints and known negatives;
- documentation, examples, tests and evidence handles where available;
- artifact/body handle separated from the search card;
- candidate/truth/authorization state and rights/policy evidence;
- independent conformance or behavior oracle for every promoted behavioral claim;
- exact extraction, promotion and usage receipts;
- deterministic rebuild or explicit nondeterminism ledger.

## 104. Harness, tool, hook, agent and instruction-file integration

`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, skills, plugins, hooks, MCP servers, A2A agents and harness graphs help when treated as adapters into the same control loop rather than parallel sources of authority.

### What an integration declares

``` yaml
integration:
  id: ...
  kind: instruction_file | hook | skill | plugin | mcp_server | a2a_agent | harness
  revision_digest: ...
  capabilities: [...]
  input_output_error_schemas: ...
  authority_and_effects: ...
  state_and_idempotency: ...
  context_budget: ...
  supported_task_cells: ...
  evidence_and_verifiers: ...
  cost_latency_health: ...
  policy_constraints: ...
```

### Integration pattern

- Instruction files establish repository-local policy and preferred workflows, but do not silently override tenant or system authority.
- Skills compile into capability cards with eligibility, inputs, outputs, effects and verification contracts.
- Hooks emit typed observations/transitions; they do not mutate canonical truth without evidence/promotion.
- MCP exposes a few progressive-disclosure meta-tools rather than millions of entities as tools.
- A2A agent cards map into harness capability candidates; every nested model/tool call receives its own lower-plane receipt.
- Harness topology is versioned as an arm and evaluated end to end.
- Tools and agent descriptions are untrusted claims until schema, permission and behavior checks establish the needed evidence class.

This integration layer is valuable because it lets Taedri move between coding harnesses without rebuilding the code graph or collapsing product logic into vendor-specific prompt files.

## 105. Prohibited shortcuts

The implementation must not:

- rename source symbols to obtain global uniqueness;
- equate embedding proximity, hash collision or lexical match with identity/compatibility;
- call missing edges false without a completeness certificate;
- overwrite prior descriptions, embeddings or analyzer claims with a preferred model output;
- mark generated/tested/local code as production truth automatically;
- treat popularity, stars or downloads as correctness;
- feed every candidate, edge or body into every model call;
- let an LLM invent SQL/graph/vector queries before cheaper exact/template/compiled mechanisms are attempted;
- materialize package bodies during broad retrieval;
- use a model’s confidence or self-grade as the sole oracle;
- mix semantic model selection, provider failover and endpoint scheduling in one opaque fallback label;
- retry a possibly committed effect without reconciliation/idempotency;
- learn from logged choices without propensities, independent outcomes and drift controls;
- use tenant filters as the only authorization boundary;
- rely on one unreplicated local volume for canonical state;
- adopt a graph database, embedding family, router or workflow engine as an irreversible semantic dependency;
- claim token, energy or customer savings that were not measured on a frozen paired workload.

## 106. Immediate next sprint

The highest-value next sprint is deliberately narrow:

1.  Create `schemas/v1/` for identity, assertion/evidence, entity, anchor, edge, description, compatibility, DemandIR, route, resolution and receipts.
2.  Build canonical JSON serialization and multihash IDs with property tests.
3.  Add a manifest-only PyPI acquisition worker for three releases each of `requests`, `pydantic` and `pytest`.
4.  Build the no-execution Python extractor for modules, classes, functions, methods, variables, attributes, parameters, imports, decorators, definitions/references and exact spans.
5.  Create 30–50 adversarial micro-fixtures before indexing a large package.
6.  Implement exact/qualified identifier lookup plus raw-evidence inspection.
7.  Freeze an initial capability-question set and gold source anchors.
8.  Emit deterministic extraction receipts and run reproducibility/false-merge gates.
9.  Implement fielded BM25 and typed graph expansion only after the identity gate passes.
10. Carry one mixed-origin route through digest-checked materialization, execution, independent verification and rollback.

Deliverables are executable fixtures and receipts, not another architecture-only milestone.

## 107. Decisions still intentionally open

The following remain experimental mechanism choices:

- OpenSearch + vector store versus Vespa consolidation;
- PostgreSQL adjacency versus a specialized distributed adjacency plane;
- exact embedding models, dimensions, quantization and promoted online variants;
- Temporal versus another workflow implementation behind the task contract;
- Fly versus a cloud/Kubernetes mix at each scale tier;
- Tree-sitter/SCIP/compiler/LSP coverage per language;
- local ranker/SLM and hosted router portfolio;
- factor-graph, CSP/SMT and semiring solver mix;
- open-core versus source-available boundaries;
- exact pricing and customer-facing usage units.

Each is decided by conformance and workload evidence. The canonical identities, evidence semantics, progressive disclosure and acceptance receipts should survive a change in every item above.

## 109. Primary standards and implementation references

The research in this edition prioritizes primary specifications and official project documentation. Particularly important anchors include:

- code intelligence: [SCIP](https://github.com/scip-code/scip), [Kythe schema](https://kythe.io/docs/schema/), [LSP](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.18/specification/), [Tree-sitter](https://tree-sitter.github.io/tree-sitter/), [CodeQL](https://codeql.github.com/docs/), [Joern CPG](https://docs.joern.io/code-property-graph/) and [LLVM IR](https://llvm.org/docs/LangRef.html);
- package/build identity: [Package URL](https://github.com/package-url/purl-spec), [Python Core Metadata](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/core-metadata/), [Clang compilation database](https://clang.llvm.org/docs/JSONCompilationDatabase.html), [BSP](https://build-server-protocol.github.io/docs/specification) and [Bazel BEP](https://bazel.build/remote/bep);
- ports and provenance: [WIT](https://component-model.bytecodealliance.org/design/wit.html), [ECMA-426 source maps](https://tc39.es/ecma426/), [SPDX 3.0.1](https://spdx.github.io/spdx-spec/v3.0.1/), [CycloneDX](https://cyclonedx.org/specification/overview/), [SLSA 1.2](https://slsa.dev/spec/v1.2/provenance) and [GUAC](https://docs.guac.sh/);
- routing and orchestration: [RouteLLM](https://github.com/lm-sys/RouteLLM), [LiteLLM routing](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/routing), [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/latest), [A2A](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/), [Kubernetes Inference Extension](https://gateway-api-inference-extension.sigs.k8s.io/) and [OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/);
- serving/storage: [Vespa phased ranking](https://docs.vespa.ai/en/ranking/phased-ranking.html), [Qdrant multitenancy](https://qdrant.tech/documentation/manage-data/multitenancy/), [PostgreSQL row security](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-rowsecurity.html) and [Fly Machines](https://fly.io/docs/machines/).

The governing end state is not an LLM that writes more code. It is a system in which the agent recognizes what is already solved, expresses the unresolved work compactly, materializes only what it needs, and proves that the assembled result satisfies the real request.
