# Part XVII — Work-node RouterMesh, context compiler and harness integration

## 178. Route each work node, not the whole session

A user request is not one homogeneous model call. It is a graph of jobs with different difficulty, risk, information and tool needs:

``` text
request
  -> normalize and classify
  -> retrieve and inspect
  -> plan
  -> transform or execute
  -> test and verify
  -> repair or escalate
  -> compose and cite
```

RouterMesh should assign a mechanism independently to each node. Exact parsing can handle a traceback; a local encoder can select candidate packages; a constrained SLM can fill DemandIR; a code model can propose a narrow patch; a deterministic AST transformer can apply it; and a separate verifier can determine acceptance. The frontier model appears only for residual ambiguity or hard reasoning.

This is recursive. A planning node may decompose into repository exploration, constraint discovery and route solving; each child is routed again. Every node has an explicit input contract, output contract, authority level, cost ceiling, deadline, assurance requirement and escalation policy.

## 179. Keep three budgets independent

One scalar “LLM budget” hides the largest optimization opportunities. Maintain three ledgers:

| Budget    | Controls                                                                        | Typical waste                                                 |
|-----------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| Reasoning | model tier, reasoning effort, samples, branches and retries                     | using a frontier model for deterministic or narrow work       |
| Context   | instructions, history, cards, graph neighborhoods, code bodies and tool schemas | repeatedly transmitting stable or irrelevant material         |
| Assurance | tests, static analyzers, differential runs, judges, proofs and human review     | verifying every node equally or trusting correlated verifiers |

Optimize accepted outcomes per total cost:

``` text
total_cost =
  retrieval_and_index_cost
  + selector_cost
  + reasoning_cost
  + context_and_cache_cost
  + tool_and_execution_cost
  + verification_and_repair_cost
  + expected_failure_consequence
```

A smaller model with a bloated context can cost more than a stronger model with a precise projection. Likewise, a cheap unverified answer that causes a full rerun is not cheap.

## 180. Work-node and route contracts

``` yaml
work_node:
  work_node_id: taedri://work-node/<digest>
  parent_and_dependency_ids: []
  task_cell: retrieve | inspect | plan | edit | apply | execute | test | review | compose
  demand_slice_id: ...
  input_schema_id: ...
  output_schema_id: ...
  effect_class: pure | read | reversible_write | irreversible_write
  risk_and_consequence:
    correctness_floor: ...
    confidentiality_class: ...
    monetary_or_operational_exposure: ...
  budgets:
    context_tokens: ...
    reasoning_cost: ...
    assurance_cost: ...
    deadline_distribution: ...
  eligible_mechanism_classes: []
  required_capabilities: []
  required_verification_claims: []
  stop_and_escalation_policy_id: ...

role_route:
  route_id: taedri://role-route/<digest>
  work_node_id: ...
  selector_arm_and_version: ...
  chosen_mechanism:
    kind: deterministic | encoder | reranker | slm | llm | tool | agent | human
    implementation_and_version: ...
  semantic_model_contract: ...
  provider_and_endpoint_contract: ...
  context_plan_id: ...
  tool_projection_id: ...
  cache_plan_id: ...
  verifier_plan_id: ...
  alternatives_considered: []
  predicted_quality_cost_latency: ...
  observed_outcome_and_receipts: ...
```

The same nominal model hosted by two providers or runtimes remains two arms until tokenizer, structured-output, tool-call, sampling and behavioral equivalence tests pass.

## 181. Local-to-frontier mechanism ladder

| Tier | Mechanism                                  | Best initial uses                                                                           |
|------|--------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| L0   | exact deterministic operator               | normalization, cache keys, symbol lookup, schema checks, query templates, patch application |
| L1   | local lexical, sketch, encoder or reranker | blocking, intent prototypes, relevance, duplicate and failure clustering                    |
| L2   | small grammar-constrained SLM              | DemandIR slots, conditionals, tool arguments, format repair, log classification             |
| L3   | local specialized code SLM                 | narrow explanation, edit proposal, test repair and code transformation                      |
| L4   | strong local general/code model            | bounded planning, repository reasoning, private work and review                             |
| L5   | cheap hosted general/code model            | unresolved low- or medium-risk semantic nodes where egress is permitted                     |
| L6   | strong/frontier model                      | ambiguous architecture, difficult multi-file debugging and novel reasoning                  |
| L7   | diverse panel or human                     | consequential disagreement, irreversible effects or unresolved assurance gaps               |

Eligibility comes before scoring. Residency, tenant policy, capability, license, latency, effect authority and context-window requirements remove arms from consideration. The selector then minimizes expected cost subject to quality and assurance floors; it must be allowed to abstain.

## 182. Selector mechanism portfolio

No learned router should ship without defeating simple arms under the same quality constraint:

1.  exact task-cell and policy rules;
2.  history lookup by normalized DemandIR and failure signature;
3.  keyword and fielded lexical classifier;
4.  local embedding centroid or k-nearest-neighbor classifier;
5.  calibrated logistic, tree or gradient-boosted feature model;
6.  cross-encoder pairwise chooser;
7.  grammar-constrained local SLM;
8.  contextual bandit with bounded exploration;
9.  cascade with conformal abstention;
10. strong-model selector;
11. managed external router;
12. oracle hindsight arm for evaluation only.

The feature vector should include task cell, languages, graph width, unresolved type/effect constraints, repository size, changed-file classes, test surface, requested effect, history, model/harness versions, context estimate, candidate entropy, deadline and verification cost. Raw user identity and protected attributes must not become accidental quality proxies.

## 183. Managed routers are experimental arms

Current managed systems demonstrate useful mechanisms but also expose why Taedri must retain its own outcome truth. [Amazon Bedrock intelligent prompt routing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-routing.html) predicts quality between configured models in one family, returns the selected model and documents application-specific limitations. [Microsoft Model Router](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-foundry/openai/concepts/model-router) and [OpenRouter Auto](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/routers/auto-router) provide other hosted selection policies. Evaluate each as a versioned MechanismArm:

- log the submitted projection and actual selected model;
- measure independently verified task outcomes, not router confidence;
- include router overhead and downstream repair;
- stratify by task cell, language, harness and repository scale;
- retain an always-strong, always-cheap and simple deterministic baseline;
- disable automatically on drift or quality-floor breach.

Provider routing is different from semantic routing. [Cloudflare AI Gateway dynamic routing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/features/dynamic-routing/) can express conditions, splits and budget policies; [Kong AI Proxy Advanced](https://developer.konghq.com/plugins/ai-proxy-advanced/) and [Envoy AI Gateway](https://aigateway.envoyproxy.io/docs/next/capabilities/) provide gateway algorithms and protocol controls. They may enforce a locked provider route, but they must not silently substitute a semantically different model.

## 184. Separate model, provider and endpoint selection

The route stack is ordered:

``` text
task eligibility
  -> semantic mechanism/model
  -> provider/runtime
  -> region/endpoint
  -> prefill/decode topology
  -> verifier
```

Semantic choice depends on competence and policy. Provider choice depends on price, contracts, privacy, availability and API fidelity. Endpoint scheduling depends on queue, locality and deadline. Conflating them makes receipts misleading and allows an infrastructure fallback to violate a semantic quality floor.

Endpoint selection should use latency distributions:

``` text
eligible(e) iff
P(TTFT(e, queue, prefix_overlap)
  + predicted_output_tokens / decode_rate(e)
  <= deadline)
>= required_deadline_confidence
```

Record the model revision, tokenizer, adapter, quantization, runtime, provider, region, endpoint class and fallback transition that actually executed.

## 185. Prefix-, KV- and topology-aware inference

[llm-d precise prefix routing](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/blob/main/guides/precise-prefix-cache-aware/README.md) and [NVIDIA Dynamo’s KV router](https://docs.nvidia.com/dynamo/latest/components/router) illustrate physical scheduling that considers prefix locality rather than load alone. [LMCache](https://docs.lmcache.ai/) extends KV reuse across memory and storage tiers. These mechanisms belong after semantic model selection.

Add separate arms for:

- least-loaded scheduling;
- exact prefix-affinity scheduling;
- joint queue and prefix score;
- deadline-probability scheduling;
- prefill/decode disaggregation;
- local automatic prefix caching;
- distributed KV transfer;
- n-gram or small-draft speculative decoding;
- request coalescing for identical verified prefixes;
- admission control that protects high-priority assurance work.

KV compatibility requires exact model, tokenizer, adapter, runtime-layout, positional-encoding and quantization evidence. A semantic-prefix digest is not enough to reuse activations.

## 186. ContextPlan as a compiled artifact

Context is selected, ordered and encoded—not concatenated.

``` yaml
context_plan:
  context_plan_id: ...
  work_node_id: ...
  semantic_input_digest: ...
  stable_prefix:
    policy_and_instruction_handles: []
    selected_tool_card_handles: []
    output_contract_handle: ...
  task_projection:
    demand_slice_handle: ...
    candidate_and_edge_handles: []
    evidence_handles: []
  volatile_suffix:
    latest_observations_and_errors: []
  omitted_items:
    - handle: ...
      reason: redundant | low_marginal_value | resolvable_on_demand | unauthorized
  detail_level_by_handle: {}
  token_estimate_by_block: {}
  cache_write_and_read_plan: ...
  resolution_callbacks: []
```

Use stable instructions and schema summaries first, volatile observations last, canonical field ordering, immutable handles and post-selection body resolution. The semantic digest proves the logical inputs; a byte digest proves cache compatibility.

## 187. Cache portfolio and invalidation

“Cache hit” must identify what was reused:

| Cache               | Object                        | Required key/invalidation                               |
|---------------------|-------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|
| accepted-outcome    | independently verified result | DemandIR, state, artifact, policy, oracle and freshness |
| route/PlanLock      | selected composition          | demand, catalog epochs, environment and policy          |
| retrieval           | candidate handles and scores  | normalized query, index epoch, filters and ranker       |
| tool projection     | selected cards/interfaces     | task cell, authorization and catalog epochs             |
| body/artifact       | code or package body          | immutable content digest                                |
| provider prompt     | provider-side prefix          | exact content/order, tenant, provider and model rules   |
| local KV            | activations                   | exact tokens, tokenizer, model, adapter and runtime     |
| distributed KV      | serialized activation blocks  | local-KV fields plus encoding, engine and tier          |
| build/test          | build and test artifacts      | source, dependency, toolchain and environment closure   |
| verification        | scoped oracle outcome         | candidate/effect, oracle version and relevant state     |
| negative capability | known failing route           | task cell, failure signature, arm/version and expiry    |
| memory              | compact accepted facts        | source turns, summarizer, authorization and validity    |

Write a prompt prefix only when expected reuse savings exceed write premium, fragmentation and invalidation loss. Do not use a provider prompt-cache hit as evidence that an answer is correct.

## 188. Compile instruction surfaces into InstructionIR

Coding harnesses expose overlapping instruction files, rules, skills, agents and hooks. Compile them once into a source-preserving representation:

``` yaml
instruction_ir:
  instruction_id: ...
  source_kind: agents_md | claude_md | rule | skill | hook | agent_profile
  source_uri_and_digest: ...
  scope:
    repository_and_paths: ...
    task_cells: []
    harnesses: []
  precedence:
    authority_level: ...
    directory_specificity: ...
    explicit_priority: ...
  activation:
    always: false
    triggers_and_capabilities: []
  content:
    summary_handle: ...
    body_handle: ...
    estimated_tokens: ...
  effects_and_permissions: []
  conflicts_and_resolution: []
  invalidation_dependencies: []
```

Preserve originals, resolve path scope deterministically, detect conflicts before a model call, keep only brief policy in always-loaded context, and move long workflows into on-demand bodies. Translate enforceable rules into deterministic hooks; count prompt or agent hooks as model calls.

## 189. Normalize hook and harness lifecycles

Map vendor events to a canonical event stream:

| Canonical event          | Meaning                                                  |
|--------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| session.start            | initialize policy, repository and environment identities |
| turn.input               | accept and normalize a user turn                         |
| node.start / node.stop   | begin or complete a typed work node                      |
| tool.before              | authorize and validate a proposed effect                 |
| tool.after               | capture result, state delta and receipt                  |
| tool.failure             | classify failure and select repair transition            |
| agent.start / agent.stop | delimit isolated delegated context                       |
| context.compact          | preserve source handles and summary lineage              |
| run.stop / run.failure   | close route, cost, evidence and effect ledgers           |

Adapters may project this stream to CLAUDE.md/skills/hooks, AGENTS.md/custom agents, local harnesses or future systems. Portability means equivalent policy and receipts, not identical hidden prompts.

## 190. Progressive tool and schema disclosure

Do not transmit hundreds of full schemas. Use a resolution ladder:

``` text
server or package card
  -> capability family card
  -> interface summary and typed ports
  -> selected operation schema
  -> executable body or remote endpoint
```

At each stage, exact requirements and typed compatibility prune candidates. Lexical, embedding and learned scores order survivors. Resolve full schemas only for finalists, and resolve implementations only after a route locks.

Tool discovery must be permission-aware: an unauthorized tool is ineligible, not merely down-ranked. Record cards shown, cards omitted, resolver calls, schema versions and final authority.

## 191. MCP and A2A become typed capability sources

MCP servers and A2A agents should enter the same graph as packages and functions:

- declared cards and registry metadata are claims;
- live handshake, schema and conformance results are evidence;
- each protocol/interface/version is a separate projection;
- extensions and required capabilities are hard compatibility constraints;
- remote actions expose effect, authorization, idempotency and compensation ports;
- durable task identifiers bind to one Taedri job/effect identity;
- behavior suites remain separate from protocol conformance.

The [MCP task utility](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/utilities/tasks), [MCP Inspector](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/tools/inspector) and [MCP conformance framework](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/conformance) provide useful ingestion and test surfaces. A2A Agent Cards, interfaces and extensions should be signature-checked and behavior-tested before promotion.

## 192. Durable execution and local repair

Long-running routes require crash-safe state, idempotent effects and resumable waits. A durable workflow engine may own timers, retries and recovery while Taedri owns semantic plan, authority and effect identities. [Temporal](https://temporal.io/) and [Pydantic AI durable execution](https://ai.pydantic.dev/durable_execution/overview/) are candidate adapters rather than canonical data models.

On failure:

1.  classify the failure into a typed transition;
2.  determine the smallest affected route subgraph;
3.  preserve valid retrieval, plans, effects and evidence;
4.  reselect only failed nodes;
5.  reverify changed claims and downstream dependents;
6.  escalate only if local repair exhausts its budget.

Never repeat an irreversible effect merely because the model response was lost. Reconcile external state using the effect identity first.

## 193. RouterMesh build sequence

### P0 — deterministic control and measurement

1.  Add WorkNode, TaskCellFeatureVector, RoleRoute, ContextPlan, CachePlan, InstructionIR, HookEvent, VerifierPlan and RoutingReceipt.
2.  Implement deterministic decomposition for retrieve, inspect, plan, edit, apply, execute, test, review and compose.
3.  Build exact/template, lexical, encoder, tree and constrained-local-SLM selector arms.
4.  Compile instruction files, skills and hooks with scope, precedence, conflict and digest preservation.
5.  Build server→capability→interface→schema progressive disclosure.
6.  Capture actual model, provider, endpoint, prefix, tool projection, caches and verifiers.
7.  Establish always-strong, always-local and fixed-waterfall baselines.
8.  Add typed abstention, escalation and failure-transition fixtures.

### P1 — external and physical-routing arms

9.  Add AWS, Microsoft and OpenRouter managed-router adapters in shadow mode.
10. Add one versioned gateway route graph.
11. Add local constrained-output serving and explicit competence profiles.
12. Add queue, prefix, prefill and decode telemetry.
13. Build provider/runtime equivalence probes.
14. Run MCP/A2A discovery, conformance and behavior probes.
15. Export normalized traces joined to route and evidence IDs.
16. Add durable work and exactly-once logical effect reconciliation.

### P2 — adaptive optimization

17. Add step-level shadow routing and logged selection propensities.
18. Calibrate acceptance and abstention per task cell.
19. Implement verification-triggered subgraph repair.
20. Add negative-capability memory with expiry and version invalidation.
21. Distill verified escalation-failure clusters into cheaper arms.
22. Add prefix canonicalization and cache-affinity scheduling.

24. Roll back automatically on quality, calibration, cost or drift breach.

## 194. Router and harness falsification suite

| Experiment                  | Arms                                                                             | Ship gate                                                                                                |
|-----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| router baseline tournament  | always-strong, fixed waterfall, rules, tree, encoder, local SLM, managed routers | adaptive arm beats best simple baseline on cost per independently accepted outcome at same quality floor |
| session versus node routing | one model for session versus per-node routes                                     | at least 25% lower total cost with pass rate within one preregistered percentage point                   |
| role specialization         | one model versus specialist retriever/editor/test/reviewer                       | at least 20% lower cost and no rise in invalid patches                                                   |
| instruction compilation     | monolithic files versus concise policy plus on-demand bodies/hooks               | at least 30% fewer repeated instruction tokens with unchanged success                                    |
| tool disclosure             | full schemas versus 8/16/32 cards and deferred resolution                        | at least 99% needed-tool recall with lower schema tokens and equal validity                              |
| candidate disclosure        | 1/2/4/8 alternatives at multiple detail levels                                   | choose Pareto frontier by accepted outcome, tokens and missed-route rate                                 |
| prefix canonicalization     | current prompt order versus stable-prefix compiler                               | at least 20% relative cache-hit gain with equivalent semantic digest                                     |
| endpoint routing            | least-load versus prefix-aware versus joint distributional score                 | lower TTFT without more than 5% p95 completion regression                                                |
| KV hierarchy                | no cache, local prefix cache, distributed cache                                  | distributed tier must beat local after transfer/storage overhead                                         |
| managed-router audit        | internal arms versus hosted routers                                              | external arm wins on Taedri tasks after router and repair cost                                           |
| step-level downgrade        | replay strong trajectories with one node downgraded                              | discover safe cheap cells without changing verified final outcome                                        |
| assurance routing           | verify-all, risk tiers, EVSI-selected                                            | at least 25% lower verifier cost with no increase in false acceptance                                    |
| local repair                | complete rerun versus affected-subgraph rerun                                    | at least 40% less repeated work with equivalent final pass rate                                          |
| negative memory             | no memory versus expiring failure cache                                          | halve repeated known-bad selections with less than 1% false exclusion after upgrades                     |
| drift and manipulation      | workload/model drift and irrelevant complexity prefixes                          | detect breach early; irrelevant text must not materially alter tier                                      |
| durable faults              | cancellation, endpoint death, duplicate delivery and committed effect            | one logical effect and a complete receipt in every fixture                                               |
| cross-harness projection    | same tasks through multiple harness adapters                                     | equivalent policy/test behavior with every difference attributable                                       |
| end-to-end economics        | ordinary coding RAG versus compiled Taedri route                                 | higher independently accepted outcomes per dollar and per uncached token                                 |

Report input, cached-input, reasoning and output tokens separately; selector overhead; tool-discovery recall; cache reuse; escalation, repair and abstention; verifier cost; false acceptance; repeated effects; TTFT and completion percentiles; and results by task cell, language, repository size, harness and model epoch.

# Part XVIII — Information-theoretic control, epistemic contracts and self-optimization

## 195. Put every inference in an epistemic envelope

Taedri combines exact facts, sound approximations, heuristic scores, model proposals, observations and proofs. They must never collapse into one untyped confidence value.

``` yaml
formal_artifact:
  artifact_id: taedri://formal-artifact/<digest>
  subject_revision_ids: []
  formalism:
    family: exact | datalog | egraph | abstract_interpretation | type_system |
            smt | csp | planner | petri_net | model_checker | probabilistic |
            statistical | information_theoretic
    implementation_and_version: ...
    semantics_id_and_version: ...
  inputs:
    graph_snapshot_id: ...
    entity_descriptor_and_evidence_ids: []
  assumptions:
    - statement: ...
      machine_expression: ...
      origin: asserted | inferred | observed | verified
      scope_and_expiry: ...
  result:
    kind: proof | witness | unsat_core | equivalence_class | derivation |
          overapproximation | underapproximation | posterior | ranking | counterexample
    payload_handle: ...
  guarantees:
    epistemic_class: exact | proved_given_assumptions | sound_overapproximation |
                     empirically_observed | calibrated_statistical | heuristic
    covered_domain: ...
    known_incompleteness: ...
  verification_and_replay:
    checker_and_version: ...
    replay_recipe_handle: ...
    receipt_digest: ...
```

Promotion follows an explicit partial order. More evidence can strengthen a scoped claim, contradict it or narrow its domain; it cannot silently convert observed behavior into universal behavior, probability into proof, or solver satisfiability into correctness of omitted assumptions.

## 196. Define the complete optimization target

For demand d, candidate route r, context projection c, mechanism allocation m and assurance plan v:

``` text
minimize
  E[cost_retrieval + cost_context + cost_reasoning + cost_execution
    + cost_verification + cost_repair + loss_of_failure]

subject to
  P(independent_acceptance | d,r,c,m,v) >= quality_floor(d)
  policy(d,r,m) = eligible
  effect_authority(d,r) = granted
  latency_quantile(d,r,m,v) <= deadline(d)
  residual_required_claims(d,r,c,m,v) = empty
```

When the constraints cannot be established, return abstention, clarification or a no-route certificate—not a plausible best effort disguised as success. Keep Pareto fronts for cost, latency, privacy, energy and assurance because one global weighted sum cannot represent every tenant or task.

## 197. ContextCodec and the disclosure lattice

Every graph object should have independently addressable encodings rather than one canonical prose card:

| Level | Payload                                                            | Typical use                |
|-------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------|
| C0    | global ID, kind, version and digest                                | exact cache/history lookup |
| C1    | name, namespace, keywords and compact type/effect keys             | blocking                   |
| C2    | one-line black-box capability and primary ports                    | cheap candidate choice     |
| C3    | typed compatibility surface, constraints and negative capabilities | route solving              |
| C4    | evidence-backed behavioral summary, examples and failures          | semantic selection         |
| C5    | selected source spans, tests, traces or schemas                    | planning and verification  |
| C6    | full body, artifact or executable environment                      | implementation/execution   |

``` yaml
context_codec_record:
  subject_revision_id: ...
  codec_id_and_version: ...
  detail_level: C0 | C1 | C2 | C3 | C4 | C5 | C6
  facet: identity | behavior | signature | type | effect | examples | failures |
         operational | provenance | security | compatibility
  payload_handle_and_digest: ...
  estimated_tokens_by_tokenizer: {}
  derivation_and_evidence_ids: []
  loss_profile:
    preserved_queries: []
    known_omissions: []
    empirical_error_by_task_cell: {}
  parent_and_refinement_handles: []
```

The model first receives handles and C1–C3 projections. It can deterministically resolve one facet or one body after selection. This makes context a queryable graph with refinement edges rather than a monolithic prompt.

## 198. MDL, rate-distortion and information bottleneck policies

Minimum Description Length asks whether a representation saves enough future error to justify its complexity. Rate-distortion asks for the minimum number of bits or tokens that keeps task loss below a chosen bound. The information bottleneck asks for a projection that retains information about the downstream decision while discarding irrelevant input detail.

For task cell t and context projection c:

``` text
rate_distortion(t, epsilon) =
  min expected_tokens(c)
  subject to E[decision_loss(t,c)] <= epsilon

mdl_score(c) =
  code_length(c)
  + code_length(observed_outcomes | c)

information_bottleneck(c) =
  I(c; raw_context)
  - beta * I(c; independently_verified_outcome)
```

The quantities are estimated empirically, not assumed. Maintain curves by task cell, model, repository scale and descriptor version. A summary that works for package discovery may be too lossy for migration or security review. The safe policy selects the cheapest detail point whose upper confidence bound on loss remains below the task’s distortion budget.

## 199. Diverse candidate panels under a token budget

Top-k relevance often returns near duplicates. Select candidate cards, edges and evidence jointly:

``` text
maximize over selected set S
  coverage_of_demand_facets(S)
  + compatibility_path_gain(S)
  + uncertainty_reduction(S)
  + evidence_independence(S)
  + diversity(S)
  - redundancy(S)
  - risk_and_token_cost(S)

subject to
  tokens(S) <= context_budget
  required_hard_facets_covered(S) = true
```

Implement and compare:

- maximal marginal relevance for a cheap greedy baseline;
- monotone submodular coverage with lazy greedy selection;
- knapsack-aware submodular selection for unequal card sizes;
- determinantal point processes for quality-weighted diversity;
- facility-location coverage of demand senses;
- residual-error diversity, which prefers alternatives likely to fail differently;
- constrained set cover for mandatory type/effect/evidence facets;
- Pareto panels that expose one cheapest, one safest, one fastest and one most-established route.

Do not add alternatives merely to fill k. Stop when marginal coverage is nonpositive. Test 1/2/4/8 alternatives and C1–C5 detail schedules jointly because candidate count and per-candidate detail compete for the same context.

## 200. Active acquisition by expected value of computation

At any uncertainty state s, choose among exact lookup, graph expansion, descriptor resolution, static analysis, test, sandbox run, local model, strong model, verifier or clarification:

``` text
EVOC(action | s) =
  expected_reduction_in_decision_loss
  + expected_reduction_in_failure_consequence
  - monetary_cost
  - latency_penalty
  - privacy_and_effect_risk
  - opportunity_cost
```

Execute only if the best eligible action has positive EVOC and remaining budget. Approximate cheaply with calibrated outcome models; periodically compare with exhaustive small-domain oracles. Distinguish:

- value of information: learn an uncertain fact;
- value of computation: reason longer with current facts;
- value of execution: observe behavior;
- value of verification: detect a harmful error;
- value of clarification: ask the user for a missing preference or authority.

Myopic EVOC is only a baseline. Add two-step lookahead for actions that unlock high-value tests, branch-and-bound over expensive acquisition sequences and an option value for preserving reversible routes.

## 201. No-route certificates and residual proof obligations

Failure should be useful and compact.

``` yaml
no_route_certificate:
  demand_ir_digest: ...
  catalog_and_policy_epochs: ...
  searched_scope_and_completeness: ...
  hard_constraints: []
  eliminated_candidate_classes:
    - candidate_or_class: ...
      failed_constraints: []
      evidence_ids: []
  solver_result:
    status: unsatisfiable | incomplete_search | policy_blocked | budget_exhausted
    unsat_core_or_cut_set: ...
  unresolved_open_world_regions: []
  minimal_relaxations:
    - change: ...
      newly_feasible_route_handles: []
  clarification_options: []
  replay_receipt: ...
```

Every selected route also carries residual proof obligations: claims required for acceptance that have not yet been established. Verification is a set-cover problem over these obligations. If obligations remain after the assurance budget, the route stays provisional. Unsatisfiable cores and minimal cut sets should become indexed negative evidence only within their exact version, environment and closed-world scope.

## 202. Formal-method and verifier routing

The system should route uncertainty to the cheapest adequate formalism:

| Question                              | First mechanism                        | Escalation                                 |
|---------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
| exact identity or field               | hash/index/schema lookup               | source inspection                          |
| local type/shape/effect compatibility | unification and constraint propagation | SMT/refinement solver                      |
| graph reachability and derivation     | Datalog/semiring traversal             | CSP/SMT                                    |
| equivalent expressions                | rewrite rules/e-graph                  | proof checker or differential test         |
| may/must runtime behavior             | abstract interpretation                | symbolic execution/test                    |
| action decomposition                  | templates/HTN                          | general planner/LLM proposal plus checking |
| concurrent workflow soundness         | workflow/Petri analysis                | model checking                             |
| uncertain semantic suitability        | calibrated statistical ranker          | execution and independent verifier         |

Selection depends on soundness required, domain support, expected pruning, proof-checking cost, path explosion, latency and consequence. A solver is not “stronger” in the abstract; it is adequate only when the encoded semantics cover the relevant claim.

## 203. Learn routing safely from delayed verified outcomes

Each decision log needs context, eligible arms, selected arm, selection probability, exact arm versions, downstream costs and independently verified reward. Without propensities and overlap, counterfactual evaluation is unreliable.

Use a staged policy lifecycle:

1.  deterministic baseline and frozen evaluation corpus;
2.  supervised prediction on historical verified outcomes;
3.  shadow selection with no behavior change;
4.  inverse-propensity, doubly robust and SWITCH-style off-policy estimates;
5.  confidence bounds and slice-level stress tests;
6.  bounded canary on reversible, low-risk cells;
7.  sequential monitoring with automatic rollback;
8.  targeted distillation from verified escalation failures;
9.  periodic rebaseline after model, index, harness or workload change.

The [SWITCH estimator](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v70/wang17a.html) is relevant because it explicitly manages off-policy bias and variance; it does not remove the need for support diagnostics. Avoid causal overclaiming: historical selection is confounded by prior policy, tools, prompts, user population and changing model versions. Randomized exploration supplies identification only in the narrow cells where it was actually performed.

## 204. Information-control and policy-learning experiments

1.  **Rate-distortion curves:** test C0–C6 and mixed facet projections by task cell; publish accepted-outcome loss versus uncached tokens.
2.  **MDL descriptor promotion:** compare human-chosen fields with descriptors admitted by lifetime compression plus error; reject fields that add storage/tokens without predictive gain.
3.  **Information bottleneck:** train task-conditioned projections and compare against extractive summaries at equal token budgets; audit omitted hard constraints.
4.  **Panel selection:** compare top-k, MMR, lazy submodular, DPP and residual-diversity panels at 1/2/4/8 candidates.
5.  **Count-detail factorial:** jointly vary candidate count and C-level; identify whether four terse candidates beat one detailed candidate by task cell.
6.  **EVOC controller:** compare fixed waterfall, myopic EVOC and two-step lookahead against an exhaustive oracle on small tasks.
7.  **No-route precision:** seed satisfiable and unsatisfiable demands; require certificates never claim completeness beyond searched scope.
8.  **Minimal relaxation quality:** compare suggested relaxations with expert judgments and newly executable routes.
9.  **Formalism router:** compare fixed SMT, fixed execution and routed formalism on proof coverage, wall time and false assurance.
10. **Verifier set cover:** choose verifiers by residual obligations and compare with verify-all on cost and false acceptance.
11. **Off-policy support:** measure effective sample size, propensity overlap and estimator disagreement before approving a policy.
12. **Shadow-to-canary prediction:** require offline confidence intervals to cover observed canary value by task slice.
13. **Delayed reward:** compare immediate proxy optimization with final accepted-outcome reward; quantify proxy-induced regressions.
14. **Drift:** change model, embedding, corpus and task mix independently; test detection and rollback latency.
15. **Confounding trap:** construct logs where a weak arm was historically given easy tasks; verify that naive averages choose incorrectly.
16. **Exploration safety:** compare uniform exploration with conservative constrained exploration on regret and quality-floor violations.
17. **Targeted distillation:** train on random examples versus escalation-failure clusters; report frontier-call reduction per training example.
18. **Epistemic integrity:** inject probability/proof, observation/universality and attestation/correctness confusions; require the promotion engine to reject every invalid conversion.

## 205. Conformal risk, abstention and shift control

Model confidence is not a safety guarantee. Maintain nested policies from cheap acceptance through additional retrieval, verification, model escalation and abstention. Calibrate the least costly policy whose upper bound on scoped loss stays under the task’s risk budget. [Conformal Risk Control](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.02814) provides a relevant framework for controlling expected monotone loss under its assumptions.

Useful losses include unsafe acceptance, unsupported material claims, false bounded no-route certificates, repeated effects and severity-weighted verification failures. Calibrate separately for read-only analysis, code generation, sandboxed execution, security-sensitive work, license-sensitive reuse and production effects when sufficient data exists; otherwise back off hierarchically to broader task/risk groups.

``` text
accept arm a only if
  upper_bound(P(failure | task_cell, a, current_epoch))
  * consequence_severity
  <= task_risk_budget
```

Track embedding and feature shift, unseen package/version rate, candidate entropy, failure residuals, model and harness changes, verifier failure rate and conformal score distributions. On shift: increase abstention/escalation, suspend online learning, collect verified outcomes, recalibrate, replay against the prior policy and require a fresh promotion gate.

## 206. Build order for the self-optimizing plane

### P0 — semantics and replay

1.  Implement FormalArtifact, ContextCodecRecord, ResidualProofObligation, NoRouteCertificate and RouterDecisionLog.
2.  Distinguish UNSAT, NOT_FOUND, UNKNOWN, POLICY_BLOCKED, BUDGET_EXHAUSTED and ABSTAIN in every API.
3.  Canonicalize token, latency, money, privacy, energy, evidence and outcome accounting.
4.  Store full eligible action sets and logging propensities, not just selected arms.
5.  Reproduce decisions from immutable graph, index, policy, codec and arm snapshots.

### P1 — deterministic research arms

6.  Implement C0–C6 codecs and empirical distortion tables.
7.  Implement top-k, MMR, budgeted submodular, DPP and constrained-set-cover selectors.
8.  Add authority, evidence-independence and route-family constraints.
9.  Propagate proof obligations and resolve bodies only after selection.
10. Build seeded route/no-route, context-omission and misleading-metadata benchmarks.

### P2 — measured adaptation

11. Train calibrated cost, latency, outcome and information-gain models.
12. Add one-step EVOC plus clarification EVSI, then shallow lookahead.
13. Add direct, IPS, self-normalized IPS, doubly robust and SWITCH evaluation.
14. Gate deployment on overlap, effective sample size, estimator agreement and slice confidence.
15. Run randomized comparisons only inside deterministic low-risk eligibility envelopes.

### P3 — assurance and promotion

16. Add conformal acceptance and abstention controllers.
17. Add shift detection and conservative automatic fallback.
18. Add independent solver/proof rechecking and proof-artifact storage.
19. Add policy shadowing, canaries, sequential stopping and rollback.
20. Promote a policy only if it adds a non-dominated point to the independently verified cost-quality-risk frontier.

# Part XIX — One hundred additional mechanisms for the research and build backlog

These are additive hypotheses, not mandatory architecture. Each receives an owner, simplest baseline, frozen corpus, metric, failure threshold and retirement rule before implementation.

## 207. Stable identity and evolution — M001–M010

- **M001 — Normalized symbol fingerprints:** Hash language, package coordinate, qualified path, normalized signature and alpha-renamed AST structure; test recall across rename-only, formatting-only and file-move commits.
- **M002 — Version-lineage matching:** Build a weighted bipartite matcher over syntax, behavior, documentation and callers; score it against labeled split, merge, move and rewrite histories.
- **M003 — Alias-equivalence ledger:** Record imports, re-exports, wrappers, forwarding methods, compatibility aliases and vendored copies as typed claims; measure removed duplicate retrieval and double-counting.
- **M004 — Generated-artifact lineage:** Connect generated entities to OpenAPI, Protobuf, ORM, parser-generator or other generation inputs; test whether schema changes reach every affected symbol.
- **M005 — Build-variant identities:** Give conditional-compilation, platform, feature-flag and optional-dependency variants explicit sub-identities; verify that impossible cross-variant routes disappear.
- **M006 — Cross-language bridge identities:** Join Python bindings, native symbols, FFI declarations, JNI methods, WebAssembly exports and RPC handlers; test end-to-end tracing across language boundaries.
- **M007 — Runtime object archetypes:** Cluster dynamic instances by observed fields, protocols and state transitions while retaining class identity; measure gains for duck-typed and metaprogrammed libraries.
- **M008 — Identity tombstones:** Preserve retired IDs with replacements, removal reasons and last-seen metadata; test safe resolution of old prompts and cached routes after upgrades.
- **M009 — Collision canaries:** Generate adversarial packages with identical names, signatures, docs or syntax but different behavior; quantify false identity merges before every release.
- **M010 — Identity-confidence ledger:** Store method, evidence, confidence and dissent for each identity edge; test threshold policies for lineage precision and recall.

## 208. Descriptor and representation systems — M011–M020

- **M011 — Facet-isolated vector banks:** Embed names, signatures, docs, implementation, examples, tests, errors and traces separately; ablate each facet by task.
- **M012 — Cross-language semantic projection:** Align language-specific encoders into a capability space; evaluate Python-to-Rust and JavaScript-to-Go substitute retrieval.
- **M013 — Source-free binary descriptors:** Derive embeddings and sketches from symbols, imports, CFGs, strings and normalized disassembly; test capability matching for stripped binaries.
- **M014 — Behavioral micro-specs:** Convert bounded traces into precondition, transformation and outcome summaries; validate on unseen executions before promotion.
- **M015 — Negative-capability descriptors:** Store does-not-support, unsafe-for and counterexample statements beside positive capabilities; measure invalid-route reduction.
- **M016 — Descriptor contradiction graphs:** Link disagreements among docs, types, code, examples, tests and runtime evidence; test contradiction-aware ranking against stale claims.
- **M017 — Hierarchical summary pyramids:** Aggregate symbol summaries into class, module, package and ecosystem levels with provenance; measure compression versus fidelity at each level.
- **M018 — Polysemy-aware capability senses:** Split overloaded terms such as map, session and model by context-conditioned sense; test ambiguous-query precision.
- **M019 — Calibrated descriptor uncertainty:** Attach conformal sets or empirical error bounds to inferred labels and summaries; compare stated confidence with held-out error.
- **M020 — Descriptor distillation:** Distill expensive descriptions into templates or local-model outputs while preserving evidence handles; measure fidelity and lifetime token savings.

## 209. Compatibility and substitutability — M021–M030

- **M021 — Unit and dimension inference:** Infer physical units, currencies, coordinate systems and scaling conventions; reject numerically valid but semantically invalid compositions.
- **M022 — Shape-schema inference:** Learn tensor ranks, dataframe columns, nested shapes, sparsity and cardinality constraints; evaluate on real pipeline breakages.
- **M023 — Missingness-policy contracts:** Label behavior for null, None, NaN, empty strings, sentinels and absent fields; test preservation of missing-data semantics.
- **M024 — Encoding and locale contracts:** Extract encoding, normalization, collation, timezone, locale and newline assumptions; measure prevented text and timestamp corruption.
- **M025 — Algebraic property mining:** Test associativity, commutativity, idempotence, monotonicity and invertibility; use verified properties for reordering, batching and caching.
- **M026 — Determinism contracts:** Classify outputs as deterministic, seeded, time-dependent, environment-dependent or external-stochastic; retest under controlled perturbations.
- **M027 — Concurrency contracts:** Infer thread safety, reentrancy, coroutine safety, lock ownership and process-fork behavior; validate with stress and race detectors.
- **M028 — Resource-envelope contracts:** Learn input-conditioned memory, latency, descriptor, network and accelerator bounds; test planner compliance.
- **M029 — Wire and ABI compatibility:** Model serialization versions, endianness, alignment, calling conventions and protocol negotiation; verify with cross-version round trips.
- **M030 — Substitutability witnesses:** Package every claimed replacement with differential tests, adapters, preserved invariants and deviations; require the witness before drop-in ranking.

## 210. Dynamic behavior and effect discovery — M031–M040

- **M031 — Trace-derived state machines:** Infer guarded transitions from instrumented calls and object snapshots; test unseen valid and invalid sequences.
- **M032 — Exception-condition mining:** Associate exceptions and error codes with minimal triggering predicates; measure preflight and recovery quality.
- **M033 — Input-boundary discovery:** Adaptively sample valid ranges, singularities, discontinuities and pathological inputs; encode and rerun boundaries per release.
- **M034 — Configuration-sensitivity maps:** Perturb variables, flags, locale, filesystem and dependency versions; measure route portability across clean environments.
- **M035 — Platform portability probes:** Run standardized probes across OS, architecture, runtime and accelerator variants; publish evidence-backed matrices.
- **M036 — Fault-injection profiles:** Inject timeout, truncation, partial write, reset, corrupt record and dependency failures; score containment and recovery.
- **M037 — Dynamic taint summaries:** Trace sensitive, untrusted and licensed data from inputs to outputs and sinks; test policy-aware route blocking.
- **M038 — Performance response surfaces:** Fit latency, throughput and memory models over size, shape, concurrency and hardware; validate held-out routing choices.
- **M039 — External-effect inventories:** Observe filesystem, network, database, subprocess, clock, randomness and global-state effects; compare with declarations.
- **M040 — Streaming/backpressure profiles:** Measure buffering, watermark, ordering, cancellation and slow-consumer behavior; prevent unstable pipeline composition.

## 211. Usage, migration and ecosystem intelligence — M041–M050

- **M041 — Call-sequence mining:** Extract frequent successful API sequences into parameterized motifs; test executable first-pass synthesis.
- **M042 — Co-usage affinity graphs:** Estimate conditional association between symbols, packages, options and file types while correcting popularity; measure held-out recommendation lift.
- **M043 — Anti-pattern mining:** Learn patterns repeatedly removed by fixes, security patches or performance rewrites; test early defect warnings.
- **M044 — Argument-distribution profiles:** Summarize real keywords, ranges, shapes and option combinations; flag improbable generated invocations.
- **M045 — Migration-recipe extraction:** Align pre/post-upgrade code to derive executable transformations; validate on other projects crossing the same versions.
- **M046 — Failure-signature indexing:** Cluster issues, traces, CI logs and repair commits into symptom-cause-fix records; measure later top-k diagnosis.
- **M047 — Notebook execution mining:** Re-run notebooks to distinguish reproducible workflows from stale or order-dependent examples; retain executable cells as evidence.
- **M048 — Test-intent extraction:** Classify tests by invariant, edge case, regression, interoperability and performance intent; measure label improvements.
- **M049 — Ecosystem bridge scoring:** Find primitives connecting otherwise weakly linked formats, frameworks or communities; prioritize by route-coverage gain.
- **M050 — Popularity-debiased sampling:** Weight novelty, domain coverage, maintenance and failure diversity rather than downloads alone; test long-tail recall and reliability.

## 212. Trust, security, rights and governance — M051–M060

- **M051 — Signed extraction attestations:** Sign source digest, extractor version, build environment and output partition; verify byte-for-byte reproducibility.
- **M052 — Symbol-level license lineage:** Propagate notice and license obligations through copied, generated, wrapped and vendored code; test curated mixed-license repositories.
- **M053 — Vulnerability reachability graphs:** Connect advisories to affected symbols and actual call paths rather than package presence; compare with conventional scans.
- **M054 — Package-behavior quarantine:** Monitor install and import for unexpected network, credential, persistence or filesystem behavior; block anomalous publication.
- **M055 — Maintainer-risk signals:** Track ownership concentration, release-key changes, dormancy, abrupt dependencies and takeover indicators; backtest known incidents.
- **M056 — Privacy-transform labels:** Mark collection, derivation, anonymization, joining, retention and emission of personal data; test end-to-end purpose and retention rules.
- **M057 — Data-residency constraints:** Attach execution, storage, transfer and subprocess-egress rules; prove routes cannot cross prohibited boundaries.
- **M058 — Least-authority manifests:** Infer required files, hosts, variables, devices and credentials; execute with only those capabilities.
- **M059 — Deprecation-horizon forecasting:** Combine warnings, notes, replacement adoption and maintainer activity; score forecasts against later releases.
- **M060 — Revocation propagation drills:** Inject a compromised package, invalid license or retracted dataset; withdraw every derived card, cache, route and artifact within an RTO.

## 213. Execution packaging and composition — M061–M070

- **M061 — Hermetic primitive capsules:** Package selected functions with pinned dependencies, fixtures and capabilities in OCI- or WebAssembly-compatible capsules; compare clean-host behavior.
- **M062 — Executable example fixtures:** Convert docs examples to versioned I/O fixtures with environment metadata; use pass rates as evidence and regression alarms.
- **M063 — Adapter synthesis with obligations:** Generate schema, type, unit and protocol adapters plus loss and invariant checks; accept only discharged adapters.
- **M064 — Compatibility-shim registry:** Store reusable version and framework shims as graph nodes with supported ranges and expiry; measure avoided bespoke code.
- **M065 — Transaction-boundary inference:** Detect routes requiring atomicity and synthesize staging or commit protocols; inject failures after every step.
- **M066 — Compensating-action catalog:** Pair external effects with idempotent compensation recipes and preconditions; test interruption recovery.
- **M067 — Execution-topology synthesis:** Map logical routes onto processes, containers, queues, devices and regions; compare predicted and observed cost, latency and reliability.
- **M068 — Batch-stream transducers:** Verify adapters among scalar, batch, iterator, async stream and event windows under empty, partial, reordered and cancelled inputs.
- **M069 — Hardware-specialized variants:** Register CPU, GPU, TPU, SIMD and low-memory implementations behind one contract; benchmark placement.
- **M070 — Warm-state lifecycle management:** Record initialization, reusable state, eviction safety and version affinity; reduce cold starts without stale-state errors.

## 214. Learning and self-optimization — M071–M080

- **M071 — Contextual experiment allocation:** Use constrained bandits for descriptor, route and verifier variants under safety floors; compare regret with static policies.
- **M072 — Doubly robust offline evaluation:** Estimate policy value from logged propensities plus outcome models; validate against controlled online experiments.
- **M073 — Disagreement-driven labeling:** Send maximal extractor, model or verifier disagreement to high-assurance review; measure information gained per label.
- **M074 — Continuous hard-negative mining:** Promote near-miss retrievals and failed compositions into reason-labeled negatives; track neighborhood false-positive reduction.
- **M075 — Representation-drift alarms:** Monitor neighborhoods, descriptor distributions and compatibility rates after corpus/model changes; trigger calibrated rollback.
- **M076 — Counterfactual route replay:** Re-execute history against new graph, model and policy versions; measure broad versus easy-slice gains.
- **M077 — Multi-objective Pareto archives:** Preserve non-dominated policies across accuracy, latency, tokens, energy, privacy and assurance; select per request constraints.
- **M078 — Sequential experiment stopping:** Use confidence sequences to end clearly winning or losing arms under repeated looks; measure saved compute.
- **M079 — Failure-slice dashboards:** Report by language, package age, domain, task, ambiguity, route length and risk; block hidden minority regressions.
- **M080 — Shadow and canary promotion:** Run candidates invisibly and then on limited traffic; promote only through predefined quality and rollback gates.

## 215. Storage, synchronization and operations — M081–M090

- **M081 — Event-sourced graph mutations:** Record ingestion, inference, correction, revocation and compaction as immutable events; reconstruct historical views after schema changes.
- **M082 — Bitemporal facts:** Store real-world validity and database-observation times; answer what was true and what was believed at any past instant.
- **M083 — Conflict-preserving distributed ingestion:** Merge concurrent outputs with set-like convergence while retaining contradictory assertions; stress reorder and duplicate delivery.
- **M084 — Content-addressed evidence storage:** Deduplicate fragments, traces, fixtures and receipts by digest with manifests; measure storage reduction and tamper detection.
- **M085 — Temperature-aware tiering:** Place active adjacency and evidence on fast media while archiving cold history; benchmark p95 latency per storage dollar.
- **M086 — Locality-preserving graph partitioning:** Co-locate by package, call community and route traffic with boundary summaries; compare cross-shard fan-out to hash partitioning.
- **M087 — Incremental snapshot manifests:** Publish immutable changed partitions plus signed manifests; test bounded rollback and reproducible synchronization.
- **M088 — Ingestion watermarks and backpressure:** Expose source completeness and throttle producers when validation/indexing lags; prevent partial data from appearing absent.
- **M089 — Evidence-aware garbage collection:** Consider lineage, legal holds, replay windows and active receipts before deletion; ensure retained claims remain reproducible.
- **M090 — Recovery-game automation:** Corrupt indexes, lose shards and revoke sources on schedule; enforce graph recovery-point and recovery-time objectives.

## 216. Developer tooling, standards and ecosystem growth — M091–M100

- **M091 — Language-extractor SDK:** Define a minimal parser/identity/type/effect/docs/provenance adapter with reusable fixtures; measure time to conformance for a new language.
- **M092 — Namespaced extension registry:** Assign stable semantic IDs and version rules to third-party fields, edges and evidence; require unknown-extension round trips.
- **M093 — Adversarial conformance corpus:** Publish tiny repositories for aliases, metaprogramming, generation, conditional builds, FFI, monkey-patching and malformed packages; require expected facts and uncertainty.
- **M094 — Graph-schema linter:** Validate ID stability, edge direction, evidence, units, cardinality and extension compatibility before indexing; count production defects prevented.
- **M095 — IDE evidence lens:** Show capability, compatibility, provenance, risk and usage evidence beside symbols; measure dependency-choice time and reversals.
- **M096 — Route-explanation CLI:** Render selected nodes, rejected alternatives, adapters, constraints, costs and evidence as a replayable explanation; measure diagnosis time.
- **M097 — Interactive evidence browser:** Traverse package→symbol→claim→source/test/trace→route; test independent reviewer reproduction.
- **M098 — Policy-as-code packs:** Version organization rules for license, vulnerability, privacy, authority, maintenance and assurance; validate golden decisions.
- **M099 — Extractor/verifier marketplace:** Distribute signed plugins with schemas, benchmarks, permissions and ranges; enforce quarantine and conformance while measuring coverage.
- **M100 — Open longitudinal benchmark:** Maintain versioned discovery, substitution, composition, migration, diagnosis and verification tasks with frozen corpora and hidden tests; measure real progress.

The point of the hundred-item atlas is controlled optionality. It prevents the initial vertical slice from hard-coding today’s representations while still forcing every new idea through evidence, cost and retirement gates.

# Part XX — Target implementation overlay and decision program

## 217. The smallest system that tests the whole thesis

Do not begin with 100M entities, a universal ontology or an autonomous learning router. Build one end-to-end closed loop over a deliberately difficult Python package cohort:

``` text
artifact bytes + source revision
  -> stable symbol/revision identity
  -> AST/type/doc/example/test extraction
  -> extensible PrimitiveCard + typed ports + evidence claims
  -> exact/BM25/sketch/dense indexes
  -> DemandIR + compiled QueryPlanIR
  -> typed single- and multi-primitive route candidates
  -> 1/2/4/8 candidate/detail projections
  -> deterministic/local-SLM/strong-selector arms
  -> post-selection body resolution
  -> sandbox execution + independent verification
  -> exact cost/evidence/effect receipt
  -> frozen replay and comparison
```

This slice exercises identity, extensibility, retrieval, composition, context control, routing and truth. A component that does not affect this loop is research backlog until evidence says otherwise.

Start with 25–40 packages selected for contrasting semantics rather than popularity alone:

- dataframe/query engines: pandas, Polars, DuckDB and PyArrow;
- validation/serialization: Pydantic, marshmallow, jsonschema and orjson;
- text/data cleaning: regex, ftfy, Unidecode, rapidfuzz and clean-text;
- HTTP/retry: HTTPX, Requests, urllib3, Tenacity and backoff;
- imaging: Pillow, OpenCV and scikit-image;
- configuration/CLI: Click, Typer, Rich and Dynaconf;
- graphs/workflows: NetworkX and one lightweight orchestration package;
- ML transforms: scikit-learn and one imbalanced-data or feature-engineering package.

Pin exact versions and source/artifact digests. Include at least five version transitions, three wrapper/re-export families and known semantic incompatibilities. The goal is a high-information laboratory, not a representative PyPI census.

## 218. Repository work packages

Use independently testable packages or modules:

| Work package | Owns                                                                | Must not own                       |
|--------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| tcg-identity | coordinates, artifact digests, symbol/revision IDs, lineage         | semantic ranking                   |
| tcg-extract  | parser adapters, raw observations, source spans                     | promoted truth                     |
| tcg-schema   | extensible cards, ports, claims, evidence and receipts              | storage engine policy              |
| tcg-index    | exact, lexical, sketch, vector and graph projections                | final compatibility decisions      |
| tcg-query    | RequestEnvelope, DemandIR, QueryPlanIR and operators                | model/provider execution           |
| tcg-compose  | GraphIR, route solver, constraints and no-route status              | semantic guessing without receipts |
| tcg-context  | ContextCodec, candidate panels, resolution and cache plans          | correctness claims                 |
| tcg-router   | WorkNode, eligibility, arm selection and escalation                 | provider-side hidden substitution  |
| tcg-execute  | hermetic capsules, tools, effects and durable jobs                  | acceptance policy                  |
| tcg-verify   | obligations, verifiers, counterexamples and evidence reconciliation | route generation                   |
| tcg-lab      | frozen tasks, replay, OPE, experiments and dashboards               | production mutation                |
| tcg-api      | query/explanation/evidence interfaces                               | duplicated domain logic            |

Enforce ownership with import boundaries and schemas. Each package emits content-addressed artifacts and can be replaced by an alternative implementation.

## 219. Six-week build plan with exit artifacts

### Week 1 — identity and evidence skeleton

- define JSON Schema or typed models for ArtifactRevision, EntityRevision, Descriptor, Port, EdgeAssertion, EvidenceClaim and ExtractionReceipt;
- ingest five packages without embeddings;
- parse modules, functions, methods, classes, variables, imports, calls, docs, signatures and source spans;
- produce deterministic IDs twice from clean checkouts;
- publish an adversarial identity fixture suite.

**Exit:** the same bytes and extractor versions produce identical graph partitions; collisions, unresolved symbols and dynamic uncertainty are explicit.

### Week 2 — extensible cards and indexes

- implement namespaced extension fields and unknown-extension round trips;
- produce C0–C4 cards;
- build exact/history, fielded BM25, MinHash/SimHash and one dense facet index;
- add index manifests and per-projection epochs;
- create 200 labeled discovery/substitution queries.

**Exit:** every hit resolves to an immutable entity and source evidence; no index score is presented as compatibility truth.

### Week 3 — demand compilation and route solving

- implement deterministic RequestEnvelope and DemandIR extraction;
- compile logical/physical QueryPlanIR with exact and lexical-first rules;
- define input/output/type/schema/effect/version ports;
- solve typed bidirectional one- to four-node routes;
- emit near misses, failed constraints and NOT_FOUND versus UNSAT.

**Exit:** at least 50 multi-primitive tasks have hand-reviewed accepted routes or bounded failure labels.

### Week 4 — context and selector tournament

- implement C-level projections and post-selection resolution;
- generate 1/2/4/8 panels using top-k, MMR and constrained coverage;
- add deterministic, local encoder/tree, local constrained-SLM and strong-model selectors;
- log complete eligible sets, chosen arm, context bytes/tokens and propensities;
- freeze always-strong and fixed-waterfall baselines.

**Exit:** replay produces identical deterministic arms; every model call identifies exactly which cards, edges and instructions it saw.

### Week 5 — execution and verification

- build network-denied capsules with resource limits;
- implement schema/type checks, package tests, property fixtures and differential tests for selected families;
- propagate residual obligations and counterexamples;
- reconcile effects and prevent duplicate logical execution;
- emit an accepted or provisional result with exact receipts.

**Exit:** no route is labeled accepted without its required claims; injected failures are caught or explicitly remain residual.

### Week 6 — end-to-end evaluation and decision

- run retrieval, composition, routing, context and verification factorials;
- report accepted outcome, route recall, false acceptance, total tokens, dollars, latency and repair;
- perform slice analysis by package family, task, route length and ambiguity;
- publish all failing examples and counterexample capsules;
- decide which P1 mechanisms earn implementation.

**Exit:** one reproducible benchmark report shows whether the vertical slice beats dense-RAG plus strong-model and fixed-waterfall baselines.

## 220. Initial benchmark task families

Use tasks with executable or independently checkable truth:

1.  locate the exact entity from name/signature/error evidence;
2.  find a behaviorally suitable substitute under version/effect constraints;
3.  clean text, normalize encoding and deduplicate approximately;
4.  validate nested records and emit canonical JSON;
5.  transform dataframe schemas across pandas/Polars/PyArrow/DuckDB;
6.  compose retry, timeout, HTTP and validation behavior safely;
7.  read, transform and verify an image while preserving declared properties;
8.  migrate an invocation across a breaking version transition;
9.  explain a traceback and identify the minimal compatible repair;
10. construct a two- to four-primitive route under package restrictions;
11. reject a route with nullability, unit, async, effect or version conflicts;
12. return a scoped no-route or NOT_FOUND status correctly;
13. choose a cheaper model for deterministic/narrow nodes without changing final truth;
14. detect misleading documentation contradicted by code/tests/runtime;
15. replay a prior accepted route after a package or index change.

Each task stores DemandIR, allowed corpus snapshot, expected claims, acceptable route families, verifier bundle and severity. Hidden tests prevent selectors from optimizing to visible wording.

## 221. Quantitative promotion and kill gates

The first slice advances only if:

- exact symbol identity precision is at least 99.9% on labeled fixtures;
- lineage precision is at least 99% where automatically promoted;
- required-tool or primitive recall is at least 99% before aggressive context pruning;
- typed route validity is at least 95% before semantic execution;
- false acceptance is no worse than the strong-model baseline, with confidence intervals reported;
- the best Taedri arm reduces total uncached input tokens by at least 30% at the same acceptance floor;
- post-selection resolution reduces transmitted implementation/schema material by at least 50%;
- node-level routing reduces total model cost by at least 20% without more than one percentage point task-pass loss;
- local repair avoids at least 40% of repeated work on seeded failures;
- deterministic replay reproduces IDs, plans and receipts exactly;
- every revoked entity is removed from eligible projections within the declared freshness objective.

Kill or defer a mechanism when:

- its selector/control overhead exceeds the savings it creates;
- it cannot beat exact/BM25/simple-tree baselines;
- confidence cannot be calibrated by task slice;
- it adds an index with negligible unique oracle recall;
- its false negative suppresses valid routes;
- it produces evidence that cannot be independently replayed;
- it requires open-world completeness to make a safety claim;
- it improves proxy scores but not independently accepted outcomes.

## 222. What not to build yet

Defer these until the vertical slice establishes demand:

- a universal cross-language semantic ontology;
- global renaming of source variables for uniqueness;
- automatic execution of arbitrary newly ingested packages;
- a single learned embedding intended to represent every facet;
- online reinforcement learning on production effects;
- a 100M-entity distributed graph before query/operator profiles exist;
- a bespoke vector database, workflow engine or model-serving runtime;
- unbounded multi-agent deliberation;
- proof generation without an independent checker;
- marketplace publication without signing, conformance and revocation;
- broad long-term memory without authorization and invalidation;
- a single “trust score” that erases evidence type and scope.

Globally unique external symbol URIs solve collision and tracing problems without mutating code. Existing databases, queues, solvers, sandboxes and inference gateways remain replaceable infrastructure until measured constraints justify specialization.

The near-term product is therefore precise: a code-capability compiler that turns an existing package release into a searchable, composable and verifiable graph; turns a user demand into a small typed route; and proves exactly what was reused, executed, observed and accepted at materially lower context and model cost.

# Taedri business model, reuse economics, and coding-agent execution guide

> **ANNEX STATUS — TARGET BUSINESS/PRODUCT DOCTRINE.** This source-era guide is
> preserved for design coverage. It is not evidence of an activated tier, validated
> pricing, production operation, or customer outcome; Part 0 controls those claims.

**Status:** living canonical doctrine, product-market-fit thesis, and mechanism-neutral implementation guide
**Date:** 2026-07-16
**Audience:** product builders, design partners, investors, coding agents, and Taedri contributors
**Governing rule:** describe freely, materialize selectively, reuse before rewriting, and verify decisively

## How to read this guide

This guide separates four kinds of statement so a current implementation does not become an accidental permanent architecture:

| Kind                  | Meaning                                                                                                          |
|-----------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Invariant**         | A safety, evidence, identity, or outcome property that every implementation must preserve                        |
| **Goal**              | A capability or economic result Taedri should optimize, subject to measured tradeoffs                            |
| **Mechanism example** | One useful way to achieve a goal; replaceable when another mechanism preserves the contracts and performs better |
| **Current evidence**  | What the repository proves now, with its exact scope and limitations                                             |

Technology names, model families, storage engines, providers, deployment shapes, ranking algorithms, plan syntaxes, and worker boundaries are examples or current defaults unless a versioned public contract explicitly requires them. Taedri should standardize **interfaces, semantics, evidence, policy, and receipts** more strongly than it standardizes vendors or algorithms.

The intended architecture is registry-driven and late-bound. A policy can select a deterministic function, package call, remote tool, workflow engine, local model, hosted model, human approval, or another eligible mechanism for one atomic task. The selected mechanism must still satisfy the same typed demand, authority, effects, evidence, budget, and acceptance contract.

## 1. Executive answer

Taedri should become the **verified reuse and decision layer for software work**. Its purpose is not merely to store functions, proxy model calls, search code, or generate more code. It should help a human or coding agent obtain an accepted result by:

1.  understanding the requested outcome and constraints;
2.  finding capabilities that already exist in standard libraries, PyPI and other package ecosystems, repositories, internal code, APIs, or Taedri-authored primitive capsules;
3.  selecting the smallest compatible capability or composition;
4.  letting a model return the smallest sufficient plan representation—from one handle or `A>B>C` through a typed DAG, state machine, component architecture, or deployment plan— instead of asking it to rediscover and rewrite every implementation;
5.  downloading implementation bodies only after selection and authorization;
6.  executing with explicit effects and permissions;
7.  verifying the requested result with an appropriate oracle;
8.  retaining the successful route, versions, usage, evidence, and failure history so the next equivalent task can take a shorter path.

The commercial value is not “we have many primitive records.” The value is:

> More independently accepted software outcomes per dollar, with less repeated model work, less custom code, lower integration risk, and an auditable path from request to implementation and verification.

The default should be **reuse before generation** and **maintained upstream code before new custom code**, but this is a preference policy rather than an unconditional rule. Security, privacy, determinism, latency, licensing, portability, offline operation, maintenance, or ownership constraints may justify a different eligible path. Custom primitives remain supported when they are genuinely required, but they enter through the same capsule, evidence, test, policy, and versioning gates as external code.

## 2. The customer problem

Modern coding agents repeatedly spend context and inference on work that is already solved:

- searching documentation and repositories from scratch;
- recreating small parsers, validators, adapters, pagination helpers, retry policies, serializers, and data transformations;
- reading entire packages to discover one public callable;
- generating glue code without checking whether a maintained library already provides it;
- selecting APIs from prose while ignoring types, effects, versions, licenses, and failure behavior;
- re-solving the same repository convention in later sessions;
- carrying thousands of tool schemas or huge source files in context;
- trusting plausible generated code without independent execution or verification;
- adopting copied or custom code whose origin, license, maintenance burden, and security assumptions are unclear;
- losing the useful result after a session ends because the accepted route was never stored as a reusable asset.

This produces several forms of waste:

| Waste                  | Typical cause                                                 | Taedri response                                                      |
|------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Model-token waste      | Re-reading docs, source, tool schemas, and prior conversation | Body-free cards, graph slices, compact routes, exact replay          |
| Engineering-time waste | Reimplementing solved utilities and integrations              | Ecosystem ingestion, primitive search, verified route reuse          |
| Technical debt         | One-off custom helpers with inconsistent semantics            | Preferred contracts, maintained upstream pointers, bounded adapters  |
| Reliability debt       | Generated code is accepted without a decisive oracle          | Contract, test, execution, and verifier gates                        |
| Integration debt       | Similar-looking functions are assumed compatible              | Directional typed compatibility and adapter witnesses                |
| Knowledge loss         | Successful work disappears in chat history                    | Immutable route, usage, artifact, and verification receipts          |
| Supply-chain risk      | Code is copied without exact origin or license evidence       | Artifact identity, capsule lineage, license assertions, policy gates |

## 3. The solution as a configurable control loop

``` text
request + workspace + authority + acceptance criteria
                         |
                         v
               typed Demand / Outcome IR
                         |
              +----------+----------+
              | policy and hard gates|
              +----------+----------+
                         |
                         v
        eligible mechanism and capability portfolios
   exact | replay | package | internal | tool | model | human
                         |
                         v
       plan proposal at the smallest sufficient resolution
 handle | chain | DAG | state machine | architecture | change set
                         |
                         v
      deterministic validation, binding, and budget allocation
                         |
                         v
```
