## 19. Fully extensible registry architecture

The kernel should standardize the envelope and registry protocol, not freeze the universe of possible attributes.

### 19.1 Description portfolio

``` yaml
DescriptionPortfolio:
  subject_ref: ...
  snapshot_id: ...
  projection_refs: []             # unbounded
  descriptor_state_manifest_ref: ...
  coverage_manifest_ref: ...
  preferred_view_bindings: []     # preferred only for a scope/purpose
  contradiction_set_refs: []
  policy_projection_refs: []
  graph_epoch: ...
```

### 19.2 Provider manifest

``` yaml
DescriptorProviderManifest:
  provider_namespace: org.example.python-security
  provider_version: 2.4.1
  implementation_and_digest: ...
  supported_subject_kinds: []

  descriptor_definitions:
    - descriptor_key: org.example.python-security.deserialization_risk
      family: structured_claim
      value_schema_ref: https://example.org/schema/deserialization-risk-v2.json
      cardinality: many
      merge_policy: preserve_all_claims
      missing_semantics: explicit_state
      compatibility_role: hard_gate
      validators: []
      index_recipes: []

  description_views: []
  embedding_recipes: []
  fingerprint_recipes: []
  edge_predicate_definitions: []
  migrations: []
  default_trust_status: candidate
  policy_requirements: ...
```

### 19.3 Cardinality and immutable variant-production rules

Every semantic attribute is a **set of immutable typed variants**, not a privileged scalar:

``` yaml
AttributeVariantSet:
  subject_id: ...
  attribute_key: uceg.attribute.effects
  variant_refs: []                # unbounded
  combination_refs: []
  preferred_view_refs: []
  extension_registry_refs: []
```

This rule applies to identities, kinds, names, aliases, descriptions, keywords, languages, translations, labels, types, schemas, ports, effects, errors, permissions, lifecycle, trust, measurements, embeddings, hashes, structural views, nodes, edges, compatibility judgments, tests, observations, retrieval outcomes, route candidates, and model-visible projections.

Unlimited variants do **not** mean recursively turning every field into `any[]`:

- the entity has an unlimited collection of typed variant records;
- one variant describes one exact production or observation event;
- intrinsically plural fields such as evidence inputs may be collections inside that record;
- a different model, revision, prompt, seed, preprocessor, environment, scope, or output creates another record;
- exact duplicate payloads may share content-addressed bytes, while their production and evidence lineages remain distinct.

Variants remain separate whenever any of these differ:

- producer, provider, runtime, endpoint, implementation, or version;
- model family, checkpoint, weights digest, tokenizer, pooling, dimension, dtype, or quantization;
- prompt program, rendered prompt, system instruction, persona, parameters, or random seed;
- ordered inputs, artifact, build, dependency closure, preprocessing, postprocessing, or environment;
- output bytes, human edit, evidence, intended purpose, audience, language, detail level, policy, access scope, or time.

``` yaml
GenerationRun:
  generation_run_id: ...
  task_key: ...
  producer_ref: ...
  model_or_tool_ref: ...
  prompt_program_ref: ...
  rendered_prompt_digest: ...
  ordered_role_labeled_inputs: []
  preprocessing_chain: []
  parameters: {}
  random_seed: ...
  artifact_build_environment_scope: ...
  started_at: ...
  completed_at: ...
  output_variant_refs: []
  usage_and_cost_receipt_refs: []
  failure_ref: ...
```

Representation lineage is a many-to-many DAG. Derived variants store ordered or role-labeled inputs, derivation activity, supersession, invalidation, and output refs; a single `parent_id` is insufficient.

### 19.4 Required extension guarantees

- namespaced subject kinds, facets, descriptors, labels, predicates, roles, models, and view keys;
- semantic versions and immutable definition versions;
- schema references and schema validation;
- unknown-field round-tripping;
- no fixed attribute, description, keyword, label, fingerprint, embedding, edge, example, or evidence count;
- multiple provider and model versions at once;
- append-only original facts and claims;
- explicit derivation, invalidation, supersession, and retirement rather than overwrite;
- deterministic input digests and reproducible recipes;
- provider-specific validators, evidence requirements, compatibility roles, index mappings, policies, and UI projections;
- registry collision detection and namespace ownership;
- local/private/tenant namespaces;
- import/export without semantic loss;
- offline operation and local-model support;
- independent logical schema and physical materialization/index policy;
- reprocessing and re-embedding as new projection epochs;
- per-projection ACL, secrecy, license, retention, and egress controls;
- explicit graph/snapshot/build/environment scope;
- typed `not_computed`, `not_applicable`, `unknown`, `withheld`, `failed`, and `stale` states.

An open `extensions: map<string, any>` may preserve unknown data, but it must not be the only extension mechanism. Useful extensions should be registered, schema-validated, versioned, and independently indexable.

### 19.5 Multi-view axes

Keep all of these axes independent:

- subject kind and referent layer;
- programming language and language version;
- natural language, locale, script, and translation lineage;
- domain, framework, ecosystem, and organization;
- audience and purpose;
- retrieval direction and role;
- detail and abstraction level;
- source, producer, model, prompt/rule, and evidence grade;
- version, snapshot, build, platform, dependency, environment, input region, and time;
- tenant, principal, access, secrecy, license, retention, and egress policy.

### 19.6 Preferred values are scoped views

A preferred value is a reversible, versioned selection result—not privileged storage and never deletion of alternatives.

``` yaml
PreferredValueView:
  view_id: ...
  subject_id: ...
  attribute_key: ...
  consumer_or_purpose: retrieval|solving|selection|execution|verification|human
  scope:
    task_families: []
    natural_languages: []
    programming_languages: []
    environments: []
    tenants: []
    policies: []
  eligible_variant_refs: []
  selected_variant_refs: []
  selection_mode: single|ordered|set|combined
  selection_policy_ref: ...
  selection_policy_version: ...
  explanation_and_evidence_refs: []
  valid_interval: ...
```

Several preferred views may coexist. Retrieval may prefer a locally generated multilingual description, the solver may prefer compiler-derived contracts, and a verifier may ignore both in favor of tests and exact evidence. Every underlying variant remains directly listable, filterable, comparable, and traversable through lineage.

### 19.7 Representation combinations are first-class variants

``` yaml
RepresentationCombination:
  combination_id: ...
  subject_ids: []
  purpose: retrieval|ranking|solving|selection|disclosure
  combination_kind: union|intersection|ordered_fallback|cascade|rrf|weighted_sum|vote|concatenation|late_interaction|learned_fusion|graph_projection
  members:
    - variant_ref: ...
      role: ...
      weight: ...
  combiner_ref_and_version: ...
  configuration: {}
  training_or_calibration_ref: ...
  output_variant_refs: []
  lineage_and_evidence_refs: []
```

Valid combinations include lexical candidate unions, hard-filter intersections, several blocking families, rank fusion, multi-vector late interaction, description/model cross-products, analyzer consensus, graph projections, label votes, compatibility witnesses, and progressive disclosure bundles. Combination semantics—AND, OR, order, fallback, weighting, voting, calibration, or composition—must be explicit.

Do not eagerly materialize the Cartesian product of every description, model, preprocessor, and index. Register the possible axes; materialize useful runs; retain every executed combination with exact lineage and measured operating characteristics.

## 20. Physical index mapping

Logical descriptions can be materialized into several independently replaceable index planes.

| Descriptor family           | Primary indexes                                                      | Verification/source of truth              |
|-----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| Identity and exact facts    | key/value, relational uniqueness, content-addressed store            | canonical entity/fact store               |
| Source/evidence             | blob/content store, source-span table, Merkle store                  | exact artifact and acquisition receipt    |
| Plain text                  | fielded BM25/BM25F, phrase, prefix/suffix, identifier-aware postings | underlying description assertions         |
| Keywords/keyphrases         | postings, positional index, weighted sparse vector                   | term projection and source refs           |
| Labels/taxonomies           | bitmap/facet index, hierarchy closure, ontology graph                | label assertions and scheme definitions   |
| Scalars/quantities/versions | typed columns, range/interval/unit-aware indexes                     | typed assertion                           |
| Types/schemas/contracts     | structural indexes, unification/constraint solver                    | canonical contract and evidence           |
| Exact hashes                | hash table/KV/content store                                          | exact bytes or canonical serialization    |
| MinHash/LSH/fuzzy           | bucket tables and candidate postings                                 | exact comparison/typed verifier           |
| Embeddings                  | ANN per vector space plus exact rerank store                         | source projection and downstream verifier |
| Graph facts                 | adjacency/CSR, graph database, path/motif indexes                    | first-class typed edge assertions         |
| Temporal/history            | bitemporal/interval index, epoch/delta store                         | versioned facts and provenance            |
| Runtime/performance         | trace store, columnar series, sketch store                           | exact observations/workload metadata      |
| Evidence/trust              | evidence graph, claim table, contradiction index                     | signed/source/test/verification records   |
| Policy                      | authoritative policy engine and ACL prefilter                        | policy decision and audit receipt         |

Index manifests record shard, tenant/policy filter, snapshot/graph epoch, projection versions, build time, feature/model/seed/configuration, item counts, calibration, measured recall, and invalidation state.

### 20.1 Retrieval waterfall enabled by the portfolio

1.  Authenticate and apply tenant, ACL, secrecy, license, retention, and policy filters.
2.  Reuse exact query, verified route, user/org history, and cache hits.
3.  Resolve exact CEID, native/qualified name, alias, package, signature, error, and literal matches.
4.  Run fielded BM25/keyword/label/ontology and deterministic string matching.
5.  Compile typed demand into type/schema/unit/version/environment/policy constraints.
6.  Run bidirectional provider/consumer port blocking and graph route solving.
7.  Use membership filters to skip definitely absent shards/neighborhoods.
8.  Generate token/winnowing/MinHash/weighted-MinHash/SimHash/fuzzy candidates.
9.  Add AST/CFG/DFG/graph/motif/path candidates.
10. Add one or more relevant embedding spaces and late-interaction candidates.
11. Fuse calibrated ranks while retaining per-arm results.
12. Apply hard typed compatibility gates and evidence/freshness/quality ranking.
13. Resolve source bodies only for finalists.
14. Cross-encode or invoke an SLM/LLM only when uncertainty and expected value justify it.
15. Execute or independently verify where the task requires correctness.
16. Store exact success, failure, incompatibility, adapter, and receipt evidence for reuse.

This is the practical token-saving payoff: most queries can be compiled from the user demand into exact fields, terms, labels, sketches, graph constraints, and templates before any model drafts a custom query.

### 20.2 Role-specific canonical and disclosure views

Canonical views are versioned selection policies over retained variants:

``` text
RetrievalView
  aliases, keywords, descriptions, examples, sparse/dense variants

SolverView
  ports, types, schemas, effects, constraints, adapter witnesses

SelectorView
  contrastive alternatives, decisive differences, risk, cost, evidence, uncertainty

ExecutionView
  immutable artifact, runtime, dependency closure, authority, policy, secret classes

VerificationView
  claims, oracles, expected evidence, reconciliation and receipt requirements

HumanView
  readable explanation, provenance, alternatives, limitations, expansion handles
```

Progressive model disclosure:

``` text
D0  opaque stable handle
D1  name, labels, and one-line capability
D2  ports, effects, failures, state, and operational constraints
D3  decisive edges and contrastive alternatives
D4  selected examples, tests, evidence, and uncertainty
D5  full entity/edge/group/route card
D6  selected implementation body only when inspection or modification requires it
```

Search may use thousands of variants outside the model. Model-visible exact and near-duplicate variants should normally be clustered; provenance differences or semantic disagreements are exposed as deltas when they can change the decision. The disclosure optimizer minimizes context subject to preserving every decision-changing fact.

## 21. Generation and invalidation waterfall

1.  Acquire and content-address exact artifacts without executing them.
2.  Inventory every file, region, occurrence, symbol, binding, callable, type, port, relation, test, artifact, and failure.
3.  Emit exact identities, source facts, tokens, AST/CST, metadata, docs, and evidence.
4.  Resolve symbols, scopes, types, imports, calls, aliases, control/data flow, effects, and errors.
5.  Deterministically render plain-text cards, keywords, labels, schemas, contracts, and graph features.
6.  Produce exact and normalized hashes, shingles, sketches, LSH buckets, and membership filters.
7.  Produce cheap sparse and local dense embeddings for separately selected facets.
8.  Aggregate class/module/package/group boundaries bottom-up, retaining coverage and abstraction loss.
9.  Run framework/domain analyzers and add domain-specific facets.
10. Run sandboxed tests, traces, fuzzing, profiling, or reflection only under an explicit execution policy.
11. Generate higher-cost descriptions, embeddings, pair assessments, and route projections only when evaluation or demand justifies them.
12. Validate model-generated claims against facts; unsupported claims remain candidate hypotheses.
13. Publish an immutable graph/projection epoch atomically.
14. Invalidate projections by dependency/input digest; recompute only affected records.
15. Keep old epochs addressable for reproduction, comparison, rollback, and model evaluation.

### 21.1 Broad initial materialization profile—not a schema limit

For every discovered entity, broadly materialize:

- exact identity, occurrence, source handle, kind, scope, version, and provenance;
- native/qualified names and identifier-aware lexical forms;
- deterministic one-line and structured black-box cards;
- author docs and examples;
- labels for kind, visibility, lifecycle, execution mode, state, effect, error, domain, and trust where known;
- signature/type/schema/port/effect/error/state contracts;
- exact source/signature/schema hashes;
- several normalized source/token fingerprints;
- token shingles plus MinHash/SimHash candidates where size permits;
- fielded sparse search representation;
- exact typed graph adjacency and core graph statistics;
- evidence, contradiction, coverage, freshness, and policy records;
- at least independent text, code, and port/contract embedding arms when models are available and policy permits.

Then materialize additional models, detail levels, fingerprints, graph embeddings, runtime projections, pair assessments, and route descriptions according to measured value, query demand, policy, and compute/storage budgets. This is an open scheduling policy, not a feature cap.

### 21.2 Lifecycle, supersession, revocation, and deletion

- Creation is append-only.
- Corrections create new variants.
- Rejection retains the attempted run and negative evidence.
- Supersession and invalidation are explicit typed edges.
- Revocation prevents selection or execution without erasing audit history.
- Model, analyzer, prompt, preprocessor, or tokenizer upgrades create new variants.
- Re-embedding, rewording, recalibration, and index rebuilds create new projection epochs.
- Preferred pointers can change independently of retained records.
- Time-, environment-, version-, policy-, and tenant-scoped validity is explicit.
- Physical deletion follows privacy, access, retention, license, or legal policy.
- Deletion leaves an authorization-safe tombstone, digest, or non-disclosing audit marker where permitted.
- Downstream projections are invalidated through lineage and input digests, not by global rebuild assumptions.

## 22. Coverage and completeness ledger

“Describe every entity” requires a negative-space manifest.

``` yaml
CoverageManifest:
  snapshot_id: ...
  graph_epoch: ...
  entity_counts:
    discovered: ...
    parsed: ...
    resolved: ...
    typed: ...
    documented: ...
    runtime_observed: ...

  descriptor_coverage:
    uceg.identity: 1.0
    uceg.description.black_box: 0.93
    uceg.contract.errors: 0.41

  by_subject_kind: {}
  by_module_package_visibility: {}
  by_provider_and_version: {}
  by_environment_and_input_region: {}
  by_evidence_grade: {}

  unsupported_constructs: []
  failed_subjects: []
  unknown_reasons: []
  withheld_counts: []
  analyzers_run: []
  verification_coverage: ...
```

Coverage should be queryable by entity kind, facet, provider, package/module, visibility, version, environment, input region, policy, and verification level.

## 23. Evaluation atlas

### 23.1 Query classes

- exact symbol/name/package lookup;
- typo, alias, historical-name, and multilingual lookup;
- natural-language intent-to-code;
- code-to-code and cross-language analogy;
- copied-region, clone, lineage, containment, and refactoring lookup;
- signature/type/schema/unit/effect/error compatibility;
- producer-to-consumer and consumer-to-provider search;
- behavior, example, test, error, trace, and incident retrieval;
- graph neighbor, path, motif, role, and route retrieval;
- substitute, adapter, migration, deprecation, and change-impact search;
- quality-, trust-, freshness-, license-, security-, environment-, and policy-constrained retrieval;
- package/subsystem/group-level capability and boundary search.

### 23.2 Metrics

- Recall@k, precision@k, MRR, nDCG, MAP, and calibrated score quality;
- exact-name and rare-identifier recall;
- clone/containment recall by edit and normalization type;
- compatibility false-positive and false-negative rates per dimension;
- typed-solver agreement and adapter correctness;
- route discovery, verified execution, output correctness, rollback, and receipt reproducibility;
- retrieval-to-body-resolution ratio and tokens avoided;
- local compute, model tokens, latency, storage, index build time, memory, and energy;
- ANN/LSH recall against exact samples;
- evidence coverage, contradiction rate, staleness, and claim calibration;
- cross-version, cross-language, platform, framework, and package generalization;
- tenant/policy isolation and sensitive-data leakage;
- marginal utility and cost of every descriptor/model/index arm.

### 23.3 Hard-negative and poison suites

- sibling overloads differing by one decisive constraint;
- same name/different behavior and different name/same behavior;
- syntax-similar/behavior-different and syntax-different/behavior-similar entities;
- renamed-but-semantically-changed entities;
- same type but incompatible units, shapes, ownership, effects, error model, state, platform, version, or policy;
- comments/docstrings contradicting source;
- adversarial identifier and documentation search poisoning;
- clone boilerplate and generated code overwhelming unique logic;
- missing/stale graph edges and incomplete dynamic coverage;
- one rare decisive member hidden by a group centroid;
- cross-tenant, secret, license, and policy leakage attempts;
- LSH, fuzzy-hash, graph-hash, short-ID, and ANN collisions/misses;
- model/tokenizer/index upgrades and mixed-space corruption tests.

Code-retrieval evaluation should not rely on one benchmark. CodeSearchNet established a large multi-language corpus but its human relevance set is small relative to the corpus; [CoIR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.02883) broadens code-information-retrieval tasks, while [CoQuIR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.11066) explicitly separates relevance from code quality. Taedri needs its own compatibility, evidence, package-scale, route, and execution benchmarks in addition to these public references.

### 23.4 Real-world proof and promotion gate

Projected savings, invented workloads, synthetic provider receipts, and fabricated results must never be presented as real-world proof. Promotion tests use, where lawfully available:

- real released packages, source repositories, artifacts, and version incompatibilities;
- real package tests, builds, compiler or analyzer outputs, and execution environments;
- real user or production-derived demands with privacy and access controls;
- actual provider, model, or tool calls and provider-returned usage records;
- independent deterministic, test, domain, security, policy, or formal oracles;
- failure-inclusive costs per independently verified success.

For every representation, generator, model, preprocessor, blocking policy, index, fusion, selector, and disclosure policy, run individual-arm, cumulative-addition, leave-one-out, equal-candidate-budget, equal-latency-budget, frozen-candidate selector, frozen-selector retrieval, generator-by-generator, model-by-model, and description-source × embedding-model cross comparisons.

A variant earns a default or production role only when its measured marginal improvement repays storage, index-build, update, latency, compute, token, verification, error, and governance cost. Experimental variants may remain queryable without being promoted.

## 24. Design anti-patterns

- one universal code embedding;
- one summary field presented as truth;
- one closed list of labels, descriptions, edges, or models;
- fixed columns named after current embedding or hash providers;
- global source-code renaming to obtain uniqueness;
- missing value encoded as false, zero, empty, or an all-zero vector;
- unversioned canonicalization, preprocessing, tokenizer, prompt, model, seed, or index;
- comparing unrelated vector spaces or LSH configurations;
- using a fuzzy digest, vector score, or graph hash as equivalence proof;
- direction-normalizing relations without ontology permission;
- collapsing producer and consumer port semantics into one symmetric score;
- averaging all facets or all group members;
- flattening exact facts, generated claims, observations, and verified claims together;
- treating runtime observations as universal behavior;
- treating test coverage as correctness;
- all-pairs compatibility materialization;
- indexing unauthorized source before policy filtering;
- embedding raw secrets or sensitive runtime values;
- generated descriptions recursively used as evidence for themselves;
- destructive overwrite instead of append, supersession, and invalidation;
- benchmark optimization without hard negatives, execution, or independent verification;
- relying on an LLM to rediscover exact names, signatures, types, or graph paths already available deterministically.

## 25. Research and standards foundation

### Code identity, structure, and package facts

- [SCIP Code Intelligence Protocol](https://scip-code.org/)
- [Kythe schema reference](https://kythe.io/docs/schema/)
- [Python AST](https://docs.python.org/3/library/ast.html), [symbol tables](https://docs.python.org/3/library/symtable.html), [inspection](https://docs.python.org/3/library/inspect.html), [bytecode](https://docs.python.org/3/library/dis.html), and [data model](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/datamodel.html)
- [PyPA core metadata](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/core-metadata/)
- [Package URL](https://github.com/package-url/purl-spec) and [Software Heritage identifiers](https://docs.softwareheritage.org/devel/swh-model/persistent-identifiers.html)
- [SPDX 3.0.1](https://spdx.github.io/spdx-spec/v3.0.1/)

### Provenance, labels, and schemas

- [W3C PROV-O](https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/)
- [W3C SKOS](https://www.w3.org/TR/skos-reference/)
- [JSON Schema 2020-12 validation vocabulary](https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/json-schema-validation)
- [OpenTelemetry code semantic attributes](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/registry/attributes/code/)

SKOS’s distinction among preferred, alternate, and hidden labels is especially useful for public names, synonyms, misspellings, and retrieval-only aliases. OpenTelemetry’s separate code-function, namespace, file, line, column, and stack-trace attributes reinforce occurrence-level rather than prose-only observability.

### Sparse, fingerprints, sketches, and graphs

- [Winnowing](https://theory.stanford.edu/~aiken/publications/papers/sigmod03.pdf)
- [SimHash near-duplicate detection](https://research.google/pubs/detecting-near-duplicates-for-web-crawling/)
- [Weighted MinHash](https://research.google/pubs/improved-consistent-sampling-weighted-minhash-and-l1-sketching/)
- [SourcererCC](https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.06448)
- [TLSH](https://github.com/trendmicro/tlsh) and [ssdeep](https://ssdeep-project.github.io/ssdeep/index.html)
- [Weisfeiler–Lehman graph kernels](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v12/shervashidze11a.html)
- [SPLADE v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.10086)

### Learned code, text, and graph representations

- [CodeBERT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.08155)
- [GraphCodeBERT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.08366)
- [UniXcoder](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.03850)
- [CodeT5+](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.07922)
- [code2vec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.09473)
- [ColBERT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.12832)
- [Matryoshka Representation Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.13147)
- [node2vec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.00653), [GraphSAGE](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.02216), [TransE](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2013/hash/1cecc7a77928ca8133fa24680a88d2f9-Abstract.html), and [RotatE](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.10197)
- [Code Vectors from symbolic traces](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.06686)

## 26. Final architecture recommendation

Implement `TaedriCodeGraph` around five open registries:

1.  `SubjectKindRegistry` — every semantic, occurrence, runtime, relation, group, and route referent.
2.  `DescriptorRegistry` — exact facts, text views, keywords, labels, schemas, contracts, behavior, history, trust, and policy.
3.  `FingerprintRegistry` — canonical hashes, clone fingerprints, sketches, LSH families, graph/trace signatures, filters, and ANN-code projections.
4.  `EmbeddingRegistry` — unbounded facet/view/model/role/vector-space projections.
5.  `IndexRecipeRegistry` — exact, full-text, bitmap/range, constraint, LSH, ANN, graph, temporal, trace, and evidence indexes.

Then give every subject a `DescriptionPortfolio` and every portfolio a coverage ledger. The exact source graph remains authoritative; descriptions make it understandable; sparse features, fingerprints, and embeddings make it findable; typed ports and constraints make it composable; evidence and verification make it trustworthy.

The condensed operating rule is:

``` text
exact identity and facts
  → cheap lexical, label, schema, history, and graph retrieval
  → fingerprint/LSH and selected embedding candidates
  → typed directional compatibility
  → evidence-aware ranking
  → post-selection body resolution
  → execution or independent verification
  → exact reusable receipt
```

# Taedri source-acquisition and primitive-mining atlas

> **ANNEX STATUS — TARGET ACQUISITION RESEARCH.** Packages, corpora, templates,
> benchmarks, and workers listed here are candidates or plans unless Part 0 identifies
> a checked-in, executed artifact.

**Date:** 2026-07-16
**Revision:** 2 — long-tail capability, worker, template and benchmark expansion
**Project:** TaedriCodeGraph / Teleon / AIDevObserver
**Purpose:** Decide which packages, specifications, integration catalogs, code corpora, competitions, benchmarks, and evidence systems should populate Taedri's entity graph, primitive database, composition graph, and evaluation system.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Executive decision

Yes—heavily used PyPI packages, code competitions, and existing solution catalogs can all make Taedri materially better, but they should not enter one undifferentiated database.

The highest-leverage acquisition strategy is a **balanced, rights-aware source portfolio**:

1.  **Popular and central packages** teach Taedri the APIs people actually encounter.
2.  **Machine-readable specifications and integration ecosystems** yield typed ports and compatibility edges far more cheaply than reverse-engineering raw code.
3.  **Tests, examples, issue/patch histories, and accepted/failed submissions** supply behavioral evidence, failure modes, repairs, and executable oracles.
4.  **Competitions and agent benchmarks** reveal real demand, but their protected test sets and gold solutions must remain outside retrieval and training indexes.
5.  **Dependency, provenance, vulnerability, and repository graphs** determine which artifacts are compatible, current, attributable, and safe enough to execute.

The first non-package source I would add is **Apache Camel Kamelets**. A Kamelet is unusually close to Taedri's desired primitive representation: it declares whether it is a source, sink, or action; exposes a JSON Schema configuration contract; names dependencies and media types; contains a route body; and often includes examples and tests. The repository is Apache-2.0. [Apache Camel Kamelets](https://github.com/apache/camel-kamelets)

The first PyPI portfolio should not be “the top 100 downloads.” It should deliberately cover:

- packaging and environment compatibility;
- typed data contracts;
- HTTP, async, and protocol state;
- web routing and dependency injection;
- databases and transactions;
- arrays, tables, estimators, and files;
- test oracles and property generation;
- cloud service specifications;
- developer tools, diagnostics, and transformations;
- security/authentication contracts;
- model, agent, and tool protocols;
- graphs, search, retries, and algorithms.

The first competition sources should be split into three policies:

- **INGEST:** licensed training tasks, public tests, metadata, and explicitly reusable solutions.
- **DEMAND-ONLY:** prompts, tags, metrics, failure categories, and aggregate statistics; no answer bodies.
- **EVAL-ONLY:** sealed problems, hidden tests, and gold patches that are never available to retrieval, indexing, embeddings, or model-facing tools.

This separation is not paperwork. Without it, Taedri can appear to improve while merely retrieving benchmark answers.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 1. What Taedri is selecting for

Raw corpus size is a poor objective. The unit of value is a **new, verified capability or composition edge** that improves retrieval, planning, compatibility checking, execution, or verification.

For a source set (S), optimize something closer to:

``` text
maximize
    demand_coverage(S)
  + capability_novelty(S)
  + compatibility_coverage(S)
  + composition_edge_yield(S)
  + oracle_strength(S)
  + version_and_failure_diversity(S)
  + provenance_quality(S)
  - duplicate_content(S)
  - extraction_cost(S)
  - execution_risk(S)
  - rights_uncertainty(S)
```

The objective should be **submodular**: a fifth HTTP client is worth less than the first transaction manager, even when the fifth HTTP client has more downloads. The scheduler should therefore select the next package or source by *marginal verified coverage per unit cost*, not by a static global rank.

### 1.1 Signals that should contribute to source priority

| Signal                      | Why it matters                                                              | Typical source                             |
|-----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
| Qualified usage             | Likelihood of appearing in real user code                                   | PyPI BigQuery, repository imports, surveys |
| Direct reverse dependents   | Ecosystem blast radius without CI-download distortion                       | Reconstructed dependency graph             |
| Compatible transitive reach | How much of the graph a package unlocks in a specific environment           | Version-aware dependency solver            |
| API surface yield           | Number and richness of public entities and ports                            | AST, stubs, schemas, reflection in sandbox |
| Capability novelty          | New intent, protocol, domain, type, effect, or failure mode                 | Descriptor and graph coverage analysis     |
| Composition density         | Number of trustworthy producer→consumer routes                              | Typed schemas, examples, workflows, tests  |
| Oracle strength             | Whether behavior can be verified independently                              | Tests, validators, benchmark graders       |
| Documentation quality       | Ability to create useful black-box descriptions without expensive inference | Official references and examples           |
| Version diversity           | Migration, compatibility, and deprecation knowledge                         | Release histories and diffs                |
| Provenance strength         | Ability to bind a body to release, source, publisher, and license           | Digests, attestations, SWHIDs              |
| Maintenance and risk        | Selection and execution policy                                              | OSV, Scorecard, release/activity data      |
| Marginal extraction cost    | Storage, parsing, execution, and model cost                                 | Taedri telemetry                           |

### 1.2 A practical initial package score

Before enough Taedri outcomes exist to learn the weights, use:

``` text
0.25 distinct reverse runtime dependents
+ 0.15 compatible transitive reach / graph centrality
+ 0.10 observed direct imports and human-use evidence
+ 0.10 qualified recent downloads
+ 0.15 marginal capability and protocol coverage
+ 0.10 typed API, documentation, and test/oracle yield
+ 0.10 maintenance, provenance, and security evidence
+ 0.05 version and implementation diversity
```

Then replace this fixed score with a contextual bandit or Bayesian scheduler whose reward is measured retrieval, route, execution, and verification improvement.

### 1.3 A practical initial structured-source score

``` text
0.22 typedness
+ 0.20 composition-edge density
+ 0.17 oracle/test strength
+ 0.15 license clarity
+ 0.10 updateability
+ 0.08 adoption
+ 0.08 provenance quality
- rights uncertainty
- execution risk
- acquisition and normalization cost
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 2. Required source partitions

Every acquisition target belongs to a policy lane. The same upstream may produce records in more than one lane.

| Lane            | What Taedri may retain                                                           | Model/retrieval exposure              | Typical examples                                      |
|-----------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| `CATALOG`       | Identifier, upstream URL, version, declared metadata, digest, license evidence   | Search handles only                   | Proprietary connector catalog, public package record  |
| `DESCRIPTOR`    | Derived facts, schemas, signatures, embeddings, LSH keys, black-box descriptions | Retrieval allowed under policy        | Package API cards, OpenAPI operations                 |
| `LICENSED_BODY` | Source, docs, examples, tests, specs, workflows                                  | Body resolution allowed under license | Apache/MIT repositories, permissively licensed wheels |
| `EXECUTABLE`    | Frozen artifact plus verified environment and sandbox receipt                    | Tool execution allowed by policy      | Tested package version, verified Kamelet              |
| `EVAL_ONLY`     | Encrypted/sealed task material, hidden tests, gold result                        | Never available during task solving   | SWE-bench holdout, MLE-bench grader                   |
| `QUARANTINE`    | Artifact pending rights, malware, provenance, or quality review                  | No model or executor access           | Unknown-license submission, suspicious package        |

Three state transitions must be explicit:

``` text
CatalogHandle
    -> LicensedArtifact       only after artifact-specific rights evidence
    -> ExecutablePrimitive    only after static and sandbox verification
```

“Public,” “open API,” “verified publisher,” “archived,” and “downloadable” are not substitutes for either of those transitions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 3. The source registry Taedri needs

Do not mix acquisition policy into the entity graph as ad hoc fields. Maintain a source registry that governs what the extractors, retrievers, body resolver, and executor may do.

### 3.1 Core source records

``` yaml
SourceCandidate:
  source_id: globally stable Taedri ID
  source_kind: package_registry | repository | specification | catalog | competition | benchmark | telemetry
  canonical_uri: upstream identity
  acquisition_connectors: []
  update_protocol: snapshot | event_feed | polling | immutable
  expected_artifacts: []
  expected_entity_kinds: []
  estimated_typedness: 0.0
  estimated_oracle_strength: 0.0
  estimated_edge_yield: 0.0
  estimated_cost: {}
  policy_lane: CATALOG | DESCRIPTOR | LICENSED_BODY | EXECUTABLE | EVAL_ONLY | QUARANTINE

SourceSnapshot:
  source_snapshot_id: content-addressed identity
  source_id: ...
  upstream_version: ...
  upstream_revision: ...
  retrieved_at: ...
  acquisition_method: ...
  artifact_digests: []
  parser_version: ...
  raw_storage_handle: ...

LicensePolicyRecord:
  subject_digest: exact artifact or path digest
  license_expression: SPDX expression when supported
  license_confidence: declared | detected | inherited | reviewed | unknown
  copyright_holders: []
  attribution_text: ...
  redistribution_allowed: true | false | unknown
  commercial_use_allowed: true | false | unknown
  modification_allowed: true | false | unknown
  training_use_reviewed: true | false
  descriptor_derivation_allowed: true | false | unknown
  execution_allowed: true | false | unknown
  upstream_terms_snapshot: ...
  takedown_policy: ...

ExtractionReceipt:
  input_digests: []
  extractor_build: ...
  configuration_digest: ...
  output_partition_digests: []
  warnings: []
  elapsed_and_resource_cost: {}
  deterministic_replay_command: ...

VerificationReceipt:
  artifact_digest: ...
  environment_digest: ...
  sandbox_policy_digest: ...
  test_or_probe_ids: []
  passed: []
  failed: []
  observed_effects: []
  resource_envelope: {}
  nondeterminism: {}
  verified_at: ...
```

### 3.2 Corpus-derived records

At minimum, sources can generate the following first-class records:

- `UsageObservation`
- `Package`, `PackageVersion`, `DistributionArtifact`
- `Repository`, `Revision`, `File`, `DocumentationUnit`
- `CodeEntity`, `Binding`, `Port`, `TypeSchema`
- `DependencyRequirement`, `ResolvedDependencyEdge`, `EnvironmentConstraint`
- `Capability`, `IntentPhrase`, `DomainConcept`, `ProtocolState`
- `PrimitiveCard`, `PrimitiveImplementation`, `PrimitiveVariant`
- `CompositionEdge`, `AdapterEdge`, `ConflictEdge`, `SupersessionEdge`
- `CallSite`, `ExampleInvocation`, `WorkflowRoute`, `CompositionRoute`
- `TestOracle`, `Property`, `Invariant`, `Metric`, `Validator`
- `FailureCase`, `Diagnostic`, `FixTransition`, `Counterexample`
- `BenchmarkTask`, `DemandIntent`, `ResourceBudget`, `EvaluationResult`
- `Vulnerability`, `AffectedRange`, `FixedRange`, `RiskObservation`
- `LicensePolicyRecord`, `Attestation`, `ExtractionReceipt`, `ExecutionReceipt`

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 4. PyPI: use popularity, but correct it

PyPI is the right first package ecosystem because Taedri already targets Python and because releases, artifacts, requirements, hashes, metadata, and download observations are available in structured form. It is not safe to equate download rank with human demand.

[PyPA's download-analysis guidance](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/guides/analyzing-pypi-package-downloads/) explicitly notes distortion from caches, mirrors, automation, download inflation, and transitive installation, and cautions that popularity is not quality. The public [`bigquery-public-data.pypi.file_downloads`](https://docs.pypi.org/api/bigquery/) table should therefore be one input to a rank, not the rank itself. The [PyPI JSON API](https://docs.pypi.org/api/json/) exposes artifact hashes, requirements, metadata and yanked state, but its embedded download counts are `-1` and must not be used as popularity observations.

### 4.1 Current scale signals

The PSF-hosted [PyPI Stats top-packages page](https://pypistats.org/top) and the reproducible [top-pypi-packages dataset](https://github.com/hugovk/top-pypi-packages) show the enormous installation footprint of infrastructure packages. A July 2026 30-day snapshot included approximately:

| Package             | Approximate 30-day downloads | Why the number needs interpretation                     |
|---------------------|-----------------------------:|---------------------------------------------------------|
| `boto3`             |                        3.58B | Direct use plus very large automated cloud/CI footprint |
| `packaging`         |                        2.10B | Deep transitive infrastructure dependency               |
| `urllib3`           |                        1.73B | Direct and transitive HTTP use                          |
| `requests`          |                        1.65B | Directly used API plus transitive use                   |
| `typing-extensions` |                        1.58B | Compatibility dependency across most typed Python       |
| `botocore`          |                        1.41B | Mostly generated AWS service substrate                  |
| `cryptography`      |                        1.35B | Security infrastructure and transitive dependency       |
| `numpy`             |                        1.09B | Direct scientific/data substrate                        |
| `pydantic`          |                        1.06B | Data contracts and modern web/agent stacks              |
| `pytest`            |                        1.02B | Test/dev dependency; high evidence yield                |
| `click`             |                        1.00B | Direct and transitive CLI framework                     |
| `litellm`           |                         633M | Provider abstraction; likely automation-heavy           |
| `fastapi`           |                         506M | Direct framework use                                    |
| `sqlalchemy`        |                         408M | Direct data-access and ORM use                          |
| `scikit-learn`      |                         220M | Direct ML/data-science use                              |

Human-use evidence helps counterbalance transitive infrastructure. The [PSF/JetBrains Python Developers Survey 2024](https://lp.jetbrains.com/python-developers-survey-2024/) reports substantial use of FastAPI, Django, Flask, Requests, pytest, pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, PyTorch, Transformers, and SQLAlchemy among applicable respondents. Taedri should track both machine download observations and human/repository import signals.

### 4.2 Reconstruct dependency centrality instead of buying a ranking

Build the versioned graph from normalized `Requires-Dist` records:

- separate runtime, build, test/dev, optional-extra, platform, and conditional requirements;
- count unique downstream projects and repositories, not release files or CI installs;
- compute direct reverse in-degree, compatible transitive reach, PageRank/Katz, articulation risk, and version-specific blast radius;
- evaluate marker and version edges for concrete Python/OS/architecture environments;
- track declared and actually resolved environments separately;
- distinguish distribution names, import namespaces, repositories, and generated-family identities;
- discount abandoned projects, duplicated stubs, and generated client families;
- retain historical centrality per API version.

The graph can be enriched with [deps.dev](https://docs.deps.dev/), which exposes cross-ecosystem package versions, requirements, dependency graphs, licenses, advisories, attestations, and source-project mappings, but Taedri should retain the raw evidence and calculate its own selection features.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 5. Recommended PyPI deep-ingest portfolio

The following families produce complementary records. Packages are candidates, not a permanent whitelist.

### 5.1 Packaging, resolution, and environment compatibility

**Candidates:** `packaging`, `pip`, `setuptools`, `wheel`, `build`, `hatchling`, `flit-core`, `poetry-core`, `virtualenv`, `importlib-metadata`, `importlib-resources`, `platformdirs`, `filelock`, `tomli`, `tomlkit`, `installer`, `resolvelib`.

**Primitive yield:**

- version and specifier parsers;
- environment marker predicates;
- normalized project names;
- wheel tag and ABI/platform compatibility;
- build-backend hook contracts;
- dependency resolution constraints and conflicts;
- entry-point and plugin discovery;
- editable-install and source/wheel distinctions;
- resolution failures and remediation routes.

**Why early:** these primitives can power Taedri's own package and environment compatibility solver.

### 5.2 Types, validation, serialization, and schemas

**Candidates:** `typing-extensions`, `attrs`, `pydantic`, `pydantic-core`, `annotated-types`, `jsonschema`, `referencing`, `marshmallow`, `cattrs`, `msgspec`, `protobuf`, `grpcio-tools`, `dataclasses-json`, `typeguard`, `beartype`.

**Primitive yield:**

- aliases, generics, protocols, type variables, overloads and variance;
- fields, defaults, factories, validators and computed fields;
- coercion versus strict-validation behavior;
- JSON Schema nodes, references, vocabularies and constraints;
- serializers/deserializers and round-trip properties;
- validation errors, paths, error codes and repair hints;
- Python type ↔ JSON/Protobuf representation edges.

### 5.3 HTTP, networking, async, streaming, and protocols

**Candidates:** `requests`, `urllib3`, `httpx`, `httpcore`, `aiohttp`, `anyio`, `trio`, `async-timeout`, `h11`, `h2`, `websockets`, `yarl`, `multidict`, `sniffio`, `tenacity`, `backoff`, `grpcio`.

**Primitive yield:**

- request/response ports and body encodings;
- URL/query/header/cookie/auth transformations;
- sync/async compatibility and adapters;
- client, transport, connection, pool and stream lifecycles;
- redirects, retries, timeouts, proxies, TLS and certificates;
- HTTP and WebSocket protocol states;
- exception taxonomies and retryability predicates;
- streaming and backpressure behavior.

### 5.4 Web applications, routes, middleware, and dependency injection

**Candidates:** `fastapi`, `starlette`, `uvicorn`, `django`, `djangorestframework`, `flask`, `werkzeug`, `jinja2`, `gunicorn`, `hypercorn`, `asgiref`, `channels`, `strawberry-graphql`, `graphene`, `ariadne`.

**Primitive yield:**

- method/path route cards;
- path, query, header, cookie and body schemas;
- dependency injection and provider graphs;
- middleware and exception-handler chains;
- ASGI/WSGI request lifecycles;
- status codes, response models and media types;
- authentication, permissions and policy gates;
- templates and server-rendering transformations;
- GraphQL types, resolvers and selection paths.

### 5.5 Databases, storage, transactions, and migrations

**Candidates:** `sqlalchemy`, `alembic`, `psycopg`, `psycopg2-binary`, `asyncpg`, `aiosqlite`, `redis`, `pymongo`, `motor`, `peewee`, `tortoise-orm`, `django` ORM, `duckdb`, `sqlite-utils`.

**Primitive yield:**

- engines, dialects, drivers, URLs and connection contracts;
- tables, models, columns, keys, constraints and relationships;
- query expression and result-shape transformations;
- sessions, transactions, isolation levels and savepoints;
- pools, concurrency limits and lifecycle requirements;
- migration operations, reversibility and schema diffs;
- database-specific capability and failure edges;
- sync/async and ORM/raw-query adapters.

### 5.6 Arrays, tables, science, statistics, and visualization

**Candidates:** `numpy`, `pandas`, `scipy`, `scikit-learn`, `pyarrow`, `polars`, `xarray`, `dask`, `fsspec`, `s3fs`, `joblib`, `numba`, `statsmodels`, `matplotlib`, `seaborn`, `plotly`, `pillow`, `openpyxl`.

**Primitive yield:**

- shape, dtype, axis, broadcasting and memory-layout contracts;
- labeled tabular schemas and column/index transformations;
- missing-value, timezone and categorical behavior;
- dense/sparse and CPU/GPU representation edges;
- `fit`, `transform`, `predict`, `score`, `partial_fit` protocols;
- feature transformers, estimators, metrics, splitters and pipelines;
- file-format readers/writers and schema preservation;
- plots, marks, encodings and render targets;
- numerical warnings, convergence conditions and tolerances.

### 5.7 Cloud and generated service clients

**Candidates:** `boto3`, `botocore`, `s3transfer`, `aiobotocore`, `google-auth`, `google-api-core`, `google-cloud-storage`, `azure-core`, `azure-identity`, representative generated clients, `kubernetes`.

**Primitive yield:**

- service operations and endpoint identities;
- request/response/error schemas;
- paginators, waiters and long-running operations;
- credentials, regions, scopes and identity chains;
- retry, quota and idempotency policies;
- generated exception hierarchies;
- sync/async and high-/low-level client projections.

**Critical rule:** ingest canonical service models before generated clients. For AWS, use [botocore service models](https://github.com/boto/botocore/tree/develop/botocore/data) as the shared operation substrate and link `boto3`, `botocore`, and `aiobotocore` methods as language/runtime projections. Apply the same pattern to Google discovery/protobuf models and Azure REST specifications.

### 5.8 Testing, evidence, property generation, and environments

**Candidates:** `pytest`, `pluggy`, `iniconfig`, `pytest-asyncio`, `pytest-cov`, `coverage`, `hypothesis`, `tox`, `nox`, `freezegun`, `responses`, `respx`, `factory-boy`, `faker`, `unittest-mock`.

**Primitive yield:**

- fixture dependency and scope graphs;
- hook specifications and implementations;
- parametrized examples and environment matrices;
- expected values, exceptions, warnings and side effects;
- property strategies, shrinkers and counterexamples;
- coverage observations and untested-path evidence;
- mocks, fakes, clocks and network-test adapters;
- executable verification routes.

**Why early:** tests create evidence for every other package family and can become independent `TestOracle` objects.

### 5.9 Developer tools, parsers, diagnostics, and transformations

**Candidates:** `ruff`, `mypy`, `pyright`-related Python clients, `black`, `isort`, `pre-commit`, `click`, `typer`, `rich`, `docutils`, `sphinx`, `mkdocs`, `libcst`, `astroid`, `tree-sitter`, `parso`, `jedi`.

**Primitive yield:**

- diagnostics with rule IDs, locations and messages;
- source-to-source transformations and autofixes;
- formatting and idempotence invariants;
- configuration schemas and precedence rules;
- CLI commands, options, environment variables and exit codes;
- AST/CST/query primitives and symbol resolution;
- documentation directives, roles and render trees.

### 5.10 Security, identity, cryptography, and policy

**Candidates:** `cryptography`, `cffi`, `pycparser`, `pyopenssl`, `certifi`, `bcrypt`, `pynacl`, `pyjwt`, `authlib`, `oauthlib`, `requests-oauthlib`, `passlib`, `itsdangerous`, `keyring`.

**Primitive yield:**

- key, algorithm, nonce, salt, mode and length constraints;
- hazardous-operation and misuse labels;
- certificate and trust-store operations;
- token claims, encoders, decoders and verification policies;
- OAuth/OIDC flows and state transitions;
- credential storage and provider selection;
- verification failures and remediation requirements.

### 5.11 AI, model, agent, and tool ecosystems

**Candidates:** `torch`, `transformers`, `huggingface-hub`, `tokenizers`, `safetensors`, `datasets`, `accelerate`, `openai`, `anthropic`, `litellm`, `langchain-core`, `llama-index-core`, `pydantic-ai-slim`, `mcp`, `sglang`, `vllm`, `sentence-transformers`.

**Primitive yield:**

- model/task registries and capability cards;
- tensor, tokenizer and batch-shape contracts;
- provider request/response schemas;
- streaming event discriminated unions;
- tool definitions, resources, prompts and transports;
- rate-limit, retry and context-window failures;
- agent/tool routes and provider adapters;
- embedding and reranking descriptors;
- quantization, device and resource compatibility.

### 5.12 Graphs, algorithms, matching, search, and reliability

**Candidates:** `networkx`, `igraph`, `rustworkx`, `sympy`, `sortedcontainers`, `rapidfuzz`, `xxhash`, `mmh3`, `datasketch`, `faiss-cpu`, `hnswlib`, `annoy`, `whoosh`, `rank-bm25`, `tenacity`, `joblib`.

**Primitive yield:**

- graph algorithms and transformation contracts;
- symbolic transformations and assumptions;
- sorted/indexed collection complexity;
- edit-distance and fuzzy-match metrics;
- hashes, MinHash, LSH, ANN, BM25 and reranking operations;
- retry/backoff/circuit predicates;
- parallel and cached execution contracts.

### 5.13 Cross-language and native-boundary stress packages

**Candidates:** `pydantic-core`, `ruff`, `uv`, `orjson`, `cryptography`, `tokenizers`, `grpcio`, `numpy`, `pyarrow`, `polars`, `duckdb`.

These deliberately exercise Rust/C/C++/Cython/FFI boundaries, wheels, ABI tags, opaque built-ins, generated bindings, platform variation, and behavior that a Python-only AST cannot see.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 6. Tiered PyPI acquisition plan

| Tier                     | Scope                                                            | Extraction depth                                                                                                                                          |
|--------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **S: anchor portfolio**  | 80–120 deliberately diverse packages                             | Current source/wheels, public docs/examples/tests/stubs, selected historical boundaries, runtime probes, full descriptors, routes, failures, verification |
| **A: ecosystem core**    | Top 500 by composite score                                       | Full public API and dependency extraction; latest secure release, previous major/minor boundary, common constrained version                               |
| **B: broad capability**  | Top 5,000 plus novelty-selected tail                             | Symbols, types, contracts, docs, selected tests, dependency/compatibility graphs; bodies and probes on demand                                             |
| **C: popular inventory** | Roughly top 15,000 qualified usage                               | Metadata, artifacts, hashes, exports, signatures, import/dependency graph, sparse/vector descriptors                                                      |
| **D: complete catalog**  | All PyPI releases                                                | Immutable metadata, requirements, artifact and source handles, license/provenance/risk, minimal symbol inventory                                          |
| **Historical/negative**  | Yanked, removed, vulnerable, incompatible and abandoned versions | Preserve as negative and migration evidence; nonselectable/nonexecutable by default                                                                       |

There is no permanent cap. These tiers control extraction spend and body materialization, not what Taedri may eventually understand.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 7. A structural stress-test ladder

Use package complexity as a deliberate sequence. Each rung should add a new extractor or graph challenge.

| Rung | Target                     | New challenge                                            | Exit condition                                              |
|-----:|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
|    0 | `usaddress`                | Small modules, model asset, CLI, tests                   | Deterministic cards and receipts reproduce exactly          |
|    1 | `requests`                 | Public API, sessions, adapters, HTTP errors              | Query→port→verified example works without source dump       |
|    2 | `packaging`                | Formal parsers and compatibility predicates              | Version/marker/tag route solver agrees with tests           |
|    3 | `pydantic`                 | Generated schemas, validators, Rust core                 | Python↔schema↔core projections remain one logical graph     |
|    4 | `pytest` + `pluggy`        | Dynamic plugins, fixtures, hooks, parametrization        | Fixture/hook graph and executable oracles resolve correctly |
|    5 | `SQLAlchemy`               | Fluent DSL, generics, dialects, transactions             | Query/result and transaction-state contracts are searchable |
|    6 | `botocore`/`boto3`         | Huge generated service surface                           | Canonical service model prevents projection duplication     |
|    7 | `pandas`                   | Large API, dtype/shape state, native core                | Schema/shape/effect descriptors improve task retrieval      |
|    8 | `Django`                   | Framework convention, settings, ORM, routing             | Cross-module framework declarations form composable routes  |
|    9 | `scikit-learn`             | Protocol families and estimator composition              | `fit/transform/predict` compatibility solved structurally   |
|   10 | `Apache Airflow`           | Providers, DAGs, operators, hooks, sensors               | Workflow graph and provider variants normalize correctly    |
|   11 | `PyTorch` + `Transformers` | Enormous dynamic API, devices, tensors, model registries | Progressive disclosure controls token and storage costs     |

Run a fixed task suite after every rung. The ladder is complete only when earlier accuracy and latency do not regress.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 8. Exact PyPI source-to-record map

| Source surface                          | Taedri records                                                                                                          |
|-----------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| PyPI `file_downloads`                   | `UsageObservation(package, version, artifact, time, installer, Python, OS, architecture)`                               |
| Immutable distribution metadata         | `PackageVersion`, `DependencyRequirement`, `Extra`, `EnvironmentMarker`, `PythonConstraint`, classifiers, project URLs  |
| JSON/Index APIs                         | `DistributionArtifact`, SHA-256/BLAKE2 digest, file type, wheel tags, upload time, yanked state/reason, metadata digest |
| Wheel `METADATA`, `WHEEL`, `RECORD`     | Artifact manifest, dependencies, hashes, ABI/platform compatibility, installed paths                                    |
| `entry_points.txt` and package metadata | CLI commands, plugin groups, load targets, import namespace projections                                                 |
| Source AST/CST and `.pyi`               | Modules, bindings, variables, functions, methods, classes, signatures, overloads, calls, imports, inheritance           |
| Docs and examples                       | Descriptions, recipes, positive examples, counterexamples, parameter semantics, warnings, deprecations                  |
| Tests                                   | Fixtures, input cases, expected values/exceptions/effects, properties, oracles, compatibility witnesses                 |
| Framework declarations                  | HTTP/CLI routes, schemas, ORM entities, task graphs, middleware, hooks and plugins                                      |
| Release diff                            | Added, removed, renamed, deprecated, superseded, behavior-changed, adapter and breaking edges                           |
| PyPI attestations                       | Artifact→publisher/workflow/repository/commit provenance                                                                |
| OSV                                     | Vulnerability, affected interval, fixed version, severity, references and remediation edges                             |
| Sandboxed probes                        | Imports, files, commands, network attempts, syscalls, output/exception observations, time/memory and nondeterminism     |

Use the [PyPI Simple Repository API](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/simple-repository-api/) and official [Index API](https://docs.pypi.org/api/index-api/) for discovery, the [Integrity API](https://docs.pypi.org/api/integrity/) and recorded hashes for validation, and [digital attestations](https://docs.pypi.org/attestations/) where present for publisher/build provenance.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 9. Generated-package and duplicate-family policy

Generated ecosystems can create millions of nearly identical entities and overwhelm lexical, vector, and graph retrieval unless Taedri distinguishes a canonical contract from its projections.

### 9.1 Canonicalization pattern

``` text
CanonicalServiceOrProtocolModel
  -> Operation / TypeSchema / Error / StateMachine
  -> GeneratedProjection(generator, language, runtime, version)
  -> PackageEntity(symbol, signature, implementation handle)
```

### 9.2 Families to collapse structurally

- AWS botocore service JSON → boto3, botocore, aiobotocore projections;
- Google Discovery, protobuf and GAPIC specs → `google-cloud-*` clients;
- Azure REST/OpenAPI specs → `azure-*` clients;
- Kubernetes OpenAPI models → generated API clients;
- `mypy-boto3-*` type-stub family;
- OpenTelemetry instrumentation/provider packages;
- LangChain and LlamaIndex integration packages;
- generated Protobuf/gRPC classes;
- vendored code, compatibility shims and backports;
- wheels whose compiled bodies differ by platform but whose public logical API is shared.

Content-deduplicate bodies by digest, structure-deduplicate generated schemas, but preserve every package artifact, version, namespace, ABI, provenance and compatibility record.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 10. Structured solution ecosystems: higher edge yield than raw code

Maintainers of integration and specification ecosystems already publish much of what Taedri would otherwise infer: names, descriptions, typed inputs, typed outputs, configuration schemas, dependencies, examples, compositions, tests, lifecycle status, and compatibility constraints.

### 10.1 Priority-zero structured sources

| Source                                                                                                  | What to ingest                                                                                              | Primitive and edge yield                                                                                      | Rights posture                                                                                        |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [Apache Camel Kamelets](https://github.com/apache/camel-kamelets)                                       | Kamelet YAML, JSON Schema properties, dependencies, route templates, examples, tests, verification metadata | Near-native source/sink/action `PrimitiveCard`; ports; media types; executable routes; verification           | Apache-2.0 repository                                                                                 |
| [APIs.guru OpenAPI Directory](https://github.com/APIs-guru/openapi-directory)                           | OpenAPI documents and origin metadata                                                                       | API→operation→request/response/auth/error/schema graph; examples and tags                                     | Contributions are CC0; preserve `x-origin` because some definitions were gathered from public sources |
| [SchemaStore](https://github.com/SchemaStore/schemastore)                                               | Catalog and JSON Schemas                                                                                    | Configuration types, properties, defaults, enums, constraints, deprecations, compatible documents             | Apache-2.0 repository                                                                                 |
| [Pulumi Registry](https://github.com/pulumi/registry)                                                   | Package schemas, resources/functions/types, examples                                                        | Inputs, outputs, secrets, replacement behavior and multi-language projections                                 | Registry code Apache-2.0; provider artifacts retain their licenses                                    |
| [Terraform Registry API](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/registry/api-docs)                   | Public module/provider metadata, versions, source links                                                     | Module inputs/outputs/resources/dependencies and version graph                                                | Metadata API; bodies have individual rights                                                           |
| [Exercism problem specifications](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications)                   | Canonical problem definitions and tests                                                                     | Behavioral contracts, scenarios, expected outcomes, stable test UUIDs and lineage                             | MIT; exclude private/user submissions                                                                 |
| [Official MCP Registry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/)                                      | Server records, packages, transports, arguments, environment and remotes                                    | Discoverable tool/server handles and declared capabilities                                                    | Registry metadata is neither security verification nor a body license                                 |
| [MeltanoHub](https://github.com/meltano/hub)                                                            | Plugin definitions, settings, capabilities and variants                                                     | Source/target ports, configuration, compatibility and route candidates                                        | Hub metadata Apache-2.0; implementations vary                                                         |
| [Airflow provider packages](https://airflow.apache.org/docs/apache-airflow-providers/packages-ref.html) | Provider metadata/docs/source, operators, sensors, hooks, triggers, examples                                | Workflow primitives, connection contracts and provider-specific variants                                      | Apache-2.0                                                                                            |
| [OpenTelemetry Collector Contrib](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib)    | Component metadata, config, tests and examples                                                              | Receivers, processors, connectors, exporters, extensions; signal and stability compatibility; pipeline routes | Apache-2.0                                                                                            |

### 10.2 Priority-one structured sources

| Source                                                                           | Taedri value                                                                                                | Caveat                                                                |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [Artifact Hub](https://artifacthub.io/docs/topics/repositories/)                 | One index spanning Helm, operators, Tekton, policies, containers, Krew, KEDA, Argo and other artifacts      | Each indexed artifact has its own license and execution risk          |
| [Airbyte](https://github.com/airbytehq/airbyte)                                  | Connector specs, catalogs, auth, cursors, incremental state, manifests, tests and source→destination routes | Mixed/custom licensing; decide per connector/path                     |
| [Apache Camel components](https://camel.apache.org/components/latest/)           | Hundreds of endpoints and Enterprise Integration Patterns with generated option metadata                    | Normalize component versions and runtime flavors                      |
| [Ansible Galaxy](https://galaxy.ansible.com/api/)                                | Collections, modules, roles, plugins, argument specs, playbooks and dependencies                            | Per-collection license                                                |
| [OperatorHub](https://operatorhub.io/)                                           | CRDs, owned/required APIs, RBAC, install modes, channels, dependencies and upgrades                         | Verify each operator's body rights                                    |
| [Node-RED Flow Library](https://flows.nodered.org/)                              | Node ports/configuration, npm dependencies, example flows and reusable subflows                             | Individual packages and contributed flows retain their licenses       |
| [dbt Package Hub](https://github.com/dbt-labs/hub.getdbt.com)                    | SQL macros/models/tests/adapters/variables and transformation DAGs                                          | Package licenses vary                                                 |
| [GitHub Actions starter workflows](https://github.com/actions/starter-workflows) | Workflow DAGs, triggers, jobs, matrices, conditions, permissions, inputs/outputs and calls                  | Starter repository is MIT; Marketplace actions are separate artifacts |
| [Home Assistant Core](https://github.com/home-assistant/core)                    | Integration manifests, services, devices, events, config flows, dependencies and quality metadata           | Large/dynamic; statically index before any integration execution      |

### 10.3 Discovery-only or permission-gated sources

| Source                                                | Useful information                                        | Default policy                                                |
|-------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| [n8n integrations](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/) | Actions, triggers, schemas and workflow patterns          | Catalog/descriptor only pending fair-code terms or permission |
| Postman Public API Network                            | Request collections, environments, examples and workflows | Metadata and links unless terms/owner rights authorize bodies |
| Zapier and Make catalogs                              | App/action/trigger concepts and compatibility demand      | Demand/category mining only                                   |
| Confluent Hub                                         | Connector capabilities and data-system compatibility      | Metadata by default; artifact-specific review                 |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 11. Service and protocol specifications

Specifications often provide the canonical entity that multiple client packages project.

| Source                                                                                      | Canonical records                                                  | Projection opportunities                        |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| [AWS botocore models](https://github.com/boto/botocore/tree/develop/botocore/data)          | Services, operations, shapes, errors, paginators, waiters, regions | boto3, botocore, aiobotocore, typed stubs       |
| [Azure REST API specifications](https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs)              | Resource providers, operations, schemas and API versions           | Azure SDKs across languages                     |
| [Google Discovery APIs](https://developers.google.com/discovery/v1/reference/apis)          | Services, resources, methods, parameters and schemas               | Google API clients across languages             |
| [Stripe OpenAPI](https://github.com/stripe/openapi)                                         | Operations, request/response objects, errors                       | Stripe SDK projections                          |
| [Kubernetes OpenAPI](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/api/openapi-spec) | Resources, versions, fields and validation                         | Python/Go/JavaScript clients, CRD compatibility |
| [Protocol Buffers](https://protobuf.dev/) and public IDLs                                   | Messages, services, RPCs, fields and evolution constraints         | Generated clients and servers                   |
| [AsyncAPI](https://www.asyncapi.com/docs/reference/specification/latest) documents          | Channels, messages, operations and bindings                        | Messaging clients, brokers, event routes        |
| [GraphQL introspection](https://spec.graphql.org/)                                          | Types, fields, arguments, directives and deprecations              | Client queries and resolver projections         |

These sources should create stable canonical IDs so a user query retrieves “the capability” before selecting a language/version-specific implementation.
