## 12. Package ecosystems beyond PyPI

PyPI proves the representation; these registries test the language-neutral kernel. Every artifact retains its own license and provenance.

| Ecosystem     | Authoritative acquisition surface                                              | Valuable language constructs                                                                 |
|---------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| npm           | [Registry API](https://github.com/npm/registry/blob/main/docs/REGISTRY-API.md) | TypeScript declarations, ESM/CJS exports, scripts, browser/server targets, peer dependencies |
| Rust          | [crates.io data access](https://crates.io/data-access)                         | Traits, lifetimes, features, `unsafe`, macros, target triples and semver                     |
| Maven Central | [REST API](https://central.sonatype.org/search/rest-api-guide/)                | classes/interfaces, annotations, generics, POM scopes, service providers, JVM bytecode       |
| Go            | [Module proxy protocol](https://go.dev/ref/mod#goproxy-protocol)               | modules, packages, interfaces, build tags, goroutines/channels, immutable source ZIPs        |
| NuGet         | [Server API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/api/overview)             | assemblies, namespaces, methods, attributes, target frameworks and nullable types            |
| RubyGems      | [RubyGems.org API](https://guides.rubygems.org/rubygems-org-api/)              | gems, modules/classes, mixins, dynamic methods and native extensions                         |
| Packagist     | [Packagist API](https://packagist.org/apidoc)                                  | Composer packages, PHP namespaces/interfaces/traits and platform requirements                |
| Conda         | repodata channels                                                              | build variants, native libraries, solver constraints and non-Python dependencies             |
| OCI           | registry/distribution APIs                                                     | content-addressed images, manifests, platforms, layers, entry points and SBOM links          |

[Software Heritage](https://www.softwareheritage.org/legal/content-policy/) is valuable as a content-addressed provenance/history layer using SWHIDs. It is an archive, not a blanket redistribution license.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 13. Code competitions, task corpora, and benchmarks

These sources contribute four different things:

1.  **Demand:** what people ask systems to build or repair.
2.  **Oracles:** tests, graders, metrics, validators, resource limits.
3.  **Solutions and failures:** accepted, rejected, inefficient and repaired implementations.
4.  **Evaluation:** sealed evidence of whether Taedri improves real outcomes.

Do not assume one source should serve all four purposes.

### 13.1 Recommended status vocabulary

| Status              | Meaning                                                                                 |
|---------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `INGEST`            | Eligible licensed content can enter descriptors, graphs, retrieval and body resolution  |
| `INGEST_TRAIN_ONLY` | Only an explicit train/public subset may be indexed; holdout remains sealed             |
| `DEMAND_ONLY`       | Extract intent, tags, constraints and aggregate outcomes; exclude solutions/gold bodies |
| `EVAL_ONLY`         | No task/gold/test content is visible to retrieval or generation during evaluation       |
| `REVIEW`            | Rights, terms, provenance, or contamination status must be resolved first               |

### 13.2 Coding and software-engineering sources

| Source                                                                                | Recommended status                                                          | Scale/shape                                                           | What Taedri can learn                                                                                     | Key caveat                                                                                                           |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [Exercism problem specifications](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications) | `INGEST`                                                                    | Cross-language concept/practice specifications with canonical tests   | Behavioral primitive cards, scenarios, properties, expected outputs, test lineage                         | Exclude private/user solution submissions unless separately licensed                                                 |
| [Project CodeNet](https://github.com/IBM/Project_CodeNet)                             | `REVIEW` then license-filtered `INGEST`                                     | About 14M code samples, thousands of problems, 50+ languages          | Equivalence, correct/incorrect contrast, performance labels, cross-language projections, repair/reranking | Repository code license does not automatically settle all original-submission rights; preserve provenance and review |
| [DeepMind CodeContests](https://github.com/google-deepmind/code_contests)             | `INGEST_TRAIN_ONLY`                                                         | Problems, tests, correct and incorrect solutions                      | Algorithmic capabilities, failure contrast, complexity/performance and cross-language routes              | Respect third-party material notices; seal evaluation split                                                          |
| [SWE-bench](https://github.com/SWE-bench/SWE-bench)                                   | Train split `INGEST_TRAIN_ONLY`; Verified/Multilingual holdouts `EVAL_ONLY` | Repository issue→patch→test tasks; Verified has 500 curated instances | Issue intent, code-context selection, fix transitions, test impact, environment reproduction              | Harness MIT; upstream repository files/patches keep upstream licenses; contamination is a major risk                 |
| [SWE-smith](https://github.com/SWE-bench/SWE-smith)                                   | Explicit train data `INGEST_TRAIN_ONLY`                                     | Scalable software-engineering tasks built from repositories           | Fault localization, mutation/fix pairs, test oracles and repair primitives                                | Hold out repository/time partitions; retain upstream licenses                                                        |
| [BigCodeBench](https://bigcode-bench.github.io/)                                      | Training-safe/public subset only; hard set `EVAL_ONLY`                      | 1,140 tasks involving 139 libraries and multi-library composition     | Library selection, multi-primitive composition, tests and tool-use demand                                 | Particularly prone to direct-answer and near-duplicate leakage                                                       |
| [DS-1000](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.11501)                                           | Primarily `EVAL_ONLY`; derived demand descriptors allowed                   | 1,000 realistic data-science problems over seven libraries            | NumPy/pandas/SciPy/sklearn/PyTorch/TensorFlow/Matplotlib usage and error patterns                         | Do not index gold solutions or hidden tests used for evaluation                                                      |
| [DS-bench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.15621)                                          | `EVAL_ONLY` with demand-only metadata                                       | 1,000 GitHub-derived data-science tasks across ten libraries          | Realistic package compositions and repository context                                                     | Newer benchmark; aggressively check corpus overlap                                                                   |
| [Defects4J](https://github.com/rjust/defects4j)                                       | Project/time-split `INGEST`; selected projects `EVAL_ONLY`                  | Reproducible Java bugs and tests                                      | Bug/fix/test graphs, fault localization and cross-language kernel validation                              | Avoid using the same defects for both retrieval and reporting                                                        |
| [CodeQL](https://github.com/github/codeql)                                            | `INGEST` for licensed queries/libraries/tests                               | Query suites, data-flow models, metadata and expected results         | Detection primitives, taint/data-flow edges, rule/test oracles                                            | CodeQL CLI is distributed separately under different terms                                                           |
| [Semgrep rules](https://github.com/semgrep/semgrep-rules)                             | `REVIEW`                                                                    | Patterns, metadata, messages, fixes and tests                         | Detection/fix primitive cards and language patterns                                                       | Semgrep Rules License is not a standard permissive OSS license                                                       |

### 13.3 Data-science and applied competitions

| Source                                                              | Recommended status                                                             | Primitive yield                                                                                             | Notes                                                                                                       |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [OpenAI MLE-bench](https://github.com/openai/mle-bench)             | Lite/selected competitions `EVAL_ONLY`; public metadata `DEMAND_ONLY`          | Dataset contracts, metrics, train/validation/test handling, resource-aware agent routes, submission graders | Covers 75 Kaggle competitions; Kaggle terms and competition-specific data licenses still govern acquisition |
| [OpenML benchmark suites](https://docs.openml.org/benchmark/)       | `INGEST` metadata/runs under applicable rights; frozen suites also `EVAL_ONLY` | Dataset/task/flow/run graph, splits, metrics, hyperparameters, reproducible results                         | Excellent structured baseline and compatibility source                                                      |
| [DrivenData competitions](https://www.drivendata.org/competitions/) | Licensed winning repositories `INGEST`; active/holdout tasks `EVAL_ONLY`       | Social-impact domains, data contracts, metrics, feature/model/ensemble routes and postmortems               | Check each challenge's dataset and solution license                                                         |
| [Zindi competitions](https://zindi.africa/competitions)             | `DEMAND_ONLY` or `EVAL_ONLY` by competition                                    | Regionally diverse applied ML tasks, metrics and constraints                                                | Competition-specific terms/data rights                                                                      |
| [AIcrowd challenges](https://www.aicrowd.com/challenges)            | `DEMAND_ONLY` or `EVAL_ONLY`                                                   | Agent/robotics/ML environments and graders                                                                  | Challenge-specific rules                                                                                    |
| [Codabench](https://www.codabench.org/) / Codalab bundles           | Public licensed bundles `INGEST`; active benchmarks `EVAL_ONLY`                | Reproducible tasks, ingestion/scoring programs, phases and leaderboards                                     | Bundle owners set licenses and visibility                                                                   |
| Kaggle competitions                                                 | Generally `DEMAND_ONLY`/`EVAL_ONLY` unless explicit rights                     | Enormous task, metric, notebook and solution diversity                                                      | Public visibility is not blanket redistribution/training permission                                         |

### 13.4 Agent, tool-use, and system benchmarks

These are disproportionately useful for testing Taedri's retrieval waterfall and composition engine, but they should usually be held out.

| Benchmark family                              | Default status | What it tests                                                              |
|-----------------------------------------------|----------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| SWE-bench Verified / Multilingual / PolyBench | `EVAL_ONLY`    | Repository navigation, issue repair, language and environment breadth      |
| Terminal-Bench                                | `EVAL_ONLY`    | Long-horizon terminal execution, environment manipulation and verification |
| BFCL                                          | `EVAL_ONLY`    | Function selection, argument construction and tool-call correctness        |
| tau-bench / tau3                              | `EVAL_ONLY`    | Stateful tool interaction, policies and multi-turn completion              |
| LiveMCPBench                                  | `EVAL_ONLY`    | Live Model Context Protocol discovery and tool use                         |
| BigCodeBench-Hard                             | `EVAL_ONLY`    | Difficult library composition and code execution                           |
| MLE-bench Lite                                | `EVAL_ONLY`    | End-to-end machine-learning engineering under compute/time constraints     |
| SWE-Skills-Bench                              | `EVAL_ONLY`    | Reusable skill/tool scaffolding for software tasks                         |

For each, Taedri may retain public identifiers and aggregate scores in the main database. Task bodies, hidden tests, gold traces and answer-derived embeddings belong to a physically and logically isolated evaluation store.

### 13.5 Records produced by competitions

A competition is not merely a prompt/answer pair. Normalize it into:

- `DemandIntent` and intent paraphrases;
- `DataContract` and dataset lineage;
- `InputSchema` / `OutputSchema` / `SubmissionSchema`;
- `MetricPrimitive` including direction, aggregation and tie rules;
- `SplitScheme` / `CrossValidationScheme` / temporal or group constraints;
- `ResourceBudget` and execution environment;
- `BaselineRoute` and `WinningRoute` when licensed;
- `FeaturePrimitive`, `ModelRecipe`, `TrainingPrimitive`, `EnsembleRoute`;
- `SubmissionValidator` and `TestOracle`;
- `FailureCase`, rejected result, diagnostic and repair edge;
- `PerformanceObservation` with hardware/software context;
- `LeaderboardObservation` separated from reproducible local verification;
- `ContaminationFingerprint` and partition status.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 14. Benchmark-contamination firewall

Maintain four physically distinguishable corpus partitions:

``` text
mining_and_training
validation_and_tuning
public_benchmark
sealed_cold_holdout
```

### 14.1 Mandatory controls

- Never ingest holdout gold solutions, patches, hidden tests or answer explanations into the entity/embedding/LSH indexes.
- Tag every task, file, code block, patch and test with corpus partition and source lineage.
- Calculate exact content digests, normalized-token MinHash, AST fingerprints, Winnowing fingerprints, identifier-normalized hashes and embeddings across all partitions.
- Detect train↔holdout overlap at file, function, snippet, problem-description, test and semantic-task levels.
- Split repository tasks by repository and time, not only random task ID.
- Record whether a public solution appeared before or after the evaluation cutoff.
- Disable network and general source search during controlled evaluations unless the benchmark explicitly allows them.
- Record every retrieved entity, resolved body and tool invocation in the evaluation receipt.
- Report clean, contaminated, and unknown-contamination subsets separately.
- Keep a never-tuned cold holdout for architectural decisions.

### 14.2 Similarity cascade for leakage detection

``` text
exact digest
  -> normalized exact digest
  -> token/Winnowing fingerprints
  -> MinHash / LSH candidate blocking
  -> AST/CFG/data-flow structural match
  -> embedding neighborhood
  -> expensive semantic adjudication only for ambiguous candidates
```

This is itself a useful Taedri retrieval-waterfall test.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 15. Repository, dependency, provenance, and evidence sources

These do not primarily contribute new primitives; they make other primitives traceable and selectable.

| Source                                                                 | Taedri use                                                                                                   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [GH Archive](https://www.gharchive.org/)                               | Time-stamped public GitHub events for adoption, issue/PR/fix and maintenance observations                    |
| [deps.dev](https://docs.deps.dev/)                                     | Cross-ecosystem package/version/dependency/license/advisory/source mapping                                   |
| [ecosyste.ms](https://ecosyste.ms/)                                    | Broad repository/package/dependency/issue/PR indexes and services; respect CC BY-SA data and AGPL code terms |
| [Software Heritage](https://www.softwareheritage.org/)                 | Content-addressed source history and SWHIDs; provenance pointer, not blanket licensing                       |
| [OSV](https://google.github.io/osv.dev/)                               | Version/commit vulnerability queries and affected/fixed ranges                                               |
| [OpenSSF Scorecard](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard)                 | Heuristic project-practice observations; evidence, not an absolute trust verdict                             |
| [OpenSSF Criticality Score](https://github.com/ossf/criticality_score) | Activity/dependency-oriented prioritization features; Taedri should still calculate its own package graph    |
| [OpenSSF Package Analysis](https://github.com/ossf/package-analysis)   | Static/dynamic package behavior and gVisor observations; model for sandbox probes                            |
| [OpenSSF Package Feeds](https://github.com/ossf/package-feeds)         | Standardized PyPI/npm/RubyGems release-update events                                                         |
| [Typeshed](https://github.com/python/typeshed)                         | Versioned third-party and standard-library type contracts; external evidence distinct from implementation    |
| [The Stack v2](https://huggingface.co/datasets/bigcode/the-stack-v2)   | Enormous discovery/provenance corpus with SWHIDs and license metadata                                        |

The Stack v2 contains billions of files and hundreds of languages, but it should be used as a discovery/history layer only under its provenance, opt-out/removal, Software Heritage access, and source-license obligations—not as a blind body import.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 16. Rules, policies, workflows, and executable patterns

These are valuable because they encode conditions and expected effects explicitly.

| Source                                                                                                       | Records                                                                                                               |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [GitHub Action metadata](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/metadata-syntax) | Actions, inputs, outputs, runtime, entry point and branding; workflows add triggers/jobs/steps/conditions/permissions |
| [Gatekeeper Library](https://github.com/open-policy-agent/gatekeeper-library)                                | Constraint templates, Rego policy, parameters, violations and tests                                                   |
| [Kyverno Policies](https://github.com/kyverno/policies)                                                      | Match conditions, validation/mutation/generation behavior, policies and tests                                         |
| [CodeQL](https://github.com/github/codeql)                                                                   | Query metadata, language libraries, data-flow paths, detections and expected-result tests                             |
| SARIF-producing rule collections                                                                             | Stable rule IDs, locations, severities, code flows, fixes and tool metadata                                           |
| CI workflow corpora                                                                                          | Environment matrices, build/test/deploy routes, cache keys and failure transitions                                    |
| Infrastructure examples                                                                                      | Resource graphs, desired state, providers, diffs and apply/destroy lifecycle                                          |

Policy and security rules should preserve “detects,” “requires,” “forbids,” “mutates,” and “verifies” as different primitive capabilities.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 17. What not to ingest naïvely

### 17.1 Common traps

- **Top-download-only selection:** overweights transitive plumbing, bots and generated SDKs.
- **One logical entity per symbol spelling:** conflates versions, overloads, projections, aliases and namespace collisions.
- **One license per project:** source, wheel, docs, tests, examples, datasets and generated specs may differ.
- **Repository license applied to submissions:** competition or user-submitted code may have separate rights.
- **Public API catalog treated as executable:** schemas and manifests do not prove server safety or correctness.
- **Archived body treated as redistributable:** Software Heritage preservation is not a universal license grant.
- **Generated clients expanded before schemas:** creates enormous duplicate descriptor and edge noise.
- **Tests treated as implementation detail:** discards Taedri's best source of independent behavior evidence.
- **Benchmark answers indexed with training data:** invalidates measured improvements.
- **Package import during indexing:** allows install/import-time code to run before review.
- **Single latest-version graph:** erases real compatibility, migration and historical failure evidence.
- **JSONL or SQLite as the final bulk fact plane:** does not match tens of millions of entities and large descriptor bodies.

### 17.2 Physical storage recommendation

- content-addressed object storage for raw artifacts and resolved bodies;
- compressed Parquet/Iceberg/Delta-like fact partitions for bulk immutable extraction output;
- PostgreSQL for governance, identities, jobs, policy, receipts and transactional state;
- fit-for-purpose lexical/vector/graph indexes derived from the fact plane;
- a hot entity/card cache for progressive disclosure;
- append-only evidence and evaluation logs;
- no unconditional duplication of full bodies into every index.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 18. Ingestion pipeline

``` text
discover
  -> snapshot and hash
  -> determine rights/policy lane
  -> static unpack (never import/setup.py)
  -> parse native schemas, metadata, AST/CST, stubs, docs, examples and tests
  -> establish canonical identities and generated-family projections
  -> emit typed fact partitions and receipts
  -> exact/lexical/fingerprint/embedding indexes
  -> compatibility and composition-edge derivation
  -> cheap deterministic verification
  -> isolated sandbox probes when justified
  -> independent oracle verification
  -> publish selectable cards and route handles
  -> measure marginal yield and schedule next extraction depth
```

### 18.1 Static extraction first

For packages:

- download and verify wheel/sdist digest;
- never execute `setup.py`, build hooks or package imports during ordinary indexing;
- inspect archives, metadata, source, stubs, docs and tests as data;
- identify native extensions and opaque/generated regions;
- resolve dependencies without installing when possible;
- queue behavioral work only after rights, provenance and risk gates.

### 18.2 Dynamic verification later

When behavior is worth the cost:

- build a pinned, disposable environment;
- deny network by default;
- use read-only source/artifact mounts and an ephemeral writable layer;
- cap CPU, memory, processes, files, time and output;
- capture file, command, network-attempt, syscall, import, exception and resource observations;
- distinguish documented, statically inferred, experimentally observed and independently verified claims;
- publish exact receipts tied to artifact and environment digests.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 19. Adaptive acquisition scheduler

The scheduler should choose both **which source** and **which extraction depth** to run next.

### 19.1 Candidate actions

``` text
catalog(package/version)
extract_symbols(package/version)
extract_types_and_contracts(package/version)
extract_docs_examples_tests(package/version)
derive_composition_edges(package/version)
diff_versions(package, from, to)
run_sandbox_probe(entity_or_package)
verify_route(route_id)
ingest_structured_catalog(source, shard)
refresh_usage_or_risk_observations(source)
```

### 19.2 Reward

``` text
reward =
    newly_answered_demand_weight
  + verified_new_capabilities
  + verified_new_composition_edges
  + retrieval_recall_gain
  + route_success_gain
  + verifier_discrimination_gain
  - compute_and_storage_cost
  - duplicate_yield
  - unresolved_rights_or_security_risk
```

Use a contextual bandit initially. Context features include package family, graph centrality, task demand, missing descriptor channels, previous extractor yield, source update cadence, and current retrieval failure clusters. Preserve a deterministic exploration budget so long-tail domains are not starved.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 20. Concrete first vertical slice

The best first multi-source experiment is not enormous:

### 20.1 Inputs

- 12 PyPI anchor packages: `packaging`, `requests`, `pydantic`, `fastapi`, `sqlalchemy`, `pytest`, `hypothesis`, `numpy`, `scikit-learn`, `botocore`, `networkx`, `cryptography`;
- 100–500 artifacts each from Camel Kamelets, APIs.guru, SchemaStore, Exercism specifications and the official MCP Registry;
- PyPI metadata/dependency inventory for all packages, without deep bodies;
- a sealed task suite drawn from unused packages and benchmark subsets.

### 20.2 Normalize all sources into the same kernel

``` text
PrimitiveCard
Port
TypeSchema
Capability
CompositionEdge
EnvironmentConstraint
ExampleInvocation
TestOracle
FailureCase
ProvenanceRecord
LicensePolicyRecord
ExtractionReceipt
VerificationReceipt
```

### 20.3 Experiments

1.  Compare deterministic fielded retrieval, BM25, LSH, embeddings and graph-route retrieval by entity family.
2.  Test route handles with 1, 2, 4 and 8 alternatives at progressively disclosed detail levels.
3.  Measure whether schema/spec-native cards outperform LLM-generated package summaries.
4.  Measure whether test-derived edges predict real composability better than doc co-occurrence.
5.  Compare raw generated-client entities with canonical service-model projections.
6.  Hold model quality constant and measure prompt/input token reduction from body resolution after selection.
7.  Let the adaptive scheduler choose the next deep package; compare with download-rank and random baselines.
8.  Attempt cross-source composition, such as SchemaStore config → package constructor or OpenAPI operation → Pydantic model → HTTP client.
9.  Run contamination detection against the sealed suite before every evaluation.
10. Require exact source, extraction, selection, body-resolution, execution and verification receipts for every claimed success.

### 20.4 Success gates

| Gate                            | Initial target                                            |
|---------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| Entity identity reproducibility | 100% stable for unchanged artifact/parser                 |
| Artifact and fact provenance    | 100% of selectable records trace to digest and source     |
| License/policy coverage         | 100% before body exposure or execution                    |
| Public API recall               | ≥95% on manually sampled anchor-package surfaces          |
| Signature/port accuracy         | ≥98% on statically available contracts                    |
| Retrieval recall@20             | Improve over BM25-only and embedding-only baselines       |
| Route executable success        | Statistically higher than untyped/vector-only composition |
| Unsupported-edge rate           | Monotonically decline with verification feedback          |
| Token cost/task                 | Material reduction versus whole-doc/source prompting      |
| Cold-holdout quality            | Improvement without detected exact/near/semantic leakage  |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 21. Build backlog

### Phase 0 — source governance and reproducibility

- Define `SourceCandidate`, `SourceSnapshot`, `LicensePolicyRecord`, corpus partition and receipts.
- Add artifact/path-level rights rather than project-level-only license.
- Implement content-addressed raw artifact storage.
- Implement deterministic extractor version/configuration identities.
- Create benchmark isolation and contamination fingerprinting before importing benchmark-derived material.

### Phase 1 — PyPI catalog and ranking plane

- Ingest immutable PyPI distribution metadata and artifact digests.
- Build normalized distribution/version/artifact/requirement/environment records.
- Reconstruct version-aware runtime/build/extra dependency graphs.
- Load qualified download observations and aggregate by useful environment dimensions.
- Add direct-import and repository-use evidence where legally/operationally available.
- Calculate centrality, blast radius and generated-family redundancy.
- Produce a reproducible Tier-S/Tier-A candidate report.

### Phase 2 — static deep extractor

- Unpack wheels/sdists without execution.
- Parse Python AST/CST, `.pyi`, metadata, entry points, docs/examples/tests.
- Resolve exports, aliases, overloads, decorators, class members and inheritance.
- Emit facts to compressed columnar partitions.
- Produce deterministic entity IDs and extraction receipts.
- Add opaque/native/generated-region records instead of silently dropping them.

### Phase 3 — structured ecosystem adapters

- Implement a generic JSON Schema/OpenAPI/AsyncAPI normalizer.
- Add Kamelets, APIs.guru, SchemaStore, Exercism and MCP Registry connectors.
- Add canonical contract→implementation projection edges.
- Derive ports, capabilities, dependencies, examples, tests and route templates.
- Benchmark verified edge yield per CPU-hour and per stored byte against raw-code extraction.

### Phase 4 — evidence and execution

- Convert tests into independent `TestOracle` and `ExampleInvocation` records.
- Add pinned environment builder and network-denied sandbox.
- Capture effects, failures, resource behavior and nondeterminism.
- Add verifier independence checks so the same inferred claim is not its own oracle.
- Publish `ExecutablePrimitive` only after policy and verification gates.

### Phase 5 — competitions and demand graph

- Add competition/task/metric/split/resource schemas.
- Ingest Exercism specifications and explicitly licensed training subsets.
- Add OpenML task/flow/run records.
- Mine demand descriptors from competition catalogs without importing answers.
- Build sealed evaluation store and access audit.
- Implement exact, token, AST, LSH and semantic contamination tests.

### Phase 6 — adaptive scheduler and scale

- Estimate marginal capability/edge/oracle yield before deep extraction.
- Train the scheduler on observed yield and downstream task gain.
- Add generated-family canonicalization for AWS, Google, Azure, Kubernetes and protobuf.
- Expand across npm/crates/Maven/Go/NuGet using the same language-neutral kernel.
- Move bulk facts and descriptor matrices to partitioned columnar storage; retain governance in PostgreSQL.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 22. High-value research experiments

1.  **Popularity correction:** predict direct human imports from downloads, reverse dependencies, surveys and repository samples; quantify transitive-install bias.
2.  **Marginal package selection:** compare submodular portfolio selection with top-download, centrality-only and random selection.
3.  **Edge-yield economics:** facts and verified edges per CPU-hour for raw Python, type stubs, docs, tests, OpenAPI, Kamelets and workflows.
4.  **Oracle hierarchy:** compare docs, examples, unit tests, property tests, integration tests and sandbox probes as predictors of route success.
5.  **Canonicalization:** measure storage, candidate duplication and retrieval error before/after service-model projection collapse.
6.  **Descriptor ablation:** exact names, signatures, types, keywords, sparse lexical, MinHash/LSH, embeddings, graph neighborhoods and behavioral fingerprints.
7.  **Version-aware retrieval:** whether environment-filtered candidates reduce invalid code generation more than extra model reasoning.
8.  **Progressive disclosure:** entity count, edge count and detail level per model call at 1/2/4/8 alternatives.
9.  **Failure-as-primitive:** whether indexed exceptions, rejected submissions and bug fixes improve repair and prevention.
10. **Cross-source composition:** structured spec primitive with raw package primitive, such as OpenAPI→Pydantic→HTTPX.
11. **Cold-start scheduler:** hand weights versus contextual bandit versus Bayesian experimental design.
12. **Long-tail exploration:** fixed exploration budget versus pure marginal-yield exploitation.
13. **Test-derived compatibility:** infer producer/consumer edges from fixtures and parametrization; validate independently.
14. **Call-site evidence:** compare documentation co-occurrence with repository call-site data for argument and route prediction.
15. **Graph-negative evidence:** explicit incompatible/conflicting/deprecated edges versus positive-only graphs.
16. **Body-on-selection:** retrieval quality and token spend when bodies resolve only after card/route selection.
17. **Local-SLM descriptors:** compare deterministic extraction, local SLM, small hosted model and frontier model only on unresolved fields.
18. **Contamination cascade:** accuracy/cost of exact→LSH→AST→embedding→semantic leakage adjudication.
19. **Executable verification value:** task gain per sandbox dollar and which entity families justify probes.
20. **Cross-language kernel:** represent one OpenAPI/protobuf service across Python, TypeScript, Go, Java and Rust without losing language-specific constraints.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 23. Recommended first decisions

1.  **Adopt the source-policy lanes now.** Retrofitting evaluation isolation and artifact-level rights after corpus growth is much harder.
2.  **Build the all-PyPI metadata graph before all-PyPI deep extraction.** It is cheap context for prioritizing expensive work.
3.  **Use a diverse 80–120 package Tier-S, not a top-download list.** Include structural stress cases and high-oracle packages.
4.  **Add Camel Kamelets, APIs.guru, SchemaStore, Exercism and MCP Registry beside PyPI.** This tests whether one kernel handles integrations, APIs, configs, behavior and tools.
5.  **Canonicalize specifications before generated clients.** This prevents duplicate entities from dominating search.
6.  **Treat tests as first-class primitives and evidence.** They should create oracles, examples, failure edges and compatibility witnesses.
7.  **Make benchmark isolation a system invariant.** Sealed tasks must be invisible to every retriever, embedding index and agent tool.
8.  **Let measured marginal yield choose expansion.** Downloads, centrality and human demand seed the scheduler; verified downstream gain updates it.
9.  **Keep bulk bodies out of prompts and hot transactional tables.** Resolve them only after a compact card or route is selected.
10. **Publish receipts for every stage.** A Taedri result should say exactly which artifact, entity, descriptor, route, body, environment and oracle produced it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

If the team can start only ten acquisition tracks, use:

1.  all-PyPI release/dependency metadata;
2.  Tier-S PyPI anchor packages;
3.  Apache Camel Kamelets;
4.  APIs.guru OpenAPI Directory;

This shortlist covers adoption, compatibility, structured primitives, composition, behavioral oracles, applied demand, provenance/risk, generated-client canonicalization and uncontaminated evaluation.

### 25.6 Evidence weighting

When the same route appears in multiple sources, weight it by:

``` text
reproduced independent tests
  > deterministic local grader
  > hidden external grader
  > public leaderboard observation
  > repository test claim without reproduction
  > author prose or community discussion
```

Preserve all layers. A weaker observation may explain intent or failure even when it cannot verify behavior.

## 26. Workflow and orchestration packages to add to the PyPI portfolio

This family deserves its own anchor cohort because it directly teaches Taedri how primitives are composed, scheduled, retried and observed.

**Candidates:** `apache-airflow`, `prefect`, `dagster`, `celery`, `ray`, `dask`, `luigi`, `temporalio`, `kedro`, `dbt-core`, `mlflow`, `optuna`, `hydra-core`, `omegaconf`, `apscheduler`, `rq`, `dramatiq`, `langgraph`, `pydantic-ai`, `litellm`.

**Primitive and edge yield:**

- tasks/activities/assets/ops/jobs/flows and their typed ports;
- DAG, dynamic-map, fan-out/fan-in and conditional edges;
- schedule, event, sensor and trigger contracts;
- queue, worker, executor, pool and resource constraints;
- retry, timeout, cancellation, idempotency and compensation policies;
- checkpoint, result, artifact and cache semantics;
- workflow state machines and failure recovery;
- secrets, connections, deployment environments and permissions;
- telemetry, lineage and execution receipts;
- local/distributed and sync/async compatibility;
- agent/model/tool routing and fallback policies.

Prefer framework-declared graphs and serialized manifests over reconstructing every route from generic calls. Keep runtime execution disabled until task/operator implementations and their dependencies pass policy gates.

## 27. Master source-to-primitive mapping

| Source class                      | Best authoritative signals                       | Primary graph objects                            | Unique value                            |
|-----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| Package registry                  | releases, artifacts, hashes, requirements, usage | packages, versions, dependencies, environments   | adoption and compatibility universe     |
| Package source/stubs              | syntax, types, exports, implementations          | code entities, ports, calls, inheritance         | fine-grained callable inventory         |
| Documentation                     | intent, semantics, warnings, examples            | descriptions, capabilities, recipes, constraints | human-facing meaning                    |
| Tests/property suites             | inputs, expected output/effects/errors           | oracles, examples, invariants, negative edges    | executable behavioral evidence          |
| OpenAPI/IDL/schema                | canonical typed contracts                        | operations, messages, types, auth, error ports   | cheap and precise compatibility         |
| Integration catalog               | declared capabilities and compositions           | primitives, routes, configs and dependencies     | dense producer→consumer graph           |
| Workflow corpus                   | explicit control and data flow                   | DAGs, conditions, retries and state              | multi-primitive composition patterns    |
| Call-site corpus                  | observed imports, arguments and sequences        | use edges, co-call routes, argument shapes       | real-world usage evidence               |
| Issue/patch history               | intent, changed context and tests                | failure, diagnostic, fix and migration edges     | repair knowledge                        |
| Accepted/rejected submissions     | behavioral equivalence and outcomes              | equivalence sets, negative edges, performance    | contrastive and cross-language evidence |
| Competition definition            | task, data, metrics and budgets                  | DemandIR, validators, resource constraints       | real-world problem distribution         |
| Benchmark                         | task, sealed oracle and result                   | evaluation manifests and receipts                | unbiased progress measurement           |
| Vulnerability/supply-chain source | affected versions and provenance                 | risks, attestations, remediation edges           | safe selection and execution            |
| Runtime sandbox                   | observed behavior and resources                  | effects, failures, performance, nondeterminism   | closes static-inference gaps            |

No source is “ground truth” for every field. Each field on a card should retain its evidence origin and confidence so contradictory claims can coexist until adjudicated.

## 28. Concrete 14/30/90-day plan

### Days 1–14: prove the common kernel

- Freeze the source registry, artifact-level rights, policy lanes and corpus partitions.
- Implement deterministic source snapshot, digest and receipt generation.
- Ingest all-PyPI package/version/artifact/requirement metadata into the governance and columnar fact planes.
- Deep-extract `usaddress`, `packaging`, `requests`, `pydantic` and `pytest` without importing them.
- Build one generic JSON Schema/OpenAPI normalizer.
- Ingest 100 Kamelets, 100 APIs.guru documents, 100 SchemaStore schemas and 100 Exercism specifications.
- Create a 100-task cold suite from packages/sources not present in the deep cohort.
- Establish BM25, embedding and typed-route baselines with exact receipts.

**Day-14 proof:** one query can retrieve a compact capability card, solve compatible ports, resolve only the selected body, execute under policy where permitted, verify with an independent oracle and emit a replayable receipt.

### Days 15–30: prove portfolio selection and composition

- Calculate qualified usage, reverse dependencies and compatible centrality for PyPI.
- Select the first 80–120 Tier-S packages by submodular capability coverage.
- Add test/example→oracle extraction and package version diffs.
- Add canonical AWS service-model→Python client projections.
- Add structured cross-source routes: config→constructor, schema→validator, API operation→HTTP client, dataset→estimator→metric.
- Run route-handle 1/2/4/8 and detail-level experiments.
- Add exact/token/AST/MinHash/embedding contamination scans.
- Seal SWE-Skills-Bench, BigCodeBench-Hard, DS-1000 and a repository-repair subset as evaluation-only.

**Day-30 proof:** Taedri outperforms BM25-only and embedding-only retrieval on verified success per token, and canonicalization reduces duplicate candidates without reducing recall.

### Days 31–90: prove adaptive scale

- Expand static public-API extraction to Tier A and metadata/minimal inventory to all PyPI.
- Add OpenML, DrivenData licensed winners, CodeSearchNet license-filtered train data and SWE-smith train partitions.
- Add a network-denied behavioral sandbox and OpenSSF/OSV risk observations.
- Train a contextual acquisition scheduler from measured fact/edge/oracle yield and downstream task gain.
- Add Camel components, Airflow providers, OpenTelemetry Collector, MeltanoHub and Home Assistant adapters.
- Move bulk immutable facts and descriptor matrices to compressed partitioned storage; keep transactional governance in PostgreSQL.
- Add one second-language registry and extractor—npm/TypeScript or crates.io/Rust are the strongest contrast tests.
- Publish clean, contaminated and unknown-overlap evaluation strata.

**Day-90 proof:** the scheduler selects the next extraction action more efficiently than download rank, the system supports millions of entity records without body duplication, and sealed multi-domain evaluations show a real cost/quality frontier improvement.

## 29. Why the esoteric capability tail matters

The previous sections deliberately begin with central packages and structured ecosystems. The next expansion should mine the **narrow capability tail**: packages and templates that solve one awkward, reusable problem extremely well.

Examples include:

- repair mojibake without translating or paraphrasing text;
- infer a malformed CSV dialect;
- normalize international phone, IBAN, postal-address or measurement strings;
- block and probabilistically link duplicate records;
- compare nested JSON while ignoring order or selected paths;
- identify mislabeled examples or bad annotators;
- convert an estimator to ONNX or generated native code;
- enforce a grammar during token generation;
- identify image color-space, alpha, EXIF-orientation or compression defects;
- detect video cuts, frozen frames, timestamp discontinuities or subtitle drift;
- instantiate a queue worker with retries, idempotency, dead-letter routing and event-driven autoscaling;
- generate a complete application skeleton with build, test and deployment proofs.

These tend to have better black-box boundaries than large frameworks. A narrow library can often be represented as a small collection of typed transforms and verifiers instead of thousands of loosely related symbols.

### 29.1 Compile sources into registry-native capsules

Packages, repositories and templates are **acquisition sources**, not the default deployment unit. Taedri should compile their reusable knowledge into registry-native capsules:

``` text
upstream package/repository/template
  -> canonical source snapshot
  -> functions/classes/specs/examples/tests
  -> capability-level PrimitiveCards and RouteCards
  -> implementation/body handles back to the exact artifact
  -> compatibility, evidence, license and verification records
```

One package may generate hundreds of capsules; one capsule may have implementations from many packages. This avoids one-repository-per-primitive sprawl and makes replacements, fallbacks and version-aware selection natural.

### 29.2 Long-tail selection objective

Let each candidate source (p) cover a vector of capabilities, formats, effects, environments and failure modes (x_p). Select a portfolio (S) by maximizing:

``` text
F(S) = Σ_d w_d · min(1, Σ_{p∈S} coverage[p,d])
     + λ · log det(K_S + εI)
     + μ · verified_edge_yield(S)
     + ν · oracle_yield(S)
     - α · extraction_cost(S)
     - β · duplicate_projection_cost(S)
     - γ · unresolved_rights_or_execution_risk(S)
```

The weighted saturation term rewards demand coverage; the log-determinant diversity term favors nonredundant sources; verified-edge and oracle terms favor composability and falsifiability. This is superior to maximizing package count, symbol count or downloads.

### 29.3 Discovery signals for obscure but valuable packages

- unusually high direct-import frequency relative to downloads;
- high co-import lift with an anchor package;
- frequent appearance in winning notebooks or reproducible pipelines;
- high reverse-dependency centrality inside a narrow domain cluster;
- many tests/examples per public symbol;
- a formal schema, plugin registry or estimator protocol;
- distinctive file-format, codec, standard or jurisdiction coverage;
- frequent “small custom helper” code that a package already replaces;
- high issue frequency for a task but few competing packages;
- a native executable or cross-language library hidden behind a thin Python adapter;
- deterministic behavior suitable for cheap verification;
- a small API surface with large token-saving potential;
- capability coverage absent from the current primitive basis.

Use PyPI, conda-forge feedstocks, dependency graphs, lockfiles, notebook imports, container SBOMs, GitHub code search, OpenML flows and curated lists as **discovery evidence**. None alone establishes quality or body-ingestion rights.

### 30.3 Time-series, forecasting and temporal structure

| Family                      | Candidates                                                                                                                                                                                               | Capsule yield                                                                                    |
|-----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| protocol and classical      | [sktime](https://github.com/sktime/sktime), [StatsForecast](https://github.com/Nixtla/statsforecast), [statsmodels](https://github.com/statsmodels/statsmodels)                                          | forecaster/transformer/detector protocols, statistical models, prediction intervals, backtesting |
| ML/deep forecasting         | [MLForecast](https://github.com/Nixtla/mlforecast), [NeuralForecast](https://github.com/Nixtla/neuralforecast), [Darts](https://github.com/unit8co/darts), [GluonTS](https://github.com/awslabs/gluonts) | lag/rolling features, covariates, probabilistic forecasts, global/local models, ensembles        |
| hierarchical/reconciliation | [HierarchicalForecast](https://github.com/Nixtla/hierarchicalforecast)                                                                                                                                   | summing matrices, reconciliation methods and coherent forecast constraints                       |
| anomaly/change              | STUMPY, ruptures, ADTK, [Merlion](https://github.com/salesforce/Merlion)                                                                                                                                 | anomaly scores, change points, transforms and ensembles                                          |
| decomposition/spectral      | statsmodels, [PyWavelets](https://github.com/PyWavelets/pywt), [ssqueezepy](https://github.com/OverLordGoldDragon/ssqueezepy)                                                                            | seasonal/trend decomposition, wavelets, time-frequency transforms                                |
| interval/event evaluation   | sktime metrics, [portion](https://github.com/AlexandreDecan/portion)                                                                                                                                     | interval algebra, temporal overlap and event metrics                                             |

Every temporal card needs frequency, timezone, regularity, horizon, context length, covariate availability, leakage boundary, probabilistic output type and missing-time policy.

### 30.4 Weak supervision, active learning and annotation

| Candidates                                                                                                          | Primitive yield                                                                                      |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [Snorkel](https://github.com/snorkel-team/snorkel)                                                                  | labeling functions, coverage/conflict/overlap analysis, generative label model and slicing functions |
| [skweak](https://github.com/NorskRegnesentral/skweak)                                                               | weak supervision for sequence labeling and NER                                                       |
| [modAL](https://github.com/modAL-python/modAL) and [small-text](https://github.com/webis-de/small-text)             | query strategies, uncertainty/diversity selection and active-learning loops                          |
| [Cleanlab](https://github.com/cleanlab/cleanlab)                                                                    | multi-annotator consensus, annotator quality and active relabeling                                   |
| [Label Studio SDK](https://github.com/HumanSignal/label-studio-sdk) and [CVAT SDK](https://github.com/cvat-ai/cvat) | task/project/annotation schemas, import/export adapters and human-review routes                      |
| [FiftyOne](https://github.com/voxel51/fiftyone)                                                                     | sample/label schemas, dataset views, evaluation, error analysis and curation                         |

Useful edges include `labels`, `abstains_on`, `conflicts_with`, `subsumes`, `requires_annotation_type`, `selects_next`, `exports_to_format`, and `verified_by_consensus`.

### 30.5 Probabilistic programming, causal inference and uncertainty

| Family                             | Candidates                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Primitive yield                                                                                                 |
|------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Bayesian modeling                  | [PyMC](https://github.com/pymc-devs/pymc), [NumPyro](https://github.com/pyro-ppl/numpyro), [Pyro](https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro), [Bambi](https://github.com/bambinos/bambi)                                                       | distributions, priors, likelihoods, models, samplers, variational inference and posterior prediction            |
| posterior diagnostics              | [ArviZ](https://github.com/arviz-devs/arviz)                                                                                                                                                                                          | inference-data schema, convergence diagnostics, effective sample size, comparisons and plots                    |
| uncertainty/calibration            | [MAPIE](https://github.com/scikit-learn-contrib/MAPIE), [netcal](https://github.com/EFS-OpenSource/calibration-framework)                                                                                                             | conformal intervals/sets, calibration maps and reliability metrics                                              |
| causal graphs/effects              | [DoWhy](https://github.com/py-why/dowhy), [EconML](https://github.com/py-why/EconML), [CausalML](https://github.com/uber/causalml), [causal-learn](https://github.com/py-why/causal-learn), [LiNGAM](https://github.com/cdt15/lingam) | DAGs, identification assumptions, estimands, refuters, heterogeneous treatment effects and discovery algorithms |
| sensitivity and global explanation | [SALib](https://github.com/SALib/SALib)                                                                                                                                                                                               | sampling designs, sensitivity indices and confidence estimates                                                  |

Store assumptions and identification conditions as ports/preconditions. A causal estimator without graph, treatment, outcome, adjustment set and interference assumptions is not a safe primitive.

| Candidates                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Primitive yield                                                                                                                   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [SHAP](https://github.com/shap/shap), [Captum](https://github.com/pytorch/captum), [Alibi Explain](https://github.com/SeldonIO/alibi), [InterpretML](https://github.com/interpretml/interpret), [LIME](https://github.com/marcotcr/lime), [DALEX](https://github.com/ModelOriented/DALEX) | local/global attribution, counterfactual/anchor explanations, partial dependence, surrogate models and explanation-quality checks |
| [Fairlearn](https://github.com/fairlearn/fairlearn), [AIF360](https://github.com/Trusted-AI/AIF360), [Aequitas](https://github.com/dssg/aequitas)                                                                                                                                         | group metrics, disparity reports, mitigation constraints and threshold/postprocessing routes                                      |
| [Adversarial Robustness Toolbox](https://github.com/Trusted-AI/adversarial-robustness-toolbox), [Foolbox](https://github.com/bethgelab/foolbox), [RobustBench](https://github.com/RobustBench/robustbench)                                                                                | attacks, defenses, threat models, robust accuracy and benchmark recipes                                                           |
| [Giskard](https://github.com/Giskard-AI/giskard), [Deepchecks](https://github.com/deepchecks/deepchecks)                                                                                                                                                                                  | automated tests, slices, vulnerability/failure scans and reports                                                                  |

Attribution methods must declare compatible model access (`black_box`, gradients, layers), background/reference data, output type and perturbation assumptions. Fairness primitives must declare sensitive groups, aggregation and policy context.

### 30.7 Search, AutoML, optimization and experiment design

|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [Optuna](https://github.com/optuna/optuna)                                                                                                                                                           | samplers, pruners, studies, multiobjective trials, storage and visualization; direct model for Taedri's experiment scheduler |
| [Nevergrad](https://github.com/facebookresearch/nevergrad)                                                                                                                                           | gradient-free optimizers, parameter spaces and noisy/parallel black-box optimization                                         |

| [Ray Tune](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/tune/)                                                                                                                                                      | distributed search algorithms, schedulers, trial resources and fault recovery                                                |
| [Ax](https://github.com/facebook/Ax), [BoTorch](https://github.com/pytorch/botorch)                                                                                                                  | adaptive experimentation, Bayesian optimization, acquisition functions and constraints                                       |
| [SMAC3](https://github.com/automl/SMAC3), [ConfigSpace](https://github.com/automl/ConfigSpace), [DEHB](https://github.com/automl/DEHB)                                                               | conditional configuration spaces, multi-fidelity and evolutionary optimization                                               |
| [pymoo](https://github.com/anyoptimization/pymoo), [DEAP](https://github.com/DEAP/deap), [scikit-optimize](https://github.com/scikit-optimize/scikit-optimize)                                       | multiobjective/evolutionary/Bayesian optimization primitives                                                                 |
| [OR-Tools](https://github.com/google/or-tools), [CVXPY](https://github.com/cvxpy/cvxpy), [Pyomo](https://github.com/Pyomo/pyomo), [PuLP](https://github.com/coin-or/pulp)                            | constraint, linear/integer/convex/routing/scheduling solvers with feasibility and optimality receipts                        |
| [PyCaret](https://github.com/pycaret/pycaret), [AutoGluon](https://github.com/autogluon/autogluon), [TPOT](https://github.com/EpistasisLab/tpot), [MLJAR](https://github.com/mljar/mljar-supervised) | end-to-end model/pipeline search routes, ensembles and leaderboard evidence                                                  |

The important primitive is not “run Optuna.” Extract the search-space schema, conditional parameter edges, sampler/pruner protocol, objective direction, fidelity/resource budget, parallelism, reproducibility and trial receipt.

| [Hummingbird](https://github.com/microsoft/hummingbird), [Treelite](https://github.com/dmlc/treelite), [m2cgen](https://github.com/BayesWitnesses/m2cgen)                                                                       | classical-model compilation to tensors/native code/textual languages                     | supported estimator/operator, precision, target runtime   |

| [OpenVINO](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino), [Apache TVM](https://github.com/apache/tvm), [IREE](https://github.com/iree-org/iree)                                                                                  | graph lowering, target compilation and optimized runtimes                                | operator support, target, shape, precision and memory     |

Conversion edges must be empirically verified. “Exports successfully” is weaker than numerical agreement across a test input suite and weaker still than task-metric equivalence.

## 31. LLM routing, retrieval, structured generation and evaluation packages

These packages are valuable twice: as callable primitives and as experimental arms for Taedri's own control plane.

### 31.1 Cheap-to-expensive routing and prompt/program optimization

| Package                                                            | Taedri use                                                                                                                                        |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [RouteLLM](https://github.com/lm-sys/RouteLLM)                     | trained strong/weak model routers, threshold calibration and router evaluation; use as an external selector arm and mine router features/receipts |
| [semantic-router](https://github.com/aurelio-labs/semantic-router) | low-latency semantic route classification and multimodal routing; compare with exact/lexical/graph selectors                                      |
| [LiteLLM](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm)                      | provider/model normalization, budgets, retries, fallbacks and proxy telemetry; treat provider capabilities as versioned projections               |
| [DSPy](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy)                        | signatures, modules, optimizers and compiled LM programs; convert signatures/program traces into route and optimization records                   |
| [optillm](https://github.com/codelion/optillm)                     | inference-time optimization techniques behind a proxy                                                                                             |
| [guidance](https://github.com/guidance-ai/guidance)                | interleaved generation/control and constrained structures                                                                                         |
| [Instructor](https://github.com/567-labs/instructor)               | typed structured extraction with retries/validation                                                                                               |

Do not inherit historical benchmark claims as current truth. Replay every router on Taedri's demand distribution, model/version pair and price/latency table.

### 31.2 Constrained and structured outputs

| Package                                                             | Primitive yield                                                                     |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [Outlines](https://github.com/dottxt-ai/outlines)                   | JSON Schema, regex, grammar and choice-constrained generation across model backends |
| [LM Format Enforcer](https://github.com/noamgat/lm-format-enforcer) | character/token parser integration for regex and JSON Schema enforcement            |
| [XGrammar](https://github.com/mlc-ai/xgrammar)                      | fast grammar-guided structured generation and compiled grammar artifacts            |
| [Guardrails](https://github.com/guardrails-ai/guardrails)           | validators, structured schemas, reasks and failure handling                         |
| [Jsonformer](https://github.com/1rgs/jsonformer)                    | fixed-token JSON structure generation for supported transformer models              |
| Pydantic, JSON Schema, msgspec                                      | deterministic validation/coercion after generation                                  |

Represent `constrains_tokens`, `validates_after_generation`, `repairs_invalid_output`, and `guarantees_parseable_under_conditions` as different claims. A post-hoc parser is not equivalent to token-level constrained decoding.

### 31.3 Sparse, dense and late-interaction retrieval

| Package/source                                                                                                                                                      | Primitive yield                                                                    |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [BM25S](https://github.com/xhluca/bm25s), `rank-bm25`, Whoosh                                                                                                       | tokenization, weighting, sparse indexing and deterministic lexical retrieval       |
| [ColBERT](https://github.com/stanford-futuredata/ColBERT)                                                                                                           | late-interaction token embeddings, indexing and MaxSim scoring                     |
| [USearch](https://github.com/unum-cloud/usearch), FAISS, hnswlib, Annoy                                                                                             | ANN index/build/query variants, metrics, quantization and recall/latency tradeoffs |
| [Sentence Transformers](https://github.com/UKPLab/sentence-transformers), [FastEmbed](https://github.com/qdrant/fastembed), [txtai](https://github.com/neuml/txtai) | embedding, cross-encoder reranking and semantic workflow primitives                |
| [Pyserini](https://github.com/castorini/pyserini), [ranx](https://github.com/AmenRa/ranx), [ir-measures](https://github.com/terrierteam/ir_measures)                | reproducible IR indexes, fusion, run evaluation and standardized metrics           |
| [datasketch](https://github.com/ekzhu/datasketch), `ssdeep`, TLSH, `simhash` packages                                                                               | MinHash/LSH, locality-sensitive and fuzzy fingerprints for cheap blocking          |

Every retriever card should declare corpus size regime, update mode, metric, normalization, memory/storage, filter support, training dependency, determinism and measured recall/latency curve.

### 31.4 LLM, agent and RAG evaluation harnesses

| Package/source                                                                                                                                                                                           | Primitive yield                                                                   | Policy note                                                                                |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [LM Evaluation Harness](https://github.com/EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness)                                                                                                                             | YAML tasks, model adapters, prompt templates, filters, metrics and cached results | framework ingestible; benchmark task bodies partitioned by their own rights/holdout policy |
| [Lighteval](https://github.com/huggingface/lighteval)                                                                                                                                                    | backend-neutral tasks, metrics and distributed evaluation                         | same task-level firewall                                                                   |
| [Inspect AI](https://github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_ai)                                                                                                                                             | tasks, solvers, tools, sandboxes, scorers and evaluation logs                     | excellent execution/evidence schema source                                                 |
| [promptfoo](https://github.com/promptfoo/promptfoo)                                                                                                                                                      | declarative prompt/agent/RAG tests, assertions, provider comparisons and CI       | JavaScript ecosystem projection; test content has source-specific rights                   |
| [DeepEval](https://github.com/confident-ai/deepeval), [Ragas](https://github.com/explodinggradients/ragas), [TruLens](https://github.com/truera/trulens), [Phoenix](https://github.com/Arize-ai/phoenix) | LLM/RAG metrics, traces, datasets, judges and evaluations                         | distinguish deterministic, reference-based, model-judge and human evidence                 |
| [lmms-eval](https://github.com/EvolvingLMMs-Lab/lmms-eval), [VLMEvalKit](https://github.com/open-compass/VLMEvalKit)                                                                                     | multimodal model adapters and broad task implementations                          | benchmark bodies and images remain isolated by dataset policy                              |

Compile evaluation frameworks into `TaskAdapter`, `ModelAdapter`, `Solver`, `Scorer`, `Judge`, `Sandbox`, `DatasetHandle`, and `EvaluationReceipt` capsules. This lets Taedri mix compatible components without copying protected tasks into retrieval.

## 32. Universal capsule schema for narrow packages and templates

The esoteric expansion needs several fields beyond ordinary function signatures.

``` yaml
CapabilityCapsule:
  identity:
    capability_id: stable semantic identity
    implementation_id: package/version/artifact/entity projection
    subject_kind: function | class | transform | verifier | workflow | template | benchmark | adapter
  semantics:
    intents: []
    non_goals: []
    transformations: []
    invariants_preserved: []
    information_lost: []
  ports:
    inputs: []
    outputs: []
    errors: []
    side_effects: []
    state_transitions: []
  compatibility:
    data_models: []
    formats: []
    schemas: []
    units_and_coordinate_systems: []
    encodings_and_locales: []
    versions_and_environment_markers: []
    runtimes_devices_and_resources: []
    determinism_and_randomness: {}
  quality:
    complexity: {}
    fidelity_metrics: []
    performance_envelope: []
    known_failure_regions: []
  evidence:
    documentation_claims: []
    static_inferences: []
    examples: []
    tests: []
    independent_oracles: []
    sandbox_observations: []
    receipts: []
  descriptors:
    text_views: []
    keywords_and_labels: []
    sparse_vectors: []
    hashes_and_sketches: []
    embeddings: []
    graph_views: []
  governance:
    source_and_path_digests: []
    license_policy: ...
    corpus_partition: ...
    selectable: false
    executable: false
```

Record project health and lineage; a useful historical corpus need not be a recommended runtime.

### 33.2 Missingness, imputation and anomaly niches

| Source                                                        | Primitive candidates                                                        | Required fields                                                                        |
|---------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [HyperImpute](https://github.com/vanderschaarlab/hyperimpute) | plugin registry of statistical, iterative, matrix, deep and causal imputers | dtype/shape, missingness mechanism, optional dependency, fit state and uncertainty     |
| [miceforest](https://github.com/AnotherSamWilson/miceforest)  | chained multiple imputation and completed-dataset generation                | predictor sets, categorical objectives, convergence, seeds and completed-dataset index |

| PyOD / Alibi Detect                                           | tabular and multimodal anomaly detectors                                    | modality, score range/direction, contamination/threshold and calibration               |
| STUMPY / ruptures / ADTK                                      | temporal motifs, discords, changes and events                               | window, frequency, penalty, event interval and streaming state                         |

Benchmark MCAR, MAR and MNAR separately. Score reconstruction, coverage/uncertainty and downstream utility; a low reconstruction error does not prove unbiased inference.

| [Record Linkage Toolkit](https://github.com/J535D165/recordlinkage)                           | index→compare→classify→evaluate stages                                                                 | indexer→pairs; comparator→field pair; feature vector→classifier; labels→metrics         | P1       |
| [pyJedAI](https://github.com/AI-team-UoA/pyJedAI)                                             | blocking, block/comparison cleaning, matching, joins, clustering and evaluation                        | ER stage→valid next stage; matcher→similarity; clusterer→graph                          | P0/P1    |
| [clkhash](https://github.com/data61/clkhash) + [Anonlink](https://github.com/data61/anonlink) | privacy-preserving field encoders, candidate generation, similarity and assignment                     | schema/secret→encoded record; similarity threshold→pairs; privacy/recall tradeoff       | P1 niche |

An entity-resolution package should not become one capsule. Extract blocker/indexer, comparison metric, feature learner, probability calibrator, threshold, cluster/assignment solver and evaluator independently, then retain verified reference routes.
