[REIN](https://github.com/BigDaMa/REIN), [Raha](https://github.com/BigDaMa/raha), [Baran](https://github.com/BigDaMa/baran) and [HoloClean](https://github.com/HoloClean/holoclean) contribute corruption taxonomies, detection/repair tasks, labeled errors and comparison routes even when their runtime implementation is not the preferred current tool. Dataset rights remain independent.

## 38. Data-specific falsification experiments

1.  **Dirty Table Gauntlet:** encoding, whitespace/case, type drift, malformed dates, duplicates, invalid identifiers, missing values and outliers; compare discover→repair→validate routes.
2.  **Cross-DataFrame Semantic Matrix:** matched operations over pandas, Polars, DuckDB, Arrow, Spark and Daft; compare values, schema, order, nulls, time, memory and materialization.
3.  **Contract Round Trip:** ODCS→JSON Schema→Avro→dbt→SodaCL→ODCS; classify preserved/defaulted/weakened/lost constraints.
4.  **Entity-Resolution Router:** select Splink/Dedupe/recordlinkage/pyJedAI by scale, density, fields, labels and privacy.
5.  **String-Corruption Router:** typo/OCR/mojibake/transliteration/punctuation/token-order perturbations and route selection.
6.  **Missingness Challenge:** MCAR/MAR/MNAR with reconstruction, uncertainty, predictive utility and runtime.
7.  **Quality Compiler Equivalence:** express one contract in Pandera/cuallee/GX/Soda/TDDA and compare semantics/backend/reporting.
8.  **JSON Query/Streaming:** JMESPath/JSONPath/glom/dpath/ijson over deep/wide/large/malformed/chunked inputs.
9.  **Receipt Fidelity:** structlog/Eliot/OpenTelemetry→ECS JSON; reconstruct causal order, retries, exceptions and versions.
10. **SQL Dialect/Lineage:** SQLGlot plus SQLLineage/dbt/OpenLineage across CTEs, macros, nested/dynamic SQL.
11. **Graph Recovery:** compare static and runtime DAGs for Hamilton, Dagster, Prefect, Airflow, Kedro and Metaflow.
12. **Streaming Semantics:** late/duplicate/out-of-order events, watermarks, state recovery and replay across runners.
13. **Connector Route:** Salesforce-like source→DuckDB→phone normalization→key validation→lineage, using synthetic services.
14. **Version Breakpoints:** replay the same capsule across releases and detect signature/behavior/schema changes.
15. **Negative Edges:** reject eager vs streaming, record vs aggregate, lossy vs reversible, SQL-only vs in-memory and batch vs online mismatches.

## 39. Charting, visualization and visual-design primitive sources

The best chart sources are not screenshot galleries. They are declarative grammars and serializable scene graphs that expose data transforms, marks, channels, scales, projections, layout and interaction.

### 39.1 Highest-yield chart and UI sources

| Source                                                                                                                                          | Why it is primitive-shaped                                                   | Records to extract                                                                                        |

| [Vega-Lite](https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/docs/) and [Vega schemas](https://github.com/vega/schema)                                          | Declarative JSON grammar with validation and compilation                     | mark, encoding, transform, scale, projection, facet/layer/concat, selection, config and renderer capsules |
| [Plotly JSON schema](https://plotly.com/chart-studio-help/json-chart-schema/)                                                                   | Cross-language trace/layout/interaction contract                             | trace types, properties, layout, transforms, animation, export and renderer compatibility                 |

### 39.3 Required chart ports

``` text
ChartSpecification[
  grammar,
  grammar_version,
  data_schema,
  semantic_field_types,
  transforms,
  marks,
  encodings,
  scales,
  projections,
  interactions,
  composition,
  renderer,
  output_format,
  accessibility_metadata,
  responsive_behavior,
  locale,
  timezone,
  theme_tokens
]
```

Verification should proceed from schema validation and data-transform equality to SVG/DOM structure, text/OCR, layout, perceptual difference and only then a visual judge. Pixel equality alone is brittle because fonts, OS, browser, GPU and antialias settings affect renders; [Playwright explicitly documents environment sensitivity](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-snapshots).

- [MediaPipe](https://github.com/google-ai-edge/mediapipe): graph-defined calculators, typed streams and side packets.

### 40.4 OCR, document layout and machine-readable visual content

**Candidates:** [docTR](https://mindee.github.io/doctr/), [PaddleOCR](https://www.paddleocr.ai/latest/en/index.html), Kraken, Tesseract/pytesseract, OCRmyPDF, LayoutParser, `unstructured`, deepdoctection, hOCR/ALTO XML tooling, ZXing-cpp, pyzbar and pylibdmtx.

Required ports include language/script, orientation, bounding polygon, confidence, reading order, page, hierarchy, character encoding, table cell/formula representation and source coordinate system.

### 40.5 Image quality, deduplication and conformance

| Purpose              | Candidates                                                                                | Result records                                                                      |
|----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| exact identity       | SHA-256/BLAKE3 plus decoded-pixel digest                                                  | file identity versus visual-content identity                                        |
| perceptual hashes    | ImageHash, `imagededup`, PDQ, [Thorn perception](https://github.com/thorn-oss/perception) | hash type/size, distance, threshold, transformation tolerance and duplicate cluster |
| ANN dedup            | FAISS, ScaNN, HNSWlib, LSH                                                                | neighbors, cluster, embedding model and recall evidence                             |
| dataset diagnostics  | [CleanVision](https://github.com/cleanlab/cleanvision), FiftyOne, Datumaro                | blur, exposure, duplicates, low information, unusual size/aspect and label issues   |
| reference quality    | PSNR, SSIM/MS-SSIM, CW-SSIM, FSIM, VSI, LPIPS, DISTS                                      | per-image/per-region quality with metric/version/threshold                          |
| no-reference quality | BRISQUE, NIQE, PIQE, MUSIQ, TOPIQ, NIMA, CLIP-IQA                                         | predicted quality and calibration population                                        |
| metric suites        | [pyiqa](https://github.com/chaofengc/IQA-PyTorch), PIQ, TorchMetrics                      | metric registry and backend/device compatibility                                    |
| distribution quality | CleanFID, torch-fidelity, KID/FID                                                         | dataset/model/sample-count and feature-extractor-qualified evidence                 |
| semantic alignment   | CLIPScore, DINO, ImageReward, VQA scorers                                                 | instruction/subject/unchanged-region evidence                                       |
| provenance           | C2PA, EXIF/XMP/IPTC, ExifTool                                                             | signatures, ingredients, actions and metadata lineage                               |
| conformance          | JHOVE, jpylyzer, pngcheck, jpeginfo, `rio-cogeo`, FITS verification                       | standard violations, decoder disagreement and repairability                         |

`pyiqa` is especially interesting for Taedri's cost waterfall because it combines deterministic metrics and learned scorers of different sizes. Any learned quality score should be calibrated against task type and human judgments before it controls promotion.

### 40.6 Generative editing components

**Candidates:** Diffusers pipelines, ControlNet auxiliary preprocessors, `rembg`, IOPaint/LaMa, SAM/SAM2, GroundingDINO, Real-ESRGAN, BasicSR, GFPGAN, CodeFormer, SwinIR, `spandrel`, `facexlib`, pose/depth/line-art preprocessors and LUT/style systems.

Separate wrapper code, configuration, model architecture, weights, training data and acceptable-use terms. A permissive Python wrapper does not grant rights to its weights.

### 40.7 Required image ports

``` text
ImageArtifact[
  container, mime_type, codec,
  width, height, orientation, pages, frames, pyramid_levels,
  channels, channel_order, alpha_mode, sample_dtype, bit_depth, endianness,
  colorspace, icc_profile, ocio_space, primaries, transfer_function,
  matrix_coefficients, range, hdr_metadata,
  dpi, pixel_aspect_ratio,
  tiled, chunk_shape,
  geospatial_crs, affine_transform, nodata_value,
  tensor_layout, value_range, device,
  metadata_namespaces, provenance_manifest
]
```

### 40.8 Image verification waterfall

1.  file magic, MIME and parser validation;
2.  exact file digest;
3.  decoded-pixel digest;
4.  dimensions/channels/dtype/alpha/colorspace/profile checks;
5.  structural SVG/layer/metadata comparison;
6.  exact/RMS/pixel-mask difference;
7.  SSIM/MS-SSIM/XPSNR/ΔE;
8.  LPIPS/DISTS/DINO preservation;
9.  OCR/layout comparison;
10. task-specific object/mask/keypoint/count/spatial predicates;
11. no-reference quality estimate;
12. small local visual judge;
13. stronger multimodal judge only when unresolved;
14. human review for high-value calibrated uncertainty.

## 41. Video, audio, timeline and subtitle primitive sources

### 41.1 Highest-priority media graphs

| Source                                                             | Why it is unusually valuable                                                                                                               |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [FFmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg-all.html)                       | Enumerates filters, codecs, muxers/demuxers, protocols, bitstream filters, devices, formats and accelerators for the exact installed build |
| [GStreamer](https://gstreamer.freedesktop.org/documentation/)      | Plugins expose typed pads and `Caps`; negotiation already resembles a compatibility hypergraph                                             |
| [OpenTimelineIO](https://opentimelineio.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) | Typed edit graph of timelines, stacks, tracks, clips, gaps, transitions, effects, time ranges, media references and adapters               |
| MLT and GStreamer Editing Services                                 | producers/consumers, profiles, tracks, clips, transitions, filters and rendering graphs                                                    |
| [OpenFX](https://openfx.readthedocs.io/en/main/) and frei0r        | standardized visual-effect parameters, clip contexts and host compatibility                                                                |
| [LV2](https://lv2plug.in/ns/)                                      | RDF-described audio/control/event ports, units, features and extensions                                                                    |

### 41.2 Video package families

| Family                | Candidates                                                                          | Capsule opportunities                                                                             |
|-----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| codec/container       | FFmpeg/ffprobe, [PyAV](https://pyav.org/docs/stable/), GPAC, Bento4                 | containers, streams, packets, frames, codecs, bitstreams, reformatters, resamplers and time bases |
| negotiated pipelines  | GStreamer                                                                           | elements, pads, Caps ranges, ranks, devices, clocking and latency                                 |
| editorial interchange | OpenTimelineIO                                                                      | clips/tracks/transitions/effects, rational time, media references and format adapters             |
| nonlinear editors     | GES, MLT, libopenshot, Blender VSE                                                  | timelines, producers, consumers, effects and render routes                                        |
| lazy frame graphs     | VapourSynth, AviSynth+                                                              | clip formats, frame functions, plugins and random access                                          |
| high-level Python     | MoviePy, VidGear, imageio, mediapy                                                  | clip composition, overlays, text, audio and export                                                |
| accelerated decode    | TorchCodec, decord, DALI, PyNvVideoCodec                                            | device surfaces, batch decode, seek, zero-copy and tensor layouts                                 |
| tracking/analysis     | PySceneDetect, TransNetV2, supervision, Norfair, BoxMOT, trackpy, SLEAP, DeepLabCut | boundaries, detections, tracks, zones, pose and motion graphs                                     |

### 41.3 FFmpeg primitive worker

An FFmpeg worker should fingerprint the binary and parse:

``` text
ffmpeg -buildconf
ffmpeg -filters
ffmpeg -encoders
ffmpeg -decoders
ffmpeg -muxers
ffmpeg -demuxers
ffmpeg -bsfs
ffmpeg -protocols
ffmpeg -pix_fmts
ffmpeg -sample_fmts
ffmpeg -layouts
ffmpeg -hwaccels
ffmpeg -h filter=<name>
ffmpeg -h encoder=<name>
ffprobe -show_format -show_streams -show_frames -of json
```

Capabilities and effective license depend on build flags and linked libraries, so every card is scoped to a build fingerprint rather than the abstract FFmpeg version.

### 41.4 Scene, tracking and motion evidence

- [PySceneDetect](https://www.scenedetect.com/docs/latest/): content/adaptive/threshold/histogram detectors.
- TransNetV2: learned shot boundaries.
- OpenCV, RAFT and GMFlow: optical flow and motion.
- supervision and Norfair: detection/annotation/tracking/zone utilities.
- BoxMOT: many tracker projections; isolate current AGPL implications.
- Trackpy, SLEAP and DeepLabCut: trajectories and animal pose.

Oracles include boundary precision/recall/F1, IoU, HOTA, MOTA, IDF1, identity switches, fragmentation, trajectory smoothness, optical-flow residual and temporal consistency.

### 41.5 Subtitle, speech and audio alignment

| Candidates                                                                            | Primitive yield                                                                                        |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [pysubs2](https://pysubs2.readthedocs.io/en/latest/), `srt`, `webvtt-py`, `pycaption` | subtitle parsers/converters/retiming across ASS/SSA/SRT/WebVTT/TTML and other formats                  |
| [ffsubsync](https://github.com/smacke/ffsubsync)                                      | VAD/cross-correlation synchronization, frame-rate correction, segmented alignment and confidence gates |
| WhisperX, stable-ts, whisper-timestamped                                              | timestamped transcripts, word alignment and diarization routes                                         |
| Montreal Forced Aligner, aeneas                                                       | text/audio forced alignment                                                                            |
| pyannote.audio, WebRTC/Silero VAD, Auditok                                            | speakers, speech intervals and segmentation                                                            |
| librosa, Essentia, aubio                                                              | audio features, beats, pitch, onsets and analysis                                                      |
| pyloudnorm and FFmpeg `ebur128`                                                       | loudness measurement and normalization contracts                                                       |

``` text
AudioStream[sample_rate, sample_format, channel_layout, time_base,
            start_pts, duration, loudness_standard, language]

SubtitleTrack[format, encoding, time_base, language, forced,
              hearing_impaired, styled, frame_or_time_based]

TimedTranscript[segments, words, confidence, speaker, language,
                timestamps, alignment_model]
```

### 41.6 Video quality and conformance

FFmpeg exposes deterministic QC primitives including `blackdetect`, `blackframe`, `blurdetect`, `blockdetect`, `freezedetect`, `silencedetect`, `signalstats`, `idet`, `ebur128`, `psnr`, `ssim`, `xpsnr`, `libvmaf`, `corr`, frame digests and MPEG-7 signatures. Add [VMAF](https://github.com/Netflix/vmaf), MediaInfo/pymediainfo, QCTools, MediaConch, Bento4/GPAC inspectors and container-specific validators.

### 41.7 Required video ports

``` text
VideoStream[
  container, codec, profile, level, tier, pixel_format,
  width, height, sar, dar,
  frame_rate_mode, average_frame_rate, time_base, start_pts, duration,
  primaries, transfer, matrix, range, chroma_location, bit_depth, hdr_metadata,
  scan_type, field_order, gop_structure,
  hardware_surface, seekability
]
```

### 41.8 Video verification waterfall

1.  `ffprobe` structural contract;
2.  selected or complete packet/frame decode;
3.  timestamp monotonicity and duration;
4.  frame count, time base and CFR/VFR contract;
5.  audio rate/layout/clipping/loudness;
6.  subtitle encoding and interval validation;
7.  black/freeze/silence/block/blur/signal checks;
8.  frame digests for lossless routes;
9.  VMAF/XPSNR/SSIM for reference routes;
10. optical-flow/flicker/scene/tracking metrics;
11. subtitle WER and timestamp IoU;
12. VBench or a small video judge;
13. strong VLM only for unresolved semantic/physical-coherence questions.

## 42. Kubernetes, cloud-native workers and declarative template sources

Kubernetes ecosystems are unusually valuable because their artifacts already expose many of the fields Taedri otherwise has to infer: inputs, outputs, lifecycle, retries, resources, security boundaries, schemas, controllers, status conditions and compatibility requirements. A chart, task, operator or composition should therefore be compiled into multiple registry-native capsules, not indexed as one YAML blob.

### 42.1 Core workload and packaging grammars

| Source                                                                                                                                                            | What Taedri should extract                                                                                                   | High-value evidence and tests                                                  |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [Kubernetes Jobs](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/job/) and CronJobs                                                                    | completion modes, parallelism, backoff, deadlines, pod failure policy, indexed jobs, success policy, TTL and suspension      | OpenAPI schema, controller tests, examples and status transitions              |
| [Helm charts](https://helm.sh/docs/topics/charts/) and [Artifact Hub](https://artifacthub.io/docs/topics/repositories/)                                           | values schemas, templates, dependencies, hooks, install/upgrade notes, Kubernetes-version constraints and rendered resources | `helm lint`, values-schema validation, golden rendering, install/upgrade tests |
| [Kustomize](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/manage-kubernetes-objects/kustomization/)                                                                            | bases, overlays, strategic/JSON patches, replacements, generators, transformers and target selectors                         | build output, patch applicability, idempotence and overlay-conflict tests      |
| [CUE Central Registry](https://registry.cue.works/)                                                                                                               | constraints, defaults, unification, schemas and generated projections                                                        | `cue vet`, evaluation, subsumption and export round trips                      |
| [KCL modules](https://github.com/kcl-lang/modules)                                                                                                                | typed configuration models, validation rules, modules and rendered manifests                                                 | compile/evaluate tests and output-schema validation                            |
| [go-jsonnet](https://github.com/google/go-jsonnet), [Tanka](https://github.com/grafana/tanka) and [ytt](https://github.com/carvel-dev/ytt-library-for-kubernetes) | functions, mixins, overlays, assertions, environment inheritance and generated objects                                       | evaluator tests, golden manifests and overlay algebra                          |
| [KRM Functions Catalog](https://github.com/kptdev/krm-functions-catalog)                                                                                          | resource-list input/output contracts, mutations, validators and pipeline composition                                         | container/function specs, example packages and idempotence tests               |

These sources should produce at least four distinct capsule families:

1.  **renderers**: parameterized input to one or more resources;
2.  **transformers**: resource set to modified resource set;
3.  **validators**: resource set to diagnostics or a policy decision;
4.  **controllers**: desired state plus observed state to actions and a new status.

### 42.2 Workflow, task and event catalogs

| Ecosystem                                                                                | Primitive-rich artifacts                                                                           | Ports and compatibility facts                                                                            |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [Tekton Catalog](https://github.com/tektoncd/catalog)                                    | Tasks, Pipelines, step images, workspaces, parameters, results and examples                        | typed parameter/result/workspace contracts, image architecture, side effects, timeout and retry behavior |
| [Argo Workflows examples](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-workflows/tree/main/examples) | DAGs, steps, artifacts, parameters, loops, synchronization, retries, memoization and exit handlers | artifact repositories, executors, templates, conditional edges and failure paths                         |
| [Argo Events](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-events)                                   | event sources, sensors, filters, transformations and triggers                                      | CloudEvents-like payload shapes, delivery behavior, dependencies and trigger targets                     |
| [Argo Rollouts](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-rollouts)                               | canary/blue-green strategies, analysis templates and rollback conditions                           | traffic provider, metric provider, analysis result and promotion edges                                   |
| Kubeflow Pipelines components                                                            | component specs, container commands, artifacts, parameters and metadata                            | ML artifact types, caching keys, executor constraints and pipeline interfaces                            |
| [Dagger modules](https://docs.dagger.io/extending/modules/)                              | portable functions, typed objects, containers, services and files                                  | SDK/language projection, cache behavior and runtime dependencies                                         |
| GitHub starter workflows and reusable workflows                                          | triggers, permissions, inputs, secrets, jobs and artifacts                                         | event schema, permission scope, runner, marketplace action and output compatibility                      |

A single Tekton task, for example, can yield separate capsules for cloning, dependency caching, compilation, testing, image construction, signing, attestation and publishing. The original task remains provenance; the extracted unit becomes independently searchable and executable only after its contract is verified.

### 42.3 Compositions, platforms and workload specifications

- [Crossplane Compositions](https://docs.crossplane.io/latest/composition/compositions/) and [function-patch-and-transform](https://github.com/crossplane-contrib/function-patch-and-transform) provide typed composite resources, managed-resource projections, patches, transforms, readiness checks and connection details.
- [KubeVela Catalog](https://github.com/kubevela/catalog) provides component, trait, policy and workflow definitions.
- [Score specification](https://github.com/score-spec/spec) provides workload metadata that can project into multiple platform implementations.
- [Devfile Registry](https://github.com/devfile/registry) provides development components, commands, events, projects and starter projects.
- [Kratix](https://github.com/syntasso/kratix) provides promises, resource requests and state-store pipelines.
- Cloud Native Buildpacks define build, detect, analyze, restore, build and export phases with explicit build/run image contracts.
- Pulumi, Terraform/OpenTofu modules and AWS CDK constructs add imperative and declarative infrastructure projections; ingest schemas, plans and provider constraints before implementation bodies.

These are high-value sources for `implements_same_intent_as` edges. A Score workload, Helm chart, Kustomize overlay, CUE instance and Crossplane composition can express overlapping intent while differing in rendering, ownership and reconciliation semantics.

### 42.4 Operators, queues, autoscaling and specialized workers

| Source family                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Capabilities worth compiling                                                                                        |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [Kubebuilder](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kubebuilder), [Operator SDK](https://github.com/operator-framework/operator-sdk), [OLM](https://olm.operatorframework.io/docs/tasks/creating-a-catalog/) and [OperatorHub](https://operatorhub.io/) | CRD schemas, watches, owned/dependent resources, RBAC, finalizers, webhooks, conditions, upgrades and install modes |
| Kubeflow Trainer and Spark Operator                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | distributed training/compute roles, replica policies, rendezvous, restart and completion semantics                  |
| [KubeRay](https://github.com/ray-project/kuberay)                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Ray clusters, jobs, services, autoscaling, head/worker groups and accelerator resources                             |
| Kueue and Volcano                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | queues, cohorts, quotas, admission, gang scheduling, preemption and topology-aware scheduling                       |
| [KEDA](https://github.com/kedacore/keda)                                                                                                                                                                                                             | event-source scalers, authentication, polling, activation thresholds, fallback and scale-to-zero                    |
| Knative Serving/Eventing                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | revisions, traffic splits, autoscaling, brokers, triggers, channels and delivery policies                           |
| Strimzi, Flink Kubernetes Operator and CloudNativePG                                                                                                                                                                                                 | domain-specific reconciliation for streams, jobs and stateful data systems                                          |

Do not treat an operator as an opaque “deploy X” primitive. Split it into:

- schema and defaulting;
- desired-state projection;
- observation/discovery;
- create/update/delete action selection;
- readiness and condition calculation;
- retry/backoff;
- finalizer cleanup;
- migration and upgrade;
- status/report emission.

This decomposition exposes reconciliation algebra: convergence, idempotence, monotonicity, oscillation risk, ownership conflict and safe replay.

### 42.5 Policy, observability, testing and failure injection

Add dedicated source partitions for:

- Gatekeeper Library constraints and templates;
- Kyverno policies and tests;
- Falco rules and macros;
- OpenTelemetry Collector Contrib receivers, processors, exporters, connectors and extensions;
- Sigstore policy-controller, Cosign verification and in-toto attestations;
- Chainsaw, KUTTL and `envtest` controller scenarios;
- Sonobuoy conformance plugins;
- kube-burner load definitions;
- Chaos Mesh and LitmusChaos experiments;
- Prometheus rules and Alertmanager configurations;
- Kubernetes audit policies, Pod Security Standards and NetworkPolicies.

These supply negative constraints and executable oracles: `DENIES`, `MUTATES`, `ADMITS`, `OBSERVES`, `ALERTS_ON`, `INJECTS_FAILURE_INTO`, `RECOVERS_FROM` and `CONFORMS_TO`.

### 42.6 `WorkerTemplateCard`

``` yaml
worker_template_card:
  identity:
    canonical_id: taedri://worker/<ecosystem>/<source-digest>/<symbol>
    source_locator: {}
    version_scope: {}
    build_fingerprint: {}
  trigger:
    kind: [manual, schedule, queue, event, webhook, reconciliation, metric]
    event_schema: {}
    filters: []
  interface:
    parameters: []
    inputs: []
    outputs: []
    artifacts: []
    messages: []
  delivery:
    guarantee: [best_effort, at_most_once, at_least_once, effectively_once]
    acknowledgement: {}
    ordering: {}
    deduplication_key: null
  execution:
    command_or_handler: {}
    concurrency: {}
    timeout: null
    retries: {}
    backoff: {}
    dead_letter: {}
    checkpoint: {}
    cancellation: {}
    graceful_shutdown: {}
  algebra:
    deterministic: unknown
    idempotent: unknown
    commutative: unknown
    order_sensitive: unknown
    monotonic: unknown
    reversible: unknown
    lossy: unknown
    convergence_evidence: []
  runtime:
    cpu_memory_ephemeral_storage: {}
    accelerator: {}
    architecture_os: {}
    network: {}
    persistent_storage: {}
    secrets_config: {}
    security_context: {}
    service_account_rbac: {}
  operations:
    probes: {}
    autoscaling: {}
    metrics_logs_traces: {}
    alerts: []
    runbook: null
  deployment:
    renderer: null
    controller: null
    namespace_scope: null
    crds_required: []
    version_constraints: []
  evidence: []
  rights_and_policy: {}
```

The delivery guarantee must be inferred conservatively. “Exactly once” is not accepted because a README says it; it requires an end-to-end invariant across producer, broker, worker, side effects and checkpoint/transaction boundary.

## 43. Software generators, architecture templates and reference systems

Template ecosystems are executable design knowledge. Their value is not the generated boilerplate itself, but the mapping from intent and parameters to an artifact graph, plus the validations, migrations and operational assumptions surrounding that graph.

### 43.1 Generator sources

| Family                          | Sources                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Extractable primitive types                                                                                |
|---------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| repository/project templates    | [Backstage Software Templates](https://backstage.io/docs/features/software-templates/), [Copier](https://github.com/copier-org/copier), [Cookiecutter](https://github.com/cookiecutter/cookiecutter), Yeoman, Hygen and Plop | questions, defaults, conditional files, actions, validations, hooks and generated graph                    |
| monorepo/build generation       | Nx generators, Projen, Bazel rules and Pants plugins                                                                                                                                                                         | project graph mutation, targets, dependencies, cache boundaries and migrations                             |
| protocol/SDK generation         | OpenAPI Generator, AsyncAPI Generator, Smithy, Buf/Protobuf, gRPC Gateway and GraphQL codegen                                                                                                                                | schema-to-server/client/model/test projections, language/runtime compatibility and serialization contracts |
| application starters            | Spring Initializr, JHipster, `.NET new`, `cargo-generate`, Vite templates and framework CLIs                                                                                                                                 | feature selections, dependency constraints, layout, configuration and smoke tests                          |
| environment/deployment starters | Dev Container templates, GitHub starter workflows, Pulumi templates, Terraform modules and Helm starters                                                                                                                     | runtime/toolchain, CI triggers, permissions, infrastructure parameters and deployment artifacts            |

### 43.2 `GeneratorCard`

``` text
GeneratorCard[
  generator_identity, version, input_questionnaire_schema,
  defaults, conditional_rules, template_fragments,
  pre_actions, render_actions, post_actions,
  generated_artifact_graph, dependency_constraints,
  secret_handling, destructive_operations,
  update_strategy, migration_strategy, verification_plan,
  source_provenance, output_rights
]
```

The key graph is not merely `TEMPLATE -> FILE`. It is:

``` text
UserIntent
  -> ParameterAssignment
  -> ConditionalFeatureSet
  -> GeneratorActions
  -> ArtifactGraph
  -> Build/Test/Deploy Oracles
  -> Update/Migration Path
```

Store unanswered questions and rejected combinations as first-class constraints. They are often more useful to a route solver than the happy-path output.

### 43.3 Reference architectures as motif corpora

Mine, but do not copy wholesale, reference applications such as:

- `.NET` eShop;
- Google Cloud's microservices demo;
- Dapr quickstarts and samples;
- Spring Petclinic variants;
- AWS serverless sample applications;
- Azure Search/OpenAI reference applications;
- language/framework “real world” implementations;
- CNCF project examples and conformance fixtures.

Compile these into architecture motifs:

- request/reply and service invocation;
- pub/sub and event fan-out;
- saga/process manager;
- transactional outbox and inbox deduplication;
- API gateway and backend-for-frontend;
- retry, timeout, circuit breaker and bulkhead;
- cache-aside and write-through;
- work queue and scatter/gather;
- leader election and leases;
- health/readiness propagation;
- telemetry-context propagation;
- identity, trust and authorization boundaries;
- secret/config distribution;
- database-per-service and data ownership;
- deployment, rollback and migration topology.

Each motif needs preconditions, prohibited combinations, failure behavior and evidence. A diagram alone is descriptive evidence, not an executable compatibility claim.

### 43.4 Architecture-decision and diagram grammars

Add [Structurizr DSL](https://docs.structurizr.com/dsl), C4-PlantUML, [arc42](https://arc42.org/overview) and [MADR](https://adr.github.io/madr/) as sources of:

- system/container/component/person relationships;
- deployment nodes and environments;
- architectural decisions, status and consequences;
- quality scenarios and constraints;
- alternatives considered and supersession chains;
- traceability from decision to component, test and incident.

Useful edges include `DECIDED_BY`, `SUPERSEDES_DECISION`, `CONSTRAINED_BY`, `DEPLOYED_ON`, `COMMUNICATES_WITH`, `OWNS_DATA`, `TRUSTS`, `THREATENS` and `VERIFIED_BY_SCENARIO`.

### 43.5 Design-system and UI-template sources

Storybook, design tokens and component registries deserve their own workers because they combine code, states, visual examples, accessibility and interaction tests.

Priority sources include:

- [Storybook Component Story Format](https://storybook.js.org/docs/api/csf), args, controls, play functions and test-runner evidence;
- [shadcn registry](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/registry), Radix primitives and React Aria behaviors;
- Carbon, PatternFly, USWDS, Fluent, Chakra and Ant Design components;
- [Design Tokens Community Group format](https://www.designtokens.org/tr/drafts/format/) for typed token/alias graphs;
- WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices for roles, states, keyboard interaction and accessibility oracles;
- Custom Elements Manifest and framework component metadata;
- Playwright interaction and screenshot fixtures;
- icon, typography, layout and theme packages as separately licensed assets.

Compile one UI component into:

``` text
UIComponentCard[
  semantic_role, props, slots, events, controlled_state, variants,
  token_dependencies, composition_rules, keyboard_model,
  focus_behavior, aria_contract, responsive_behavior,
  visual_states, interaction_stories, accessibility_oracles,
  screenshot_oracles, framework_projection, browser_support
]
```

Keep code license, documentation license, token license, icon/font license, screenshot rights and external design-file rights separate. “The repository is open source” is not sufficient provenance for every artifact it contains.
