## 44. Coding, data-science, agent and multimodal task corpora

Task corpora should populate a separate **task and oracle plane**. They can teach Taedri how capabilities are requested, decomposed and verified without making benchmark solutions retrievable during evaluation.

### 44.1 Coding and repository-level tasks

| Source                                                                   | What it contributes                                                  | Safe use                                                                                    |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [SWE-bench](https://www.swebench.com/) and SWE-smith                     | issue-to-patch tasks, repository context and executable tests        | sealed evaluation; extract only public task metadata into the task plane                    |
| BigCodeBench and LiveCodeBench                                           | library-use and recent coding problems with tests                    | task archetypes, signature/constraint features and held-out scoring                         |
| DS-1000                                                                  | realistic data-science library tasks                                 | API-composition archetypes and test styles; keep answers isolated                           |
| MLE-bench                                                                | end-to-end ML-engineering competitions                               | environment, artifact, metric and resource-contract patterns                                |
| Terminal-Bench                                                           | terminal/agent tasks with containerized verification                 | shell/tool action graphs, state transitions and executable graders                          |
| CRUXEval                                                                 | execution reasoning over code                                        | input/output and execution-trace oracles                                                    |
| CodeContests, APPS, HumanEval, MBPP and EvalPlus                         | algorithmic and function-level tasks                                 | constraints, metamorphic tests and language projections                                     |
| BFCL/Gorilla                                                             | function/tool calling                                                | tool-schema selection, argument construction and stateful/multi-turn routes                 |
| Exercism, CodeNet, CodeSearchNet, MultiPL-E, RepoBench and CrossCodeEval | language idioms, solution families, retrieval and cross-file context | deduplicated training partition or task mining according to rights and contamination status |
| Spider, BIRD and ODEX                                                    | text-to-SQL and data queries                                         | schema linking, query plans, result equivalence and execution oracles                       |

### 44.2 Interactive-agent and environment tasks

- VisualWebArena and WebArena: browser goals, site state and environment-based success.
- OSWorld: multimodal computer-use tasks and stateful evaluation.
- AndroidWorld: mobile interaction tasks and emulator-state oracles.
- GAIA: multi-tool research and reasoning tasks.
- `tau-bench`: tool-agent conversations with policy and database-state checks.
- Kubernetes debugging games, incident-response exercises and CTF-style labs: failure localization, remediation and negative-policy constraints.

For each task, distinguish:

1.  stated goal;
2.  observable initial state;
3.  hidden state;
4.  allowed actions/tools;
5.  constraints and policy;
6.  intermediate observations;
7.  success oracle;
8.  efficiency/cost measure;
9.  unsafe or disallowed states;
10. contamination and disclosure status.

### 44.3 Image, chart and video benchmarks

| Corpus or suite                                                                                                  | Primitive/oracle value                                                      | Important policy                                                              |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [VBench](https://github.com/Vchitect/VBench) and EvalCrafter                                                     | decomposed video-generation quality dimensions                              | use as evaluator/feature sources; inspect model and data licenses separately  |
| GenEval and T2I-CompBench                                                                                        | object/count/color/position and compositional text-to-image adherence       | convert dimensions into independent semantic oracles                          |
| [MagicBrush](https://github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/MagicBrush), InstructPix2Pix, ImagenHub, UniEditBench and I2EBench | instruction-based image editing, preservation and human-preference evidence | honor dataset-specific redistribution rules; keep hidden test material sealed |
| LMM4Edit and ImgEdit                                                                                             | complex edit instructions and edit evaluation                               | quarantine sources without clear artifact rights until reviewed               |
| ChartQA, PlotQA, DVQA and FigureQA                                                                               | chart understanding and data/visual consistency                             | derive chart-table-text consistency oracles                                   |
| Design2Code and WebSight                                                                                         | screenshot-to-code and rendered-page correspondence                         | isolate source images, generated code and site-content rights                 |
| [VMAF](https://github.com/Netflix/vmaf), FFmpeg FATE, OpenCV extra and Web Platform Tests                        | deterministic conformance and regression fixtures                           | especially valuable for implementation equivalence and version drift          |
| Khronos glTF sample assets                                                                                       | format/renderer conformance and pathological assets                         | preserve per-asset license and expected-result metadata                       |

Multimodal verification must remain an ensemble:

``` text
container/schema conformance
  -> pixel/frame/audio invariants
  -> mask/region preservation
  -> requested-change measurement
  -> temporal/identity/geometry consistency
  -> perceptual metrics
  -> calibrated small judge
  -> strong multimodal judge
  -> human adjudication sample
```

Never promote one VLM score to “ground truth.” Store the judge model/version/prompt, input transformation, calibration set, uncertainty and known blind spots in the receipt.

### 44.4 `BenchmarkTask` and `OracleCard`

``` yaml
benchmark_task:
  task_id: taedri://task/<source>/<digest>
  goal: {}
  initial_state: {}
  hidden_state_ref: null
  allowed_actions: []
  constraints: []
  resources: {}
  target_capabilities: []
  expected_artifacts: []
  oracle_refs: []
  cost_metrics: []
  disclosure_partition: [development, validation, sealed_test]
  contamination_fingerprints: []
  rights: {}

oracle_card:
  oracle_id: taedri://oracle/<kind>/<digest>
  observes: []
  method: [exact, schema, property, execution, metamorphic, differential,
           perceptual, model_judge, human]
  threshold_or_predicate: {}
  invariances: []
  false_positive_risks: []
  false_negative_risks: []
  calibration_evidence: []
  independence_from_candidate: {}
  runtime_cost: {}
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 45. Specialized records and compatibility edges

The universal `CapabilityCapsule` remains the envelope. These specialized records are projections, not competing schemas:

- `TemplateCard`, `TemplateParameter` and `RenderedArtifact`;
- `WorkerTemplateCard`, `WorkloadCard`, `ControllerContract` and `ReconciliationStep`;
- `CompositionCard`, `PolicyTransform` and `CompatibilityClaim`;
- `GeneratorCard`, `ReferenceArchitecture`, `ArchitectureDecision` and `MotifCard`;
- `UIComponentCard`, `DesignTokenCard` and `StoryOracle`;
- `BenchmarkTask`, `OracleCard` and `ContaminationRecord`;
- `MediaTransformCard`, `CodecCapability`, `TimelineOperation` and `RightsRecord`.

Add the following typed edge vocabulary to the port-level hypergraph:

### Generation and transformation

`PARAMETERIZES`, `GENERATES`, `RENDERS_TO`, `PATCHES`, `OVERLAYS`, `DEFAULTS`, `VALIDATES`, `MUTATES`, `MIGRATES_TO`, `REPLACES`, `ROUND_TRIPS_TO`, `PROJECTS_TO_LANGUAGE`.

### Runtime and controller behavior

`TRIGGERS`, `CONSUMES_EVENT`, `EMITS_EVENT`, `ACKNOWLEDGES`, `RETRIES_AS`, `DEAD_LETTERS_TO`, `CHECKPOINTS_IN`, `SCALES_ON`, `SCHEDULES_ON`, `REQUIRES_CRD`, `WATCHES`, `OWNS_RESOURCE`, `RECONCILES`, `FINALIZES`, `ROLLS_BACK_WITH`.

### Compatibility and constraints

`REQUIRES_CAPABILITY`, `COMPATIBLE_WITH`, `CONFLICTS_WITH`, `SUBSUMES_SCHEMA`, `SATISFIES_POLICY`, `DENIED_BY`, `LOSSY_TO`, `PRESERVES`, `INVALIDATES`, `ONLY_VALID_WHEN`, `VERSION_GATED_BY`.

### Evidence, tasks and provenance

`TESTED_BY`, `SCORED_BY`, `CALIBRATED_BY`, `FALSIFIED_BY`, `DERIVED_FROM`, `LICENSED_AS`, `CONTAMINATES`, `DUPLICATES`, `VARIANT_OF`, `IMPLEMENTS_PATTERN`, `SUPERSEDES_DECISION`.

Every asserted edge needs:

``` text
EdgeAssertion[
  subject_port_or_node, predicate, object_port_or_node,
  qualifiers, version_scope, environment_scope,
  evidence_refs, inference_method, confidence,
  verified_state, verifier, verified_at,
  counterexamples, invalidation_conditions
]
```

This is particularly important for negative and conditional facts. “Supports JSON” is too weak. A useful claim records JSON dialect, byte/text type, streaming behavior, duplicate-key policy, number handling, Unicode/error policy, schema support, limits and failure semantics.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 46. Ingestion priority for the esoteric capability tail

The goal is not to rank by stars. Rank by marginal verified capability and compatibility knowledge per unit of extraction and execution cost.

### Wave A — deterministic, schema-rich and immediately testable

1.  Pandera, Frictionless, TDDA, cuallee and CleverCSV;
2.  RapidFuzz, ftfy, `python-stdnum`, DeepDiff, JSON Patch and JMESPath;
3.  Narwhals, Ibis, SQLGlot, PyArrow and DataFusion;
4.  structlog, OpenTelemetry semantic conventions and Collector components;
5.  Vega-Lite schema, FFmpeg/`ffprobe`, GStreamer registries, OpenImageIO/OpenColorIO and OpenTimelineIO;
6.  Kubernetes OpenAPI/Jobs, Helm values schemas, Kustomize, Tekton Catalog and Argo examples;
7.  OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/Protobuf generators, Storybook CSF and DTCG tokens;
8.  FFmpeg FATE, Web Platform Tests and selected package test suites as oracle sources.

Why first: these sources expose machine-readable surfaces, have cheap exact oracles and create dense typed edges without requiring an LLM to understand the entire implementation.

### Wave B — stateful, cross-engine and controller semantics

1.  Splink, Dedupe, pyJedAI, Cleanlab, River and change/drift libraries;
2.  Hamilton, dlt, Dagster, Prefect, dbt/SQLMesh and OpenLineage;
3.  libvips, ImageMagick, scikit-image, Kornia, VMAF, subtitle and audio-alignment tools;
4.  KEDA, KubeRay, Kueue, Crossplane compositions, KRM/KCL/CUE and policy libraries;
5.  Backstage, Copier/Cookiecutter, OpenAPI Generator and reference-architecture motifs;
6.  deterministic task generators and development partitions of coding/media benchmarks.

### Wave C — expensive, ambiguous or judge-dependent

1.  learned image/video quality, OCR and semantic-edit verification;
2.  multimodal task corpora and interactive GUI environments;
3.  full operator reconciliation mining and distributed failure injection;
4.  human-preference datasets and strong-model-generated descriptions;
5.  sources with incomplete rights, unclear provenance or no independent execution oracle.

Wave C is not less valuable. It is delayed until Taedri can quantify uncertainty, isolate contamination and decide when expensive verification changes a routing decision.

### Source acquisition score

``` text
gain(source) =
    w1 * novel_verified_capabilities
  + w2 * novel_typed_edges
  + w3 * independent_oracles
  + w4 * cross_backend_equivalences
  + w5 * negative_constraints
  + w6 * task_demand_coverage
  + w7 * version_drift_information
  - w8 * extraction_cost
  - w9 * execution_cost
  - w10 * rights_risk
  - w11 * contamination_risk
  - w12 * duplicate_saturation
```

Use submodular coverage or log-determinant diversity over capability/edge embeddings so the scheduler does not keep selecting near-duplicate libraries from the same ecosystem.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 47. Cross-domain experiments that can falsify the architecture

These experiments are more useful than a larger uncontrolled crawl because each can disprove a specific Taedri assumption.

### 47.1 One worker, eight representations

Encode the same idempotent data-cleaning worker as:

1.  Kubernetes Job;
2.  Helm chart;
3.  Kustomize base/overlay;
4.  CUE instance;
5.  KCL module;
6.  Jsonnet/Tanka object;
7.  Argo workflow template;
8.  Tekton task.

Normalize all eight into GraphIR. Test whether the route solver can recover common input/output, runtime, retry, resource and observability semantics while preserving representation-specific behavior. Failure reveals missing schema or edge types.

### 47.2 Hidden-parameter template retrieval

Create held-out generator tasks whose correct template and parameter combination are not named in the prompt. Compare:

- exact/history retrieval;
- fielded BM25;
- typed graph route solving;
- LSH/embedding retrieval;
- local SLM selection;
- strong-model full-source reasoning.

Measure task success, invalid render rate, execution success, tokens, latency, verification cost and unsupported claims. Vary route handles at 1/2/4/8 alternatives and card detail levels.

### 47.3 Reconciliation torture suite

For selected controllers, inject deletion, stale caches, partial status, duplicate events, unavailable APIs, admission rejection, upgrade, finalizer failure and worker restart. Verify convergence, idempotence, bounded retry and cleanup. Store minimal counterexample traces against the implicated edge assertions.

### 47.4 Cross-engine data route equivalence

Compile the same cleanse → validate → join → aggregate → serialize route to pandas, Polars, DuckDB, Ibis/DataFusion and Spark where supported. Generate adversarial fixtures for nulls, NaNs, time zones, duplicate keys, Unicode, decimal precision, categorical order and empty partitions. Record exact semantic divergences instead of labeling all backends compatible.

### 47.5 Media capability graph

- Harvest FFmpeg filters/encoders/decoders/formats and GStreamer factories/pad templates/caps.
- Generate only type-valid candidate pipelines.
- Test negotiation, decode, timestamp, color, alpha, metadata and round-trip properties.
- Compare graph-only composition with LLM-authored commands.

Success means fewer invalid pipelines and fewer prompt tokens, not merely matching a judge's preference.

### 47.6 Chart grammar compiler

Map a common `ChartSpecification` into Vega-Lite, Plotly, Observable Plot and selected native chart libraries. Verify data-domain, scales, marks, legends, accessibility tree, interaction and screenshot invariants. Separate renderer differences from actual semantic loss.

### 47.7 Mask-aware image-edit verifier

Build an ensemble over structural checks, alpha/color integrity, pixel/feature change inside the requested mask, preservation outside it, OCR/object/count/geometry constraints and calibrated visual judges. Ablate each oracle and measure whether it improves agreement with human adjudication enough to justify its cost.

### 47.8 Timeline and video torture suite

Generate clips with variable frame rate, non-zero start PTS, B-frames, rotation metadata, HDR, odd dimensions, multiple audio/subtitle tracks, discontinuities and corrupt packets. Run FFmpeg/GStreamer/OTIO/MLT routes; verify stream structure, timing, sync, edit decisions, loss and quality.

### 47.9 Task-contamination firewall

Compute exact, normalized-AST, MinHash/LSH, embedding, test-signature, prompt and media-perceptual fingerprints across source, generated artifacts and benchmark partitions. Deliberately inject paraphrases, translations, renamed code and transformed media; measure missed leakage and false quarantine.

### 47.10 Worker algebra and delivery claims

Replay duplicate and reordered messages across candidate workers. Kill them before and after side effects and acknowledgements. Test whether declared idempotence, commutativity and delivery claims hold. Promote only verified claims into route constraints.

### 47.11 Cheap verifier/router cascade

For data, Kubernetes and media tasks, route verification through:

``` text
exact/schema/property checks
  -> differential/metamorphic execution
  -> small specialized model
  -> general small model
  -> strong model
  -> human sample
```

Train the escalation policy on expected value of additional information: escalate only when the next verifier is likely to alter accept/reject, route selection or uncertainty enough to repay its cost.

### 47.12 Catalog-yield tournament

Give every ingestion worker a fixed compute/time budget. Rank sources by verified capsules, novel ports, novel edges, counterexamples and task-demand coverage per extraction hour. Feed the receipts into the adaptive acquisition scheduler.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 48. Concrete build: the Esoteric Capability Worker Pack

The most useful next implementation is one shared ingestion framework plus eight source-specific workers.

### Worker 1 — data contract and cleansing compiler

Targets Pandera, Frictionless, TDDA, cuallee, CleverCSV, PyJanitor and package tests. Emits field/domain constraints, repair transforms, failure policies, fixtures and executable validators.

### Worker 2 — cross-engine semantic compiler

Targets Narwhals, Ibis, SQLGlot, Arrow/DataFusion and backend test matrices. Emits normalized relational/expression operations, engine projections and verified divergence edges.

### Worker 3 — JSON, logging and telemetry compiler

Targets JSON Schema/OpenAPI dialects, JMESPath/JSONPath, structlog, OpenTelemetry semantic conventions and Collector component metadata. Emits event/log schemas, processors, exporters, privacy/redaction and trace-correlation contracts.

### Worker 4 — visual/media capability harvester

Targets FFmpeg, GStreamer, libvips, OpenImageIO/OpenColorIO, Vega-Lite and OpenTimelineIO. Emits capability cards directly from registries/schemas/help output, then attaches deterministic conformance fixtures.

### Worker 5 — Kubernetes/template compiler

Targets Jobs, Helm, Kustomize, Tekton, Argo, Crossplane, KRM/KCL/CUE, KEDA and KubeRay. Emits worker, renderer, controller, trigger, resource, retry, policy and observability contracts.

### Worker 6 — generator and architecture compiler

Targets Backstage, Copier/Cookiecutter, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI generators, Storybook and selected reference applications. Emits parameter graphs, artifact graphs, migration behavior, UI contracts and architectural motifs.

### Worker 7 — task/oracle and contamination compiler

Targets package tests plus approved development partitions of coding, data and media suites. Emits `BenchmarkTask`, `OracleCard`, fingerprints and partition gates; never places sealed answers in the retrieval index.

### Worker 8 — conformance and receipt runner

Creates disposable environments, resolves bodies only after selection, executes candidates, runs independent verifiers, minimizes counterexamples and writes exact receipts.

All workers should use the same staged interface:

``` text
discover
  -> fingerprint and rights gate
  -> extract machine-readable surface
  -> static symbol/schema graph
  -> candidate capsule generation
  -> evidence attachment
  -> cheap validation
  -> isolated execution
  -> independent verification
  -> counterexample minimization
  -> publish immutable versioned records
```

### First 30-day acceptance criteria

- ingest at least 20 heterogeneous sources from Waves A and B;
- produce at least 10,000 candidate capsules and 50,000 typed edge assertions;
- independently verify at least 2,000 capsules across two environment versions where applicable;
- identify at least 100 concrete incompatibilities or semantic divergences;
- answer 200 held-out demand prompts with an exact receipt;
- compare 1/2/4/8 route handles and three card-detail levels;
- demonstrate post-selection body resolution;
- report token, latency, execution and verification cost per successful task;
- show zero sealed-answer retrieval in deliberate contamination probes;
- preserve source, version, build, environment, rights and evidence identity on every published record.

The count targets are instrumentation goals, not quality claims. A capsule is not “verified” until an independent oracle has tested the exact version/environment-scoped claim.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 49. Final answer

The right question is not “which large corpus can we copy?” It is:

> Which next source gives Taedri the greatest marginal amount of attributable, searchable, compatible, composable, executable and independently verifiable capability knowledge?

Popular PyPI packages answer **what code people depend on**. Esoteric single-purpose packages often answer **one narrow question much more precisely**. Schemas, media registries, workflow catalogs, controller APIs and generator templates answer **what can connect, under which conditions**. Tests and issue histories answer **what behavior is true and how it fails**. Competitions answer **what users need systems to accomplish**. Sealed benchmarks answer **whether Taedri actually improved**.

Taedri should ingest all of these, but compile them into small registry-native capability capsules rather than retain them as monolithic library cards. Each capsule needs typed ports, conditional compatibility edges, version/build/environment scope, evidence, counterexamples, execution state, artifact rights and an exact receipt. The package or catalog remains the attributable source; the capsule becomes the cheap searchable and composable unit.

The practical first build is the eight-worker Esoteric Capability Worker Pack above. It tests the central bet across data, telemetry, media, Kubernetes, generators and benchmarks: that most requests can be satisfied by cheap deterministic retrieval and typed route solving, with local models and stronger LLMs used only for unresolved interpretation, composition or verification.

# Taedri RouterMesh and Code Entity Graph

> **ANNEX STATUS — TARGET ROUTING ARCHITECTURE.** The router portfolio, harness
> integrations, learning loop, and scale design are research/build targets. They are
> not a claim that a production routing fleet or self-optimizing service is operating.

**Deep research on cheap model routing, harness integration, universal code-entity representation, package-scale indexing, and execution-grounded learning**

**Research current through 2026-07-15**

## Executive answer

Yes—the combined idea is larger and stronger than a token-saving query waterfall.

The architecture should become two coupled control planes:

1.  **RouterMesh:** a typed, auditable system that chooses the cheapest safe action, context projection, model, provider, endpoint, verifier, and escalation path for each task node.
2.  **Code Entity Graph (CEG):** a language-neutral, evidence-bearing graph of packages, artifacts, files, symbols, functions, classes, variables, interfaces, tests, effects, calls, flows, builds, and observed behavior.

The graph makes routing cheaper and more accurate. It supplies exact task features—languages touched, graph radius, effect risk, dynamic dispatch, test coverage, interface stability, context size, and historical outcomes—so the router does not need to infer everything from a prose prompt. The router makes the graph usable without flooding a model with millions of nodes. It selects a tiny, task-specific projection and decides whether a deterministic tool, local model, small hosted model, strong model, or no model at all should act.

The target system is:

``` text
prompt / event / IDE state
        │
        ▼
ContextManifest + DemandIR + authority/policy
        │
        ├── exact handle / replay / deterministic tool ───────────────┐
        │                                                             │
        ▼                                                             │
Code Entity Graph: exact IDs → typed retrieval → local graph slice    │
        │                                                             │
        ▼                                                             │
Task features + eligible actions/models + verification plan           │
        │                                                             │
        ▼                                                             │
RouterMesh: deterministic → local ranker/SLM → learned router → LLM   │
        │                                                             │
        ▼                                                             │
Harness node + projected tools/context + immutable RouteLease          │
        │                                                             │
        ▼                                                             │
Provider gateway → deployment → endpoint/replica                      │
        │                                                             │
        ▼                                                             │
execute → verify → accept / repair / explicit escalate → exact receipt┘
        │
        ▼
execution-grounded outcome memory and cheaper future route
```

The key conclusion from current products and research is that **there is no single router to buy**. “Routing” currently names several different decisions. Azure, Bedrock, OpenRouter Auto, Not Diamond, Plano, LiteLLM, and vLLM Semantic Router address parts of task-to-model selection. Portkey, Bifrost, Kong, Cloudflare, Vercel, and LiteLLM are primarily provider policy and reliability layers. Kubernetes Gateway API Inference Extension chooses serving endpoints. LangGraph, Pydantic AI, Mastra, Google ADK, AutoGen, LlamaIndex, and similar frameworks route workflow nodes or agents. Temporal supplies durable recovery. None owns Taedri’s typed demand, code graph, application-specific truth, or independent verification.

Therefore, Taedri should own the portable semantic decision contract and use other systems as replaceable selector, gateway, harness, and runtime adapters.

### The most important design decisions

1.  **Do not globally rename program variables.** That breaks public APIs, reflection, serialization, ABI assumptions, stack traces, patches, examples, and developer comprehension. Assign collision-resistant sidecar IDs while preserving native names.
2.  **Do not invent one universal entity ID.** “Same bytes,” “same package release,” “same function in one build,” “same logical API across versions,” and “same bounded behavior” are different claims. Use an identity lattice.
3.  **Do not use one universal AST.** Preserve language-native indexes and compiler facts, then normalize a common envelope of identities, occurrences, ports, typed edges, effects, evidence, and provenance.
4.  **Do not let an AI gateway silently change semantic models.** Task-to-model selection, provider failover, and endpoint selection need separate receipts and failure rules.
5.  **Do not equate fallback with escalation.** A timeout retry, same-model provider failover, different-model availability fallback, verifier-triggered semantic escalation, formatting repair, and full replan are different state transitions.
6.  **Do not route from raw prompt alone.** Route from `DemandIR + CodeSliceManifest + policy + model profiles + cache state + verification plan`.
7.  **Do not train on conversational proxies when executable truth exists.** User corrections and “thanks” are weak signals. Prefer tests, schema validity, tool success, patch acceptance, security checks, and independent task oracles.
8.  **Do not expose every primitive or code entity as a tool.** Expose a small meta-tool surface for search, graph expansion, impact analysis, route solving, detail resolution, execution, and verification.
9.  **Do not pin a model blindly for an entire conversation.** Use phase- or task-node affinity with explicit reclassification triggers. Conversation-wide stickiness helps prompt caching but can trap later work on the wrong model.
10. **Do not optimize token price in isolation.** Optimize failure-inclusive cost per verified success: selection, generation, cache loss, retries, tools, verification, latency, and expected rework.

### Recommended first implementation

Build a **Python/PyPI vertical slice** with ecosystem-neutral contracts:

- package/release/source/distribution/build identity;
- SCIP-derived symbols, occurrences, definitions, references, imports, and type/interface facts;
- docs, tests, examples, package metadata, and evidence provenance;
- `DemandIR`, `CodeSliceManifest`, `ModelProfile`, `RouteRequest`, `RouteDecision`, `RouteLease`, `RouteOutcome`;
- hard eligibility gates, exact/history routes, deterministic complexity/task signals, and three selector arms: deterministic, local SLM/ranker, strong model;
- Pydantic AI and LangGraph adapters, with Mastra as the first TypeScript adapter;
- one provider gateway adapter, but no unrecorded model rewrite;
- post-selection body resolution, sandboxed execution, independent verification, and exact receipts;
- 1/2/4/8 route alternatives crossed with handle/card/signature/body detail levels;
- shadow evaluation against fixed-cheapest, fixed-frontier, and offline-oracle baselines.

Do not begin with all of PyPI, every programming language, an online contextual bandit, or a distributed graph database. Begin with 100–1,000 packages chosen to represent pure libraries, compiled extensions, dynamic frameworks, CLI tools, web clients, data packages, and poorly documented packages. Prove identity, extraction, incremental invalidation, route quality, and end-to-end savings before scaling.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 1. The corrected mental model: six routing planes plus an evidence plane

The market’s terminology hides different control problems. Treat them as explicit planes with different inputs, outputs, owners, and failure semantics.

| Plane                    | Decision                                                                           | Typical inputs                                          | Output                                           | Representative systems                                                  | Taedri ownership           |
|--------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------|
| R0 — action/bypass       | Does this require a generative model at all?                                       | Exact ID, command, AST, schema, history, policy         | Deterministic action, cached result, or continue | Compiler, parser, cache, rules, tools                                   | Own                        |
| R1 — semantic task/model | Which action or model is cheapest while meeting the task’s quality and risk floor? | DemandIR, graph slice, capabilities, outcome history    | Semantic model/action class                      | vLLM Semantic Router, Plano, Not Diamond, Azure Router, OpenRouter Auto | Own contract; plug in arms |
| R2 — provider/deployment | Where should the selected semantic model run?                                      | Model ID, region, policy, health, price, cache affinity | Provider/deployment                              | LiteLLM, Bifrost, Portkey, Kong, OpenRouter provider routing            | Adopt/adapter              |
| R3 — endpoint/replica    | Which GPU replica or inference endpoint should serve it?                           | Queue, prefix cache, LoRA, load, topology               | Endpoint                                         | Kubernetes Gateway API Inference Extension, serving scheduler           | Adopt                      |
| R4 — workflow/agent      | Which node, agent, tools, instructions, and permissions should act next?           | Typed workflow state and plan                           | Node/agent invocation                            | LangGraph, Google ADK, Mastra, AutoGen, LlamaIndex                      | Harness adapter            |
| R5 — post-result control | Accept, repair, retry, escalate, replan, or abstain?                               | Output, tool receipts, verifier evidence                | Explicit next state                              | Guardrails, validators, Temporal workflow                               | Own policy                 |
| E — evidence/learning    | What did the route actually accomplish, under what conditions?                     | All route and execution receipts                        | Calibrated profiles, caches, invalidations       | Eval pipelines, contextual bandits, OTel                                | Own truth                  |

This separation prevents five common errors:

- choosing a gateway because it advertises “smart routing” when it only load-balances providers;
- allowing a gateway to rewrite a model without rechecking tool or output-schema capability;
- escalating to a stronger model for a provider rate limit;
- retrying a mutating tool call because an orchestration framework catches every exception;
- training the semantic router on endpoint latency or conversational sentiment rather than task success.

### 1.1 Planes may be colocated, but their contracts must remain separate

A first deployment can be one modular process. The planes are semantic boundaries, not service mandates. A single broker can implement R0, R1, and R5; LiteLLM or Bifrost can implement R2; a local vLLM scheduler can implement R3; and Pydantic AI or LangGraph can implement R4. Split services only when scale, security isolation, ownership, or availability requires it.

### 1.2 The semantic router selects a bundle, not just a model name

The real decision is:

``` text
RouteBundle =
  action/model
  prompt program
  context projection
  primitive/tool projection
  token/reasoning budget
  provider eligibility policy
  retry/fallback policy
  verifier policy
  affinity scope
```

A cheap model with 40,000 unnecessary context tokens may cost more than a stronger model receiving a 2,000-token verified slice. A model that generates valid prose but cannot reliably call the required tools is not eligible. A model that is cheap to call but often requires repair and verification escalation may be more expensive per accepted result.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 2. The expanded cheap-to-expensive waterfall

This is a conditional action graph, not a rule that every request must traverse every level.

| Level | Mechanism                                                         |   Provider calls | Appropriate output                          | Main guardrail                                   |
|------:|-------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------:|---------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
|     0 | Hard policy, authorization, residency, modality, capability gates |                0 | Eligible action/model set                   | Fail closed on prohibited effects                |
|     1 | Explicit handle, exact command, exact package/symbol/standard ID  |                0 | Direct entity or action                     | Revalidate epoch and authority                   |
|     2 | Exact request/route/result replay                                 |                0 | Bound prior route/result                    | Match demand, graph, policy, environment, oracle |
|     3 | Deterministic templates and structured slot extraction            |                0 | QueryIR or GraphIR                          | Grammar and schema validation                    |
|     4 | Exact/history/fielded lexical retrieval                           |                0 | Candidate entities/routes                   | Tenant-scoped indexes                            |
|     5 | Typed bidirectional graph solving                                 |                0 | Compatible route handles                    | Effects, types, capability, lifecycle            |
|     6 | Cheap signals and classifiers                                     |                0 | Task/domain/complexity/risk features        | Explicit `unknown` outcome                       |
|     7 | Local embeddings, sparse model, ranker, or local SLM              |         0 hosted | Reranked routes or structured fields        | Confidence/calibration and latency budget        |
|     8 | Application-trained outcome router or contextual bandit           | 0 hosted or tiny | Model/action choice                         | Exploration propensity and drift control         |
|     9 | Cheap hosted general model                                        |          1 small | Resolve bounded ambiguity or choose handles | Strict output schema and context cap             |
|    10 | Strong model on unresolved delta                                  |         1 strong | Novel plan, adapter, or difficult selection | Full compiler/verifier validation                |
|    11 | Bounded cascade, panel, or fusion                                 |          several | High-value uncertainty reduction            | Explicit value-of-information gate               |
|    12 | Human clarification/review or safe abstention                     |           varies | Discriminating input or decision            | Do not invent missing authority or truth         |

Every stage implements the same small protocol:

``` text
accept(route_or_action, confidence, expected_regret)
abstain(reason, missing_information)
escalate(next_arm, required_signal, spend_ceiling)
```

This is more useful than forcing every arm to emit a model name. An exact tool path can accept. A local classifier can abstain. A strong model can request a missing graph field instead of consuming the full repository.

### 2.1 Additional paths beyond the waterfall

The controller should also support:

- **verification-first planning:** start with available oracles and search only for routes they can certify;
- **probe-first discrimination:** run harmless examples against ambiguous candidates instead of asking another model;
- **counterexample-guided refinement:** compile/test a route, add the failure as a constraint, and search again;
- **route-macro retrieval:** reuse a verified topology and bind new parameters;
- **tool-first parsing:** use AST, compiler, schema, file state, or UI selection to establish intent;
- **clarification-first routing:** ask one question when it eliminates more expected cost than another retrieval/model step;
- **offline compile/online execute:** prebuild routes, proofs, summaries, and model policies for frequent task families;
- **portfolio selection:** choose among retrieval and solver algorithms before choosing an LLM;
- **shadow exploration:** invoke a non-serving candidate only on sampled traffic to learn without risking the user result;
- **safe no-op:** return an incompatibility or unverifiability certificate when no admissible route exists.

## 3. Current router and gateway landscape

Product details in this section are current as of 2026-07-15 and are volatile. Treat every external router as a benchmark arm behind Taedri’s contract, not as permanent truth.

### 3.1 Task-to-model routers

| System                                                                                                             | Actual routing mechanism                                                                                        | Strongest idea                                                                                                                                           | Material limitation                                                                                              | Taedri use                                                     |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| [vLLM Semantic Router](https://vllm-sr.ai/)                                                                        | Composable heuristic and learned signals feed configurable decisions and multiple selection algorithms          | Best open reference for signal → decision → selector → plugin separation; deployment via Envoy/Gateway API/Kubernetes/local; replay and OTel orientation | Young, operationally broad, and application calibration is not automatic                                         | Reference implementation and experimental arm                  |
| [Plano](https://docs.planoai.dev/guides/llm_router.html)                                                           | Local 1.5B router maps requests to domain/action preferences, then can optimize candidate order by cost/latency | Separates task classification, declared preferences, and economic ordering; explicit model affinity                                                      | Description match is not execution success; documentation/version maturity risk                                  | Local-SLM arm and affinity reference                           |
| [Bifrost Complexity Router](https://docs.getbifrost.ai/features/governance/complexity-router)                      | Deterministic prompt signals produce SIMPLE/MEDIUM/COMPLEX/REASONING, then CEL rules route                      | Zero-model, sub-millisecond-style first arm with explicit unknown/fallthrough                                                                            | Complexity is only one feature; lexical rules are language/domain brittle                                        | Implement an equivalent local baseline                         |
| [LiteLLM Auto Routing](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/auto_routing)                                            | Heuristic, keyword/semantic, or LLM classification into tiers; random or Thompson-sampled model pools           | Packaged multi-arm waterfall, cause logs, session affinity                                                                                               | Extremely new/experimental in July 2026; semantic mode adds latency; adaptive feedback has documented weaknesses | Evaluate, do not make foundational                             |
| [LiteLLM Adaptive Router](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/adaptive_router)                                            | Request-type quality/cost observations influence model choice                                                   | Practical online adaptation interface                                                                                                                    | Beta; no latency scoring; English-biased feedback heuristics; capped/no-decay observation behavior               | Borrow arm interface, replace learning logic                   |
| [OpenRouter Auto](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/routers/auto-router)                                   | Opaque router powered by Not Diamond chooses from a curated changing pool                                       | Allowed-model patterns, cost/quality knob, actual model return, session stickiness                                                                       | Opaque uncertainty/training and changing pool; cloud dependency                                                  | External comparison arm only                                   |
| [Not Diamond](https://docs.notdiamond.ai/docs/what-is-model-routing)                                               | Decision-only API; pretrained or custom router trained from prompts, outputs, and eval scores                   | Clean selector/executor split; application-specific offline training                                                                                     | Public contract is light on calibration, propensities, drift, and OPE                                            | Training/API pattern, not source of truth                      |
| [Azure Model Router](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/concepts/model-router)                 | Managed predictor uses prompt complexity, reasoning, and task type to select an underlying model                | Explicit quality-regret bands: Balanced, Cost, Quality; allowed model subsets                                                                            | Opaque and updated in place; smallest candidate can constrain context; routing can reduce cache hits             | Copy regret-budget abstraction; pin Taedri policy epochs       |
| [AWS Bedrock Intelligent Prompt Routing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-routing.html) | Predictor chooses between exactly two same-family models using a quality-difference threshold                   | Very clear fallback-anchor baseline                                                                                                                      | Preview, English-only, two models/same family, no application-specific learning                                  | Baseline arm                                                   |
| [OpenRouter Pareto Code](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/routers/pareto-router)                          | User sets coding-capability tier; router chooses cheapest or fastest candidate meeting it                       | Qualify first, optimize economics second                                                                                                                 | Coding-only; relative benchmark percentile drifts                                                                | Copy capability-floor pattern with Taedri-owned absolute evals |
| [Kong semantic balancing](https://developer.konghq.com/plugins/ai-proxy-advanced/examples/semantic/)               | Embedding similarity between request and model-specialty descriptions                                           | Simple, interpretable candidate generation                                                                                                               | Description similarity is not capability or measured success                                                     | Candidate nomination only                                      |
| [Requesty Smart Routing](https://docs.requesty.ai/features/smart-routing)                                          | Public docs claim task-aware model choice                                                                       | Convenient external arm inside a broader gateway                                                                                                         | Insufficient public detail on signals, confidence, training, and evaluation                                      | Treat as opaque benchmark only                                 |

Two managed examples demonstrate why Taedri must own versioning. Azure documents a router version that can update its underlying pool and behavior; OpenRouter Auto can also change its curated pool. Those conveniences are reasonable for general chat but conflict with reproducible plan replay. Taedri should pin `RouterPolicyEpoch`, `ModelProfileEpoch`, and `CandidateSetHash` in every `RouteLease`.

### 3.2 Provider and policy gateways

These systems are valuable below semantic routing:

| System                                                                                               | Best role                                                                                                | Not sufficient for                                                               |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [Bifrost](https://docs.getbifrost.ai/overview)                                                       | High-performance provider normalization, retries/fallbacks, governance, caching, CEL routing, OTel, MCP  | Application-specific semantic quality decision by itself                         |
| [LiteLLM](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/routing)                                                      | Broad provider abstraction, load balancing, cooldown, fallbacks, budgets, distributed state              | Typed code-task truth unless Taedri supplies it                                  |
| [Portkey](https://portkey.ai/docs/product/ai-gateway)                                                | Conditional metadata/body/path policies, fallbacks, cache, budgets, guardrails, canaries                 | Inferring task semantics that are not already metadata                           |
| [Kong AI Gateway](https://developer.konghq.com/ai-gateway/)                                          | Enterprise plugin chain: routing, RAG, PII, cache, MCP/A2A, load balancing, OTel                         | Portable semantic selector without enterprise/platform coupling                  |
| [Cloudflare Dynamic Routing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/features/dynamic-routing/) | Versioned deterministic visual/JSON flow with conditions, splits, rate/budget nodes, deployment/rollback | Learned task-to-model capability choice                                          |
| [Vercel AI Gateway](https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway)                                              | Unified provider surface, provider routing/fallbacks, AI SDK integration                                 | Stable semantic control plane; routing rules remain beta and mostly rewrite/deny |
| [OpenRouter provider selection](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/provider-selection)        | Health, price, latency, throughput, region, privacy, quantization, parameter-aware provider selection    | Choosing which semantic model the task needs                                     |
| [Envoy AI Gateway](https://aigateway.envoyproxy.io/docs/)                                            | Kubernetes-native policy and provider traffic plane                                                      | Task-specific quality prediction                                                 |
| [Kubernetes Gateway API Inference Extension](https://gateway-api-inference-extension.sigs.k8s.io/)   | Replica selection using serving state such as queue, prefix cache, and adapter availability              | Prompt/task → semantic model selection                                           |

Cloudflare’s versioned route graph is worth copying as a `RouterPolicy` authoring experience. Bifrost and Portkey demonstrate why deterministic policy should consume typed request metadata. OpenRouter’s clean separation between model and provider routing is the correct conceptual boundary. Kubernetes Inference Extension belongs beneath all of them for self-hosted replicas.

### 3.3 Important product-status corrections

- LiteLLM Auto Routing was extremely new in mid-July 2026; evaluate it as experimental.
- Cloudflare Dynamic Routing and Vercel Routing Rules are beta.
- AWS still documents intelligent prompt routing as preview.
- ArchGW has evolved into Plano; use current Plano documentation rather than old Arch comparisons.
- TensorZero’s repository was archived in June 2026; its evaluation ideas remain useful, but it is not a prudent new dependency.
- Current Martian public docs emphasize a gateway/integrations rather than a sufficiently documented learned router.
- Old comparisons of Unify as a standalone router are stale after its product shift.
- Do not list a general Vertex cross-model router based on outdated secondary comparisons; current official evidence supports other optimizer products, not an equivalent control plane.

## 4. Academic routing methods and what they really buy

Academic results are useful design evidence, not production guarantees. Many use static benchmark matrices, binary strong/weak pools, one-shot prompts, nominal prices, or LLM judges. Taedri’s coding and primitive workloads require execution-grounded, step-level evaluation.

| Method family                   | Mechanism                                                               | Representative primary work                                     | Best use                                            | Failure mode                                                          |
|---------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Static rules                    | Length, keywords, task/domain, complexity thresholds                    | Production baselines such as Bifrost complexity                 | Cheapest initial arm                                | Brittle, biased, cannot learn model-specific success                  |
| Similarity/profile match        | Embed request and model/task descriptions                               | Kong semantic routing; similarity baselines                     | Candidate narrowing and cold start                  | Semantic similarity ≠ capability                                      |
| Preference classifier           | Predict strong-vs-weak win from prompt                                  | [RouteLLM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.18665)                    | Binary downgrade policy with preference data        | Preference labels may not match application correctness               |
| Matrix factorization            | Learn query and model latent factors                                    | RouteLLM variants                                               | Sparse multi-model performance surfaces             | New tasks/models and distribution shift                               |
| Heterogeneous graph             | Task/query/model nodes and predicted effect/cost edges                  | [GraphRouter](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.03834)                 | Natural match for Taedri’s task/entity/model graph  | Predicted edges still require calibration and live evidence           |
| Capability/domain-action router | Map prompt to interpretable task labels, then match model profiles      | [Arch-Router](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.16655)                 | Transparent cold start and adding candidates        | User preference/profile may diverge from actual success               |
| Pre-generation selector         | Predict best model before any answer                                    | RouteLLM, Hybrid LLM                                            | One paid generation per request                     | Router must infer difficulty without answer evidence                  |
| Cascades                        | Invoke cheap model, accept or escalate based on confidence              | [FrugalGPT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.05176)                   | Tasks with cheap reliable verifier/confidence       | Multiple calls; confidence may be uncalibrated                        |
| Self-verifying cascade          | Small model produces answer and self-verifies; POMDP chooses escalation | [AutoMix](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.12963)                     | Bounded QA/reasoning with useful self-signal        | Self-verification errors are correlated with generation errors        |
| Calibrated uncertainty          | Calibrate token/answer uncertainty then choose cost-optimal threshold   | [UCCI](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.18796)                        | Narrow repeated classification/generation tasks     | Assumptions and calibration may not transfer to open-ended agent work |
| Conformal/cost control          | Bound budget or regret using calibration sets                           | [C3PO](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.07396)                        | Explicit probabilistic budget constraints           | Guarantees depend on exchangeability and evaluation setup             |
| Contextual bandit               | Explore models and update expected reward/cost online                   | Recent budget-paced and correlation-aware routing work          | Non-stationary model pools with observable outcomes | Exploration harms, delayed/partial reward, selection bias             |
| Execution-grounded agent router | Context → action → verifier feedback → memory                           | [Agent-as-a-Router](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22902)           | Coding tasks with tests and streaming outcomes      | New work; memory contamination and benchmark transfer need scrutiny   |
| Signal composition              | Many cheap/learned signals feed declarative rules and selectors         | [vLLM Semantic Router report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.04444) | Enterprise policy and mixed routing arms            | Complexity and operational calibration                                |
| Multi-model fusion              | Generate several answers and judge/merge                                | OpenRouter Fusion; ensemble research                            | Rare high-value uncertainty                         | Multiplies cost and correlated judge error                            |

### 4.1 The important shift: from one-shot classification to closed-loop routing

[Agent-as-a-Router](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22902) is especially relevant because it frames routing as `Context → Action → Feedback → Context` and evaluates coding tasks using verified outcomes. Its reported finding—that adding task-dimension performance statistics materially improves a generic router—supports Taedri’s thesis that a code/entity graph and historical task outcomes can matter more than a larger router model.

The implication is not “put an agent in charge of everything.” It is:

- create structured task dimensions from the code graph;
- select an action/model with a recorded propensity;
- observe independent execution outcomes;
- update time-scoped, conditional model evidence;
- never rewrite exact semantic facts with behavioral heuristics;
- retain a fixed holdout and shadow exploration path.

### 4.2 Why standard router benchmarks are insufficient

[RouterBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.12031) provides a valuable multi-model outcome matrix, but ordinary offline matrices do not reproduce:

- multi-turn context accumulation;
- tool availability and schema size;
- prompt-cache effects;
- intermediate node choice in an agent trajectory;
- side effects and retry safety;
- provider outages and version drift;
- verification cost;
- a cheaper model changing downstream behavior even when its immediate answer looks acceptable.

Recent step-level and live-agent benchmark proposals such as [TwinRouterBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.18859) point in the right direction: expose the router-visible prefix at each node and score final task resolution and realized spend. Taedri should use this pattern but retain its own workload, graph features, exact receipts, and oracles.

### 4.3 Recommended selector portfolio

Implement all selectors behind one interface:

``` text
SelectorArm.select(RouteRequest, CandidateSet, spend_limit)
  -> Accept(RouteDecision)
   | Abstain(reason)
   | Escalate(next_arm, missing_signal)
```

Initial arms:

1.  Fixed cheapest eligible.
2.  Fixed strongest eligible.
3.  Deterministic task/domain/complexity/risk rules.
4.  Historical exact-cell lookup.
5.  k-nearest successful task/model cells.
6.  Local logistic/GBDT/ranker over typed features.
7.  Local domain-action SLM.
8.  Application-trained pairwise or listwise router.
9.  Contextual bandit with bounded exploration.
10. Cheap general LLM classifier.
11. Strong-model selector on candidate deltas.
12. Post-answer calibrated cascade/verifier.
13. External OpenRouter/Not Diamond/Azure/vLLM arms.
14. Human policy override.

Do not force one winner globally. Learn a meta-policy by task family, risk class, data locality, and available verifier.

## 5. Harness and orchestration integration

No current harness implements Taedri’s whole system. The clean architecture is:

``` text
durable workflow (optional, outermost)
  └─ harness / agent graph
       └─ Taedri semantic broker and RouteLease
            └─ typed prompt/tool/context projection
                 └─ provider gateway
                      └─ endpoint scheduler
```

### 5.1 Framework insertion matrix

| Framework                                                                                                                    | Best insertion point                                           | What it enables                                                                               | Critical caution                                                                                              |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [Pydantic AI](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/overview/)                                                                 | `before_model_request`; set the request-context model per call | Typed models/outputs, tool filters, usage limits, concurrency, fallback, durable integrations | Validation often retries the same model; response-based fallback is non-streaming; side effects need barriers |
| [LangChain middleware](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/middleware/overview)                                  | `wrap_model_call`; override `request.model`                    | Per-turn selection, context/tool middleware, retries, deferred schema loading                 | Some dynamically selected pre-bound models conflict with structured-output paths                              |
| [LangGraph](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/graph-api)                                                       | Deterministic broker node and conditional edges                | Typed state, checkpoints, loops, interrupts, subgraphs                                        | Workflow-edge routing and model routing must remain distinct; mixed static/dynamic edges can surprise         |
| [Google ADK model routing](https://adk.dev/agents/models/routing/)                                                           | Experimental `RoutedLlm`                                       | Explicit candidates, async classifier, failure context, A/B/fallback                          | TypeScript-only and experimental; failover only before output is emitted                                      |
| [Google ADK agent routing](https://adk.dev/agents/routing/)                                                                  | Experimental `RoutedAgent`                                     | Change model, instructions, tools, and policy as a unit                                       | Partial event emission disables failover                                                                      |
| [Mastra processors](https://mastra.ai/docs/agents/processors)                                                                | `processInputStep` or `prepareStep` before every turn          | Override model, tools, tool choice, system content; typed request context and workflows       | Generic callbacks/retries need Taedri’s explicit error taxonomy                                               |
| [OpenAI Agents SDK](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/models/)                                                   | Custom `ModelProvider`, per-agent model, or run-level override | Typed tools/output, hooks, handoffs, guardrails, traces, durable integrations                 | Multi-provider prefix routing is not semantic task routing; per-turn swap surface is less direct              |
| [Semantic Kernel filters](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/semantic-kernel/concepts/enterprise-readiness/filters)           | Prompt/function/auto-function invocation filters               | Cache, request modification, result override, alternate service, early termination            | DI filter order is not guaranteed; direct service calls can bypass filters                                    |
| [AutoGen model clients](https://microsoft.github.io/autogen/stable/user-guide/core-user-guide/components/model-clients.html) | Custom `ChatCompletionClient` and candidate function           | Typed messages, cache, usage, candidate narrowing, speaker selection                          | No built-in application quality/cost router; some subscriber errors are only logged                           |
| [LlamaIndex workflows](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/python/llamaagents/workflows/)                                       | Inject Taedri broker as resource                               | Typed events; retrieval/tool routing; large-choice selectors                                  | Its routers mainly select engines/tools, not semantic models                                                  |
| [Haystack ConditionalRouter](https://docs.haystack.deepset.ai/docs/conditionalrouter)                                        | Cheap deterministic early branch                               | Typed pipeline paths, loops, parallel branches                                                | Optional type validation and unsafe-template risks                                                            |
| [Strands hooks/providers](https://strandsagents.com/latest/documentation/docs/user-guide/concepts/agents/hooks/)             | Custom provider wrapper                                        | Typed lifecycle hooks, tool interception, broad model support                                 | No clearly documented direct per-turn swap; shared mutable config risks races                                 |
| [BAML](https://docs.boundaryml.com/guide/baml-advanced/llm-client-registry)                                                  | Client selection per typed prompt function                     | Typed outputs, runtime client override, assertions, fallback accounting                       | Failure fallback is not semantic selection; put Taedri in front                                               |
| [DSPy](https://dspy.ai/getting-started/gepa-optimization/)                                                                   | Offline compile/distill                                        | Optimize cheap specialist programs using task metrics and stronger reflection                 | Not a hot-path router or durable workflow engine                                                              |
| [Temporal](https://docs.temporal.io/workflows)                                                                               | Outer execution layer                                          | Durable event history, explicit retry policies, long-running recovery                         | LLM/tool calls must be Activities and can re-execute; require idempotency                                     |
| [Prefect](https://docs.prefect.io/v3/how-to-guides/workflows/write-and-run)                                                  | Evaluation and medium-durability batch workflows               | Tasks, cache, retries, rate/concurrency controls                                              | Blocking sync calls may outlive thread timeout                                                                |
| [Dagster](https://docs.dagster.io/guides/test/asset-checks)                                                                  | Router datasets, model profiles, promotion gates               | Assets, lineage, partitions, checks                                                           | Better offline than conversational hot path                                                                   |

### 5.2 Google ADK’s failure contract is worth generalizing

The experimental Google ADK router receives candidate models or agents, the current request/context, and failure context containing failed keys and the last error. It disallows selecting an already failed candidate and only permits failover before output has been yielded. That is a strong reference contract.

Taedri should generalize it:

``` text
route(candidates, RouteRequest, FailureContext?)
  -> candidate_key | repair | replan | stop

FailureContext {
  failed_candidate_keys[]
  last_error_class
  first_output_emitted
  committed_effect_receipts[]
  remaining_budget
  prior_verifier_results[]
}
```

Once a stream is visible, Taedri must not secretly splice a second model into it. Once a side effect commits, it must not replay the call unless idempotency or compensation is explicitly proven.

### 5.3 Codex integration

Current Codex documentation supports:

- a built-in OpenAI provider redirected through `openai_base_url`;
- custom model providers with base URL, wire API, authentication, headers, retry and stream settings;
- local OSS providers such as Ollama or LM Studio;
- project/user configuration, agent role config files, MCP, skills, hooks, and OpenTelemetry.

Useful official references include [Codex configuration](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file), [hooks](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks), [skills](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills), [MCP](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp), and [AGENTS.md](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md).

Recommended Codex pattern:

1.  Point the provider at a Taedri-compatible Responses API gateway or use a verified custom provider.
2.  Route per API request inside the broker, because the provider configuration is otherwise a broader session/run setting.
3.  Use agent role config files when predictable role-level model tiers are enough.
4.  Use hooks for deterministic prompt screening, tool policy, receipts, verification triggers, and stop checks—not as the sole semantic router.
5.  Use `AGENTS.md` for durable repo conventions and compact routing guidance.
6.  Use skills for progressively disclosed workflows and scripts.
7.  Use MCP meta-tools for graph search/expansion/execution instead of one tool per entity.
8.  Export route and tool spans through OTel with prompts redacted by default.

An “OpenAI-compatible” base URL is only the beginning of compatibility. The adapter test suite must verify the exact wire API, streaming events, tool-call semantics, structured output, reasoning fields, response IDs, cache behavior, retries, cancellations, and error taxonomy.

### 5.4 Claude Code and other coding harnesses

For Claude Code, `CLAUDE.md`, skills, hooks, agents, MCP, and an Anthropic-compatible gateway can express similar responsibilities. The division should remain:

- `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`: concise durable rules and where to look;
- skill: on-demand procedure, examples, and helper scripts;
- hook: mechanical policy, redaction, tool admission, receipts, post-run checks;
- agent: isolated task/node with a bounded context/tool/model policy;
- MCP: external capabilities and compact searchable resources;
- Taedri broker: actual model eligibility, cost/quality/risk decision, and lease;
- gateway: provider health and transport.

Prompts can teach thrift. Only code can enforce budgets, residency, permissions, retry safety, and exact receipts.

### 5.5 Harness adapter interface

Every harness adapter should implement:

``` text
capture_state() -> HarnessState
build_route_request(HarnessState, DemandIR, CodeSliceManifest) -> RouteRequest
apply_route_lease(RouteLease) -> model + prompt + tools + context + budgets
capture_attempt() -> AttemptReceipt
settle_outcome(RouteOutcome)
```

Do not embed the full waterfall separately into every framework. Keep one broker and thin adapters.
