## 6. Progressive primitive and tool disclosure

The user’s primitive thesis is strongly supported by current tool orchestration work. [Bifrost Code Mode](https://docs.getbifrost.ai/mcp/code-mode), for example, replaces a large injected MCP catalog with four meta-operations: list virtual tool files, read compact signatures, resolve detailed docs for a selected tool, and execute a short orchestration program inside a restricted sandbox. Its vendor benchmark reports large input-token reductions as tool count grows; those exact numbers require independent replication, but the mechanism is directly applicable.

Recommended disclosure ladder:

| Level | Model sees                                        | Use                                        |
|------:|---------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
|    D0 | Opaque entity/route handle                        | Exact replay or deterministic choice       |
|    D1 | Name, kind, one-line contract, trust/cost         | Broad candidate ranking                    |
|    D2 | Typed ports, effects, errors, runtime constraints | Compatibility and composition              |
|    D3 | Decisive edge neighborhood and contrastive delta  | Resolve ambiguity among finalists          |
|    D4 | Full card, examples, tests, detailed docs         | Difficult selection or planning            |
|    D5 | Selected implementation body                      | Post-selection modification/execution only |

### 6.1 Adaptive number of primitives and edges

More is not inherently safer. Duplicates increase context cost, selection entropy, position bias, and the illusion that repeated correlated claims are independent evidence.

Use this sequence:

1.  Apply hard type, capability, effect, authority, lifecycle, runtime, and license filters.
2.  Cluster equivalent or near-duplicate candidates.
3.  Preserve variants only when they differ in trust, provenance, cost/latency, failure domain, or controlled experimental value.
4.  Rank by marginal edge coverage and failure-mode diversity.
5.  Begin with `k=1`; expand to `2/4/8` only when coverage or decision margin is inadequate.
6.  Expose route deltas relative to the current best instead of repeating full cards.
7.  Let the selector request one additional field or edge family by handle.

Adaptive stopping target:

``` text
choose the smallest k such that
P(at least one eligible route in top-k | evidence) >= coverage_target
and marginal value(route k+1) <= disclosure + selection + latency cost
```

### 6.2 Meta-tools, not entity tools

Recommended stable surface:

``` text
entity_resolve(exact_id | native_symbol | package_coordinate)
entity_search(DemandIR, fields, filters, limit)
graph_expand(handles, edge_types, direction, budget)
impact_analyze(handles, change_kind, scope)
route_solve(DemandIR, candidate_handles, constraints)
route_compare(route_handles, requested_deltas)
detail_resolve(handles, detail_level)
route_compile(route_handle, environment)
route_execute(compiled_handle, bound_inputs, authority_lease)
route_verify(execution_receipt, oracle_plan)
```

This surface stays small even if the graph grows to billions of occurrences.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 7. Universal code representation: a bridge standard, not a replacement universe

No existing standard jointly represents package identity, exact source, logical symbol lineage, occurrences, calls, control/data flow, tests, effects, builds, licensing, runtime behavior, and retrieval projections. The right design is a thin language-neutral **Code Entity Graph Interchange** that composes and preserves existing precise formats.

### 7.1 What to reuse

| Standard/system                                                                                    | Reuse for                                                                         | Do not expect it to solve                                     |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| [SCIP](https://github.com/scip-code/scip)                                                          | Symbols, descriptors, occurrences, definitions, references, implementations, docs | Rich effects, builds, data flow, behavior, provenance         |
| [Kythe schema](https://kythe.io/docs/schema/)                                                      | Language-neutral fact/edge kernel, VName ideas, reverse adjacency                 | Complete package/build identity and evidence semantics        |
| [LSP](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.18/specification/) | Live editor/compiler operations                                                   | Durable global index identity                                 |
| LSIF                                                                                               | Legacy persisted navigation answers                                               | Modern mergeable global identity; prefer SCIP for new indexes |
| [Tree-sitter](https://tree-sitter.github.io/tree-sitter/)                                          | Cheap incremental syntax and broad language coverage                              | Authoritative cross-file resolution                           |
| [Universal Ctags](https://docs.ctags.io/en/latest/man/ctags.1.html)                                | Very cheap declaration/tag coverage                                               | Precise semantic binding                                      |
| [Glean](https://github.com/facebookincubator/Glean)                                                | Scalable fact storage, derivation, and querying patterns                          | Universal interchange ontology                                |
| [CodeQL](https://codeql.github.com/docs/codeql-overview/about-codeql/)                             | Language-specific deep semantic/security/data/control-flow facts                  | Shared identity/interchange schema across all languages       |
| [Code Property Graph / Joern](https://docs.joern.io/code-property-graph/)                          | Unified AST/call/control/data-flow relation families                              | Package/build/global lineage                                  |
| [Package URL](https://www.packageurl.org/docs/purl/introduction)                                   | Ecosystem package/release coordinates                                             | Exact source, build, or internal entity                       |
| [SWHID](https://www.swhid.org/specification/v1.1/)                                                 | Intrinsic source content, trees, snapshots, revisions                             | Logical symbol continuity across changes                      |
| [SPDX 3](https://spdx.github.io/spdx-spec/v3.0.1/) / CycloneDX                                     | Artifacts, packages, files, dependencies, licenses, vulnerabilities               | Function-level semantics                                      |
| [SLSA provenance](https://slsa.dev/spec/v1.2/provenance) / in-toto                                 | Build recipe, inputs, producer, artifact provenance                               | Source-level calls and behavior                               |
| [PROV-O](https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/)                                                            | Derivation and evidence provenance vocabulary                                     | Efficient hot-path storage by itself                          |
| OpenAPI, protobuf, GraphQL, WIT                                                                    | External interface projections                                                    | Implementation behavior and hidden effects                    |
| MLIR/compiler IR                                                                                   | Precise compiler-stage structure for supported languages                          | Source archive and ecosystem-wide identity                    |

SCIP already treats a symbol as URI-like and includes package manager/name/version plus fully qualified descriptors; occurrences bind source ranges to symbols and roles. Kythe supplies a rich typed-edge vocabulary and VName fields for language, corpus, root, path, and signature. CodeQL creates a language-specific relational representation with AST, data-flow, and control-flow structures. Glean demonstrates scalable code facts, cross-references, call/type hierarchies, and derived queries. These are complementary, not mutually exclusive.

### 7.2 Preserve native precision

Every normalized node or edge should reference the native fact bundle and extractor version that produced it. Do not flatten away:

- overload resolution details;
- compiler flags and target platform;
- dynamic-dispatch candidate sets;
- macro/generated-source provenance;
- path-sensitive data-flow steps;
- analyzer-specific may/must semantics;
- language-specific type relationships;
- build dependency closure.

Canonical interchange can be Protobuf or Arrow/Parquet shards. JSON is useful for debugging and API boundaries. JSON-LD/RDF is useful for exchange or federation, not necessarily as the primary hot store.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 8. Identity: preserve names, add a lattice of exact and logical IDs

### 8.1 Why globally unique source variable names are unsafe

Renaming every variable, class, method, and function to a global identifier would cause more damage than value:

- public import and API breakage;
- ABI and foreign-function-interface breakage;
- reflection and dynamic attribute lookup failures;
- serialization/deserialization incompatibility;
- database/ORM field mismatch;
- configuration and dependency-injection lookup failures;
- generated-code and macro mismatch;
- documentation, examples, logs, stack traces, patches, and developer mental models diverging from source;
- third-party upgrades becoming unmergeable;
- hash/name leakage of private repository structure;
- name length and toolchain limits.

Use a sidecar ID. Native names remain display and source coordinates. The graph attaches exact IDs to source occurrences without changing the program.

### 8.2 Identity lattice

| ID                 | Answers                                                            | Construction                                                                           |
|--------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `PackageLineageID` | Which registry package family?                                     | Ecosystem + registry authority + normalization-rules version + canonical/original name |
| `ReleaseID`        | Which published version?                                           | Exact purl, including version and relevant qualifiers                                  |
| `SourceSnapshotID` | Which exact revision/tree/content?                                 | SWHID or equivalent content-addressed source identifier                                |
| `DistributionID`   | Which exact wheel/sdist/JAR/crate/image/binary?                    | Cryptographic artifact digest                                                          |
| `BuildID`          | Which build under which recipe/toolchain/platform/inputs?          | Artifact digest + SLSA/in-toto provenance and closure digest                           |
| `FileContentID`    | Which exact file bytes?                                            | Content hash/SWHID content ID                                                          |
| `OccurrenceID`     | Which exact range and role in exact file bytes?                    | File ID + byte range + role + occurrence discriminator                                 |
| `RevisionEntityID` | Which symbol/entity in one source/build context?                   | Snapshot/build + language + kind + structured symbol locator/signature                 |
| `ConceptID`        | Which logical API/entity lineage across revisions?                 | Versioned evidence-backed registry assertion                                           |
| `BehaviorID`       | Which bounded behavior under an input/environment/oracle contract? | Entity/build + domain + environment + oracle + result evidence                         |

`ConceptID` is not a content hash. It is a revisable claim. A rename, split, merge, copy, fork, or generated derivative creates evidence-bearing lineage edges such as `renamed_from`, `split_into`, `merged_from`, `forked_from`, `generated_from`, `supersedes`, and `same_concept_as`. Never destructively merge nodes merely because a heuristic predicts equivalence.

For locals, lambdas, anonymous types, macros, and generated identifiers, cross-version identity is often indefensible. Retain exact occurrence/revision identity and make any lineage match probabilistic and reversible.

### 8.3 Collision-resistant external ID

``` text
ExternalID =
  "ceg:v1:" + entity_kind + ":" +
  base32(sha256(canonical_cbor(identity_key)))
```

Store and compare the complete canonical identity key as well as its digest. A digest is an efficient lookup key, not the only source of truth. Identity keys retain registry authority, ecosystem normalization version, original spelling, exact package/source/build context, language, entity kind, locator scheme/version, descriptors, and structured signature.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 9. Core Code Entity Graph contracts

### 9.1 Artifact identity

``` yaml
ArtifactIdentity:
  artifact_id: ceg:v1:artifact:...
  package_lineage_id: optional
  purl: optional
  registry_origin: optional-but-required-for-registry-content
  source_swhid: optional
  repository_origin: optional
  revision: optional
  distribution_digest: optional
  build_id: optional
  target_platform: optional
  dependency_closure_digest: optional
  provenance_ref: optional
  license_evidence_refs: []
```

Registry authority remains explicit even when a purl exists. This prevents public/private registry collisions and dependency-confusion mistakes.

### 9.2 Entity node

``` yaml
EntityNode:
  revision_entity_id: ceg:v1:entity:...
  concept_id: optional
  artifact_id: ceg:v1:artifact:...
  kind: function|method|class|variable|endpoint|test|...
  language: python
  native_names: []
  canonical_descriptors: []
  structured_signature: {}
  visibility: public|protected|private|local|generated
  occurrence_ids: []
  input_ports: []
  output_ports: []
  error_ports: []
  capability_requirements: []
  effect_claims: []
  documentation_refs: []
  body_ast_digest: optional
  api_shape_digest: optional
  native_fact_bundle_ref: cas:...
  schema_version: 1
```

Entity kinds include ecosystem, registry, package, release, distribution, repository, snapshot, directory, file, module, namespace, class, struct, trait, interface, enum, type, alias, function, method, constructor, field, property, variable, constant, parameter, type parameter, macro, annotation, decorator, endpoint, command, event, schema, resource, test suite/case/fixture/generator/oracle, primitive, adapter, route, and workflow.

### 9.3 Occurrence

``` yaml
Occurrence:
  occurrence_id: ceg:v1:occurrence:...
  revision_entity_id: ceg:v1:entity:...
  file_content_id: swh:1:cnt:...
  byte_range: [start, end]
  line_range: optional-convenience
  roles: [definition, read, call]
  enclosing_occurrence_id: optional
  syntax_path: optional
  generated_from: optional
  producer: scip-python@...
```

Byte ranges are canonical. Line/column coordinates are encoding-sensitive convenience projections.

### 9.4 Evidence-bearing edge assertion

``` yaml
EdgeAssertion:
  edge_id: ceg:v1:edge:...
  subject_id: ceg:v1:...
  predicate: calls_may
  object_id: optional
  relation_node_id: optional
  modality: asserted|extracted|inferred|observed|verified
  polarity: positive|negative|unknown
  producer_id: codeql-python
  producer_version: ...
  producer_config_digest: ...
  analysis_id: ...
  confidence: optional
  calibration_version: optional
  evidence_refs: []
  scope_snapshot_id: optional
  scope_build_id: optional
  valid_from: optional
  valid_to: optional
  derivation_refs: []
  license_class: ...
  access_class: ...
```

The evidence modality matters:

- `asserted`: docstring, annotation, manifest, package metadata;
- `extracted`: parser, compiler, indexer;
- `inferred`: static analysis, heuristic, ML, or LLM;
- `observed`: execution trace or test run;
- `verified`: independent oracle or reproducible check.

Absence is not false. Negative and unknown assertions must be explicit.

### 9.5 N-ary relation nodes

Calls, flows, builds, tests, effects, and behavior need relation nodes rather than lossy binary edges.

``` yaml
CallRelation:
  callsite_occurrence: ...
  caller: ...
  candidate_callees: []
  argument_bindings: []
  receiver_type: optional
  dispatch_kind: static|virtual|dynamic|reflection|unknown
  resolution_kind: compiler|static-analysis|observed|heuristic
  may_or_must: may|must
  observed_count: optional
  environment: optional
```

``` yaml
BehaviorObservation:
  subject_entity_or_route: ...
  build_id: ...
  input_domain_ref: ...
  input_digest: optional
  environment_digest: ...
  result_digest: optional
  status: pass|fail|error|timeout|unknown
  observed_effects: []
  oracle: ...
  sample_count: ...
  uncertainty: ...
  timestamp: ...
```

### 9.6 Edge ontology

- Structural: `contains`, `declares`, `defines`, `member_of`, `has_port`.
- Reference: `references`, `reads`, `writes`, `imports`, `exports`.
- Type: `type_of`, `accepts`, `returns`, `instantiates`, `specializes`, `converts_to`.
- Object model: `extends`, `implements`, `overrides`, `overloaded_by`.
- Execution: `calls_may`, `calls_must`, `dispatches_to`, `awaits`, `spawns`, `sends_event`.
- Flow: `data_flows_to`, `control_flows_to`, `reaching_definition`, `dominates`, `sanitizes`.
- Tests: `tests`, `covers`, `uses_fixture`, `uses_oracle`, `observed_pass`, `observed_fail`.
- Effects: `may_effect`, `must_effect`, `requires_capability`, `idempotent_under`, `compensated_by`.
- Build/provenance: `depends_on`, `built_from`, `generated_from`, `packaged_as`, `verified_by`, `signed_by`.
- Lineage: `same_concept_as`, `renamed_from`, `forked_from`, `supersedes`, `split_into`, `merged_from`.
- Documentation: `documents`, `example_of`, `claims_behavior`, `contradicted_by`.
- Routing: `satisfies_demand`, `composes_with`, `adapter_for`, `historically_succeeded_on`, `failed_on`.

Every dynamic, reflective, native, or distributed edge is bounded by analyzer/build/runtime scope. The graph is an evidence system, not an omniscient representation of arbitrary program behavior.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 10. PyPI-scale ingestion and progressive analysis

### 10.1 A cost-aware ingestion waterfall

Do not run the deepest analyzer on every package version. Use progressively more expensive passes and publish coverage metadata.

| Pass | Inputs                   | Outputs                                                                     | Trigger                             |
|-----:|--------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
|   I0 | Registry metadata        | Package lineage, releases, project URLs, classifiers, declared license/deps | Every release                       |
|   I1 | Distribution bytes       | Exact digests, file inventory, wheel tags, metadata, RECORD                 | Every artifact                      |
|   I2 | Archive/source inventory | Language/file types, docs/tests/examples/config schemas                     | Every artifact/source snapshot      |
|   I3 | Cheap syntax             | Ctags/Tree-sitter nodes, declarations, docstrings, imports                  | Broad default                       |
|   I4 | Precise symbols          | SCIP/compiler/language-server symbols, occurrences, definitions/references  | Supported languages/builds          |
|   I5 | Interface extraction     | Signatures, types, CLI/OpenAPI/protobuf/GraphQL/database/event schemas      | Public/API-bearing packages         |
|   I6 | Deep semantics           | Calls, CFG, data flow, taint, effects via CodeQL/CPG/compiler analyzers     | High-value/risky/ambiguous packages |
|   I7 | Build/provenance         | Builds, toolchains, dependency closure, SLSA/in-toto/SBOM                   | Reproducible or controlled builds   |
|   I8 | Behavioral evidence      | Tests, examples, property probes, runtime traces                            | Sandboxable packages with oracles   |
|   I9 | Lineage                  | Rename/copy/fork/split/merge hypotheses                                     | Multi-version/high-demand packages  |
|  I10 | Retrieval projections    | Exact, fielded lexical, sparse/dense, adjacency, cards, route macros        | Published graph epoch               |

### 10.2 PyPI-specific first slice

Extract:

- normalized and original package names plus registry authority;
- purl and release metadata;
- wheel/sdist hashes and tags;
- `METADATA`, `Requires-Dist`, extras, Python version constraints, entry points;
- source repository link and exact resolved revision when defensible;
- modules, exports, functions, classes, methods, variables/constants, parameters;
- decorators and type annotations;
- imports and optional dependency guards;
- public API surface and deprecation markers;
- docstrings, README usage blocks, examples, and tests;
- CLI commands, config schemas, environment variables, filesystem/network/subprocess effects;
- compiled/native extension boundary and unavailable-analysis flags.

For dynamic Python, distinguish:

- syntactically declared exports;
- runtime-observed exports;
- `__all__` claims;
- monkey-patched/generated attributes;
- dynamic import/reflection uncertainty.

### 10.3 Incremental invalidation

``` text
AnalysisKey = H(
  graph_schema_version,
  source_and_artifact_digests,
  dependency_closure_digest,
  compiler/indexer/grammar versions,
  flags/configuration,
  target platform
)
```

Invalidation differs by fact family:

- syntax facts reuse by file digest + parser version;
- name/type resolution also pins dependencies, interpreter/compiler, config, generated inputs;
- call/data-flow facts pin the semantic dependency closure;
- build facts pin recipe, toolchain, inputs, platform;
- behavior remains historical but stops being current when build/environment changes;
- logical lineage is recalculated independently from exact entity IDs.

Derived assertions retain input fact IDs so reverse dependencies can invalidate affected shards instead of rebuilding the corpus.

### 10.4 Publication and storage

At 50M entities, expect hundreds of millions or billions of occurrences/edges. Use multiple projections:

1.  Immutable Protobuf or Arrow/Parquet fact shards.
2.  Object storage for source/native analyzer payloads/evidence.
3.  Exact-ID key/value index.
4.  Fielded lexical index for names, signatures, docs, effects, packages.
5.  Compressed forward/reverse adjacency indexes and bitmaps.
6.  Columnar analytical projection with graph epochs.
7.  Optional sparse/dense indexes.
8.  Graph database only for selected interactive workloads.

Publish atomically: validate candidate shards, check referential integrity and ID collisions, publish a signed epoch manifest, pin queries to an epoch, and allow policy overlays to suppress revoked content immediately.

### 10.5 Licensing and privacy are graph facts

Track source, docs, package metadata, fact redistribution, snippet display, embedding/model-use, acquisition origin, tenant ACL, retention, and takedown separately. A package’s declared license field is evidence, not verified legal truth.

Policy propagates like taint:

- summaries and embeddings inherit relevant source restrictions;
- graph neighborhoods never mix tenants before authorization;
- identical content deduplication does not erase origin-specific obligations;
- internal symbol names and call graphs are protected even without source bodies;
- cross-tenant aggregate learning requires privacy thresholds and explicit policy.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 11. How the code graph improves model routing

The CEG turns vague “complexity” into exact or measured features.

### 11.1 Task features from the graph

| Feature family | Examples                                                        | Routing value                                      |
|----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| Scope          | files/entities/packages/repositories touched; k-hop radius      | Predict context and coordination difficulty        |
| Language/build | languages, native code, macros, generated code, toolchain       | Exclude incapable models/tools; choose specialist  |
| Topology       | branching, cycles, fan-in/fan-out, centrality, adapter count    | Estimate composition and blast radius              |
| Semantics      | dynamic dispatch, reflection, unresolved types, data-flow depth | Measure analysis uncertainty                       |
| Effects        | filesystem/network/secrets/database/subprocess/deployment       | Set risk tier, tools, permissions, verifier        |
| Interface      | public API/ABI/schema/serialization surface                     | Raise compatibility and test requirements          |
| Evidence       | test/oracle coverage, static-analysis confidence, provenance    | Decide cheap acceptance versus strong planning     |
| History        | route/model success by task cell and graph pattern              | Application-specific model prediction              |
| Context        | required slice bytes/tokens, duplicate ratio, cacheable prefix  | Optimize projection and model context eligibility  |
| Change         | rename/local edit/cross-cut refactor/new API/security repair    | Route to deterministic refactor tool or model tier |

### 11.2 Example

User request: “Rename `timeout` to `request_timeout` safely.”

Raw-prompt router may see a simple rename. CEG reveals:

- 42 static references;
- 3 string-based config lookups;
- one environment variable mapper;
- public constructor parameter serialized in saved configs;
- two downstream packages importing by keyword;
- high-confidence compiler references but low-confidence reflection edges;
- migration tests available.

The right route becomes:

1.  deterministic symbol rename for exact references;
2.  compatibility adapter/deprecation alias for public surface;
3.  targeted model review only for string/config/reflection sites;
4.  run migration and downstream tests;
5.  no need for a frontier model to read the whole package.

### 11.3 CodeEntityCard

Models see a compact projection:

``` yaml
CodeEntityCard:
  exact_ids: []
  concept_id: optional
  kind: method
  signature: ...
  ports: ...
  effects: ...
  capabilities: ...
  compact_docs: ...
  strongest_typed_edges: ...
  test_and_behavior_evidence: ...
  runtime_and_build_constraints: ...
  license_and_acl_class: ...
  confidence_and_coverage: ...
  expansion_handles: ...
```

Historical success edges are time-scoped behavioral evidence, not source-semantic truth. Cache a route by:

``` text
DemandIR digest
+ graph epoch
+ exact entity revision IDs
+ policy epoch
+ runtime environment
+ verifier plan
```

## 12. Router contracts

### 12.1 ModelProfile

``` yaml
ModelProfile:
  semantic_model_id: ...
  provider_variants: []
  profile_epoch: ...
  context_limits: ...
```

Provider capabilities are not assumed from the semantic model name. Tool calling, response schema, streaming, reasoning, and caching may differ by provider/deployment.

### 12.2 RouteRequest

``` yaml
RouteRequest:
  route_request_id: ...
  task_node_id: ...
  demand_ir_ref: ...

  intent_and_confidence: ...

  history_and_cache_features: ...
  verification_plan: ...
  selector_spend_limit: ...
  experiment_assignment: ...
```

### 12.3 RouteDecision and RouteLease

``` yaml
RouteDecision:
  route_id: ...
  policy_version: ...
  selected_action_or_model: ...
  selected_provider_policy: ...
  prompt_program: ...
  visible_tools: []
  context_projection: ...
  max_input_output_reasoning: ...
  same_route_retry_policy: ...
  semantic_fallback_sequence: []
  verifier_policy: ...
  confidence: ...
  uncertainty: ...
  predicted_cost_latency_quality: ...
  expected_regret: ...
  selection_propensity: ...
  reason_codes: []
  candidate_set_hash: ...
  invalidation_conditions: []
```

A `RouteDecision` becomes a short-lived immutable `RouteLease`. The lease prevents a resumed workflow, second worker, changing catalog, or lower gateway from silently changing the semantic decision. Provider failover may choose a compatible deployment only within the lease. A different model requires a new decision linked to the old receipt.

### 12.4 RouteOutcome

``` yaml
RouteOutcome:
  route_id: ...
  actual_model_and_provider: ...
  attempts: []
  provider_and_model_fallbacks: []
  input_output_cached_reasoning_tokens: ...
  latency_and_ttft: ...
  tool_calls_and_effect_receipts: []
  parse_and_contract_result: ...
  independent_verifier_result: ...
  escalation_reason: optional
  disposition: accepted|repaired|rejected|abstained
  final_cost: ...
```

Reason codes should be enums and numeric fields. Generate human explanations deterministically from the receipt rather than paying an LLM to narrate every decision.

## 13. Retry, fallback, repair, escalation, and replan state machine

| Transition                  | Trigger                                                    | Allowed action                                             | Must not do                             |
|-----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| Same-route retry            | Transient connection, timeout before commit, throttling    | Retry same request/model/provider within limit             | Infinite retry or duplicate side effect |
| Provider failover           | Selected semantic model unavailable at deployment          | Same verified model/capability profile on another provider | Change semantic model silently          |
| Availability model fallback | Model unavailable everywhere and policy permits substitute | New explicit semantic route decision                       | Pretend it is provider failover         |
| Deterministic repair        | Formatting/JSON/schema wrapper defect with intact content  | Parser repair/canonicalization                             | Redo reasoning unnecessarily            |
| Cheap repair model          | Bounded representation repair                              | Isolated repair prompt with original evidence              | Grant mutating tools                    |
| Semantic escalation         | Independent verifier shows capability/quality failure      | Stronger/different specialist via new lease                | Hide the failed attempt                 |
| Context replan              | Context overflow or missing decisive evidence              | Change slice/detail/tool plan                              | Merely try another provider             |
| Workflow replan             | Primitive route/tool topology is wrong                     | Return to retrieval/route solving                          | Keep escalating model size blindly      |
| Stop/abstain                | Policy, authority, budget, or proof cannot be satisfied    | Return structured certificate                              | Invent authority or unverifiable answer |

Rules:

- Before first visible output, retry/fallback may be possible.
- After streaming starts, do not invisibly switch models.
- After a tool commits an effect, replay only with a proven idempotency key or compensation plan.
- Authentication, malformed request, policy denial, unsupported capability, and invalid schema are normally permanent failures, not reasons to try every model.
- Rate limiting is provider traffic failure before it is semantic model failure.
- Verification failure creates a new linked attempt, never overwrites the failed receipt.

Temporal is a good outer engine for critical workflows if `select_route`, `invoke_model`, tools, and verification are separate Activities. Keep semantic fallback in workflow code rather than hiding the whole waterfall inside a retried Activity.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 14. Cost model and decision mathematics

Optimize expected total cost per verified success:

``` text
E[total_cost] =
  selector_compute
  + model_input/output/reasoning
  + lost_prompt_cache_value
  + expected_provider_retry
  + expected_model_fallback
  + tool_and_execution
  + verification
  + expected_repair_or_rework
  + latency_penalty
  + privacy/risk penalty
```

Hard policy, authority, safety, residency, and capability requirements remain constraints, not soft weights.

### 14.1 Expected regret policy

Choose the cheapest eligible model whose predicted quality loss versus the best eligible model is within the request’s regret budget:

``` text
eligible(m) = all hard constraints pass

choose argmin_m E[total_cost(m)]
subject to
  P(success_m | task, graph, context, verifier) >= quality_floor
  E[quality_best - quality_m] <= regret_budget
```

This generalizes Azure’s quality-band idea while keeping model profiles and policies application-owned and versioned.

### 14.2 Value of information

Before spending on another signal, candidate, detail level, model, or panel:

``` text
VOI(action) = expected decision loss before
            - expected decision loss after
            - action cost
            - added latency/privacy/risk
```

Use VOI to decide whether to:

- expand `k` from 1 to 2/4/8;
- load full signatures or bodies;
- run a distinguishing probe;
- ask one clarification;
- invoke a cheap selector model;
- invoke a strong planner;
- run a multi-model panel.

### 14.3 Prompt cache is part of the routing cost

Model/provider switching can destroy prefix-cache value. Session stickiness can preserve it, but full-conversation pinning can make later task nodes use the wrong model. Use:

- `affinity_scope = call | task_node | phase | agent | conversation`;
- TTL and maximum spend;
- reclassification triggers for task/domain/risk/tool changes;
- cache-compatible provider set;
- an explicit cache-value feature in the cost model.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 15. Feedback, calibration, and self-optimization

### 15.1 Outcome hierarchy

From strongest to weakest:

1.  Independent executable oracle or official task resolution.
2.  Property/invariant tests and schema/tool contract validity.
3.  Static/security/type/build checks.
4.  Human acceptance with explicit criteria.
5.  Independent blinded evaluation.
6.  Downstream behavioral signals: correction, retry, rephrase, stagnation.
7.  User sentiment or lack of complaint.
8.  Model self-evaluation.

Do not collapse these into one undifferentiated reward.

### 15.2 Conditional performance cells

Store model evidence by:

``` text
task/action
domain/language
graph features
risk/effects
context projection/detail
tool projection/protocol
provider/deployment
model/profile version
prompt program version
verifier/oracle
time window
```

Use hierarchical smoothing so sparse cells inherit cautious priors from broader cells. Decay stale operational measurements. Keep exact historical receipts immutable.

### 15.3 Safe online learning

- Log candidate set, scores, chosen arm, propensity, and policy version.
- Reserve randomized exploration only for low-risk tasks with strong oracles.
- Use shadow execution when latency/cost allows.
- Maintain a frozen holdout and canary population.
- Evaluate calibration, risk–coverage, regret, and quality-floor violations.
- Detect price, latency, model-version, task-mix, and outcome drift separately.
- Require promotion gates and rollback.
- Never learn authorization, safety, or residency policy from reward.

Contextual bandits are a later layer, not the first router. Begin with deterministic and supervised/shadow policies because bandit feedback observes only the selected arm and can reinforce its own mistakes.

### 15.4 Every expensive fallback should manufacture a cheaper future path

A successful expensive attempt can produce:

- validated QueryIR template;
- route macro;
- code-slice rule;
- model task-cell observation;
- regression fixture;
- missing edge or alias correction;
- adapter PrimitiveCard;
- clarification rule;
- negative certificate for a misleading route.

The model is not merely answering; it is paying down future routing entropy.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 16. Evaluation program

### 16.1 Baseline arms

1.  Fixed frontier model.
2.  Fixed cheapest model.
3.  Fixed mid-tier model.
4.  Random eligible model.
5.  Offline oracle cheapest successful model.
6.  Exact/history route only.
7.  Deterministic complexity/task policy.
8.  Local statistical ranker.
9.  Local SLM domain/action router.
10. Application-trained pairwise/listwise router.
11. Contextual bandit.
12. Cheap general-model classifier.
13. Strong-model selector.
14. Verification-triggered cascade.
15. vLLM Semantic Router.
16. Plano.
17. OpenRouter Auto or Not Diamond.
18. Gateway-only routing without semantic router.

### 16.2 Factorial experiment axes

- Candidate routes: `1/2/4/8`.
- Primitive detail: handle, short card, port signature, full card, body.
- Edge detail: decisive only, 1-hop, typed 2-hop, broad neighborhood.
- Deduplication: off, exact cluster, semantic/behavior cluster.
- Affinity: per-call, task-node, phase, conversation.
- Context: full history, delta manifest, graph slice, graph slice + peel.
- Tool exposure: all schemas, meta-tools, deferred tool search, route-specific tools.
- Selector: deterministic, ranker, SLM, small LLM, strong LLM.
- Fallback: error-only, confidence, verifier-triggered, bounded cascade.
- Verifier: none, same-model self-check, independent model, deterministic oracle.
- Cache: off, exact request, route lease, prompt prefix, result.
- Graph: lexical only, symbol, typed edges, deep semantics, behavior evidence.

### 16.3 Primary metrics

- End-to-end verified task success.
- Cost per verified success.
- Quality-floor violation / false downgrade rate.
- Unnecessary escalation rate.
- Cheapest-success regret.
- Selector cost as percentage of savings.
- Total tokens across selector, executor, verifier, retries, tools.
- Context/tool schema tokens avoided.
- Route recall and route correctness.
- Provider versus semantic fallback rate.
- Cache hit/value retained.
- p50/p95/p99 latency and TTFT.
- Post-stream failures.
- Parse versus semantic failure.
- Side-effect replay attempts and uncertain outcomes.
- Calibration and risk–coverage.
- Route churn across equivalent turns.
- Incremental value of each graph edge/detail layer.

### 16.4 Dataset design

Include:

- exact repeats and parameterized variants;
- underspecified/no-match tasks;
- local edit, rename, API change, dependency migration, security repair, tests, docs, debugging, and architecture tasks;
- Python-only, mixed-language, native extension, generated-code, reflection-heavy cases;
- read-only and mutating tools;
- small and long multi-turn sessions;
- provider/model/tool failures;
- context overflow and stale graph epochs;
- adversarial metadata/docstring prompt injection;
- cross-tenant and license-policy cases;
- tasks where cheap models genuinely outperform or specialize;
- tasks requiring abstention or human approval.

Use paired task-level randomization, failure-inclusive accounting, fixed model/profile snapshots, exact price snapshots, and confidence intervals. Report slices, not just one aggregate percentage.

### 16.5 Decision gates

Ship a router only if it:

- meets a predeclared success non-inferiority margin;
- lowers failure-inclusive cost with uncertainty bounds;
- does not materially increase high-risk errors;
- stays calibrated on holdout and drift slices;
- has bounded selector overhead;
- produces reproducible receipts and rollback;
- beats a simple deterministic baseline, not only fixed frontier.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 17. Build/buy architecture

### Build and own

- ContextManifest and DemandIR.
- Code Entity Graph contracts, identity lattice, evidence modalities, and graph epochs.
- CodeSliceManifest and Primitive/Entity/Route cards.
- Hard eligibility, authority, effect, privacy, residency, and verifier policy.
- ModelProfile and capability registry.
- Selector-arm interface and policy compiler.
- RouteRequest, RouteDecision, RouteLease, RouteOutcome, failure taxonomy.
- Application outcome data, calibration, evaluation, and promotion.
- Exact receipts, route replay, invalidation, and negative knowledge.

### Adopt or evaluate

- SCIP indexers plus Tree-sitter/Ctags for broad extraction.
- CodeQL/CPG/Glean-style analyzers selectively.
- purl, SWHID, SPDX/CycloneDX, SLSA/in-toto, PROV.
- LiteLLM, Bifrost, or Portkey for provider normalization/reliability.
- vLLM Semantic Router and Plano as open selector/reference arms.
- OpenRouter Auto and Not Diamond as external arms.
- Kubernetes Inference Extension for self-hosted endpoint routing.
- Pydantic AI and LangGraph for Python harness adapters; Mastra for TypeScript.
- Temporal for high-assurance durable workflows.
- BAML for typed prompt functions behind the broker.
- DSPy/Dagster/Prefect for offline optimization and evaluation.

### Avoid making foundational

- opaque auto-router with changing candidate pool;
- gateway-specific request format as Taedri’s internal IR;
- one graph database as canonical truth;
- one universal AST or symbol ID;
- one LLM judge as acceptance oracle;
- conversation sentiment as router reward;
- all-tools-in-context harness configuration;
- invisible cross-model fallback.

## 18. Concrete delivery plan

### Phase 0 — contracts and truth kernel (2–3 weeks)

Deliver:

- schemas for identity lattice, EntityNode, Occurrence, EdgeAssertion, shard manifest;
- DemandIR, CodeSliceManifest, ModelProfile, route contracts;
- failure taxonomy and state machine;
- canonical serialization, digests, graph/policy/profile epochs;
- receipt event model;
- 50–100 hand-built fixtures covering identity and routing ambiguity.

Exit gate: deterministic round-trip, collision tests, referential integrity, signed epoch, and receipt reconstruction pass.

### Phase 1 — Python/PyPI graph slice (3–5 weeks)

Deliver:

- ingest 100–1,000 representative packages;
- purl/release/artifact/source identities;
- Tree-sitter/Ctags cheap pass and SCIP precise pass;
- docs/tests/examples/imports/types/public interfaces;
- exact, fielded BM25, and compressed adjacency projections;
- compact CodeEntityCard and graph expansion API;
- incremental invalidation and coverage ledger.

Exit gate: known-answer symbol/reference/import/type queries; no cross-package/tenant identity collisions; repeat analysis reuses unchanged shards.

### Phase 2 — deterministic routing and harness slice (3–4 weeks)

Deliver:

- hard eligibility gates;
- exact/history/template/typed graph route solving;
- deterministic task/domain/complexity/risk classifier;
- ModelProfile registry;
- Pydantic AI + LangGraph adapters;
- one gateway adapter;
- meta-tools and progressive disclosure;
- RouteLease and exact OTel/receipt instrumentation.

Exit gate: fixed-cheapest/frontier/deterministic benchmark with complete cost and failure receipts.

### Phase 3 — local and hosted selector portfolio (3–5 weeks)

Deliver:

- local statistical ranker;
- local domain/action SLM;
- cheap and strong LLM selector arms;
- external vLLM/Plano/OpenRouter/Not Diamond adapters;
- 1/2/4/8 and detail-level experiment harness;
- shadow candidate execution.

Exit gate: router beats deterministic baseline on cost per verified success without quality-floor regression.

### Phase 4 — execution, verification, and durable recovery (3–5 weeks)

Deliver:

- post-selection body resolution;
- restricted GraphIR execution;
- deterministic/schema/test/security verifiers;
- explicit repair/escalate/replan transitions;
- Temporal wrapper for high-risk workflows;
- idempotency/compensation receipts.

Exit gate: failure injection proves no invisible model switch and no unsafe effect replay.

### Phase 5 — deep graph and self-optimization (ongoing)

Deliver selectively:

- CodeQL/CPG call/data/effect facts;
- runtime behavior and test observations;
- logical lineage registry;
- supervised outcome router;
- low-risk contextual bandit with propensities, drift, canary, rollback;
- package/ecosystem expansion.

Exit gate: each added layer demonstrates incremental verified-success or cost value on its target slices.

## 20. Recommended first experiments

Run these before online learning:

### Experiment 1 — does typed graph context beat raw prompt routing?

Arms:

- raw prompt only;
- prompt + deterministic task features;
- prompt + CodeEntityCard summaries;
- prompt + graph-derived features, no prose cards;
- DemandIR + graph features + candidate deltas.

Measure router tokens, selection accuracy, calibration, verified task success, and false downgrade.

### Experiment 2 — how much primitive detail is enough?

Cross `k=1/2/4/8` with D0–D5 detail. Include duplicate-heavy and connector-dependent routes. Measure route recall, correct choice, selector spend, position bias, and body leakage.

### Experiment 3 — deterministic versus local versus hosted selector

Compare:

- hard rules;
- local GBDT/ranker;
- local 1–3B domain/action model;
- cheap hosted model;
- strong hosted model;
- outcome-trained router;
- offline oracle.

Report incremental value after selector cost and latency.

### Experiment 4 — routing granularity

Compare one model per conversation, per user task, per workflow phase, per agent, and per model call. Measure cache hit, route churn, final success, and cost. The likely default is phase/task-node affinity with reclassification triggers.

### Experiment 5 — fallback semantics

Inject provider throttling, timeouts, malformed tool outputs, schema failures, verifier failures, mid-stream disconnects, and post-tool failures. Prove that each produces the intended retry/failover/repair/escalate/replan state and never silently crosses a committed-effect boundary.

### Experiment 6 — package graph extraction value

On representative PyPI packages, add passes I0–I8 cumulatively. Measure graph query correctness, routing improvement, route recall, analysis cost, index size, invalidation cost, and marginal verified-task value. Do not keep a deep pass merely because it produces interesting edges.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 21. Final architecture recommendation

The strongest defensible system is not another universal proxy and not another vector database over docstrings. It is a typed, evidence-linked decision plane:

``` text
                      ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
                      │  Evidence plane                  │
                      │  graph epochs, profiles, evals,  │
                      │  receipts, drift, invalidation   │
                      └──────────────┬───────────────────┘
                                     │
Input ──► ContextManifest ──► DemandIR + CodeSliceManifest
                                     │
                                     ▼
              hard gates ──► eligible actions/models/tools
                                     │
                                     ▼
              deterministic / local / learned / LLM selectors
                                     │
                                     ▼
                 immutable RouteLease + compact projections
                                     │
                                     ▼
                  harness node / agent / typed prompt function
                                     │
                                     ▼
                     provider gateway ─► endpoint scheduler
                                     │
                                     ▼
                       execute ─► verify ─► settle outcome
```

The universal code layer should be a **bridge standard**:

- native names remain intact;
- exact identities are content/build/snapshot scoped;
- logical continuity is an evidence-bearing lineage claim;
- language-native facts are preserved;
- common entities, ports, effects, edges, evidence, and provenance are normalized;
- models receive small cards and expansion handles;
- deterministic tools operate on exact occurrences and interfaces;
- execution outcomes teach the router which model/action succeeds for which graph/task cell.

That makes the original primitive idea recursive. A package is a primitive. A module, class, function, method, field, variable, endpoint, test, schema, route, and workflow can also be a primitive at the appropriate abstraction boundary. Each has a compact semantic ABI, exact evidence-linked edges, and a hidden body. The system retrieves and composes the smallest sufficient units, resolves bodies only after selection, and uses the cheapest capable intelligence for each node.

The first product proof remains narrow: **Python/PyPI graph + typed demand + deterministic/local/strong selector portfolio + two harness adapters + one gateway + independent verification**. If that slice materially reduces cost per verified success while preserving quality and safety, the same contracts can expand to other ecosystems, richer analyzers, durable workflows, and online optimization without rebuilding the conceptual core.

# Taedri token-minimizing retrieval and composition waterfall

> **ANNEX STATUS — TARGET RETRIEVAL/COMPOSITION ARCHITECTURE.** The waterfall and
> its alternatives define experiments and intended controls. Only the narrower
> evidence summarized in Part 0 is implemented and measured in the current proposal.

**Date:** 2026-07-15
**Scope:** query understanding, candidate retrieval, fusion, route compilation, escalation, token/cost accounting, 5M/40M-corpus scaling, experiments, and build backlog
**Decision:** make model-written search queries a bounded last resort. Compile one typed, reusable demand contract from the request; let exact, structural, lexical, graph, sparse, dense, historical, and tool-derived paths consume that contract; stop as soon as a validated route is safe to execute.

## Executive answer

Yes—this makes architectural and economic sense, and it should materially reduce provider-token spend. The stronger formulation is that Taedri is an **information-budgeted planning and proof system**: cheap and accurate retrieval finds opaque reusable capabilities; cheap and accurate composition connects them through transparent, machine-checkable contracts; execution and verification remain outside the selector model.

The important version of the idea is not “replace a large query-writing model with a smaller query-writing model.” It is:

``` text
request
  -> one body-free QueryPlan / demand contract
  -> many cheap, mostly parallel retrieval views
  -> hard eligibility and typed compatibility
  -> deterministic route whenever evidence is sufficient
  -> increasingly expensive ambiguity reduction only when justified
  -> bounded model-written query deltas at the end
```

The waterfall must have an explicit **stop/abstain/escalate policy**. Otherwise it becomes a long chain that always pays every layer, or it stops early on an attractive but uncalibrated score and silently loses recall. The system should stop only when the route is eligible, covers the demand, satisfies all hard constraints, and meets a measured risk threshold. It should escalate only when the expected value of the next layer exceeds its compute, latency, privacy, and error costs.

A strong harness is central to this design. Repository instructions supply small durable invariants; skills load task-family procedures on demand; hooks enforce lifecycle and policy; typed tools do exact work; MCP/resources expose a compact control plane; agents isolate bounded subgraphs; memory/history supplies scoped priors; and a model broker escalates from deterministic code through local models to strong/frontier models only for unresolved semantic work.

The attached implementation is directionally correct: body-free retrieval, typed route compilation, handle recipes, post-compile body resolution, and zero-model execution are the right primitives. The current fusion rule, however, must be replaced before it governs early stopping. Per-signal max normalization turns the best result from every signal into `1.0` even when the best raw score is nearly meaningless. It produces a ranking score, not a probability of correctness.

The desired default is:

``` text
ZERO-MODEL FAST PATH
  exact replay / exact recipe / exact ID / validated history
        |
        v
CHEAP PARALLEL PATHS
  fielded lexical + code search + keyphrases + fuzzy + LSH + contract graph
        |
        v
LOCAL SEMANTIC PATHS
  learned sparse + dense ANN + typed graph expansion + rank fusion
        |
        v
DETERMINISTIC COMPILER
  one eligible route? -> compact recipe -> execute -> verify -> learn
        |
        +-- ambiguity worth resolving? --> local reranker / tools / small slot-filler
        |
        +-- still ambiguous? -----------> hosted model emits bounded query deltas
        |
        +-- no implementation? ---------> clarify, bypass, or compile once in foundry
```

“Waterfall” describes **escalation rights**, not a requirement that every search execute serially. The cheap independent branches should run concurrently under one time budget.

## What the attached accounting says

The old treatment recorded:

| Item                               | Provider tokens | Share of treatment |
|------------------------------------|----------------:|-------------------:|
| Query generation                   |         221,510 |             23.98% |
| Selection/integration              |         697,125 |             75.46% |
| Both model-mediated routing stages |         918,635 |             99.44% |
| Treatment total                    |         923,806 |            100.00% |
| Baseline total                     |         690,179 |                  — |

Removing only query generation would change the treatment total from 923,806 to 702,296 tokens: a 23.98% treatment reduction, but still 12,117 tokens, or 1.76%, above the baseline. That means the proposed waterfall should not stop at cheap query construction. It should also make selection and composition deterministic whenever contracts and route structure allow it.

The two named stages sum to 918,635 tokens, leaving 5,171 tokens in the attachment's accounting decomposition. That is not a forecast of production usage and must be reconciled against the underlying provider receipts before a public claim. It does show where the measured treatment overhead concentrated.

An illustrative fallback curve, assuming the old average query-stage cost applies and deterministic selection succeeds, is:

| Share reaching old-style LLM query drafting | Query-stage tokens retained | Query-stage tokens avoided | Illustrative total after also removing selection/integration\* |
|--------------------------------------------:|----------------------------:|---------------------------:|---------------------------------------------------------------:|
|                                          0% |                           0 |                    221,510 |                                                          5,171 |
|                                          5% |                      11,076 |                    210,434 |                                                         16,247 |
|                                         10% |                      22,151 |                    199,359 |                                                         27,322 |
|                                         25% |                      55,378 |                    166,132 |                                                         60,549 |
|                                         50% |                     110,755 |                    110,755 |                                                        115,926 |

\*Arithmetic scenario, not an expected production result. It excludes new local compute, build cost, verification, failures, and any compact selector tokens.

Provider-token savings are not identical to total-system savings. Deterministic parsing, local embeddings, ANN, reranking, and indexes still consume CPU/GPU, memory, storage, and engineering effort. Keep separate ledgers for provider tokens, local compute dollars, latency, energy, and downstream error loss.

## Ten design laws

1.  **Compile meaning, not prose.** The request becomes a typed `QueryPlan` AST. Search engines receive compiled, parameterized queries; no model writes raw SQL, FTS syntax, filters, or ANN code.
2.  **Separate eligibility from relevance.** Authorization, tenant, lifecycle, effects, environment, license, and mandatory contracts are gates, not weights.
3.  **Use one plan for many views.** Exact, BM25, code, LSH, sparse, dense, graph, and historical paths consume the same canonical request interpretation.
4.  **Make cheap paths parallel.** Exact, structural, lexical, keyphrase, code, history, and LSH work can share a short deadline instead of forming a latency staircase.
5.  **Retrieve body-free evidence.** Rank compact cards, handles, contracts, types, digests, and proof metadata. Resolve implementation bodies only after compilation.
6.  **Stop on validated sufficiency, never on a top score alone.** A high similarity is neither permission nor proof of route correctness.
7.  **Escalate by expected value.** Buy a new signal only if its expected reduction in decision loss exceeds its full marginal cost.
8.  **Models fill unresolved slots.** A local or hosted model returns bounded enums, spans, or query deltas with provenance—not a replacement free-form search plan.
9.  **Move reusable intelligence offline.** Aliases, embeddings, sparse expansions, type graphs, clusters, synthetic queries, and recipe priors are compiled at intake and amortized.
10. **Measure the risk-coverage curve.** Every early exit is an abstaining predictor; prove false-stop risk per task family before raising coverage.

## Offline foundry: spend once so serving stays cheap

The largest request-time reduction comes from doing expensive semantic work once at artifact ingestion or scheduled rebuild time.

For each primitive, pack, standard, workflow, or reference candidate, build and version:

- canonical identifiers, aliases, acronyms, package names, symbols, imports, paths, error strings, and version ranges;
- body-free capability cards with input/output types, effects, environment, risk, license, lifecycle, oracle status, and authorization references;
- separate lexical fields for title, capability, signature, inputs, outputs, effects, errors, standards, and examples;
- word and character shingles, MinHash signatures for set overlap, and SimHash-style fingerprints for near-duplicate blocking;
- dense vectors for distinct facets rather than one undifferentiated blob: intent/capability, input contract, output contract, effects/environment, standards, and known failure modes;
- learned sparse vectors or document-side expansions when their held-out gain justifies the index cost;
- typed compatibility edges and precomputed reachability summaries;
- cluster, taxonomy, and centroid membership for coarse semantic routing;
- validated paraphrases and synthetic request-to-artifact pairs generated offline, deduplicated, reviewed, and attached to the artifact digest;
- successful and failed recipe statistics keyed by demand family, environment, policy, artifact closure, and oracle version; and
- calibration data: per-retriever score distributions, per-family recall, correlation among retrievers, and drift baselines.

Offline model work is not free. Charge its generation, validation, review, storage, and invalidation cost to the artifact, then amortize over actual eligible reuses. If an alias or expansion changes retrieval behavior, it must be versioned and reproducible.

## The shared `QueryPlan`: one interpretation, many deterministic queries

The request should be compiled into a typed AST, not rewritten repeatedly as natural-language search text.

``` json
{
  "schema_version": "taedri.query-plan/v1",
  "request_digest": "sha256:...",
  "task_family": "distributed_page_pipeline",
  "language": "en",
  "scope": {
    "tenant": "...",
    "authorization_context_digest": "sha256:...",
    "policy_version": "..."
  },
  "literals": [
    {"text": "RawPageBatch", "kind": "type", "span": [120,132], "confidence": 1.0},
    {"text": "DatasetManifest", "kind": "type", "span": [150,165], "confidence": 1.0}
  ],
  "demand": {
    "required_capabilities": ["normalize_pages", "filter_pages", "deduplicate_pages"],
    "start_type_candidates": ["RawPageBatch"],
    "end_type_candidates": ["DatasetManifest"],
    "required_standards": [],
    "allowed_effects": ["local_read", "local_write"],
    "forbidden_effects": ["external_network"],
    "environment": {"language": "python", "runtime": ">=3.11"}
  },
  "lexical": {
    "must": ["manifest"],
    "should": ["normalize", "filter", "deduplicate", "score"],
    "must_not": ["untrusted_remote_executor"],
    "phrases": ["build manifest"],
    "acronyms": [],
    "fuzzy_terms": []
  },
  "code": {
    "languages": ["python"],
    "packages": [],
    "symbols": [],
    "imports": [],
    "paths": [],
    "error_literals": [],
    "signature_patterns": []
  },
  "semantic_views": [
    {"facet": "capability", "source_spans": [[0,96]], "weight": 1.0},
    {"facet": "output_contract", "source_spans": [[140,180]], "weight": 1.0}
  ],
  "uncertainty": {
    "unresolved_slots": [],
    "alternatives": [],
    "out_of_distribution_score": 0.04
  },
  "budget": {
    "deadline_ms": 250,
    "max_candidates_per_view": 100,
    "max_local_rerank_candidates": 50,
    "max_hosted_query_calls": 1,
    "max_hosted_output_tokens": 160
  }
}
```

Every field should retain its source span, extractor, confidence, and version. Exact quoted text and explicit identifiers outrank inferred labels. `unknown` is a valid value; a weak extractor should not manufacture a hard filter.

### Deterministic query compiler

The compiler converts the AST to validated query objects:

``` text
ExactLookup(ids=[...], digests=[...])
HistoryLookup(demand_digest=..., environment_digest=...)
EligibilityFilter(tenant=..., lifecycle=..., effects=..., policy=...)
FieldedLexical(
  must=[Phrase(field="output_type", value="DatasetManifest")],
  should=[Term(field="capability", value="deduplicate", boost=...)],
  must_not=[Effect("external_network")]
)
CodeStructural(symbols=[...], imports=[...], ast_patterns=[...])
LSHLookup(signature=..., family="minhash-jaccard", bands=...)
SparseKNN(vector_ref=..., k=...)
DenseKNN(facet="capability", vector_ref=..., k=..., filter_ref=...)
GraphReachability(start_types=[...], end_types=[...], required_capabilities=[...])
```

The model, if eventually used, edits the AST through a narrow patch schema such as `add_should_term`, `propose_type_candidate`, or `add_semantic_view`. It never emits an executable database query. This prevents syntax errors, injection, unbounded fan-out, and silent removal of policy constraints.

### Long and compound requests

Do not embed only the full prompt. Segment it into clauses and label each clause as goal, input, output, constraint, negative constraint, environment, evidence requirement, or example. Build separate semantic views for independent subgoals. Retrieve top candidates per view and required capability, then fuse and solve the route. A single whole-prompt vector tends to blur rare identifiers, negation, and multi-step requirements.

## Full retrieval and query-generation waterfall

The following is the recommended logical order. Tiers inside the same band run concurrently when allowed by the request budget.

| Band / tier | Mechanism                               | What it emits                                              |  Normal cost | Stop or escalation rule                            | Main failure controlled                         |
|-------------|-----------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|-------------:|----------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| Offline 0   | Canonical catalog and card compiler     | Compact fields, types, effects, aliases, digests           |    Amortized | Reject incomplete/unverifiable cards               | Bad metadata becoming runtime truth             |
| Offline 1   | Lexical/code indexes                    | Fielded postings, trigrams, symbol/AST/path indexes        |    Amortized | Index receipt and integrity pass                   | Full scans and runtime parsing                  |
| Offline 2   | LSH and dedupe index                    | MinHash/SimHash buckets, cluster IDs                       |    Amortized | Collision/recall tests pass                        | Near duplicates and huge candidate regions      |
| Offline 3   | Semantic compilation                    | Facet vectors, sparse expansions, centroids                |    Amortized | Frozen model/index digest                          | Repeating semantic generation per request       |
| Offline 4   | Type and recipe graph                   | Compatibility edges, reachability, validated history       |    Amortized | Contract and policy validation                     | Model guessing composability                    |
| A0          | Admission and scope                     | Tenant, authorization, policy, lifecycle filters           |    Near zero | Never bypass                                       | Cross-scope leakage                             |
| A1          | Deterministic normalization             | Unicode/case normalization, language, clauses, spans       |    Near zero | Plan schema-valid                                  | Accidental textual variation                    |
| A2          | Exact request/result replay             | Sealed result or negative cache                            |    Near zero | All request/policy/environment/oracle seals match  | Paying twice for identical work                 |
| A3          | Exact recipe replay                     | Compiled handle graph                                      |    Near zero | Artifact closure and every current gate pass       | Replanning a known route                        |
| A4          | Explicit ID/digest/name lookup          | Exact candidate/pack/standard IDs                          |    Near zero | Unique eligible exact match or exact pack          | Treating explicit IDs as fuzzy hints            |
| A5          | Validated historical recipe             | Candidate route plus posterior prior                       |     Very low | Revalidated route passes current demand and policy | Repeating successful composition                |
| B0          | Hard structural narrowing               | Eligible partitions by type/effect/env/license/risk        |     Very low | Unique compatible route may stop                   | Ranking ineligible artifacts                    |
| B1          | Fielded Boolean templates               | Exact phrases, must/should/not, prefixes, NEAR             |     Very low | Route coverage and stop policy pass                | Paying a model to write common queries          |
| B2          | BM25/BM25F/FTS                          | Ranked lexical cards per field/capability                  |          Low | Consensus/coverage sufficient                      | Basic lexical relevance                         |
| B3          | Code-aware deterministic search         | Symbol/import/path/signature/AST/error matches             |          Low | Exact structural evidence sufficient               | Natural-language search missing code facts      |
| B4          | Morphology and typo branch              | Stems, lemmas, snake/camel splits, char trigrams           |          Low | Adds eligible coverage without drift               | Typos, naming variants, inflection              |
| B5          | Keyphrase/entity branch                 | TF-IDF/specificity, noun chunks, NER, TextRank-style terms |          Low | Terms meet specificity/novelty gates               | Long-prompt noise                               |
| B6          | Controlled ontology expansion           | Approved synonyms, aliases, parent/child concepts          |          Low | Expansion remains in ontology and scope            | Vocabulary mismatch without generation          |
| B7          | LSH blocking                            | Near-duplicate/set-overlap candidate buckets               |          Low | Use as candidate generation, not final rank        | Searching millions for obviously similar cards  |
| B8          | Deterministic tool facts                | Repo/schema/package/AST/test/stack-trace facts             | Low–variable | Facts resolve a plan slot                          | Asking an LLM what tools can inspect exactly    |
| C0          | Typed graph retrieval                   | Endpoints, connectors, required-capability coverage        |          Low | One eligible complete route                        | Top-k lists omitting necessary intermediates    |
| C1          | Learned sparse retrieval                | Expanded sparse term candidates                            | Low–moderate | Marginal held-out recall worth cost                | Lexical mismatch while retaining inverted index |
| C2          | Dense ANN by facet                      | Capability/I-O/effect/standard neighbor lists              | Low–moderate | Marginal eligible recall and route gain worth cost | Semantic paraphrases and unseen terminology     |
| C3          | Cluster/centroid routing                | Candidate partitions or index shards                       |          Low | Recall floor met in shadow evaluation              | ANN fan-out at 5M–40M scale                     |
| C4          | Rank fusion                             | RRF candidate union with provenance                        |          Low | Never treats fused score as permission             | Incomparable signal scales                      |
| C5          | Deterministic route compile             | Typed routes, unsatisfied constraints, ambiguity set       |          Low | Unique eligible route, or calibrated safe choice   | LLM-based integration                           |
| D0          | Stability probes                        | Relaxed/strict query variants and retriever agreement      |          Low | Ranking/route stable under perturbation            | Brittle single-query success                    |
| D1          | Guarded pseudo-relevance feedback       | Controlled added terms or vector centroid                  | Low–moderate | Top set coherent; second pass improves confidence  | Recoverable query/document mismatch             |
| D2          | Graph neighborhood expansion            | Compatible predecessors/successors, pack closure           | Low–moderate | Complete route emerges                             | Missing connector primitives                    |
| D3          | Local cross-encoder / late interaction  | Reranked top 20–200 cards                                  |     Moderate | Calibrated route confidence crosses threshold      | Fine semantic distinctions                      |
| D4          | Lightweight learned router              | Next-best acquisition action                               |     Very low | Selects one action or abstains                     | Always paying every tier                        |
| E0          | Local classifier/NER slot filler        | Task family, types, effects, intent enums                  |          Low | Only high-confidence typed additions accepted      | Deterministic parser gaps                       |
| E1          | Small local constrained LM              | Bounded AST patch and ambiguity rationale                  |     Moderate | Compiler validates patch and route                 | Free-form local query generation                |
| E2          | Minimal clarification                   | One discriminating question                                |        Human | Answer resolves high-value slot                    | Spending compute on unknowable intent           |
| F0          | Hosted embedding/reranker, if justified | Additional scores for compact cards                        |     Variable | Incremental value exceeds call cost                | Local-model quality ceiling                     |
| F1          | Hosted LLM query-delta writer           | Capped lexical/type/semantic variants in JSON              |         High | One call; rerun compiler and stop policy           | Last-mile vocabulary/intent ambiguity           |
| G0          | Foundry compile-once path               | New candidate implementation and tests                     |    High once | Promotion gates pass                               | No reusable implementation exists               |
| G1          | Direct bypass/from-scratch              | Task result without catalog promotion                      |     Variable | Expected reuse too low for compilation             | Retrieval costing more than displaced work      |
| H0          | Verification and learning               | Oracle, receipt, history update, caches                    |     Required | Store only validated outcomes                      | Turning one success into an unsafe prior        |

[SQLite FTS5](https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html) already supports phrases, prefixes, `NEAR`, column filters, Boolean operators, tokenizers, trigram indexing, and a built-in BM25 function, which is enough for a strong first implementation. [TextRank](https://aclanthology.org/W04-3252/) is one example of graph-based unsupervised keyword extraction. [SPLADE v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.10086) supplies learned sparse expansion while retaining sparse/inverted-index behavior. [BEIR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.08663) is a useful warning against declaring one retriever universally best: in its heterogeneous evaluation, BM25 was a robust baseline, while late interaction/reranking improved average zero-shot quality at higher compute cost. [ColBERTv2](https://aclanthology.org/2022.naacl-main.272/) shows the quality/space trade-off of token-level late interaction and residual compression.

For dense scale, [HNSW](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.09320) provides a graph-based approximate-nearest-neighbor design with a recall/latency control surface. [Faiss's billion-scale GPU work](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.08734) demonstrates compressed and approximate search at far larger scale than Taedri's initial targets. These papers establish candidate technologies, not an automatic choice: benchmark HNSW, IVF-PQ/OPQ, disk ANN, and partitioned variants on Taedri's vectors, filters, update rate, and hardware.

## How each query view is built without an LLM

### 1. Exact and literal view

Extract quoted spans, URIs, digests, standard numbers, error codes, package/version strings, class/function names, paths, CLI flags, MIME types, schema names, and type-like CamelCase tokens. Preserve punctuation and case in a literal index alongside normalized variants.

### 2. Fielded lexical view

Map request clauses to catalog fields. “Takes RawPageBatch and returns DatasetManifest without network access” should compile to mandatory input/output/effect predicates plus lexical capability terms. A model should not be required to rediscover that mapping every request.

Example conceptual query:

``` text
FILTER eligible(scope, lifecycle, policy)
AND input_type = "RawPageBatch"
AND output_type = "DatasetManifest"
AND effect NOT IN {"external_network"}
MATCH capability : (normalize OR filter OR deduplicate OR score)
MATCH output_description : "build manifest"
```

### 3. Code structural view

Split snake_case, kebab-case, dotted paths, and CamelCase while retaining the exact token. Parse code blocks and stack traces. Search dedicated fields for symbols, imports, packages, signatures, decorators, schema keys, test names, error text, and AST patterns. When a repository is in scope, deterministic tools can inspect manifests, imports, definitions, call sites, schemas, and tests and add those facts to the plan.

### 4. Cheap keyphrase and entity view

Use corpus-aware term specificity, noun chunks, named entities, domain dictionaries, and an unsupervised keyphrase method. Downweight generic request language such as “help,” “build,” and “best.” Retain negation and modal language separately; a keyphrase extractor must never erase “must not,” version limits, or security conditions.

### 5. Controlled semantic view

Use taxonomy aliases and approved synonym/abbreviation maps first. Then encode separate prompt clauses into facet-specific local vectors. Search only the matching card vector family. This is cheaper and less noisy than issuing every vector against every facet.

### 6. LSH/blocking view

Use MinHash for Jaccard-like overlap of token shingles, capability/tag sets, imports, dependencies, API sets, or signatures. Use SimHash-like fingerprints for near-duplicate descriptions and query exemplars. Character n-gram buckets are often better for typos and naming variation. LSH should reduce the search region or surface near duplicates; it should not be the final relevance score.

### 7. Historical view

Retrieve previously successful demand-to-recipe bindings by exact digest, task family, environment, and nearest demand features. History is a prior, not permission. Revalidate authorization, lifecycle, contracts, effects, artifact digests, and oracle eligibility every time.

### 8. Template view

Maintain versioned templates per task family. The compiler fills typed slots and conditionally includes clauses:

``` text
if exact_ids: ExactLookup(exact_ids)
if input_types: Filter(input_type in input_types)
if output_types: Filter(output_type in output_types)
if must_terms: LexicalMust(must_terms)
if error_literals: ErrorPhraseSearch(error_literals)
if code_symbols: SymbolSearch(code_symbols)
if semantic_clauses: DenseKNN(facet=clause.label, vector=embed(clause.text))
if required_capabilities: TopKPerCapability(required_capabilities)
```

Templates should build a query AST and use parameter binding. Do not concatenate user strings into a backend query language.

### 9. Small-model view

Before any autoregressive model, try a local multilabel classifier, NER model, embedding classifier, or nearest labeled exemplar for task family, types, effects, and domain. If an autoregressive local model is needed, it should receive only unresolved slots, allowed enum values, and a compact ambiguity certificate. Its output is a bounded AST patch.
