## CLI additions

### Edge inspection and search

``` bash
# Exact edge and assertion inspection
tcg edge show <relation-id> --assertions --features --epoch <epoch>
tcg edge assertions <relation-id> --polarity all --modality all
tcg edge evidence <relation-id-or-assertion-id>
tcg edge explain <relation-id> --show-score --show-aggregation

# Fielded edge search
tcg edge search 'public methods calling network writers without direct tests' \
  --predicate calls_may \
  --source-visibility public \
  --target-effect network.write \
  --without incoming:tests \
  --evidence-min extracted \
  --limit 50

tcg edge search --source-package mypkg --target-package otherpkg \
  --predicate calls_may,data_flows_to --feature dispatch.kind=dynamic

tcg edge neighbors <entity-id> --direction both --predicate calls_may,tests \
  --edge-filter 'evidence.modality>=extracted' --page-size 100

# Bounded patterns and changes
tcg edge pattern run fixtures/queries/untested_network_path.yaml --max-expansions 100000
tcg edge diff --from <epoch-a> --to <epoch-b> --attribute-coverage-changes
tcg edge negatives search --scope <package-or-build> --authoritative-only
tcg edge features describe runtime.success_rate
tcg edge features validate <candidate-epoch>
```

### Compatibility signatures and decisions

``` bash
# Inspect variants and compare their canonical facets
tcg compat signature show <entity-or-port-id> --variants --detail full
tcg compat signature diff <signature-a> <signature-b>

# Directional checks
tcg compat check \
  --producer <entity-a>:output \
  --consumer <entity-b>:input \
  --purpose compose \
  --environment env:python312-linux-x86_64 \
  --require type,shape,effects,errors,security,runtime \
  --explain

tcg compat substitute --required <old-entity> --candidate <new-entity> \
  --demand demand.yaml --policy-epoch <epoch>

# High-recall candidates followed by exact checking
tcg compat candidates --producer <entity>:output --consumer-scope pypi \
  --limit 100 --verdict exact,proved_refinement,verified_lossless_adapter

tcg compat adapters --producer <port-a> --consumer <port-b> \
  --max-hops 3 --lossless-only --show-obligations

tcg compat explain <decision-id> --dimensions --premises --witness
tcg compat replay <decision-id>
tcg compat no-route <decision-id> --minimal-core
tcg compat materialize <decision-id> --if-verified --dry-run
```

The CLI must never default from `UNKNOWN` to compatible. A matrix command must require bounded sets; an unbounded all-pairs compatibility command should not exist.

## MCP additions without tool-catalog explosion

Add two meta-tools and extend three existing ones.

### New `code_edge_search`

Operations: `search`, `show`, `pattern`, `diff`, `negatives`, `explain`.

Inputs include text query, source/target filters, predicates, typed feature constraints, polarity, modality/evidence floor, validity, graph epoch, result/detail/token budgets, and cursor. Returns compact edge handles, endpoint handles, decisive features/assertions, coverage, and expansion handles. Source bodies are never returned inline.

### New `code_compatibility`

Operations: `signatures`, `check`, `candidates`, `adapters`, `explain`, `replay`, `minimal_core`.

Inputs include producer/consumer handles and ports, purpose, required dimensions, demand/environment/policy handles, adapter/loss policy, candidate and token budgets, and pinned epochs. Returns a compact `CompatibilityCard` containing verdict, dimension outcomes, obligations, mismatch/unknown core, adapter handles, and witness handle.

### Extend existing tools

- `code_search` accepts `target_kind: entity|edge|relation|signature` and may return edge handles while preserving distinct result schemas.
- `code_expand` accepts edge-feature filters, assertion modality/polarity, validity scope, and `include_compatibility_witnesses`.
- `code_path` distinguishes observed/extracted paths from possible compatibility routes, exposes per-edge witness handles, and never mixes them without labeling.

Add MCP resources:

- `codegraph://relations/{relation_id}/card`
- `codegraph://relations/{relation_id}/assertions`
- `codegraph://compatibility/signatures/{signature_id}`
- `codegraph://compatibility/decisions/{decision_id}`
- `codegraph://compatibility/witnesses/{witness_id}`
- `codegraph://compatibility/no-route/{decision_id}`

## Query semantics and ranking

### Hard filters precede ranking

The edge query pipeline is:

``` text
authorize request and source scopes
  -> pin graph/policy/evidence epochs
  -> exact/structured edge blocking
  -> apply polarity, validity, lifecycle, and evidence floors
  -> fielded lexical/structural/optional semantic candidate union
  -> typed edge and pattern constraints
  -> edge-specific ranking
  -> compact result and explanation projection
```

An edge ranker may use endpoint match, predicate match, call-site match, evidence authority, task affinity, graph rarity, runtime support, freshness, and cost. It must expose score contributions by feature family. It must not turn a high similarity score into an executable compatibility edge.

### Compatibility candidate pipeline

``` text
producer/consumer signature variants
  -> purpose-specific mandatory facets
  -> exact signature/type/schema/media/unit/protocol partitions
  -> environment/effect/security/policy blocking
  -> explicit adapter endpoint joins
  -> bounded request-local candidate pairs
  -> full dimension rules
  -> obligations and adapter-chain validation
  -> witness or minimal unsatisfied core
  -> optionally materialize high-value verified result
```

Blocking is allowed to over-retrieve but not to drop known compatible golden pairs. Full rules own the decision. Approximate indexes can nominate candidates only.

## Twelve-week extension plan and acceptance criteria

This plan assumes the base identity, source acquisition, entity graph, epoch, and query infrastructure from the main repository blueprint is being built in parallel. Each week has an objective exit condition rather than “feature implemented.”

### Week 1 — relation identity, assertion separation, and ontology

- Freeze `RelationKey`, `EdgeAssertion`, polarity, modality, endpoint role, and n-ary relation semantics.
- Define canonical IDs and inverse-predicate rules.
- Register the first 100 core predicates with source/target kind constraints.
- Build at least 75 golden relations covering duplicate endpoints, multiple call sites, supporting/refuting assertions, unknowns, scopes, and n-ary calls.

**Acceptance:** Python and TypeScript produce byte-identical relation/assertion IDs; no assertion producer field affects `RelationKeyID`; inverse-edge round trips and ontology constraints pass 100% of golden cases.

### Week 2 — typed edge features and projection boundaries

- Implement `EdgeFeatureDefinition`, typed values, authority classes, required scopes, and registry versioning.
- Define at least 60 core/Python/runtime/search features.
- Implement deterministic edge search documents and projection manifests.
- Add tests proving learned/rank-only features cannot enter proof or authorization APIs.

**Acceptance:** every indexed feature resolves to an exact registry definition/version; changing a projection feature does not alter canonical relation/assertion IDs; forbidden authority escalation fails closed.

### Week 3 — Python relationship extraction

- Normalize imports, definitions/references, calls/candidates, bindings, inheritance/override, type, tests, docs, effects, and entry-point relations.
- Retain call-site and argument-binding relation nodes.
- Emit explicit dynamic/reflective/native uncertainty and analyzer coverage.

**Acceptance:** supported golden relation recall is at least 99% for syntax/binding facts and at least 95% for the declared precise-reference/call subset; 100% of unsupported dynamic/native cases carry visible uncertainty rather than fabricated exact targets.

### Week 4 — exact, bitmap, lexical, numeric, and adjacency edge indexes

- Build exact relation/assertion lookup, typed bitmap filters, fielded lexical documents, numeric ranges, and paged forward/reverse adjacency.
- Handle supernodes with deterministic cursors and hard limits.
- Implement edge search explanations and baseline exact/predicate/ripgrep comparisons.

**Acceptance:** exact golden edge queries are 100% top-1; every hit reports decisive fields/assertions, epochs, coverage, and truncation; at ten million synthetic-plus-real edges on the reference host, exact lookup p95 is below 25 ms and filtered top-20 search p95 below 250 ms warm-cache.

### Week 5 — bounded edge patterns, temporal search, and diffs

- Implement typed pattern DSL, bounded matcher, temporal validity, edge/assertion diff, and coverage-change attribution.
- Distinguish “edge changed” from “analyzer or coverage changed.”
- Add negative/no-good projection with authoritative versus heuristic classes.

**Acceptance:** all pattern queries require node/edge/expansion/time budgets; stable replay under a pinned epoch is byte-deterministic; version-diff fixtures attribute 100% of expected source changes and coverage-only changes correctly; heuristic negatives never hard-exclude.

### Week 6 — compatibility signature variants

- Implement ports, canonical facet references, activation constraints, overload/configuration variants, facet digests, and unknown coverage.
- Build Python type/signature/shape/error/effect/environment facets without importing packages.
- Preserve standard-native contract references.

**Acceptance:** mutually exclusive overload/configuration variants never collapse into an artificial union; identical facets produce identical digests; a changed facet invalidates its signature while an unrelated body-only change does not; every required missing facet is `UNKNOWN`, never wildcard.

### Week 7 — deterministic directional compatibility rules

- Implement purpose-specific composition and substitution rules.
- Add exact identity, nominal/structural type, cardinality, required-field, nullability, media/serialization, units, effects, errors, runtime/version, and policy rules.
- Produce dimension decisions, witnesses, obligations, and minimal unsatisfied cores.

**Acceptance:** the golden compatibility suite, including deliberately convincing near-miss pairs, has zero false auto-wires; every `EXACT` or `PROVED_REFINEMENT` decision replays to the same proof digest; incompatibility identifies at least one authoritative minimal blocker; unsupported reasoning returns `UNKNOWN`.

### Week 8 — blocking indexes, adapter registry, and decision cache

- Build signature partitions and high-recall candidate generation.
- Implement endpoint-bound adapter contracts, verified loss/lossless classifications, obligations, and adapter-chain limits.
- Implement full compatibility cache key and fine-grained invalidation.

**Acceptance:** on a benchmark of at least 100,000 ports, blocking removes at least 99% of naïve pairs while retaining 100% of labeled compatible pairs; no generic adapter proof is reused across unverified endpoints; policy/ruleset/evidence changes invalidate decisions without re-extracting source.

### Week 9 — request-local compatibility graph and route semantics

- Construct bounded pairwise/hypergraph closures from compatible ports, state, authority, and resources.
- Distinguish observed code edges from possible compatibility edges in every path result.
- Add no-route certificates and local repair around an invalidated edge.

**Acceptance:** all route edges carry witnesses or are clearly marked non-executable candidates; global constraints catch fixtures where pairwise compatibility is insufficient; invalidating one signature repairs/rejects only dependent route regions; no all-pairs graph is materialized.

### Week 10 — CLI/API/MCP integration

- Ship edge and compatibility CLI commands, versioned endpoints, `code_edge_search`, `code_compatibility`, and extensions to search/expand/path.
- Add compact `EdgeCard`, `CompatibilityCard`, witness, and no-route resources.
- Test two coding harnesses on existing-code discovery, impact, reuse, and migration tasks.

**Acceptance:** an agent can search an edge, inspect evidence, check a directional connection, retrieve only decisive facets, and replay the witness without receiving full repository bodies; hard token/node/edge/path limits hold in all conformance tests.

### Week 11 — real corpus, calibration, security, and scale

- Index edges/signatures for at least 1,000 stratified package releases.
- Label edge-search, compatibility, adapter, hard-negative, and version-migration workloads.
- Run tenant/policy, stale-evidence, prompt-injection, supernode, malformed contract, and resource-exhaustion tests.
- Evaluate optional edge embeddings/rankers as recall/ranking arms only.

**Acceptance:** all policy-isolation tests pass; authoritative edge assertions have 100% producer/evidence/scope traceability; optional learned retrieval beats the deterministic candidate union on a named metric or remains disabled; all performance results publish corpus, hardware, cache, and coverage conditions.

### Week 12 — release gate and reproducible proof bundle

- Freeze the initial predicate, feature, compatibility-dimension, verdict, and rule registries.
- Run contract, golden, differential, determinism, invalidation, search, compatibility, adapter, security, fault, MCP, and scale suites.
- Publish exact corpus/artifact locks, analyzer/ruleset versions, decisions, witnesses, and reproduction commands.

**Acceptance:** all prior weekly gates pass; zero `UNKNOWN`, semantic-candidate, heuristic-negative, or rank-only result can authorize composition; edge search and compatibility decisions are reproducible from receipts; a clean installation can demonstrate edge discovery, impact, substitution, adapter selection, incompatibility explanation, and version migration.

## Definition of done for a searchable edge feature

An edge feature is not complete until it has:

- a stable registry key and versioned semantics;
- a typed value, unit/cardinality, missing-value meaning, and required scope;
- an authority class that is enforced in code;
- an exact producer and derivation reference;
- deterministic invalidation dependencies;
- authorization, privacy, and license propagation behavior;
- index, query, sorting, aggregation, and explanation tests;
- negative and unknown fixtures;
- storage, indexing, and latency measurements;
- an ablation demonstrating value on an edge-search, impact, route, or compatibility workload.

## Definition of done for a compatibility rule

A compatibility rule is not complete until it has:

- a stable rule ID, version, purpose, direction, and supported facet languages;
- exact premise and conclusion schemas;
- explicit `INCOMPATIBLE`, `UNKNOWN`, and obligation behavior;
- positive, negative, boundary, interaction, and adversarial near-match vectors;
- a replayable witness or minimal unsatisfied core;
- declared soundness limitations and coverage;
- cache and invalidation semantics;
- policy and adapter interaction tests;
- no path by which similarity, popularity, or an uncalibrated confidence score can upgrade its verdict.

## Final architectural rule

Make edges richly searchable, but keep search and truth separate. Make signatures compact and reusable, but keep compatibility directional, scoped, and demand-specific. The model may discover promising relationships, describe an ambiguity, or choose among already admissible alternatives. Only the versioned rule engine, evidence policy, and verified adapters may turn existing code entities into an executable connection.

# Taedri CodeGraph: First-Class Searchable Edge Subsystem

> **ANNEX STATUS — TARGET SUBSYSTEM SPECIFICATION.** This section describes the
> intended complete edge service and scale strategy, not a deployed production
> subsystem.

## Purpose

The edge subsystem makes relationships—not only nodes—addressable, searchable, rankable, explainable, composable, and verifiable. It supports two different objects without conflating them:

1.  **Observed/asserted edges:** relations already extracted, inferred, observed, or verified, such as `calls`, `reads`, `implements`, `tests`, `data_flows_to`, or `converts_to`.
2.  **Potential compatibility edges:** relationships that might validly connect two ports/entities but must be discovered and assessed on demand.

The system must never materialize every possible pair. At 100 million ports, all-pairs compatibility would require roughly `5e15` undirected pair checks. Instead, precompute unary signatures and indexes, retrieve small high-recall candidate blocks, solve only requested pairs, and materialize only frequently reused or independently verified results.

## Design invariants

1.  An edge is an evidence-bearing claim, not an unqualified fact.
2.  Exact extracted edges and possible compatibility edges use separate records and lifecycles.
3.  Every endpoint is role- and direction-aware; `output -> input` is not interchangeable with `input -> output`.
4.  Absence of an edge means unknown unless declared analysis coverage proves a negative.
5.  Hard incompatibility may only be asserted from sufficiently authoritative evidence.
6.  Low-confidence or missing fields may broaden retrieval but must not silently block candidates.
7.  Pairwise features are computed on demand; no binary feature table scales as `N^2`.
8.  Search and compatibility decisions are pinned to graph, schema, policy, signature, adapter, model, and solver versions.
9.  Authorization filters run before candidate generation and graph expansion.
10. A score never replaces the axis-level verdicts, unresolved predicates, evidence, or explanation.

## Conceptual object model

``` text
Entity/Port
  -> CompatibilitySignature        # unary, precomputed
  -> exact/block/LSH/vector indexes

EdgeAssertion                      # explicit relation claim
  -> EdgeFeatureBundle             # searchable unary edge document

(source signature, target signature, demand/policy)
  -> PairFeatureBundle             # binary, built lazily
  -> CompatibilityAssessment       # typed verdict and explanation
  -> optional MaterializedCompatibilityEdge
```

For an n-ary relation such as a call, build, test, or flow, retain one canonical relation node and expose searchable role-bound projections—such as `caller -> callee`, `argument -> parameter`, and `test -> subject`—that all point back to the same relation ID. Do not destroy argument bindings or relation-level evidence by flattening the canonical record.

## 1. EdgeAssertion

``` yaml
EdgeAssertion:
  edge_assertion_id: ceg:v1:edgeassertion:...
  edge_claim_key: ceg:v1:edgeclaim:...
  relation_id: optional
  predicate: calls_may
  endpoints:
    - {role: caller, entity_or_port_id: ...}
    - {role: callee, entity_or_port_id: ...}
  direction: caller_to_callee
  modality: asserted|extracted|inferred|observed|verified
  quantifier: may|must|observed
  polarity: positive|negative|unknown
  scope:
    source_snapshot_id: ...
    build_universe_id: ...
    environment_id: optional
    graph_epoch: ...
  producer:
    id: scip-python
    version: ...
    config_digest: ...
  evidence_refs: []
  confidence: optional
  calibration_version: optional
  coverage_ref: ...
  valid_from: optional
  valid_to: optional
```

`edge_claim_key` groups assertions about the same scoped proposition. `edge_assertion_id` includes producer/evidence identity so compiler, static-analysis, runtime, documentation, and LLM assertions can coexist and conflict without overwriting one another.

## 2. EdgeFeatureBundle

`EdgeFeatureBundle` is the versioned searchable projection for an explicit edge or relation-role projection. It contains only reproducible features and references the evidence from which each feature was derived.

``` yaml
EdgeFeatureBundle:
  bundle_id: ceg:v1:edgebundle:...
  edge_assertion_ids: []
  edge_claim_key: ...
  relation_id: optional
  predicate_family: execution|flow|type|structure|test|effect|lineage|...
  predicate: calls_may
  endpoint_roles: []
  source_endpoint_projection: {}
  target_endpoint_projection: {}

  lexical:
    native_names: []
    qualified_names: []
    aliases: []
    tags: []
    descriptions: []
    examples: []
    errors: []
    standards: []

  contract:
    input_port_refs: []
    output_port_refs: []
    precondition_refs: []
    postcondition_refs: []
    effect_refs: []
    error_contract_refs: []
    adapter_refs: []

  topology:
    endpoint_kinds: []
    containment_path_ids: []
    typed_degrees: {}
    neighborhood_signature_refs: []
    path_signature_refs: []
    centrality_bucket: optional

  operational:
    observed_successes: optional
    observed_failures: optional
    latency_distribution_ref: optional
    resource_profile_ref: optional
    freshness: ...

  policy:
    tenant_acl_bitmap_ref: ...
    access_class: ...
    license_classes: []
    trust_zone: optional

  fingerprints:
    exact: []
    lsh: []
    embedding_refs: []
    graph: []

  feature_evidence_map: {}
  feature_schema_version: ...
  generator_version: ...
  input_fact_digest: ...
  graph_epoch: ...
```

Do not store one opaque “edge embedding.” Keep independently queryable fields for predicate, endpoint roles, source semantics, target semantics, effects, errors, topology, standards, and evidence. The search planner can select the relevant channels for a task and avoid misleading similarity from irrelevant prose.

## 3. CompatibilitySignature

`CompatibilitySignature` is a compact unary projection of one port or boundary. It exists specifically to block, retrieve, and prepare pair solving.

``` yaml
CompatibilitySignature:
  signature_id: ceg:v1:compsig:...
  subject_id: ceg:v1:port:...
  owner_entity_id: ...
  orientation: produces|accepts|bidirectional|effect|control
  port_role: parameter|return|yield|error|event|resource|state|...

  type_contract:
    nominal_type_ids: []
    structural_schema_refs: []
    type_constructor_heads: []
    subtype_ancestor_ids: []
    generic_constraints: []
    nullability: ...

  value_contract:
    semantic_roles: []
    units: []
    dimensions: []
    ranges: []
    enums: []
    invariants: []

  transport_contract:
    media_types: []
    encodings: []
    protocols: []
    serialization_schemas: []
    cardinality: one|optional|many|map|unknown
    temporal_mode: sync|async|stream|batch|event|unknown
    ordering: ordered|unordered|unknown

  behavioral_contract:
    preconditions: []
    postconditions: []
    error_models: []
    mutability: ...
    ownership_lifetime: ...
    idempotency: ...
    determinism: ...
    state_requirements: []

  effect_contract:
    may_effects: []
    must_effects: []
    capabilities_required: []
    resources_required: []

  environment_contract:
    languages: []
    runtimes: []
    platforms: []
    dependency_constraints: []
    version_intervals: []

  policy_contract:
    trust_zones: []
    data_classes: []
    tenant_scope: ...
    licenses: []
    prohibited_capabilities: []

  quality_contract:
    latency_budget: optional
    memory_budget: optional
    reliability_floor: optional
    lossiness_allowed: optional

  block_keys: []
  fingerprint_refs: []
  feature_evidence_map: {}
  coverage_ref: ...
  signature_schema_version: ...
  generator_version: ...
  input_fact_digest: ...
  graph_epoch: ...
```

Fields are multi-valued because types, protocols, units, and runtime behavior can be conditional or disputed. Each value carries modality, producer, evidence, confidence, and applicable scope through `feature_evidence_map`.

## 4. Compatibility axes

Every pair assessment retains a verdict for each relevant axis:

1.  role and direction;
2.  nominal type/subtyping;
3.  structural schema/shape;
4.  generic constraints and variance;
5.  semantic role and intended meaning;
6.  units, physical dimensions, ranges, enums, and invariants;
7.  cardinality and collection semantics;
8.  ordering and duplication semantics;
9.  synchronous/asynchronous/stream/batch/event temporal mode;
10. protocol, media type, encoding, and serialization;
11. ownership, lifetime, borrowing, and mutability;
12. preconditions and postconditions;
13. error/exception/result model;
14. state transition and transaction semantics;
15. idempotency, determinism, and retry safety;
16. side effects and required capabilities;
17. language/runtime/platform/ABI compatibility;
18. dependency and version interval compatibility;
19. security, privacy, tenant, and trust-zone policy;
20. license/provenance composition policy;
21. resource, latency, throughput, and reliability budgets;
22. adapter/converter availability, cost, and lossiness;
23. test/oracle and historical success evidence;
24. freshness and analysis coverage.

Hard versus soft is demand- and policy-specific. A unit mismatch may be hard for a physical-control system and repairable with a verified conversion elsewhere. A latency miss may be soft during exploration and hard in deployment. Store this classification in the request/policy, not permanently in the signature.

## 5. CompatibilityAssessment

``` yaml
CompatibilityAssessment:
  assessment_id: ceg:v1:compassessment:...
  pair_key: ...
  source_signature_id: ...
  target_signature_id: ...
  demand_ir_digest: ...
  policy_digest: ...
  decision: compatible|incompatible|compatible_with_adapter|unknown
  hard_gate: pass|fail|unknown

  axes:
    - axis: structural_schema
      verdict: pass|fail|partial|unknown|repairable
      score: optional
      evidence_refs: []
      explanation_code: ...

  required_adapter_routes: []
  unresolved_predicates: []
  contradiction_refs: []
  unsat_core: []
  proof_or_derivation_refs: []

  probability_verified_success: optional
  probability_calibration_version: optional
  score_vector: {}
  aggregate_utility: optional
  uncertainty: ...

  solver:
    id: ...
    version: ...
    config_digest: ...
  adapter_graph_epoch: ...
  graph_epoch: ...
  created_at: ...
  expires_or_invalidates_on: []
```

`unsat_core` lists the smallest known set of hard constraints causing incompatibility. `unresolved_predicates` makes abstention actionable. `compatible_with_adapter` is not equivalent to direct compatibility and must include the exact adapter route, transformations, new effects, information loss, and cost.

## 6. Fingerprint families

Use several independent, versioned fingerprints. No fingerprint is identity or proof of compatibility.

### Exact fingerprints

- canonical endpoint contract digest;
- predicate + endpoint-role digest;
- exact nominal type and structured-signature digests;
- canonical schema-shape digest;
- effect/capability set digest;
- protocol/media/encoding digest;
- error-model digest;
- build/runtime/platform digest;
- normalized example input/output digest;
- exact adapter contract digest.

Canonicalization must specify Unicode normalization, case rules, field ordering, namespace authority, numeric/unit normalization, set versus sequence semantics, and schema version. Store the full canonical key with the digest.

### LSH and clone fingerprints

- MinHash for tag, type-path, schema-field, effect, error, import, and API-usage sets;
- weighted MinHash for weighted semantic-role and field sets;
- SimHash for short descriptions, docstrings, error vocabulary, and normalized examples;
- winnowing/Merkle-subtree hashes for code or AST clone families;
- banded locality-sensitive buckets with explicit family/version parameters.

Use these for candidate generation, never as a final compatibility verdict. Maintain separate buckets per field family so similar docs do not overwhelm incompatible schemas.

### Embedding fingerprints

Store separate vectors for:

- source/output meaning;
- target/input meaning;
- relation/predicate intent;
- pre/postconditions;
- effects and errors;
- examples and usage;
- optional graph-neighborhood embedding.

Every vector record pins model ID/checkpoint digest, tokenizer/preprocessing, dimensionality, pooling, source fact refs, quantization, and creation epoch. Model upgrades create new parallel indexes and canary evaluation; they do not overwrite old vectors.

### Graph fingerprints

- typed degree histograms;
- role-aware one-, two-, and three-hop neighborhood multiset hashes;
- bounded Weisfeiler-Lehman-style hashes using predicate and endpoint-role labels;
- containment-path and package-boundary signatures;
- bounded path MinHashes;
- test, effect, dependency, and co-change neighborhood signatures;
- strongly connected component/community IDs with algorithm/version;
- optional role-aware random-walk or graph-model vectors.

Graph fingerprints help find structurally analogous edges and routes. They are snapshot/build scoped; a matching hash is similarity evidence, not semantic equivalence.

## 7. Avoiding O(N^2): candidate generation architecture

### 7.1 Authorization and lifecycle gate

Start with tenant/ACL, graph epoch, artifact lifecycle, source/build scope, and revoked-content bitmaps. Unauthorized IDs never enter ranking statistics or graph traversals.

### 7.2 Typed block indexes

Precompute inverted indexes from block key to sorted integer port/edge IDs. Use Roaring bitmaps for fast intersection/union. Useful block families include:

``` text
orientation / port role
entity and predicate family
exact type / type constructor / subtype ancestor
schema shape family
semantic role / unit dimension
protocol / media type / encoding
cardinality / temporal mode
runtime / platform / ABI
effect and capability class
trust zone / data class / tenant
version interval bucket
adapter input/output family
```

Blocks are hierarchical and multi-valued. Search exact type first, then ancestors/structural family, then known adapter domains, then an explicit unknown bucket if budget allows. Never use a weak inferred semantic tag as a sole hard block.

### 7.3 Parallel high-recall candidate generators

Within eligible blocks, run independent generators in parallel:

- exact contract/history/cache;
- lexical BM25 and sparse features;
- structural/AST fingerprints;
- MinHash/SimHash/clone LSH;
- vector ANN for selected semantic channels;
- graph-neighborhood/path fingerprints;
- historically successful co-use/routes;
- adapter-domain lookup.

Fuse IDs by calibrated rank fusion, not naive score addition across incomparable scales. Record which generators retrieved each candidate.

### 7.4 Progressive broadening

Use a deterministic relaxation schedule:

``` text
exact direct compatibility
-> subtype/structural equivalents
-> one verified adapter
-> broader lexical/LSH/ANN blocks
-> two-adapter route
-> unknown-field canopy
-> constrained local model reformulation
-> strong-model exploration only if still unresolved
```

Each broadening has a maximum candidates, latency, compute, and uncertainty budget. Stop when enough non-dominated verified candidates exist; do not automatically traverse every stage.

### 7.5 Query-time pair solving

Build `PairFeatureBundle` only for the top `M` candidates. Compare exact axes first and short-circuit on an authoritative hard failure. Invoke more expensive schema unification, constraint solving, static analysis, sandbox probes, or model judgment only for unresolved axes whose value of information exceeds cost.

### 7.6 Selective materialization

Materialize a compatibility edge only when it is:

- independently verified;
- repeatedly requested;
- part of an accepted compiled route;
- an ecosystem-standard adapter;
- or explicitly curated.

Cache negative assessments only with exact dependency/version keys and short or event-driven validity. A negative based on missing data must not poison future retrieval after a new analyzer fills the gap.

### 7.7 Routes without global expansion

For multi-edge composition, use bounded bidirectional multi-objective Dijkstra/A\* or constrained shortest-path search:

- forward from producer/output and backward from demanded input/effect;
- expand only typed block candidates for the current frontier signature;
- carry transformed schema/type/effect/policy state in the search state;
- prune dominated states by cost, risk, loss, latency, and uncertainty;
- bound path length, branching, repeated adapter families, and total pair solves;
- use proven adapter hubs and cached successful subroutes;
- prohibit cycles unless the route contract explicitly needs feedback.

## 8. Query API

### Core operations

``` text
edge.search_assertions       Search already known relations.
edge.neighbors               Retrieve typed incoming/outgoing relation projections.
edge.compatible_from         Find targets compatible with a source port/boundary.
edge.compatible_to           Find sources compatible with a target port/boundary.
edge.assess_pair             Produce an axis-level CompatibilityAssessment.
edge.find_adapter            Find direct or bounded adapter routes.
edge.route                   Solve a typed multi-edge composition route.
edge.explain                 Resolve scores, evidence, conflicts, and exclusions.
edge.compare                 Compare edge/assessment alternatives by full vector.
edge.materialized_history    Retrieve previously verified/accepted edges and routes.
edge.resolve_body            Resolve selected endpoints/native facts after selection.
```

### EdgeSearchRequest

``` yaml
EdgeSearchRequest:
  request_id: ...
  operation: compatible_from
  demand_ir_ref: ...
  source_endpoint_ids: []
  target_endpoint_ids: []
  predicate_families: []
  required_axes: {}
  preferred_axes: {}
  prohibited_effects: []
  required_evidence_modalities: []
  environment: {}
  policy_context_ref: ...
  graph_epoch: ...
  workspace_snapshot_id: optional
  allowed_relaxations: []
  max_candidates: ...
  max_pair_solves: ...
  max_route_length: ...
  latency_budget_ms: ...
  compute_budget: ...
  token_budget: ...
  top_k: ...
  diversity_policy: ...
  explain_level: none|summary|full
```

### EdgeSearchHit

Return the edge/route handle, endpoint handles, axis vector, aggregate utility, uncertainty, direct-versus-adapted status, decisive evidence, unresolved predicates, generator provenance, and a body-resolution handle. Never force source bodies into the initial hit.

### EdgeSearchReceipt

Record graph/policy/index/solver versions, candidate count at each stage, bitmap blocks applied, exclusions by reason, generator hits, pair solves, cache hits, broadening steps, models/tools/probes invoked, timing/cost, selected alternatives, and final abstention/decision. This receipt is essential for evaluation and debugging retrieval regressions.

## 9. Scoring waterfall

1.  **Exact/replay:** explicit edge handle, exact claim key, accepted route, pair assessment cache.
2.  **Policy/lifecycle gate:** authorization, revocation, environment and version eligibility.
3.  **Hard typed block:** direction, role, known incompatible type/schema/protocol/platform/policy axes.
4.  **Exact fingerprints:** contract, schema, type, effects, protocol, and adapter hashes.
5.  **Cheap retrieval:** BM25/sparse, LSH, clone, and graph-fingerprint candidates.
6.  **Semantic ANN:** only selected channels and only inside eligible canopies.
7.  **Rank fusion/diversity:** merge generators, deduplicate aliases/copies, retain distinct route families.
8.  **Deterministic pair solve:** axis comparisons, type/schema unification, constraints, adapter lookup, unsat cores.
9.  **Local learned reranker:** calibrated probability of verified success by task/edge family.
10. **Active discrimination:** cheapest decisive static query, test, or safe sandbox probe.
11. **Constrained SLM/LLM:** fill only unresolved structured axes or choose among compact handles; preserve abstention.
12. **Independent verification:** required before a new compatibility edge becomes trusted/materialized.

Hard gates remain separate from ranking. For eligible candidate `c` under demand `d`, retain a score vector and optionally compute:

``` text
U(c|d) = P_verified_success(c|d) * V_success(d)
         - execution_cost(c)
         - adapter_cost_and_loss(c)
         - verification_cost(c)
         - failure_risk(c|d)
         - uncertainty_penalty(c)
         - staleness_penalty(c)
```

Prefer Pareto-nondominated alternatives when cost, quality, latency, lossiness, and evidence strength conflict. Test result sets at 1/2/4/8 alternatives and multiple detail levels. Do not optimize a single weighted score without also measuring false-confident compatibility and no-match abstention.

## 10. Evidence and provenance

Every feature value should be representable as:

``` yaml
FeatureAssertion:
  feature_key: ...
  value: ...
  modality: asserted|extracted|inferred|observed|verified
  polarity: positive|negative|unknown
  producer: {id: ..., version: ..., config_digest: ...}
  evidence_refs: []
  snapshot_or_build_scope: ...
  confidence: optional
  calibration_version: optional
  valid_time: optional
```

Evidence authority is fact-specific. Compiler type resolution may dominate a docstring for nominal type; a runtime trace can prove one observed dynamic target but not exclude unobserved targets; a property test can support behavior within its generated domain; an LLM description remains inferred. Conflict resolution creates a query-time projection and retains all original assertions.

An assessment explanation should answer:

- Which axes passed, failed, were repaired, or remain unknown?
- Which evidence and coverage support each verdict?
- Which blocks and candidate generators admitted this edge?
- Why were close alternatives excluded?
- What adapter or proof would change the verdict?
- What versions or events invalidate it?

## 11. Versioning and invalidation

### Immutable identifiers

``` text
EdgeClaimKey = H(canonical scoped proposition)
EdgeAssertionID = H(EdgeClaimKey + producer + analysis + evidence identity)
SignatureID = H(subject exact ID + input fact IDs + signature schema/generator)
BundleID = H(edge assertion set + feature inputs + bundle schema/generator)
EmbeddingID = H(input refs + model/checkpoint + preprocessing + quantization)
PairKey = H(source SignatureID + target SignatureID + direction)
AssessmentID = H(PairKey + demand/policy + solver + adapter graph epoch)
```

### Dependency-aware invalidation

- source/body/signature changes invalidate affected port signatures and dependent bundles;
- dependency/build/flag changes invalidate semantic type/call/flow signatures even if file bytes do not change;
- evidence additions create new assertions and may invalidate reconciled projections or assessments;
- policy/ACL changes invalidate eligibility and caches immediately without waiting for a graph rebuild;
- adapter changes invalidate assessments/routes that referenced the adapter graph epoch;
- embedding/model changes build parallel indexes and invalidate only that vector projection;
- history/outcome updates change learned ranking features, not canonical edge claims;
- graph topology changes invalidate neighborhood/path fingerprints within their declared radius or affected component;
- expired runtime evidence remains historical but is not current evidence for a new build/environment.

Maintain a reverse dependency index from derived record to exact input fact IDs. Publish immutable epochs and a small workspace overlay. Cache keys include all relevant version IDs; never “refresh” an assessment in place under the same ID.

## 12. Storage and index choices

| Need                                   | Recommended representation                                                                       |
|----------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Canonical facts/bundles/evidence       | Immutable Protobuf plus Arrow/Parquet shards in CAS/object storage                               |
| Exact IDs, pair cache, dependency map  | RocksDB/LMDB locally or a distributed KV at service scale                                        |
| Typed blocks and ACL/lifecycle filters | Dense internal integer IDs + Roaring bitmaps                                                     |
| Fielded lexical/sparse search          | Tantivy for embedded/local; OpenSearch/Elasticsearch when distributed operations justify it      |
| LSH buckets                            | KV postings keyed by fingerprint family/version/band/bucket                                      |
| Forward/reverse graph traversal        | Sorted compressed adjacency/CSR shards plus delta overlay                                        |
| Dense vectors                          | HNSW for the first slice; FAISS/Qdrant/Lance or managed equivalent according to deployment needs |
| Analytical evaluation                  | Parquet + DuckDB initially; larger columnar engine later                                         |
| Interactive graph exploration          | Optional graph DB projection; never the sole canonical store                                     |

For the first slice, use Parquet/DuckDB for truth and evaluation, an exact KV, Tantivy, Roaring bitmaps, compressed adjacency, and one HNSW index per embedding channel. This is easier to benchmark and replace than committing the entire architecture to one graph/vector database.
