### Do not split into microservices prematurely

The `api`, `indexer-worker`, and `mcp` images may initially call the same Python library. Module boundaries and storage ports are mandatory; separate network deployments are optional. Analyzer isolation is mandatory because inputs and toolchains are untrusted and language-specific. This avoids the two bad extremes: one unmaintainable script or a dozen operationally expensive services before the contracts are proven.

## Module contracts and responsibilities

### `contracts`

Protobuf is the canonical wire and durable fact-batch format. Buf linting and breaking-change detection protect it. JSON Schema is generated for REST, configuration, fixtures, and debugging. Pydantic models are validated views, not the source of the cross-language contract.

Required v1 messages:

- `SourceSpec`, `SourceSnapshot`, `ArtifactIdentity`, `AcquisitionReceipt`;
- `AnalysisPlan`, `AnalysisRun`, `AnalyzerDescriptor`, `NativeFactBundle`;
- `EntityNode`, `Occurrence`, `EdgeAssertion`, `RelationNode`;
- `EvidenceRef`, `Derivation`, `CoverageClaim`, `Uncertainty`;
- `GraphShardManifest`, `GraphEpochManifest`, `ProjectionManifest`;
- `QueryRequest`, `QueryPlan`, `QueryHit`, `QueryReceipt`;
- `CodeEntityCard`, `CodeSliceManifest`, `SliceHandle`;
- `LineageAssertion`, `GraphDiff`, `PolicyDecision`.

All messages carry `schema_version`; facts carry source/build scope and producer identity; responses carry graph and policy epochs.

### `identity`

This module owns canonical CBOR encoding, digest construction, registry-specific name normalization, structured symbol locators, byte-range occurrence IDs, and collision checks. It must never infer logical sameness while constructing an exact ID. Concept lineage belongs to `lineage`.

The module ships test vectors consumable by Python, TypeScript, Rust, and JVM clients. A given identity key must produce the same bytes and external ID in every implementation.

### `sources` and `acquisition`

Source adapters implement:

``` text
resolve(SourceSpec) -> ResolvedSource
acquire(ResolvedSource, policy) -> AcquisitionReceipt + CAS references
inventory(AcquisitionReceipt) -> SourceInventory
```

Initial adapters:

- `local`: a directory or Git working tree, with configurable dirty-file handling;
- `git`: exact commit/tree acquisition; branch names are resolved to commits before analysis;
- `archive`: wheel, sdist, zip, and tar by local path or allowed URL;
- `pypi`: explicit registry authority, normalized package, exact version, and selected artifact digest.

Every download is size-limited, content-addressed, and verified. Archive extraction rejects absolute paths, `..` traversal, device nodes, dangerous symlink/hardlink targets, duplicate normalized paths, decompression bombs, and case-folding collisions. Package setup/build/import hooks are never run during acquisition.

### `planning` and `jobs`

The planner turns desired coverage, source inventory, analyzer capabilities, prior epochs, and budgets into a DAG of analysis and projection steps. It computes keys from source/artifact digests, dependency closure, analyzer version/configuration, grammar/compiler version, platform, and graph schema. Unchanged results are reused by exact key.

Job states are explicit: `resolved`, `acquired`, `inventoried`, `planned`, `analyzing`, `normalizing`, `validating`, `projecting`, `publishing`, `complete`, `failed`, `quarantined`, `cancelled`. Each transition has an idempotency key and receipt. Partial shards never become query-visible.

### `analyzers`

Each analyzer is a separate executable or OCI image implementing a versioned streaming protocol:

``` text
Describe() -> AnalyzerDescriptor
Plan(AnalysisRequest) -> AnalyzerPlan
Analyze(AnalysisRequest) -> stream NativeFactBatch
Health() -> AnalyzerHealth
```

`AnalyzerDescriptor` declares supported languages, artifact kinds, analysis levels, emitted fact families, build/runtime requirements, network needs, determinism, expected cost, and configuration schema. The host passes read-only CAS mounts and an output channel; the analyzer cannot mutate the graph store.

The common graph never requires analyzers to discard their native formats. SCIP files, CodeQL databases, Tree-sitter captures, compiler output, or language-server facts remain immutable CAS objects referenced by normalized assertions.

### `normalize` and `graph`

Normalization maps native facts into the common ontology while retaining original identity and semantics. It must distinguish binary edges from n-ary call, flow, build, test, and behavior relations. It emits explicit `unsupported`, `ambiguous`, and `unknown` coverage claims instead of silently omitting them.

Graph validation checks:

- exact ID canonicalization and full-key equality;
- referenced entity, occurrence, relation, evidence, and producer existence;
- source/build scope consistency;
- occurrence range validity against exact file bytes;
- predicate subject/object kind constraints;
- reverse-adjacency consistency;
- modality, polarity, and may/must validity;
- derivation acyclicity where required;
- tenant, access, and license labels;
- shard completeness and checksums.

### `storage` and `publish`

The first production-capable local profile should use:

- SQLite in WAL mode for workspace, job, source, epoch, policy, and projection catalogs;
- a content-addressed filesystem store for source, artifacts, native analyzer output, and evidence;
- Zstandard-compressed Parquet/Arrow fact shards sorted by stable IDs;
- Tantivy for fielded BM25 and exact native-name/signature postings;
- sorted forward/reverse adjacency shards with Roaring bitmaps for dense ordinal sets;
- DuckDB for analytical inspection and benchmark queries;
- an optional vector projection behind a port, disabled by default.

The canonical facts are immutable shards and manifests, not rows trapped in one database. Cluster adapters can later replace the catalog with PostgreSQL, CAS with S3-compatible object storage, and search/adjacency projections with distributed implementations without changing entity IDs or contracts.

Atomic publication sequence:

1.  write content-addressed candidate shards;
2.  validate schema, checksums, references, scope, policy, and collision tables;
3.  build and validate exact/search/adjacency projections;
4.  construct a signed `GraphEpochManifest` with coverage and parent epoch;
5.  commit one catalog pointer from the previous visible epoch to the new epoch;
6.  retain prior epochs until retention policy permits garbage collection.

### `projections`, `query`, `cards`, and `slices`

The query engine composes multiple retrieval modes rather than forcing all questions into embeddings:

1.  exact external ID, purl, artifact digest, qualified symbol, or source coordinate;
2.  package/module/kind/language/visibility/effect filters;
3.  fielded BM25 over names, signatures, docs, interfaces, tests, and effects;
4.  typed forward/reverse adjacency and bounded path solving;
5.  structural fingerprints, MinHash/LSH, and duplicate candidates;
6.  optional sparse/dense semantic retrieval;
7.  optional model reranking only after deterministic candidate generation.

Every query result includes why it matched, decisive fields/edges, evidence modality, analyzer coverage, graph epoch, policy epoch, truncation, and a stable continuation handle.

`CodeEntityCard` is a deterministic projection, not free-form generated prose. A compact card contains:

- entity handle and exact ID;
- native and qualified names, kind, language, package/release, file/range;
- compact structured signature;
- input/output/error ports;
- effects and capability requirements;
- most decisive callers/callees/imports/types/tests/docs;
- evidence and coverage summary;
- available expansion/detail handles.

Optional local or hosted model summaries are separate inferred assertions with their own provenance. They never overwrite the deterministic card.

`CodeSliceManifest` selects a purpose-specific, token-bounded subgraph for `explain`, `modify`, `reuse`, `test`, `debug`, `migrate`, `secure`, or `impact`. It records seeds, inclusion rules, path budgets, token estimate, omitted high-scoring nodes, coverage gaps, and exact source-body handles. Reproducing the same request against the same epochs must produce the same ordered slice.

### `lineage`

Exact diffs compare source, occurrence, signature, API-shape, and body digests. Cross-revision identity is a separate evidence-bearing hypothesis generated from native symbol continuity, qualified names, signatures, structural fingerprints, call neighborhoods, docs, version-control rename/copy signals, and tests. Suggestions may be accepted, rejected, split, or superseded without rewriting exact entity history.

### `policy`

Authorization happens before retrieval, graph expansion, caching, embedding, or aggregation. Policy covers tenant, source origin, package/artifact license evidence, snippet/body access, model egress, retention, and takedown. Identical bytes may be deduplicated physically while retaining separate origin-specific policy labels.

### `telemetry`

Every job and query receives a causal receipt. Record content/analyzer/projection versions, cache hits, candidate counts, filters, truncation, latencies, byte/token estimates, policy decisions, and errors. Do not log source bodies or private symbol names by default. Export OpenTelemetry spans plus exact machine-readable receipts.

## Python and PyPI first vertical slice

### Acquisition and metadata

For each selected release, capture:

- registry authority and normalization-rules version;
- original and normalized package name;
- package URL, version, release metadata, project URLs, classifiers, and yanked state;
- every selected wheel/sdist URL, size, filename, digest, and wheel tags;
- `METADATA`, `WHEEL`, `RECORD`, `entry_points.txt`, direct URL/provenance metadata when present;
- `Requires-Python`, `Requires-Dist`, extras, optional dependencies, and environment markers;
- archive file inventory, language mix, docs, examples, tests, stubs, generated files, vendored code, schemas, native libraries, and license candidates.

Do not trust a homepage URL as exact source provenance. Bind a repository revision only when the release metadata, archive contents, tags, or reproducible evidence establish it; otherwise retain the link as an assertion and mark the source revision unknown.

### Python extraction passes

Run these passes independently so coverage and invalidation are measurable:

1.  **Python metadata:** wheels, sdists, distributions, dependencies, entry points, namespaces.
2.  **Cheap syntax:** files, modules, declarations, imports, decorators, docstrings, annotations, assignments, syntax nesting, tests, fixtures, and examples without import execution.
3.  **Concrete source mapping:** retain byte ranges and, where needed, LibCST/token mappings so comments, decorators, multiline signatures, and source excerpts remain exact.
4.  **Precise navigation:** SCIP-compatible symbols and occurrences from a pinned Python type/indexing toolchain.
5.  **Interface projection:** public exports, `__all__`, re-exports, type aliases, overloads, protocols, abstract methods, dataclasses, attrs/Pydantic fields, properties, CLI entry points, environment variables, and config schemas.
6.  **Effects:** bounded claims for filesystem, network, subprocess, environment, database, serialization, secrets, randomness, clock, concurrency, and process-global mutation.
7.  **Tests/oracles:** test cases, fixtures, parametrization, mocks, assertions, snapshot/golden files, property tests, and entity-under-test candidates.
8.  **Optional behavior:** selected examples/tests in a sandbox, producing observed rather than universally asserted edges.

Dynamic Python requires explicit uncertainty fields for star imports, dynamic imports, `getattr`/`setattr`, monkey patching, metaclasses, descriptors, generated members, runtime plugin discovery, conditional imports, C extensions, and missing type information. “Unresolved” is a correct result; guessed certainty is not.

### Representative package corpus

The first 100–1,000-package corpus must be stratified, not just the most downloaded pure-Python libraries. Pin exact artifacts and include:

- pure libraries and typed `py.typed` packages;
- packages with partial or no type annotations;
- namespace packages and large re-export surfaces;
- CLI tools and plugin/entry-point systems;
- async/network libraries;
- web frameworks with decorators and dependency injection;
- data/model packages with generated APIs;
- packages with compiled extensions and `.pyi` stubs;
- source-only sdists and wheel-only releases;
- monorepos publishing multiple distributions;
- packages with optional dependency guards;
- projects using dataclasses, attrs, Pydantic, protocols, overloads, metaclasses, descriptors, and dynamic attributes;
- poorly documented, deprecated, yanked, and multi-version packages.

Maintain a smaller hand-verified golden corpus and a larger real-world benchmark corpus. Real-world scale is not a substitute for exact known answers.

## CLI surface

All commands support `--output table|json|jsonl|protobuf`, return stable exit codes, and print the graph epoch and receipt ID. Mutating commands support `--dry-run`; remote job creation supports an idempotency key.

``` bash
# Workspace and source acquisition
tcg workspace init ./my-index
tcg source add local ./repo --name my-repo
tcg source add git https://example/repo.git --commit <sha>
tcg source add pypi requests --version 2.32.3 --artifact sha256:<digest>
tcg source inspect <source-id>

# Plan, run, validate, and publish analysis
tcg analyze plan <source-id> --coverage metadata,syntax,symbols,interfaces,effects
tcg analyze run <plan-id> --resume
tcg analyze status <job-id> --watch
tcg graph validate <candidate-epoch>
tcg graph publish <candidate-epoch>
tcg graph epochs
tcg graph coverage --epoch <epoch>

# Resolve and search
tcg resolve 'pypi:requests@2.32.3/requests.api.get'
tcg search 'send an HTTP request with timeout' --kind function,method --package requests
tcg entity show <entity-id> --detail compact
tcg entity occurrences <entity-id>
tcg graph neighbors <entity-id> --out calls_may,imports --in tests,references
tcg graph path <source-id> <target-id> --predicates calls_may,data_flows_to --max-hops 6

# Existing-code workflows
tcg slice <entity-id> --purpose modify --token-budget 6000
tcg impact <entity-id> --change signature --depth 4
tcg tests select <entity-id> --explain
tcg diff --from <epoch-or-revision> --to <epoch-or-revision> --public-api
tcg lineage suggest --from <old-entity> --to-scope <new-release>
tcg lineage accept <assertion-id> --evidence <ref>
tcg evidence show <assertion-or-edge-id>

# Services and diagnostics
tcg serve --http 127.0.0.1:8741 --grpc 127.0.0.1:8742
tcg mcp serve --transport stdio --read-only
tcg doctor
tcg benchmark run eval/workload_manifest.yaml
tcg receipt show <receipt-id>
```

No command may silently select “latest” when reproducibility matters. A convenience latest-release request must resolve to and record an exact version and artifact digest before analysis.

## API surface

Use REST for ordinary clients and job management, gRPC streaming for analyzer fact batches and high-volume graph reads. Version all endpoints under `/v1`; pin `graph_epoch` explicitly or return the resolved epoch in the response.

### Source and analysis APIs

- `POST /v1/sources:resolve`
- `POST /v1/sources:acquire`
- `GET /v1/sources/{source_id}`
- `POST /v1/analysis-plans`
- `POST /v1/analysis-jobs`
- `GET /v1/analysis-jobs/{job_id}`
- `POST /v1/analysis-jobs/{job_id}:cancel`
- `GET /v1/analysis-runs/{analysis_id}/coverage`
- `POST /v1/graph-epochs/{candidate_id}:validate`
- `POST /v1/graph-epochs/{candidate_id}:publish`

### Query APIs

- `POST /v1/entities:resolve`
- `POST /v1/entities:search`
- `GET /v1/entities/{entity_id}`
- `GET /v1/entities/{entity_id}/occurrences`
- `POST /v1/graph:neighbors`
- `POST /v1/graph:paths`
- `POST /v1/graph:impact`
- `POST /v1/cards:render`
- `POST /v1/slices:build`
- `GET /v1/slices/{slice_handle}`
- `POST /v1/diffs:compute`
- `GET /v1/assertions/{assertion_id}/evidence`
- `GET /v1/epochs/{epoch_id}/coverage`

Search, graph, and slice requests contain explicit hard limits: candidates, hops, returned nodes/edges, source bytes, wall time, and estimated tokens. Responses state whether limits caused truncation and return stable continuation handles. A timeout must not return an apparently complete result.

## MCP surface

Expose a small set of composable meta-tools rather than one tool for every entity or query variant. The default MCP server is read-only and cannot acquire, build, test, execute, or modify code.

### `code_search`

Search exact, fielded lexical, structural, and optional semantic projections. Inputs include query, fields, entity kinds, languages, packages/releases, source scope, effect/interface constraints, evidence floor, result limit, detail level, and graph epoch. Returns compact handles, not source bodies.

### `code_resolve`

Resolve a purl, qualified name, file/range, native symbol, external ID, or prior handle. It must return ambiguity alternatives instead of silently choosing one.

### `code_expand`

Expand handles over typed inbound/outbound predicates with depth, node, edge, token, and evidence budgets. It returns decisive edges, coverage, truncation, and a continuation handle.

### `code_path`

Find typed paths between entities or sets using allowed/forbidden predicates, direction, hop limit, path count, and cost policy. Useful for call, data-flow, dependency, provenance, and adapter routes.

### `code_slice`

Build a deterministic purpose-specific slice for explanation, modification, debugging, reuse, testing, migration, security, or impact. Inputs include seeds, task text or `DemandIR`, token budget, body budget, and required relation families.

### `code_diff`

Compare snapshots, releases, epochs, or entity sets. Returns additions, removals, signature/API/body changes, edge changes, coverage changes, and separate lineage hypotheses.

### `code_evidence`

Resolve an entity, edge, relation, or claim to producer, version, configuration, native fact bundle, source scope, derivation, modality, uncertainty, and authorized source coordinates.

### `code_coverage`

Report what was and was not analyzed for a source, package, entity, edge family, analyzer, or epoch. Agents need this to distinguish “no callers” from “call analysis was unavailable.”

Every MCP result includes:

``` text
graph_epoch, policy_epoch, receipt_id, result_handles,
coverage_summary, decisive_match_or_path_reasons,
truncated, truncation_reason, continuation_handle,
available_detail_levels, authorized_body_handles
```

Useful MCP resources are `codegraph://epochs/{epoch}/manifest`, `codegraph://entities/{id}/card`, `codegraph://slices/{handle}`, and `codegraph://receipts/{id}`. Large bodies remain behind explicit resource handles so they are not injected into every model call.

## Test architecture

### Contract and identity tests

- Protobuf/JSON round trips preserve unknown fields and canonical values.
- Buf breaking-change checks run on every schema change.
- Canonical CBOR identity vectors are identical in Python and TypeScript; add Rust/JVM vectors when those analyzers arrive.
- Registry normalization includes adversarial spelling, Unicode, separators, case, private/public authorities, and dependency-confusion cases.
- Every digest collision candidate triggers full identity-key comparison.
- Occurrence IDs remain stable for identical file bytes and change when bytes/ranges/roles change.
- Concept lineage never changes an exact `RevisionEntityID`.

### Python golden corpus

Hand-verify fixtures for:

- modules, nested functions/classes, lambdas, comprehensions, closures, globals, and nonlocals;
- sync/async functions, generators, overloads, generics, protocols, type variables, aliases, and forward references;
- inheritance, multiple inheritance, abstract methods, overrides, properties, descriptors, metaclasses, and decorators;
- dataclasses, attrs, Pydantic models, named tuples, enums, and generated members;
- absolute, relative, conditional, dynamic, star, and optional imports;
- `__all__`, re-exports, namespace packages, entry points, and plugin discovery;
- tests, fixtures, parametrization, mocks, assertions, property tests, and snapshots;
- CLI frameworks, environment variables, configuration files, schemas, and secrets;
- files with Unicode identifiers, mixed newline forms, invalid encodings, syntax errors, generated code, and source maps;
- C-extension boundaries, stubs, missing sources, and platform-specific modules.

Each fixture contains expected exact entities, occurrences, roles, edges, unsupported facts, and coverage—not only snapshots that can accept accidental changes.

### Differential tests

Compare independently derived facts where possible:

- archive metadata against wheel `RECORD` and package metadata rules;
- declaration ranges against Python AST, LibCST/token spans, and Tree-sitter;
- definitions/references against SCIP/native index results;
- import/export/public API results against static baselines and sandboxed observation on approved fixtures;
- exact-text lookup against ripgrep/native symbol lookup;
- graph reverse edges against recomputation from forward shards.

Disagreement becomes a test result and, where appropriate, graph evidence; it is not automatically resolved in favor of the more expensive analyzer.

### Determinism and incremental invalidation tests

- Analyze the same pinned input twice in clean workspaces and require byte-identical canonical fact shards and manifests, excluding explicitly declared nondeterministic observation timestamps.
- Re-run with only file timestamps changed and require zero semantic shard changes.
- Change one private function body and verify syntax/body facts plus true reverse dependencies invalidate, while unrelated package and public-interface facts reuse prior shards.
- Change a public signature and verify dependent type/interface/call projections invalidate.
- Upgrade an analyzer or configuration and verify only its declared output families and derivations invalidate.
- Crash at every job transition and prove resume does not duplicate facts or publish a partial epoch.

### Security tests

- path traversal, absolute paths, symlink/hardlink escapes, device files, case-fold collisions, duplicate archive entries, zip/tar bombs, and oversized metadata;
- packages whose import/setup/build hooks write files, open sockets, spawn processes, or raise—acquisition and static passes must never trigger them;
- malformed Protobuf/JSON/native analyzer batches, decompression limits, parser bombs, timeouts, and process crashes;
- source/docstring prompt injection remains marked untrusted data and never changes MCP or analysis policy;
- tenant-crossing graph paths, cache keys, embeddings, cards, and identical-content deduplication;
- license/takedown propagation and body/snippet authorization;
- SSRF and registry-origin confusion in source resolution.

### Query and MCP tests

- exact external ID, qualified name, purl, digest, and coordinate resolution;
- ambiguity preservation for duplicate names and overloads;
- known-answer forward/reverse edge and typed path queries;
- stable ordering and pagination under a pinned epoch;
- hard node/edge/hop/token/body/time budgets;
- honest coverage and truncation markers;
- cards contain no claim without an evidence or deterministic derivation reference;
- a compact search never leaks full source bodies;
- MCP JSON schemas pass conformance and work in at least two real coding harnesses.

### Performance and scale tests

Publish measurements against a named reference machine, cold and warm cache, instead of unsupported universal speed claims. Initial exit targets on an 8-core, 32-GB, local-NVMe host are:

- exact entity lookup p95 under 20 ms at one million entities, warm cache;
- fielded lexical top-20 search p95 under 200 ms at one million entities;
- bounded one-hop adjacency p95 under 100 ms for non-supernodes;
- a 6,000-token purpose slice p95 under 750 ms after projections are built;
- compact entity card under 350 estimated tokens and compact search hit under 100 tokens by default;
- repeated unchanged analysis reuses at least 99% of eligible fact/projection work;
- no static analysis process exceeds configured CPU, memory, output-byte, or wall limits;
- corpus growth, fact counts, projection sizes, and query latency are reported per entity/edge million.

Supernodes, pathological files, and incomplete/deep analyzers are reported separately rather than hidden in averages.

## Acceptance criteria by release gate

### Gate A: contract kernel

- All v1 identity, entity, occurrence, assertion, evidence, coverage, analysis, epoch, query, card, slice, and lineage messages exist.
- Python and TypeScript produce the same IDs for all canonical test vectors.
- Schema linting, backward-compatibility checks, canonical round trips, and full-key collision checks pass.
- Fifty or more ambiguity/adversarial fixtures have explicit expected outcomes.

### Gate B: safe Python/PyPI ingestion

- A pinned set of at least 100 representative releases is acquired by exact artifact digest.
- Metadata, archive inventory, Python syntax, docs, tests, imports, public interfaces, and entry points are extracted without executing package code.
- Golden-corpus entity and occurrence recall is at least 99% for declared supported syntax; precise definition/reference tests meet a separately reported at least 95% target on supported constructs.
- Unsupported dynamic/native cases are visible through coverage claims.
- All hostile-archive and no-import sentinel tests pass.

### Gate C: immutable graph and retrieval

- Candidate shards pass reference, scope, range, policy, and checksum validation before atomic publication.
- Repeated clean analysis of the same inputs is byte-deterministic.
- Exact symbol and coordinate queries achieve 100% top-1 on the golden suite.
- Natural-language/fielded retrieval has a labeled workload and beats exact-name-only and plain-ripgrep baselines on MRR/recall without reducing exact-query accuracy.
- Forward and reverse graph answers agree; every result carries epoch, evidence, coverage, and receipt.

### Gate D: agent-ready slices

- All eight MCP meta-tools pass schema and behavior conformance.
- Two coding harnesses can resolve a task, search, expand, request a bounded slice, and fetch selected bodies without receiving the full catalog or repository.
- 1/2/4/8-candidate and multiple card/edge/detail variants can be replayed from receipts.
- Token budgets are hard limits, and omissions/truncation are explicit.
- Human reviewers can follow every card or slice statement to source/native evidence.

### Gate E: scalable release candidate

- At least 1,000 stratified package releases or an equivalently sized corpus has been indexed with a published corpus manifest.
- Incremental invalidation, crash recovery, analyzer failure isolation, and prior-epoch rollback pass fault injection.
- Performance targets are met or exceptions are explicitly bucketed with blocking issues.
- The local installation, container deployment, and MCP setup are reproducible from a clean machine.
- A benchmark bundle includes inputs, artifact digests, analyzer versions, configurations, expected answers, receipts, and a one-command report reproduction path.

## Twelve-week build plan

This schedule assumes three focused engineers: one contracts/graph/storage engineer, one acquisition/Python-analysis engineer, and one query/API/MCP/evaluation engineer. A single engineer should expect roughly 18–24 weeks for the same gates. Parallel work is safe only after Week 2 freezes the first contract candidate.

### Week 1 — decisions, threat model, and executable contracts

- Record ADRs for identity lattice, canonical CBOR/SHA-256 IDs, Protobuf/Buf, immutable facts, analyzer isolation, local storage profile, graph epochs, and sidecar rather than source renaming.
- Define source/artifact/analysis trust boundaries and the no-execution acquisition rule.
- Write initial v1 Protobuf schemas and ontology registries.
- Create 25 identity and ambiguity fixtures before implementation.
- Stand up CI for formatting, typing, unit tests, Buf lint/breaking, dependency audit, and fixture validation.

**Exit:** generated Python and TypeScript contracts round-trip; identity fixtures have reviewed expected canonical bytes.

### Week 2 — identity engine, evidence kernel, and analyzer SDK

- Implement canonicalization, package/registry rules, exact ID constructors, collision table, evidence and coverage types.
- Implement analyzer `Describe/Plan/Analyze/Health` protocol, subprocess runner, time/resource/output limits, and conformance kit.
- Implement CAS abstraction and SQLite catalog migrations.
- Expand golden fixtures to at least 50, including private/public registries and source-range adversaries.

**Exit:** Gate A passes; a conformance analyzer emits a valid fact batch through the real isolated transport.

### Week 3 — safe acquisition and PyPI artifact truth

- Implement local, Git-at-commit, archive, and PyPI exact-release resolvers.
- Implement digest verification, safe wheel/sdist extraction, file inventory, METADATA/WHEEL/RECORD/entry-point/dependency extraction.
- Add hostile archives, decompression quotas, origin allowlists, and acquisition receipts.
- Pin the first 100-package stratified corpus manifest.

**Exit:** all 100 releases acquire reproducibly by digest; hostile acquisition and never-import sentinel tests pass.

### Week 4 — Python cheap syntax and interface surface

- Implement Python file/module/declaration/occurrence/docstring/import/decorator/annotation extraction with exact byte mappings.
- Extract tests, fixtures, examples, `__all__`, re-exports, entry points, CLI/config/environment-variable surfaces.
- Normalize to exact entities, occurrences, relations, evidence, and explicit uncertainty/coverage.
- Produce initial deterministic entity cards.

**Exit:** at least 99% supported declaration/occurrence recall on the hand-verified golden corpus; no package execution.

### Week 5 — precise symbols and Python semantic reconciliation

- Integrate a pinned SCIP-compatible Python indexer.
- Map SCIP symbols/occurrences to exact sidecar IDs while retaining the complete SCIP artifact.
- Reconcile cheap and precise passes without destructive merging.
- Add types, overrides/implementations, reference roles, call candidates where supported, and compiled/dynamic boundary flags.

**Exit:** known-answer definition/reference suite reaches the declared 95% target on supported constructs; disagreements and unresolved cases are reportable.

### Week 6 — normalization, invalidation, immutable publication

- Implement Parquet fact batches, graph validator, analysis keys, derivation dependencies, candidate epochs, and atomic publish.
- Implement file-level and semantic reverse invalidation.
- Add crash/resume tests at each job transition.
- Publish the first signed 100-package epoch with a coverage ledger.

**Exit:** identical reruns are byte-deterministic; a one-file change reuses unaffected work; no partial epoch is queryable.

### Week 7 — exact, lexical, and typed graph retrieval

- Build exact ID/name/signature/source-coordinate indexes.
- Build fielded Tantivy BM25 and forward/reverse typed adjacency projections.
- Implement resolve, search, neighbor, path, evidence, and coverage query plans with hard budgets.
- Label known-answer and natural-language retrieval workloads; implement ripgrep/exact-name baselines.

**Exit:** Gate C exact and graph invariants pass; retrieval metrics and latency are reproducible from the workload manifest.

### Week 8 — cards, slices, impact, diff, and CLI

- Finish deterministic compact/standard/full cards.
- Implement purpose-specific `CodeSliceManifest`, token budgeting, source-body handles, impact queries, and version/epoch diffs.
- Implement the full `tcg` CLI with JSON/JSONL output and receipts.
- Add lineage suggestions as reversible assertions; no automatic concept merging.

**Exit:** five real existing-code tasks can be solved from a bounded slice with every statement traceable to evidence.

### Week 9 — API and MCP integration

- Implement versioned REST and gRPC services with auth/policy hooks, epoch pinning, pagination, and rate/resource limits.
- Implement the eight read-only MCP meta-tools and resources.
- Integrate with two coding harnesses through MCP and test search → expand → slice → selected-body flow.
- Record prompt/tool token usage and compare against raw repository/catalog injection.

**Exit:** Gate D passes; MCP never leaks unselected bodies or hides truncation/coverage.

### Week 10 — effects, tests, duplicate/lineage signals, and optional semantics

- Add bounded Python effect claims, test-to-entity candidates, structural fingerprints, MinHash/LSH duplicate candidates, and richer graph diffs.
- Add optional local embeddings behind the projection port.
- If an LLM summary/reranker is tested, persist it only as an inferred assertion with model/prompt/input/output digests and measure incremental value over deterministic retrieval.
- Expand to 500+ package releases.

**Exit:** each new projection has an ablation result; features that do not improve a target metric remain optional and do not enter the hot path.

### Week 11 — scale, fault injection, security, and policy

- Scale toward 1,000 stratified releases and run cold/warm performance suites.
- Inject analyzer crashes, malformed batches, disk exhaustion, interrupted publication, stale continuation handles, and supernodes.
- Test tenant isolation, prompt-injection handling, body/snippet policy, license evidence, takedown overlays, cache partitioning, and receipt redaction.
- Optimize measured bottlenecks without changing canonical IDs or schemas casually.

**Exit:** Gate E fault, isolation, and performance requirements pass or have explicit release-blocking defects.

### Week 12 — release candidate and proof workload

- Freeze `v0.1` contracts and ontology; publish migration policy rather than claiming permanent v1 stability.
- Produce reproducible local, Docker, and MCP installation paths.
- Run the full golden, real-corpus, retrieval, graph, MCP, security, fault, and performance suites.
- Publish a benchmark report with exact artifacts, versions, configurations, receipts, coverage, and known limitations.
- Demonstrate six workflows: symbol discovery, behavioral search, API impact, test selection, version migration, and agent token-bounded code understanding.

**Exit:** all five gates pass; a new user can index a repository and a pinned PyPI release, query them through CLI/API/MCP, reproduce the epoch, and audit every answer.

## Definition of done for every analyzer or projection

No analyzer, embedding, model, database, or new edge family is “done” merely because it emits output. It must include:

- a versioned capability/coverage declaration;
- deterministic configuration and exact input keys, or an explicit nondeterminism declaration;
- native output retention and normalized evidence links;
- golden known-answer cases and negative/unknown cases;
- resource quotas, timeout behavior, failure isolation, and resumability;
- invalidation dependencies;
- policy/license/tenant propagation;
- fact counts, storage cost, latency, and incremental cost;
- an ablation showing value for retrieval, graph correctness, impact, test selection, agent token use, or another named task;
- a migration and rollback path.

## The decisive architectural principle

The graph is not a giant LLM-generated description of source code. It is a versioned evidence system in which exact identity, source coordinates, static facts, runtime observations, documentation claims, heuristics, and model inferences remain distinguishable. That distinction is what makes the system safe to search at PyPI scale, cheap enough to use before a frontier model, and precise enough for an agent to reuse or modify code without reading an entire package or hallucinating relationships.

# Taedri Architecture Atlas

> **ANNEX STATUS — TARGET ARCHITECTURE ATLAS.** This responsibility and alternatives
> inventory intentionally exceeds the current implementation. Nothing in it promotes a
> component beyond Part 0's scoped evidence.

**A 450+ responsibility, alternative-rich design for cheap retrieval, composition, execution, and proof at 5M–50M+ primitives**
**Research and architecture expansion — 2026-07-15**

## Executive answer

Yes: there are many more paths, components, and layers than the first vertical slice exposed. The seven original bullets are a good experimental spine, but they compress a complete compiler, search engine, package system, workflow runtime, evidence system, and adaptive decision controller into a few nouns.

The expanded design should not be understood as a longer mandatory waterfall. It should be a **conditional action graph** whose cheapest correct branch wins:

``` text
                         ┌─ direct handle / exact replay ───────────────┐
                         ├─ validated pack or route macro ─────────────┤
request → local gates ───┼─ deterministic template / query prototype ─┤
                         ├─ typed retrieval + route solving ───────────┼→ compile → admit → run → verify → receipt
                         ├─ statistical retrieval / local ranker ──────┤
                         ├─ local SLM interpretation or selection ─────┤
                         ├─ hosted small-model delta call ─────────────┤
                         ├─ strong-model synthesis on bounded evidence ┤
                         └─ clarify / human review / safe refusal ──────┘
```

The system should be able to skip interpretation, query generation, retrieval, planning, selection, execution, or even all provider calls when a verified handle or pack already determines the answer. It should also be able to loop from failed compilation or verification back to a narrowly targeted search step without replaying the entire pipeline.

The decisive architectural principles are:

1.  **Delete intelligence before making intelligence cheaper.** Exact replay, templates, indexes, compilers, validators, and cached proofs remove model calls entirely.
2.  **Represent uncertainty explicitly.** The controller chooses among lookup, search, probe, clarify, model, execute, or abstain based on expected value and risk—not a fixed sequence.
3.  **Separate discovery from proof.** Approximate methods may nominate; exact contracts, authorization, compilation, and independent verification decide.
4.  **Keep large implementations opaque.** Models see compact, evidence-linked semantic ABIs and contrastive deltas; bodies load only after a plan is locked.
5.  **Project graphs on demand.** At 50M primitives, do not materialize universal pairwise compatibility. Maintain indexes and verified local neighborhoods, then build request-local hypergraphs.
6.  **Treat negative knowledge as a first-class asset.** Known incompatibilities, failed routes, misleading aliases, revoked artifacts, and unsatisfied demands prevent repeated spend.
7.  **Make every expensive fallback manufacture a cheaper future path.** A successful model-generated query, adapter, plan, or clarification becomes a validated prototype, route macro, test, or catalog correction.
8.  **Do not turn logical layers into microservices.** Begin with a modular monolith, content-addressed artifacts, a transactional database, a search index, object storage, and one durable executor. Split only at measured scale, isolation, ownership, or availability boundaries.

This atlas identifies **more than 450 named responsibilities and design choices**. They are a menu and dependency map, not a mandate to build hundreds of things.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 1. The end-to-end alternatives are broader than a waterfall

The arm IDs in this section use the `END:` namespace (`END:E01` through `END:E38`); Plane E later uses a separate `ABI:` namespace. The short table labels are intentionally compact.

The following architectures can coexist as controller arms. Each can be the cheapest correct path for a different demand family.

| ID  | Architecture arm                 | Core mechanism                                                                 | Best fit                                     | Main failure mode                                |
|-----|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| E01 | Direct capability handle         | User or host supplies an immutable primitive/pack handle                       | Repeated API, UI, IDE, or automation actions | Stale or unauthorized handle                     |
| E02 | Exact semantic replay            | Canonical demand hash plus validity recheck                                    | Truly repeated tasks                         | False equivalence from over-canonicalization     |
| E03 | Parameterized recipe replay      | Retrieve a verified plan skeleton and bind fields                              | Same workflow, different values              | Hidden structural change                         |
| E04 | Pack-first                       | Match a `SolutionPack` before primitives                                       | Common product workflows                     | Pack proliferation and staleness                 |
| E05 | Template-first                   | Intent/slots select a deterministic query or plan template                     | Bounded request families                     | Long-tail requests outside ontology              |
| E06 | Case-based reasoning             | Retrieve the nearest successful case, adapt, then reverify                     | Repetitive, context-rich work                | Similarity mistaken for applicability            |
| E07 | Query-prototype retrieval        | Retrieve a validated `QueryPlan`, fill bounded conditionals                    | Repeated search patterns                     | Prototype misses decisive clause                 |
| E08 | Queryless contract cell          | Precomputed region for `(inputs, outputs, effects, environment)`               | Dense recurring contract cells               | Combinatorial cell growth                        |
| E09 | Route-first retrieval            | Retrieve prior verified route macros/subgraphs                                 | Stable composition motifs                    | Route invalidation after component changes       |
| E10 | Primitive-first retrieval        | Retrieve candidates then solve a typed route                                   | Broad catalogs with novel combinations       | Connector loss during top-k truncation           |
| E11 | Meet-in-the-middle planning      | Expand forward from inputs and backward from outputs                           | Long sparse typed paths                      | Inadequate lower bounds or join explosion        |
| E12 | Constraint-first synthesis       | Encode the task in CSP/CP-SAT/SMT/ILP                                          | Hard combinatorial constraints               | Incomplete or expensive encoding                 |
| E13 | Type-inhabitation synthesis      | Find terms/programs inhabiting a target type                                   | Pure or strongly typed primitives            | Effects and real-world state under-modeled       |
| E14 | Datalog/rule closure             | Derive reachable capabilities through rules                                    | Monotone metadata-rich domains               | Nonmonotone effects and optimization             |
| E15 | HTN/task decomposition           | Refine abstract tasks through known methods                                    | Operational procedures and playbooks         | Method authoring burden                          |
| E16 | Planner-native                   | Use PDDL/temporal/Petri/dataflow planning                                      | Explicit state and concurrency               | Modeling fidelity and solver cost                |
| E17 | Query-optimizer architecture     | Logical expressions, equivalence rules, physical implementations, cost search  | Many equivalent compositions                 | Cost-model error and search blow-up              |
| E18 | Equality-saturation architecture | Populate an e-graph of equivalent programs, extract cheapest                   | Rewrite-rich pure subgraphs                  | E-graph growth; effects complicate equivalence   |
| E19 | CEGIS loop                       | Propose a plan, test it, add counterexample, repeat                            | Checkable specifications                     | Weak oracle or expensive counterexamples         |
| E20 | CEGAR abstraction loop           | Plan over an abstraction, refine only spurious solutions                       | Huge state spaces with proof obligations     | Bad abstractions cause repeated refinement       |
| E21 | Blackboard / hypothesis market   | Independent producers post candidates and evidence                             | Heterogeneous agents and partial solutions   | Shared-state pollution and authority confusion   |
| E22 | Portfolio / algorithm selection  | Run or choose among solvers/retrievers based on instance features              | No universally best algorithm                | Selection overhead and biased training data      |
| E23 | Speculative parallel plans       | Compile or safely dry-run diverse finalists concurrently                       | High latency value, cheap sandboxing         | Resource waste or unsafe side effects            |
| E24 | Verification-first search        | Start from available independent oracles and search for plans they can certify | High assurance                               | Rejects useful but hard-to-verify plans          |
| E25 | Proof-carrying component search  | Only retrieve components with checkable evidence for required claims           | Regulated/high-risk use                      | Sparse ecosystem of proof-bearing artifacts      |
| E26 | Event-choreography composition   | Components react to typed events rather than one central DAG                   | Loosely coupled long-lived systems           | Emergent behavior and hard global reasoning      |
| E27 | Durable workflow orchestration   | Lower plans to an established workflow engine                                  | Retries, timers, long-running work           | Runtime semantics leak into planning             |
| E28 | Dataflow/streaming composition   | Compile primitives into batch/stream transforms                                | Large data movement and parallelism          | External effects and interactive steps           |
| E29 | Federated registry search        | Query authoritative native catalogs and merge evidence                         | Multiple owners or ecosystems                | Inconsistent identity, latency, and policy       |
| E30 | Offline compile, online execute  | Precompute packs/routes/proofs for known demand families                       | Very low online latency and cost             | Coverage limited to anticipated demand           |
| E31 | Human-authored skeleton          | Human chooses milestones; system fills and verifies gaps                       | High-impact or novel projects                | Interaction cost                                 |
| E32 | Human clarification-first        | Ask the minimum discriminating question before search                          | Ambiguity dominates                          | User friction and abandonment                    |
| E33 | Tool-mediated interpretation     | Deterministic parsers, schemas, IDE state, forms, and probes establish intent  | Structured hosts                             | Tool/schema coverage gaps                        |
| E34 | Local SLM compiler               | A constrained local model emits only typed fields or grammar                   | Residual semantic parsing                    | Local accuracy and operational cost              |
| E35 | Hosted model delta resolver      | Send only unresolved clauses and candidate contrasts                           | Rare ambiguous tail                          | Context omission or privacy policy               |
| E36 | Frontier synthesis fallback      | Strong model proposes new queries, adapters, or plan skeletons                 | Novel long-tail work                         | Cost, nondeterminism, and unverifiable invention |
| E37 | Primitive foundry path           | Create or wrap a missing primitive, verify, then compose                       | High-value capability gaps                   | Supply-chain and maintenance debt                |
| E38 | Safe no-op / abstention          | Return an ambiguity, incompatibility, or unverifiability certificate           | Risk exceeds value                           | Poor UX if overused                              |

These arms should not compete on model quality alone. They compete on **failure-inclusive total cost**, latency, privacy, proof strength, and the chance of producing an acceptable result.

## 2. Scale math changes the architecture

At the target scale, several seemingly reasonable designs are physically or economically wrong.

### 2.1 Multi-view representation

If 50M primitives each had 336 stored descriptions, that would be:

``` text
50,000,000 × 336 = 16.8 billion descriptions
16.8B × 25 tokens/description = 420 billion stored description tokens
```

Therefore, 336 or 360 views should be an **experimental view lattice**, not a materialization requirement. A production primitive may keep 12–32 evidence-linked core views; diagnostic, audience-specific, query-conditioned, or counterfactual views should be generated or cached on demand.

For 256-dimensional FP16 vectors:

``` text
50M × 32 channels × 256 × 2 bytes = 819.2 GB raw vectors (~763 GiB)
50M × 360 channels × 256 × 2 bytes = 9.216 TB raw vectors (~8.38 TiB)
```

Those figures exclude IDs, metadata, graph links, ANN structures, replicas, and compaction slack. Product quantization, binary sketches, tiering, and routing to only the relevant channels are not optional experiments at this scale. Faiss explicitly supports inverted files, product quantization, HNSW, binary indexes, on-disk operation, and vector filtering; DiskANN demonstrates a disk-oriented billion-point design ([Faiss documentation](https://faiss.ai/), [DiskANN paper](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/diskann-fast-accurate-billion-point-nearest-neighbor-search-on-a-single-node/)).

### 2.2 Compatibility explosion

Fifty million primitives imply:

``` text
50M² = 2.5 quadrillion ordered primitive pairs
```

Even one bit per pair would be roughly 312.5 TB before replication and indexing. Port-level pair counts can be larger. The production design must store contracts, type/capability partitions, sparse observed or verified edges, adapter rules, and negative certificates—then solve compatibility only inside a request-local candidate closure.

### 2.3 Compact metadata still becomes infrastructure

A 4 KiB verified card for 50M primitives is about 205 GB decimal before indexes and history. At an average of 20 sparse outgoing relationships, 1B edges at an illustrative 24 bytes per compact edge is 24 GB raw, but real property/index overhead can multiply that. This argues for:

- columnar or relational core facts;
- compact integer IDs and dictionaries;
- bitmap postings for common typed predicates;
- separate evidence/object blobs;
- immutable catalog epochs and tenant overlays;
- hot/warm/cold tiers; and
- request-local graph materialization.

Roaring bitmaps are a credible exact set representation for large integer postings; XOR and prefix-filter families are useful approximate membership structures, but approximate positives must never authorize or prove compatibility ([Roaring bitmap paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.07821), [Xor Filters](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.08258), [Prefix Filter](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.17139)).

### 2.4 Model-visible candidates must be a tiny projection

One hundred candidates at 200 tokens each already consume 20,000 input tokens before the request, route relations, or instructions. The selector should normally see:

- opaque handles;
- contract/effect summaries;
- decisive evidence;
- route-wide invariants;
- differences from the current best route; and
- an option to request one more field.

It should not see 100 full cards, every edge, or implementation bodies. More duplicate context can improve robustness only until it displaces decisive evidence, creates position bias, or gives correlated claims the appearance of independent support.

## 3. The control mathematics

### 3.1 Choose the next action, not merely the next model

At state `s`, the controller chooses among actions such as `replay`, `retrieve`, `expand`, `probe`, `clarify`, `select`, `compile`, `verify`, `escalate`, or `abstain`:

``` text
a* = argmin_a E[C_a + λt T_a + λr R_a + λp P_a + λe E_a | s]
     subject to authorization, safety, quality, and proof constraints
```

`C` is monetary and compute cost, `T` latency, `R` expected result loss, `P` privacy/exposure cost, and `E` external-effect risk. Hard constraints are not converted into soft score weights.

### 3.2 Value of information determines whether to ask, search, or expose more detail

``` text
VOI(action) = expected loss before action
            − expected loss after action
            − action cost
            − added latency/privacy/risk
```

Ask a clarification only if its expected decision improvement exceeds interaction cost. Request another card field only if it can change the route choice. Run a strong model only on the unresolved delta whose VOI exceeds its incremental cost.

### 3.3 Adaptive candidate count

Do not declare `1/2/4/8` a universal rule. Use those values as clean experiment arms, then learn or calibrate a stopping policy:

``` text
smallest k such that
P(at least one acceptable and authorized route in top-k | evidence) ≥ target_coverage
and expected value of route k+1 < marginal disclosure + selection cost
```

Route probabilities are correlated and should not simply be summed. Diversity should be measured over failure modes, primitive families, effects, evidence sources, and topology—not only embedding distance.

### 3.4 Retrieval and solver recall compose badly through hard blockers

If required-stage recalls are `r1 … rn`, an upper-bound intuition for end-to-end survival is their product. A 95% recall gate applied four times yields only about 81% survival under independence; correlations can make it worse. Therefore:

- preserve exact and typed bypasses;
- delay irreversible top-k truncation until graph connectors are expanded;
- keep per-signal and per-required-capability quotas;
- sample counterfactual later tiers after early stops; and
- measure route recall, not merely primitive recall.

### 3.5 Never multiply primitive reliability naïvely

Failures share providers, networks, credentials, data, and adapters. Store a dependency/failure-domain graph and estimate correlated route risk. Independent evidence means a different oracle or failure mode, not a second prompt to the same model.

# 4. Component and alternative atlas

Each row below is a **logical responsibility**. The `Default` is a sensible first implementation, not a permanent commitment.

## Plane A — ingress, identity, authority, and trust boundaries

| ID  | Responsibility                | Alternatives                                                            | Recommended first default                           | Scale/risk note                                   |
|-----|-------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| A01 | Request ingress               | HTTP/RPC, queue, event, CLI, IDE, MCP, batch manifest                   | One canonical envelope adapter layer                | Preserve native source metadata                   |
| A02 | Request identity              | Random UUID, sortable UUID, content hash, trace ID                      | Random request ID plus content digest               | Identity and equivalence are separate             |
| A03 | Tenant resolution             | Host assertion, token claim, directory lookup, isolated endpoint        | Verified auth claim before retrieval                | Tenant must constrain every index branch          |
| A04 | Actor identity                | Human, service, delegated agent, workload identity                      | Principal plus delegation chain                     | Never infer authorization from prose              |
| A05 | Session/conversation identity | Server session, event stream, client cursor, stateless token            | Explicit conversation epoch and turn references     | Avoid accidental cross-session replay             |
| A06 | Data classification           | Rule table, DLP classifier, labels, human declaration                   | Deterministic labels plus conservative classifier   | Drives local/hosted eligibility                   |
| A07 | Instruction authority         | Fixed precedence, policy engine, signed scope, capability token         | Typed role, scope, authority, and source            | Retrieved text is never automatically instruction |
| A08 | Prompt-injection boundary     | Source labels, parser isolation, allowlisted commands, taint tracking   | Mark all external content untrusted by default      | Propagate taint into tool arguments/results       |
| A09 | Request normalization         | Unicode/canonical JSON, locale rules, schema coercion                   | Lossless original plus canonical projection         | Hash canonical bytes, retain original             |
| A10 | Deduplication                 | Exact digest, idempotency key, semantic similarity, coalescing window   | Exact idempotency first; semantic only suggests     | False merging is worse than duplicate work        |
| A11 | Rate and budget gate          | Token bucket, quota ledger, admission queue, priority class             | Per-tenant and per-risk budget admission            | Reserve verification budget up front              |
| A12 | Policy snapshot               | Live query, immutable version, embedded bundle, signed decision         | Immutable policy epoch reference                    | Replay needs the historical policy                |
| A13 | Time/freshness anchor         | Wall clock, logical clock, catalog epoch, source timestamp              | Wall time plus monotonic/catalog epochs             | Time-dependent tasks cannot use timeless hashes   |
| A14 | Cancellation/deadline         | Client cancel, server deadline, lease, budget stop                      | Propagated deadline and cooperative cancel          | Receipt partial work and uncertain effects        |
| A15 | Locale/unit frame             | User preference, project convention, inferred locale, explicit ontology | Explicit unit/timezone/locale defaults              | Unit ambiguity is a compatibility defect          |
| A16 | Request risk class            | Rule taxonomy, classifier, user declaration, impact analysis            | Conservative deterministic rules with review escape | Risk governs required proof, not relevance score  |

## Plane B — context, memory, evidence, and state

| ID  | Responsibility           | Alternatives                                                                  | Recommended first default                                        | Scale/risk note                                    |
|-----|--------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| B01 | Context container        | `ContextManifest`, `RequestEnvelope`, blackboard, event projection, RDF graph | One typed envelope with immutable references                     | Split service only after real consumers emerge     |
| B02 | Source acquisition       | Eager copy, lazy resolver, snapshot, live query, subscription                 | Lazy content-addressed resolver plus snapshot option             | Receipt every resolved byte/version                |
| B03 | Context role             | Fact, instruction, preference, example, evidence, untrusted content           | Closed role enum plus extension namespace                        | Roles affect authority and model formatting        |
| B04 | Scope                    | Turn, session, project, tenant, global, artifact, route                       | Explicit scope lattice                                           | Global memory must not leak tenant data            |
| B05 | Precedence               | Fixed hierarchy, policy rules, recency, signed authority, human choice        | Fixed safety/system hierarchy then explicit conflicts            | Recency alone is unsafe                            |
| B06 | Conflict detection       | Exact keys, rules, constraint solver, NLI model, human review                 | Deterministic typed conflicts; model nominates only              | Preserve both claims and evidence                  |
| B07 | Temporal validity        | TTL, valid-time interval, bitemporal records, invalidation event              | Valid-time plus catalog/source epoch                             | Stale context invalidates replay selectively       |
| B08 | Working memory           | Rolling summary, typed slots, event projection, local KV store                | Typed state plus derived summary                                 | Summary is never sole truth                        |
| B09 | Long-term memory         | Exact cases, episodic events, semantic store, user profile graph              | Scoped cases with provenance and expiry                          | Separate preference from observed behavior         |
| B10 | Context selection        | Rules, lexical, dense, graph neighborhood, learned selector                   | Hard policy filters, then hybrid retrieval                       | Measure omitted decisive-context rate              |
| B11 | Context compression      | Extractive spans, structured facts, semantic summary, dictionary codes        | Evidence-linked facts plus extractive spans                      | Compression must retain reversibility pointers     |
| B12 | Context delta            | Full snapshot, change set, Merkle diff, event tail                            | Send only changes against a named snapshot                       | Prevent repeated prompt-prefix spend               |
| B13 | Redaction                | Regex/rules, DLP, field policies, local model, tokenization                   | Deterministic field policy plus reversible vault tokens          | Hosted model receives least privilege              |
| B14 | Taint tracking           | Boolean untrusted, source labels, lattice, information-flow types             | Small trust lattice propagated through artifacts                 | Verification cannot erase provenance               |
| B15 | Evidence ledger          | Mutable notes, append-only events, provenance graph, signed statements        | Append-only evidence events plus projections                     | Blackboard hypotheses commit only after acceptance |
| B16 | Context cache            | Request, session, tenant, global CAS, semantic memo                           | CAS for immutable sources; scoped semantic cache                 | Cache key includes policy and authorization        |
| B17 | Clause memoization       | Whole-prompt hash, sentence hash, typed clause hash, AST node hash            | Canonical typed clause hashes                                    | Reuse embeddings and interpretations independently |
| B18 | Missing-context detector | Required-field rules, entropy, verifier feedback, model critique              | Schema/contract gaps first, learned detector later               | Produces questions, not invented values            |
| B19 | Context probe            | File stat, DB schema, API capability, sandbox test, user question             | Cheapest non-destructive probe with highest VOI                  | Log probe result and freshness                     |
| B20 | Snapshot closure         | All transitive refs, selected refs, live refs, Merkle root                    | Closed immutable refs for execution; live refs explicitly marked | Required for reproducible plan locks               |

| ID  | Responsibility                 | Alternatives                                                                    | Recommended first default                                      | Scale/risk note                                    |
|-----|--------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| C01 | Demand representation          | `DemandIR`, intent/slots, acceptance tests, goal graph, PDDL/CSP, direct handle | Small typed projection embedded in request envelope            | Preserve original utterance and provenance         |
| C02 | Intent family                  | Rules, keyword/phrase map, embedding classifier, SLM, hosted model              | Exact/rules then calibrated local classifier                   | Abstain on low confidence                          |
| C03 | Goal decomposition             | None, template, HTN, task graph, model-generated milestones                     | Templates for known families; defer otherwise                  | Premature decomposition can remove valid solutions |

| C05 | Output specification           | MIME/schema/type, examples, predicates, reference artifact                      | Type plus acceptance predicates                                | Output body need not be known at planning time     |
| C06 | Effect target                  | Pure result, read, write, message, purchase, deploy, physical action            | Closed effect taxonomy plus resource scopes                    | Drives approval and verification                   |
| C07 | Prohibitions                   | Negative constraints, deny capabilities, policy rules, effect masks             | First-class hard constraints                                   | Do not bury `must_not` in embeddings               |
| C08 | Preferences                    | Weighted terms, lexicographic rules, utility function, pairwise choices         | Lexicographic hard/soft separation plus Pareto report          | Avoid arbitrary score commensuration               |
| C09 | Quality target                 | Threshold, SLO, example rubric, dominance relation, human judgment              | Measurable thresholds where possible                           | Quality metric must be independent of selector     |
| C10 | Acceptance oracle              | Schema, assertion, property, test suite, reference output, human review         | Compile at least one independent oracle before execution       | Oracle weakness caps all confidence                |
| C11 | Ambiguity model                | Missing fields, competing parses, probability distribution, belief graph        | Explicit alternative interpretations with blockers             | Do not average incompatible intents                |
| C12 | Clarification policy           | Always ask, never ask, VOI threshold, risk-triggered, UI form                   | Ask one discriminating question when VOI is positive           | Store answer as evidence, not prompt decoration    |
| C13 | Assumption ledger              | Hidden defaults, declared assumptions, branch-specific assumptions              | Typed, testable, user-visible assumptions                      | Each route binds its assumption set                |
| C14 | Demand canonicalization        | Text normalization, schema canonical form, semantic hash, theorem equivalence   | Conservative field canonicalization plus versioned hash        | False equivalence corrupts replay                  |
| C15 | Demand fingerprint             | Exact hash, MinHash/LSH, embeddings, behavior signature                         | Multiple independent fingerprints                              | Similarity nominates; it never proves sameness     |
| C16 | Risk budget                    | Fixed tier, expected loss, policy matrix, insurance-like limit                  | Tier plus maximum impact and reversibility                     | High risk forces stronger evidence path            |
| C17 | Privacy budget                 | Data labels, differential-privacy ledger, provider allowlist, local-only flag   | Field-level disclosure policy                                  | Model escalation is a data movement decision       |
| C18 | Cost/latency budget            | Static cap, user tier, deadline-derived, controller allocation                  | Reserve pools for retrieval, execution, verification, fallback | Avoid spending all budget before proof             |
| C19 | Demand satisfiability precheck | Schema checks, type closure, capability bitmap, SMT, catalog statistics         | Cheap exact infeasibility checks                               | Return a no-route certificate when possible        |
| C20 | Counterfactual demands         | None, paraphrases, relaxed constraints, near-miss variants                      | Generate only named relaxations with user approval             | Useful for explaining why no route exists          |
| C21 | Objective provenance           | User-stated, policy-derived, system default, inferred                           | Tag every goal/constraint source                               | Inferred preferences must be defeasible            |
| C22 | Demand epoch                   | Mutable latest, immutable version, event stream, branch                         | Immutable demand versions linked by change events              | Prevent plan execution against changed intent      |

## Plane D — primitive foundry, acquisition, segmentation, and onboarding

| D17 | Variant recognition          | Version lineage, forks, backends, configuration profiles, accelerators                | Explicit implementation lineage graph                  | Do not duplicate capability descriptions blindly         |
| D18 | Wrapper/adapter generation   | Handwritten, template, IDL compiler, model-generated, synthesis                       | Deterministic generation where possible; verify all    | Adapter becomes its own governed primitive               |

| D22 | Pack induction               | Frequent subgraphs, successful route mining, human curation, model summarization      | Mine then human/policy verify high-value motifs        | Pack boundaries should follow demand recurrence          |
| D23 | Missing-capability mining    | Failed routes, user demand gaps, adapter gaps, marketplace requests                   | Rank gaps by repeated failure-inclusive value          | Foundry work should amortize                             |
| D24 | Retirement/revocation        | Manual, vulnerability feed, failed SLO, supersession, policy change                   | Immediate deny overlay plus asynchronous rebuild       | Revocation must bypass stale caches                      |
| D25 | Onboarding receipt           | Plain log, provenance event, SLSA/in-toto statement, signed attestation               | Evidence-linked admission record                       | Capture extractor and verifier versions                  |
| D26 | Native-format preservation   | Normalize everything, preserve native only, dual representation                       | Teleon-owned kernel plus native artifacts and adapters | Avoid a universal super-IR                               |

## Plane E — identity, semantic ABI, contracts, compatibility, and open edges

`PrimitiveCard` should be a compact projection over lower-level identity, contract, evidence, lifecycle, and view records—not the only database row and not a blob that owns every fact.

| ID  | Responsibility              | Alternatives                                                                        | Recommended first default                                      | Scale/risk note                                         |
|-----|-----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|
| E01 | Capability-family identity  | Name, ontology URI, UUID, structural signature, behavior class                      | Stable `CapabilityFamilyId` independent of vendor/version      | Families merge only with strong evidence                |
| E02 | Implementation identity     | Semantic version, content digest, build digest, deployment ID                       | `ImplementationId` plus immutable artifact digests             | One implementation may have several deployments         |
| E03 | Alias namespace             | Flat strings, scoped symbols, package coordinates, multilingual labels              | Scoped aliases with source and validity interval               | Alias collisions are expected at 50M                    |
| E04 | `ActionSpec`                | Free prose, JSON Schema, OpenAPI operation, WIT, Protobuf, CUE                      | Small native-neutral contract with native references           | It is a projection, not a universal language            |
| E05 | Port contract               | Nominal types, structural schemas, refinement types, examples, shapes               | Structural schema plus semantic type/unit annotations          | Inputs and outputs are not only strings                 |
| E06 | Multiplicity/cardinality    | Single/list/stream, optionality, bounds, variadic, keyed collections                | Explicit cardinality and ordering                              | Hidden fan-out changes cost and semantics               |
| E07 | Effect contract             | Tags, algebraic effects, capability sets, read/write sets, syscall profile          | Closed effect taxonomy plus resource scopes                    | Effects compose differently from value types            |
| E08 | State contract              | Pure, local state, session state, remote durable state, transactional resource      | Explicit state locus and consistency model                     | State affects replay and concurrency                    |
| E09 | Temporal/session protocol   | Stateless call, session type, finite-state machine, event protocol, timed automaton | Small protocol state machine when needed                       | Compatibility can depend on call history                |
| E10 | Resource contract           | Expected/maximum CPU, memory, GPU, storage, network, tokens                         | Declared bounds plus observed distributions                    | Estimates are evidence, not guarantees                  |
| E11 | Latency/throughput contract | Point estimate, percentile SLO, service curve, queue-aware model                    | Environment-scoped percentile distributions                    | Tail latency drives portfolio choices                   |
| E12 | Quality contract            | Vendor score, benchmark vector, capability threshold, dominance relation            | Evidence-scoped quality vector                                 | Never collapse task-specific quality to one star rating |
| E13 | Determinism contract        | Deterministic, seeded, replayable, nondeterministic, externally variable            | Explicit class plus controllable entropy inputs                | Required for cache and oracle design                    |
| E14 | Error contract              | Exceptions, result union, status codes, retry classes, partial results              | Typed errors and retryability                                  | Error text is also a retrieval signal                   |
| E15 | Idempotency contract        | None, natural key, supplied key, exactly-once claim, at-least-once safe             | Explicit effect identity domain                                | Provider claims require reconciliation evidence         |
| E16 | Compensation contract       | Inverse action, saga step, snapshot restore, manual repair, irreversible            | Explicit compensation or `none`                                | Never infer reversibility from operation name           |
| E17 | Security/trust envelope     | Source reputation, signature, sandbox class, review, attestation                    | Orthogonal evidence-backed trust axes                          | “Verified” is too coarse                                |
| E18 | Privacy/residency contract  | Data classes, regions, processors, retention, logging behavior                      | Machine-enforceable allowed-flow predicates                    | Drives model/tool placement                             |
| E19 | License/usage contract      | SPDX IDs, policy tags, field-of-use, seat/API limits                                | Machine identifiers plus decision evidence                     | Route composition can alter obligations                 |
| E20 | Environment contract        | OS/arch/runtime, hardware, network, provider, locale, dependency profile            | Constraint set with compatible ranges                          | Bind exact environment only at plan lock                |
| E21 | Configuration contract      | Free map, JSON Schema, feature model, typed flags, profile IDs                      | Schema plus named verified profiles                            | Configurations can change behavior identity             |
| E22 | Observability contract      | None, logs, metrics, traces, semantic events, audit hooks                           | Minimal required events and correlation IDs                    | Verification may depend on observability                |
| E23 | `AlignmentAssertion`        | Exact type equality, subtype/refinement, conversion, empirical compatibility        | Evidence-backed relation with scope and direction              | Compatibility is directional and conditional            |
| E24 | `AdapterCard`               | Inline conversion, first-class primitive, generated glue, human wrapper             | First-class governed primitive with loss/effect metadata       | Hidden adapters are invisible risk                      |
| E25 | Behavioral refinement       | Name match, schema match, tests, simulation, formal proof                           | Liskov-style pre/post/effect refinement where encodable        | Matching fields alone is insufficient                   |
| E26 | Equivalence relation        | Manual alias, same digest, behavioral tests, theorem, e-graph equivalence           | `EquivGraph` with evidence and bounded scope                   | Equivalence may be input-domain-specific                |
| E27 | Substitutability class      | Global class, environment-specific class, demand-local relation                     | Demand/environment-scoped substitute set                       | Avoid global transitive closure of uncertain links      |
