| E28 | Semantic units/standards    | Strings, UCUM/QUDT-like units, domain ontology, conversion primitives               | Stable IDs for units/standards plus explicit conversions       | Unit conversion can be lossy/contextual                 |
| E29 | Capability closure          | Precomputed tags, Datalog rules, ontology reasoning, demand-local closure           | `CapabilityClosure` over exact facts and rules                 | Version rule sets and proof each derived fact           |
| E30 | OPE-Core                    | One card schema, extensible envelope, linked records, native-only                   | Minimal identity/lifecycle/evidence spine                      | Keep third-party extension fields namespaced            |
| E31 | OPE-Primitive               | Fixed ports, native IDLs, typed ports plus extension contracts                      | Compact port/effect core with native attachments               | Do not force every domain into one port grammar         |
| E32 | OPE-Assessment              | Single score, evidence vector, claims and oracles, external certifications          | Claim–evidence–environment triples                             | Assessments expire and can conflict                     |
| E33 | OPE-Representation          | One summary, view registry, description lattice, query-conditioned views            | Evidence-linked multi-resolution views                         | Physical materialization remains policy-driven          |
| E34 | OPE-Search                  | One universal index, federated index interface, query-plan API                      | Search contract with per-channel evidence/abstention           | Search systems retain native scoring semantics          |
| E35 | OPE-Evidence                | Log string, provenance record, signed statement, proof object                       | Typed evidence record with digests and claim scope             | Evidence itself has identity and lifecycle              |
| E36 | Contract evolution          | In-place change, semver, schema transforms, dual publishing, compatibility proof    | Immutable versions plus declared migration relation            | Revalidate dependent routes selectively                 |
| E37 | Contract confidence         | Boolean, source-weighted score, interval/posterior, proof lattice                   | Orthogonal status: declared/inferred/observed/verified/refuted | Never average contradictions away                       |
| E38 | Unknown/open edge           | Reject, optimistic accept, runtime probe, clarification, adapter search             | First-class `unknown` with next-best proof action              | Open-world catalogs require three-valued logic          |

Algebraic effects and handlers provide one useful formal lens for separating what a computation returns from what effects it requests; they are an alternative, not a mandate for every source language ([Plotkin and Pretnar](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.1539)). Behavioral substitutability should be treated as refinement within a stated domain, environment, and effect boundary, rather than as identical names or schemas ([Liskov and Wing](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~wing/publications/LiskovWing94.pdf)).

## Plane F — evidence-linked representations and the `PrimitiveFrame`/codebook

| ID  | Responsibility                  | Alternatives                                                                  | Recommended first default                                                     | Scale/risk note                                              |
|-----|---------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| F01 | Feature-channel registry        | Columns, feature store, versioned view table, opaque JSON                     | Versioned channel records with generator/evidence IDs                         | A channel is not necessarily materialized for all primitives |
| F02 | Shared semantic dictionary      | Free text, ontology, learned codebook, product quantization, symbolic atoms   | `PrimitiveCodebook` of stable atoms plus text fallbacks                       | Dictionary changes require epoching                          |
| F03 | Minimal primitive frame         | Giant card, key/value frame, typed slots, binary code                         | `PrimitiveFrame`: identity, ports, effects, triggers, blockers, evidence refs | Optimize for selection sufficiency                           |
| F04 | Exact lexical view              | Names, aliases, symbols, package coordinates, standards, errors               | Keep all evidence-linked exact strings                                        | Cheapest high-precision channel                              |
| F05 | Purpose view                    | One summary, extractive docs, generated purpose, capability atoms             | Short evidence-linked purpose statement                                       | Avoid marketing language                                     |
| F06 | Trigger/use-when view           | Historical queries, rules, generated triggers, UI actions                     | Mined and curated triggers kept separately                                    | Good for queryless routing                                   |
| F07 | Do-not-use/contrast view        | None, contraindications, nearest-substitute deltas, failure cases             | Explicit blockers and near-miss contrasts                                     | Negative descriptions reduce expensive ambiguity             |
| F08 | Input/output view               | Native signature, normalized schema, examples, compact type code              | Exact normalized types plus native refs                                       | No prose required for deterministic solver                   |
| F09 | Effect/state view               | Tags, effect rows, narrative, observed syscall trace                          | Compact exact effects plus evidence                                           | Critical even when not semantically salient                  |
| F10 | Failure/error view              | Documentation, status codes, observed failures, incident summaries            | Typed failure modes plus exact error tokens                                   | Strong retrieval channel for debugging tasks                 |
| F11 | Example view                    | Call sites, tests, synthetic examples, model-generated examples               | Verified examples with input/output digests                                   | Unverified examples are hypotheses                           |
| F12 | Behavioral fingerprint          | Test outcomes, traces, sketches, mutation response, performance signature     | Compact fingerprint for dedup and rerank                                      | Compare only in matched environments                         |
| F13 | Structural code view            | Tokens, AST paths, imports, call/data flow, type hierarchy                    | Language-native symbol/AST facts                                              | Avoid universal code AST ambitions                           |
| F14 | Composition-affordance view     | Neighbor list, port signatures, adapter motifs, route roles                   | Demand-local typed neighbors plus common motifs                               | Do not store thousands of speculative neighbors              |
| F15 | Role/audience view              | Developer, analyst, operator, end user, compliance                            | Generate only for observed audiences                                          | Most audience variants should remain virtual                 |
| F16 | Multilingual/domain-jargon view | Translation, multilingual embedding, ontology synonyms, query translation     | Demand-driven materialization                                                 | Track translation evidence/version                           |
| F17 | Multi-resolution pyramid        | Label, 16/64/256-token cards, examples, body                                  | Stable handles and progressive disclosure                                     | Invariant safety core appears at every level                 |
| F18 | Contrastive route view          | Full independent cards, deltas from incumbent, pairwise contrasts             | Incumbent plus decisive deltas                                                | Reduces tokens and position bias                             |
| F19 | Predicted-query view            | Doc2query, historical queries, template triggers, no expansion                | Offline generated only when evidence-grounded                                 | Moves work offline but can amplify hallucination             |
| F20 | Generator ensemble              | One model, multiple models, deterministic+model, critic/revision              | Independent generators only on high-value ambiguous items                     | Correlated views add storage, not information                |
| F21 | View disagreement               | Ignore, vote, confidence interval, contradiction record, probe                | Preserve disagreement and trigger evidence acquisition                        | Averages can create false claims                             |
| F22 | View quality calibration        | Human ratings, retrieval attribution, downstream success, tests               | Per-channel/task conditional utility                                          | Popularity is not truth                                      |
| F23 | Materialization scheduler       | All eager, lazy, popularity, uncertainty, active learning, tiered             | Cheap universal views; expensive adaptive views                               | Main economic control at 50M                                 |
| F24 | View distillation/pruning       | Never delete, fixed quota, redundancy clustering, sufficient-statistic search | Retain source; prune materialized redundant projections                       | Measure marginal route recall and selection value            |
| F25 | Evidence pointer granularity    | Whole artifact, file, span, AST node, execution event, test case              | Smallest stable source locator available                                      | Evidence retrieval must survive source versioning            |
| F26 | Representation privacy          | Store raw, redact, encrypt, tenant-local, derived sketch only                 | Field/channel-specific storage and disclosure                                 | Embeddings can leak sensitive attributes                     |

The useful experiment is not “336 descriptions versus one.” It is **which independently evidenced channels add marginal route recall or selection accuracy per byte, index cost, and prompt token**. Correlated paraphrases should lose to a smaller set of purpose, trigger, contract, behavior, failure, contrast, and composition views.

## Plane G — physical storage, indexing, partitioning, and catalog epochs

| ID  | Responsibility                      | Alternatives                                                                 | Recommended first default                                             | Scale/risk note                                     |
|-----|-------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| G01 | Raw artifact store                  | Git, object CAS, OCI, lakehouse, source URL                                  | Immutable content-addressed object store                              | Upstream URL alone is not evidence preservation     |
| G02 | Metadata truth store                | Relational DB, document store, graph DB, RDF store, event log                | Relational core plus append-only events                               | Most filters/joins are ordinary data operations     |
| G03 | Blob/evidence store                 | Inline fields, object store, archival tier, remote ref                       | Digest-addressed blobs separate from hot facts                        | Keep cards compact                                  |
| G04 | Exact ID index                      | Hash map, B-tree, LSM, registry service                                      | Transactional unique index                                            | Direct handles bypass all search                    |
| G05 | Alias/symbol index                  | B-tree, FST/trie, hash postings, n-gram                                      | Scoped exact postings plus prefix structure                           | Preserve alias provenance                           |
| G06 | Typed-filter index                  | SQL, column store, bitmap, roaring bitmap                                    | Bitmap/postings for common dimensions; SQL fallback                   | Apply tenant/policy filters first                   |
| G07 | Approximate membership filter       | Bloom, cuckoo, XOR, prefix filter, quotient filter                           | Per-shard negative precheck only                                      | False positives never prove eligibility             |
| G08 | Fielded lexical index               | BM25F, separate per-field indexes, FTS5, Lucene/OpenSearch                   | Separate names/contracts/docs/errors with analyzers                   | Identifiers and prose need different tokenization   |
| G09 | Fuzzy/character index               | Trigrams, edit distance, phonetic, SymSpell, FST                             | Trigrams for misspelled symbols and error text                        | Use after exact alias lookup                        |
| G10 | Learned sparse index                | SPLADE, uniCOIL, DeepImpact, expansion postings, none                        | Optional experiment after BM25 baseline                               | Posting expansion changes cost materially           |
| G11 | Dense vector index                  | Flat, HNSW, IVF, IVF-PQ, ScaNN, DiskANN                                      | Benchmark per tier/hardware; no universal winner                      | Filters and churn can dominate headline ANN recall  |
| G12 | Multi-vector/late-interaction index | ColBERT, per-field vectors, token sketches, rerank-only                      | Curated/hot-tier reranker                                             | Naïve corpus-wide storage is too large              |
| G13 | Binary/sketch index                 | SimHash, random-hyperplane LSH, MinHash, binary quantization                 | Coarse blocking and dedup candidate generation                        | Union multiple blockers for recall                  |
| G14 | Structural index                    | AST/symbol, call graph, data flow, package dependency, graph embedding       | Language-native facts plus compact postings                           | Keep native analysis outputs                        |
| G15 | Behavioral index                    | Test fingerprints, trace sketches, I/O signatures, benchmark vector          | High-value verified primitives only                                   | Environment-specific and expensive to refresh       |
| G16 | Compatibility index                 | All edges, type partitions, verified sparse edges, rule closure, none        | Type/capability partitions plus verified sparse assertions            | Request-local solver computes the rest              |
| G17 | Route/subgraph index                | Exact GraphIR hash, path trie, WL signature, route embedding, macro registry | Exact macros plus typed fragment postings                             | Retrieve compositions, not only primitives          |
| G18 | Case/history index                  | Exact demand hash, feature KV, lexical, dense, event log                     | Scoped successful cases plus failures and validity keys               | Record exposure/selection bias                      |
| G19 | Negative/no-good index              | Exact tuple, generalized solver clause, failed route, refutation proof       | `RefuteCache`/`NoGoodCache` with scope and TTL                        | Transient failures must not become global facts     |
| G20 | Tenant overlay                      | Fully separate index, ACL filter, overlay postings, encrypted namespace      | Shared public base plus exact tenant overlay where allowed            | Authorization before semantic scoring               |
| G21 | Shard key                           | Hash, source, tenant, language, domain, type, semantic centroid, hybrid      | Multi-level domain/type plus overlap/fallback                         | Hard semantic shards can destroy recall             |
| G22 | Shard router                        | Broadcast, rules, classifier, centroid ANN, learned router                   | Deterministic constraints then calibrated multi-shard router          | Always retain bounded global escape                 |
| G23 | Hot/warm/cold tier                  | Uniform, popularity, recency, trust, value, tenant                           | Tier representations rather than excluding primitives                 | Exact/lexical can remain broadly available          |
| G24 | Base-plus-delta index               | Full rebuild, LSM segments, overlay delta, live mutable graph                | Immutable base epoch plus small real-time deltas                      | Simplifies reproducible receipts                    |
| G25 | Tombstone/revocation overlay        | Rebuild, delete-in-place, deny bitmap, signed kill list                      | Immediate exact deny overlay                                          | Must override every cache/index tier                |
| G26 | Catalog epoch                       | Mutable latest, timestamp, snapshot ID, Merkle root                          | Immutable snapshot ID plus Merkle root                                | Bind retrieval and PlanLock to epoch                |
| G27 | Index build manifest                | Ad hoc job, config file, data lineage, reproducible action graph             | Generator/model/config/input digests                                  | Needed to compare channels honestly                 |
| G28 | Index consistency                   | Strong, near-real-time, eventual, session read-your-writes                   | Explicit per-index freshness and delta semantics                      | Report partial/stale search in receipt              |
| G29 | Replication/failure                 | None, replicas, erasure coding, multi-region, federation                     | Risk-tiered replicas and graceful partial results                     | Tail latency and consistency trade off              |
| G30 | Storage retention                   | Delete old, archive raw only, retain all indexes, legal hold                 | Retain raw/evidence and reconstructible manifests; expire projections | “Store everything” need not mean “serve everything” |

## Plane H — cheap query formation, retrieval, fusion, and corrective search

| ID  | Responsibility               | Alternatives                                                               | Recommended first default                                   | Scale/risk note                                   |
|-----|------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| H01 | Queryless trigger            | Handle, error code, file change, AST symbol, event, schedule, UI action    | Prefer host/tool signals over prose when available          | Can remove interpretation entirely                |
| H02 | Deterministic normalization  | Unicode, tokenization, identifier splitting, locale/unit rules             | Lossless normalized fields                                  | Keep original text for rare exact clues           |
| H03 | Clause segmentation          | Punctuation, parser, discourse model, SLM, no segmentation                 | Cheap rules plus typed clause classifier                    | Enables clause-level memoization                  |
| H04 | Keyword/keyphrase extraction | Dictionary, RAKE/TextRank, POS chunks, BM25 terms, local encoder           | Exact identifiers plus statistical keyphrases               | Do not discard negation or scopes                 |
| H05 | Entity/standard resolution   | Gazetteer, alias table, ontology, linker, model                            | Exact scoped aliases then calibrated candidates             | Preserve unresolved entities                      |
| H06 | Intent/slot mapping          | Rules, finite-state parser, classifier, CRF, local SLM                     | Templates and local classifier with abstention              | Generates typed fields, not free-form query prose |
| H07 | Query template fill          | SQL/DSL templates, conditionals, finite automaton, grammar                 | Parameterized `QueryPlan` prototypes                        | Template version becomes receipt input            |
| H08 | Query prototype retrieval    | Exact family, kNN over demands, case retrieval, route history              | Validated prototypes with applicability predicates          | Better than generating recurring queries          |
| H09 | Query-plan IR                | Raw query strings, relational algebra, boolean AST, federated plan         | Typed `QueryPlan` with channel budgets and hard predicates  | Optimizable and replayable                        |
| H10 | Field selection              | Search all, intent map, learned channel router, active view request        | Rules first; measure marginal channel utility               | Saves fanout and embedding calls                  |
| H11 | Shard selection              | Broadcast, constraints, centroid, classifier, history                      | Exact exclusions plus multi-shard semantic routing          | Retain bounded exploration path                   |
| H12 | Exact/history stage          | IDs, semantic hash, recipe cache, case cache, pack lookup                  | First stage with full validity recheck                      | A cache hit is a candidate, not authorization     |
| H13 | Sparse retrieval stage       | BM25F, trigram, learned sparse, expansion, SQL FTS                         | Fielded BM25 plus exact identifiers                         | Strong cheap baseline and explainable terms       |
| H14 | Dense retrieval stage        | Single vector, multi-view union, ANN, semantic hash                        | Route only selected clauses/views to ANN                    | Do not embed whole history automatically          |
| H15 | Graph/route retrieval        | Neighbor expansion, macro lookup, subgraph index, path trie                | Exact route macros then typed fragment search               | Preserve connectors before top-k                  |
| H16 | Federated broker             | Central index, source-native queries, scatter/gather, metasearch           | Common result/evidence envelope; native indexes retained    | Scores may be incomparable                        |
| H17 | Candidate union              | Global top-k, per-channel quotas, per-capability quotas, set cover         | Stratified union with exact blockers reapplied              | Prevent one strong channel from erasing recall    |
| H18 | Fusion                       | Weighted sum, RRF, calibrated probabilities, learning-to-rank, Pareto      | RRF baseline plus hard constraints; learned later           | Score normalization is not calibration            |
| H19 | Reranker                     | Rules, LambdaMART, cross-encoder, late interaction, SLM, hosted model      | Non-generative local ranker before generative arms          | Freeze candidate set for selector comparisons     |
| H20 | Diversity controller         | MMR, clustering, determinant point process, topology/effect diversity      | Failure-domain and route-topology diversity                 | Embedding diversity alone is inadequate           |
| H21 | Connector expansion          | None, k-hop neighbors, type-required ports, adapter closure, Steiner hints | Expand required connectors before final pruning             | Essential for complete-route recall               |
| H22 | Adaptive recall budget       | Fixed k, score margin, coverage, entropy, topology saturation, cost        | Smallest k meeting calibrated route-coverage target         | Allow k=0 for direct paths                        |
| H23 | Active discriminator         | Ask user, inspect field, probe environment, run test, widen retrieval      | Maximum VOI per cost/risk                                   | Often cheaper than another LLM                    |
| H24 | Corrective retrieval         | Reformulate, alternate index, relax shard, graph expand, acquire source    | Trigger on explicit insufficiency certificate               | Do not blindly repeat same retriever              |
| H25 | Query SLM                    | Classifier, grammar-constrained generator, local chat model                | Only unresolved typed slots or query AST nodes              | Log exactly which fields needed modeling          |
| H26 | Hosted query model           | Small hosted, strong hosted, frontier, committee                           | Bounded unresolved delta plus grammar/schema                | Worst-case tail, not normal first stage           |
| H27 | Search stop rule             | Fixed depth, score threshold, risk coverage, marginal VOI, deadline        | Stop when expected unseen value is below next action cost   | Counterfactual sampling checks missed value       |
| H28 | Search receipt               | Only final hits, full query strings, plan and per-stage evidence           | Hashable `QueryPlan`, budgets, candidates, filters, reasons | Required for cost attribution and replay          |
| H29 | Negative search result       | Empty list, unknown, proved impossible, policy-blocked, stale/partial      | Distinguish `no-match`, `not-searched`, `unknown`, `denied` | Drives correct fallback behavior                  |
| H30 | Full-scan guard              | No guard, row estimate, shard cap, query cost planner, timeout             | Hard cost/fanout ceiling with explicit override             | No production full scan at 50M                    |

The major alternatives here are not just BM25 versus embeddings. They include **no query**, prototype retrieval, template compilation, host-supplied structure, multi-pass blocking, field/channel routing, route retrieval, active probes, and corrective search. Learned sparse retrieval and late interaction are useful intermediate families between classical sparse and single-vector dense retrieval ([SPLADE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.10086), [ColBERTv2](https://aclanthology.org/2022.naacl-main.272/)).

## Plane I — request-local graph construction, route solving, and optimization

| ID  | Responsibility                      | Alternatives                                                                | Recommended first default                                          | Scale/risk note                                     |
|-----|-------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| I01 | Catalog graph projection            | Global graph, relational join, lazy neighbors, request-local hypergraph     | Build a bounded request-local port hypergraph                      | Global graph remains a derived view                 |
| I02 | Node kind model                     | Only primitives, ports as nodes, values/resources/events/states as nodes    | Separate action, port, resource, evidence, and adapter kinds       | Avoid encoding everything as unlabeled node         |
| I03 | Edge kind model                     | Compatibility only, data/control/effect/state/evidence edges                | Typed directed edges with evidence/status                          | Hyperedges represent joins/multi-input requirements |
| I04 | Type unification                    | Exact equality, nominal subtype, structural subsumption, refinements, SMT   | Structural core plus explicit alignments/adapters                  | Unknown is not compatible                           |
| I05 | Effect composition                  | Ignore, tag union, effect rows, capability logic, state transition system   | Exact effect/resource accumulation                                 | Hard safety gate                                    |
| I06 | Adapter planning                    | Preinsert all, search first-class adapters, synthesize, reject              | Search verified `AdapterCard`s; nominate missing adapters          | Penalize loss, cost, and new effects                |
| I07 | Forward search                      | BFS, Dijkstra, A\*, beam, best-first, graph DB traversal                    | Bounded A\*/best-first with admissible hard filters                | Good when inputs are selective                      |
| I08 | Backward search                     | Regression, goal-directed rules, backwards chaining                         | Backward required-port expansion                                   | Good when output is selective                       |
| I09 | Bidirectional search                | Meet-in-middle BFS/A\*, front-to-front, frontier join                       | Typed forward/backward frontiers with connector proof              | Not always best for asymmetric spaces               |
| I10 | AND/OR/hypergraph search            | Flattened graph, AO\*, generalized Dijkstra, integer programming            | Explicit AND requirements for multi-input primitives               | Prevent false routes that satisfy one input only    |
| I11 | Constraint solving                  | CSP, CP-SAT, SAT, SMT, ILP, MaxSAT                                          | Use for bounded hard combinatorial subproblems                     | Claims hold only within encoding and limits         |
| I12 | Planning language                   | None, PDDL, HTN, Petri net, BPMN, session types                             | Keep native planner adapters, not universal replacement            | Select by task semantics                            |
| I13 | Rule/logic closure                  | Datalog, Prolog, description logic, custom rules                            | Datalog-like monotone capability closure                           | Effects/nonmonotonicity need separate treatment     |
| I14 | Type inhabitation/program synthesis | Enumerative, deductive, e-graphs, neural-guided, sketches                   | Experimental for pure typed fragments                              | Real-world state reduces completeness               |
| I15 | CEGIS                               | Generate once, counterexample-guided loop, verifier-in-loop search          | Use when acceptance oracle gives actionable counterexamples        | Bound iterations and capture no-goods               |
| I16 | CEGAR                               | Full concrete planning, abstract plan then refine, predicate abstraction    | Use on state-heavy high-cost cases                                 | Bad abstractions can thrash                         |
| I17 | Query optimizer/Cascades            | Hand rules, Volcano/Cascades memo, cost-based physical planning             | Memoize equivalent logical routes and implementations              | Strong fit for many interchangeable backends        |
| I18 | Equality saturation                 | Sequential rewrites, e-graph, superoptimizer                                | Apply to pure/equivalence-proven subgraphs                         | Effects require guarded rewrite rules               |
| I19 | Algorithm portfolio                 | One solver, static rules, SATzilla-like selector, parallel portfolio        | Feature-based choice among a small measured solver set             | Log solver availability and timeout censoring       |
| I20 | Cost model                          | Declared sums, historical distributions, learned estimator, probes          | Environment-scoped distributions plus conservative bounds          | Cost errors should not violate hard constraints     |
| I21 | Multiobjective optimization         | Weighted sum, lexicographic, constrained optimization, Pareto skyline       | Hard constraints then `PathSkyline` of nondominated routes         | Preserve user-relevant tradeoffs                    |
| I22 | Route diversity                     | k shortest, disjoint paths, failure-domain diversity, semantic diversity    | Diverse Pareto finalists across correlated failures                | Eight near-identical routes are one alternative     |
| I23 | Partial-order planning              | Total DAG, dependency partial order, concurrency groups, event choreography | Preserve only necessary ordering                                   | Enables safe parallel execution                     |
| I24 | Cycle/termination analysis          | Ban cycles, loop bounds, ranking function, runtime guard                    | Acyclic first slice; explicit bounded loops later                  | Retry loops are not arbitrary cycles                |
| I25 | Route completion                    | Complete only, partial skeleton, open ports, deferred binding               | Allow explicit open edges before selection; close before admission | Useful for asking targeted questions                |
| I26 | `LemmaGraph`                        | Flat candidate graph, derived facts, proof-labeled graph                    | Store compact derived compatibility lemmas                         | Each lemma points to premises and rule version      |
| I27 | `PremiseGraph`                      | Duplicate evidence per edge, shared premise nodes, proof DAG                | Share evidence facts across claims                                 | Changes invalidate dependent lemmas efficiently     |
| I28 | `EquivGraph`                        | No equivalence, union-find, guarded equality graph, e-graph                 | Guarded equivalence classes scoped by environment/domain           | Uncertain equivalence is not transitive by default  |
| I29 | `PathSkyline`                       | Top score, k shortest, Pareto frontier, epsilon-dominance                   | Small epsilon-Pareto frontier with diversity                       | Caps candidate explosion without hiding tradeoffs   |
| I30 | No-route certificate                | Empty result, frontier dump, unsat core, missing capability, policy denial  | Minimal blockers, searched scope, and next actions                 | Distinguish impossible from unsearched              |
| I31 | Soundness checker                   | Trust solver, replay types, proof certificate, independent compiler         | Independent route checker over compact proof                       | A solver bug must not become execution authority    |
| I32 | Search completeness claim           | Unqualified, bounded, relative to candidate closure, empirical recall       | State exact search bounds and retrieval dependence                 | Never claim global completeness at 50M              |

Apache Calcite is a useful concrete analogy: immutable logical trees, semantic-preserving transformations, physical alternatives, and cost-based planning are separate concerns ([Calcite algebra](https://calcite.apache.org/docs/algebra.html), [VolcanoPlanner](https://calcite.apache.org/javadocAggregate/org/apache/calcite/plan/volcano/VolcanoPlanner.html)). Equality saturation offers another way to delay destructive rewrite choices and extract a low-cost equivalent expression ([egg](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.03082)). CEGIS makes the verifier an active search partner rather than an after-the-fact judge ([CEGIS](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.5397)).

## Plane J — route handles, progressive disclosure, selection, and action control

Selection is only one possible controller action. The correct action may instead be `accept_unique`, `retrieve_more`, `expand_graph`, `request_field`, `run_probe`, `clarify`, `compile`, `escalate`, `create_adapter`, `human_review`, or `abstain`.

| ID  | Responsibility                | Alternatives                                                               | Recommended first default                                           | Scale/risk note                                      |
|-----|-------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
| J01 | Route identity                | Array index, UUID, canonical graph hash, signed handle                     | Canonical route digest plus opaque short handle                     | Handle remains stable across presentation order      |
| J02 | Route handle payload          | ID only, embedded recipe, capability token, proof-carrying handle          | ID plus compact `PlanCodec` recipe and epoch                        | Do not expose secrets or bodies                      |
| J03 | `PlanCodec`                   | JSON graph, binary opcode stream, grammar, DSL, route macro ID             | Small versioned grammar over primitive/edge IDs                     | Measure bytes and decode correctness                 |
| J04 | Invariant safety core         | Hidden until requested, repeated full card, compact always-visible block   | Always show effects, trust blockers, unknowns, irreversible actions | Progressive disclosure must never hide decisive risk |
| J05 | Detail levels                 | One fixed view, summary/full, 16/64/256 token pyramid, field paging        | Safety core + compact card + requested evidence                     | Test decision quality per token                      |
| J06 | Contrastive presentation      | Independent full cards, pairwise compare, incumbent-plus-deltas, table     | Best current route plus decisive deltas                             | Avoid repeating identical route structure            |
| J07 | Alternative cardinality       | 1, 2, 4, 8, fixed k, adaptive k, coverage set, user-driven paging          | Preserve 1/2/4/8 experiments; production adaptive                   | k measures candidate exposure, not retrieval depth   |
| J08 | Alternative diversity         | Top scores, MMR, topology, implementation family, failure domain, evidence | Route/failure-domain diversity constraint                           | Duplicate routes create false confidence             |
| J09 | Model-visible primitive count | All route nodes, unique components, only differing nodes, on-demand        | Shared skeleton once; expose differing nodes/edges                  | Major token lever for long routes                    |
| J10 | Edge visibility               | None, all, only open/conditional, proof summary, requested                 | Show route-wide invariants and decision-changing edges              | Too few edges hides feasibility; too many adds noise |
| J11 | Evidence visibility           | Score only, citations, claim/evidence summary, proof object, tool request  | Claim status and concise supporting evidence                        | A fluent card is not evidence                        |
| J12 | No-selector path              | Always select, unique route auto-accept, policy winner, user choice        | Skip selector on one admissible nondominated route                  | Most valuable selector benchmark arm                 |
| J13 | Deterministic selector        | Weighted score, lexicographic, rules, Pareto tie-break, optimizer          | Hard constraints then lexicographic/Pareto                          | Raw scores need no natural commensuration            |
| J14 | Non-generative local ranker   | Logistic model, LambdaMART, cross-encoder, late interaction, classifier    | Add before local generative SLM                                     | Often better latency/token profile                   |
| J15 | Local SLM selector            | Free text, constrained JSON, grammar, classification token                 | Grammar-constrained decision over handles and reasons               | Never let it invent unseen handles                   |
| J16 | Cheap hosted selector         | Small general model, distilled task model, provider router                 | Bounded route deltas only                                           | Privacy and usage accounting apply                   |
| J17 | Strong/frontier selector      | Single model, multiple providers, committee, debate, critic                | Rare residual semantic tie; structured response                     | Do not use as general proof oracle                   |
| J18 | Human selector                | User choice, domain expert, operations approver, adjudication panel        | Separate preference selection from safety approval                  | Record role and evidence viewed                      |
| J19 | Selector ensemble             | Majority, pairwise tournament, stacker, disagreement escalation            | Off by default; high-risk residual arm                              | Multiple correlated models are not independent proof |
| J20 | Selector calibration          | Raw margin, Platt/isotonic, selective prediction, conformal risk control   | Coverage–risk calibration with abstention                           | Calibrate on accepted route success, not similarity  |
| J21 | Model capability registry     | Hard-coded tiers, scorecard, capability vector, online posterior           | Frozen measured task-family profiles                                | Models are versioned executors with cost/limits      |
| J22 | Model router                  | Fixed, rule, RouteLLM-like, cascade, budgeted portfolio                    | Deterministic safe paths then measured cost-aware router            | Strong model only if incremental value justifies it  |
| J23 | Context pager                 | Full prompt, fixed projection, tool paging, retrieval-as-tool              | Model may request named fields within budget                        | Prevents speculative over-disclosure                 |
| J24 | Structured decision decoder   | Parse prose, JSON retries, function call, grammar, classifier logits       | Schema/grammar-constrained output                                   | Invalid outputs are controller failures              |
| J25 | Decision explanation          | Free rationale, reason codes, evidence refs, counterfactual delta          | Reason codes plus cited decisive fields                             | Rationale is not a proof                             |
| J26 | Clarification UI              | Free text, generated form, multiple choice, route contrast                 | One minimum discriminating question                                 | Distinguish clarification from consent/approval      |
| J27 | Stop/escalate controller      | Fixed waterfall, rule DAG, sequential test, bandit, POMDP, LLM supervisor  | Explicit finite action set and deterministic risk gates             | Collapse into one module initially                   |
| J28 | Budget arbiter                | Per-call cap, request envelope, token bucket, utility optimizer            | Request-wide budget with reserved verification/fallback pools       | Optimize total accepted-outcome cost                 |
| J29 | Speculative/hedged selection  | Sequential, local+hosted parallel, delayed hedge, none                     | Off by default; latency experiment only                             | Hedging can increase tokens substantially            |
| J30 | Counterfactual logging        | Winners only, shadow later tiers, random audit, full portfolio offline     | Sample shadow actions within privacy/budget                         | Needed to calibrate early exits                      |

FrugalGPT and RouteLLM show that cost-aware cascades and learned routing can reduce expensive model use, but Taedri's action space is larger than “which model”: it includes exact replay, tools, probes, clarification, retrieval, compilation, and abstention ([FrugalGPT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.05176), [RouteLLM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.18665)). Selective prediction and conformal risk-control ideas are useful for defining an explicit coverage–risk tradeoff rather than accepting every low-margin choice ([SelectiveNet](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.09192), [Conformal Risk Control](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.02814)).

## Plane K — GraphIR, compilation, admission, `PlanLock`, and artifact closure

`GraphIR` is one alternative in a multi-dialect compiler architecture. A small common kernel should represent values, actions, dependencies, effects, claims, and artifacts; native dialects retain semantics that the kernel cannot encode losslessly. Lowering bridges must declare losses and legality conditions.

| ID  | Responsibility            | Alternatives                                                                 | Recommended first default                                         | Scale/risk note                                   |
|-----|---------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| K01 | Plan representation       | Direct route, recipe JSON, `GraphIR`, generated code, workflow-native spec   | Tiny immutable PlanAST/GraphIR kernel                             | Do not implement a universal super-IR             |
| K02 | Native dialect attachment | Strip native semantics, opaque blob, MLIR-like dialect, external ref         | Native record + normalized projection + loss map                  | Claimed round trips require conformance tests     |
| K03 | Schema migration          | Accept old, upgrade-on-read, migration graph, reject                         | Immutable versions with explicit migrators                        | Persisted plans outlive schemas                   |
| K04 | Canonicalization          | Text canonicalization, stable topological order, graph normal form           | Canonical node IDs/order plus RFC 8785-style bytes                | Enables route hashing and cache reuse             |
| K05 | Static type checker       | Runtime only, nominal, structural, refinement, constraint solver             | Structural ports plus alignment witnesses                         | Rerun independently after selection               |
| K06 | Effect/authority checker  | Tags, effect system, capability logic, policy engine                         | Compile accumulated effects against authority                     | Must precede artifact loading/execution           |
| K07 | Protocol/state checker    | None, FSM, session types, model checker, runtime monitor                     | Explicit checks only for stateful/protocol routes                 | Avoid burdening pure DAGs                         |
| K08 | Rewrite optimizer         | None, local rules, partial evaluation, fusion, e-graph, cost optimizer       | Correctness first; safe local rewrites later                      | Bind rule versions into receipt                   |
| K09 | Backend selector          | One runtime, rule mapping, cost-based placement, learned choice              | One initial backend with explicit adapter interface               | Add only after semantics are stable               |
| K10 | Backend lowering          | Interpreter, generated code, Temporal/CWL/Argo/BPMN, DB pushdown             | Deterministic lowering with round-trip/semantic tests             | Native runtimes have different guarantees         |
| K11 | Cost/resource estimator   | Declared sums, historical distributions, queue-aware predictor, probe        | Conservative declared+observed estimate                           | Estimates inform, hard quotas enforce             |
| K12 | Demand admission          | Always accept, supported-family rules, risk gate, human triage               | Explicit supported scope and missing-demand report                | Distinguish unsupported from no route             |
| K13 | Candidate admission       | Retrieval score, verified status, policy eligibility, trust threshold        | Exact tenant/policy/lifecycle gate                                | Candidate may be discoverable but non-executable  |
| K14 | Plan admission            | Type/effect/policy/resource/oracle checks                                    | Immutable `AdmissionReport` with reason codes                     | Separate from solver “found route”                |
| K15 | Artifact admission        | Trust, closure, vulnerability/license, runtime compatibility                 | Resolve and verify exact transitive closure                       | Body resolution is a fixed-point problem          |
| K16 | Effect admission          | Compile-time only, just-in-time recheck, user approval, lease                | Recheck authority/freshness/idempotency immediately before effect | Plans can go stale between compile and dispatch   |
| K17 | `AdmissionGrant`          | Boolean flag, signed decision, capability token, short-lived lease           | Scoped, expiring grant bound to plan/policy epoch                 | Do not reuse across changed plans                 |
| K18 | `PlanLock`                | None, lockfile, content-addressed lock, signed/leased/reservation/proof lock | Content-addressed signed record with dynamic slot types           | Lock exact decisions, not secret values           |
| K19 | Dynamic binding           | Recompile all, allowed slots, capability resolver, late service discovery    | Typed allowlisted slots with policies and freshness               | Dynamic freedom must be explicit                  |
| K20 | Closure constructor       | Direct artifacts only, lockfile, package graph, fixed-point closure          | Compute transitive code/data/model/prompt/policy/verifier closure | Missing verifier asset also invalidates execution |
| K21 | Content-addressed store   | Paths, version names, CAS, OCI, Nix, remote handles                          | Digest-addressed local/remote CAS                                 | Mutable names resolve before lock                 |
| K22 | Reproducibility mode      | Best effort, lock dependencies, hermetic sandbox, reproducible build         | Declare class: replayable, rebuildable, or live-dependent         | Do not overclaim remote-service reproducibility   |
| K23 | Action/cache key          | Request hash, plan hash, declared inputs, environment, policy epoch          | Hash declared closure and exact dynamic bindings                  | Inspired by build-system action caches            |
| K24 | Supply-chain manifest     | None, lockfile, SBOM, SLSA/in-toto, OCI referrers                            | Closure manifest plus attestations for risk tiers                 | Evidence and artifact identity are distinct       |
| K25 | Update trust              | Latest mutable, signatures, TUF metadata, pinned digest                      | Pinned digest plus signed freshness/revocation metadata           | Protect against rollback/freeze/key compromise    |
| K26 | Preflight                 | None, static validation, availability, credential probe, dry run             | Non-destructive closure/authority/quota checks                    | Preflight cannot prove external effect success    |
| K27 | Plan signer/approver      | System key, tenant key, human signature, threshold policy                    | Policy signer plus optional human approval evidence               | Approval identity must be role-resolved           |
| K28 | Compiler receipt          | Only binary, diagnostics, proof certificate, complete manifest               | Input/output digests, rule/tool versions, decisions, warnings     | Enables independent rechecking                    |

Nix and Bazel illustrate two useful mechanisms: content-addressed or declared-input artifact closure and reproducible action caching ([Nix content addressing](https://nix.dev/manual/nix/2.28/store/store-object/content-address), [Bazel remote caching](https://bazel.build/remote/caching)). SLSA and TUF cover different trust questions—build provenance and secure update/freshness—and should not be collapsed into a single “signed” flag ([SLSA provenance](https://slsa.dev/spec/v1.2/provenance), [TUF](https://theupdateframework.io/)).

### What `PlanLock` should actually bind

A production lock should include:

- demand, context snapshot, catalog, policy, and compiler epochs/digests;
- candidate-set and selected-route digests;
- primitive, adapter, model, prompt, skill, and lowering versions;
- exact artifacts and closure-manifest digest;
- typed allowed dynamic slots;
- environment/runtime compatibility constraints;
- effects, ordering, idempotency domains, and compensation rules;
- required capability/secret classes without the secrets themselves;
- resource, token, monetary, latency, retry, and disclosure ceilings;
- isolation and placement constraints;
- claim-to-oracle bindings;
- validity interval, revocation epoch, and revalidation triggers; and
- signer/attestation identity.

### Artifact-closure invariant

For selected nodes `S₀`, repeatedly add declared code, libraries, models, tokenizers, data, schemas, adapters, prompts, skills, policy bundles, runtime images, verifier assets, and remote contracts until reaching a fixed point `S*`:

``` text
S(i+1) = S(i) ∪ ⋃ D(v), for every v in S(i)
```

Execution is admissible only if every immutable dependency resolves by digest; every mutable binding has a typed resolver, policy, freshness rule, and failure mode; every effect has authority and idempotency semantics; every critical claim has an oracle; every executable has a compatible isolation profile; and no closure member is missing, revoked, quarantined, or outside retention guarantees.

## Plane L — execution, durability, placement, identity, and external effects

| ID  | Responsibility            | Alternatives                                                                  | Recommended first default                                     | Scale/risk note                                              |
|-----|---------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| L01 | Execution mode            | Return plan, simulate, dry-run, execute, shadow, canary                       | Explicit mode in PlanLock                                     | Never infer authorization to execute from planning           |
| L02 | Interpreter/runtime       | In-process, subprocess, container, Wasm/WASI, workflow engine, generated code | Small deterministic executor plus backend interface           | Match runtime to effect and durability needs                 |
| L03 | Isolation profile         | Trusted process, restricted subprocess, container, gVisor, microVM, VM        | Risk-tier selection enforced by admission/runtime             | One sandbox does not fit all primitives                      |
| L04 | Workload identity         | Inherited user, service account, SPIFFE, capability token, delegated OAuth    | Ephemeral least-privilege workload identity                   | PlanLock stores class/scope, not secret                      |
| L05 | Secret broker             | Environment, files, vault lease, per-step token, user-mediated grant          | Short-lived scoped resolution at execution                    | Prevent secrets entering prompts/receipts                    |
| L06 | Placement                 | Local, edge, cluster, provider, data-local, region-constrained                | Constraint-first then cost/latency selection                  | Residency and hardware are hard predicates                   |
| L07 | Scheduler                 | FIFO, priority, fair share, deadline, data/GPU aware, auction                 | Per-tenant fairness and resource quotas                       | Scale of executions, not catalog, triggers complexity        |
| L08 | Concurrency semantics     | Sequential, DAG parallel, actors, streams, database transactions              | Partial-order DAG with explicit limits                        | Preserve required ordering only                              |
| L09 | Durability                | Fire-and-forget, retry, checkpoints, event history, durable workflow          | Durable engine only for long/effectful work                   | Pure short calls can remain simple                           |
| L10 | Checkpoint/replay         | None, node outputs, event sourcing, snapshot, deterministic replay            | Content-addressed outputs plus event log                      | Nondeterministic/live inputs need classification             |
| L11 | Retry policy              | None, fixed, exponential, hedged, circuit breaker, solver-chosen              | Error-class and idempotency-aware bounded retries             | Retry can duplicate external effects                         |
| L12 | Idempotency registry      | None, request ID, natural key, provider key, effect ledger                    | Explicit effect identity and dedup state                      | Required across crashes and retries                          |
| L13 | Lease/fencing             | None, DB lock, distributed lease, fencing token, reservation                  | Fencing for shared mutable resources                          | Expired worker must not commit                               |
| L14 | Outbox/inbox              | Unsafe dual write, transaction, outbox+CDC, inbox dedup, event sourcing       | Use when crossing transactional boundaries                    | Eliminates common message/state inconsistency                |
| L15 | Transaction semantics     | Best effort, ACID, saga, two-phase commit, checkpoint rollback                | Local transactions; sagas for distributed effects             | Declare atomicity boundary precisely                         |
| L16 | Compensation              | Retry, inverse primitive, saga action, restore, manual repair                 | First-class compensation graph or explicit irreversible state | Compensation can fail too                                    |
| L17 | External-effect journal   | Tool response only, effect ID log, authoritative polling, event subscription  | State machine tied to authoritative observations              | `completed` is not one fact                                  |
| L18 | Reconciliation            | Trust acknowledgement, poll, compare ledgers, domain verifier, human          | Independent authoritative reconciliation for critical effects | Handles uncertain outcomes                                   |
| L19 | Uncertain-outcome handler | Treat failed, retry, query status, quarantine, manual repair                  | `indeterminate` state plus no blind retry                     | Essential after network loss post-dispatch                   |
| L20 | Resource enforcement      | Estimates only, OS quotas, cgroups, runtime fuel, token/time caps             | Hard CPU/memory/time/network/effect caps                      | Budget predictions alone cannot protect                      |
| L21 | Network policy            | Ambient access, allowlist, proxy, capability sockets, no network              | Deny by default then declared destinations                    | Observed network use feeds contract evidence                 |
| L22 | Filesystem policy         | Full workspace, roots, snapshot, per-file capabilities, no FS                 | Read-only snapshot plus explicit writable outputs             | Host project state needs strong scoping                      |
| L23 | Progress/backpressure     | Blocking, progress tokens, streaming, queue limits, cancellation              | Unified deadline/cancel/progress semantics                    | Prevent runaway agents and queues                            |
| L24 | Runtime observability     | Logs, metrics, traces, semantic events, eBPF                                  | Correlated structured events plus OTel export                 | Observability events are not automatically provenance claims |
| L25 | Output binding            | Mutable path, return value, digest artifact, remote object ID                 | Content digest plus type/schema and effect IDs                | Verification must bind exact outputs                         |
| L26 | Runtime fallback          | Retry same, substitute implementation, replan suffix, human                   | Revalidate a bounded repair against PlanLock policy           | Do not silently change locked semantics                      |
| L27 | Incremental replanning    | Full restart, reuse prefix/suffix, dependency-cone repair, contingency        | Later phase for long-lived routes                             | Receipt must show divergence from original plan              |
| L28 | Execution receipt         | One status, step events, state transitions, artifact/effect digests           | Exact per-node inputs, outputs, errors, attempts, effects     | Enables independent verification and cost accounting         |

External effects need a richer state machine than `pending/completed`:

``` text
planned → admitted → authorized → dispatched → acknowledged
        → externally_observed → reconciled

failure branches:
rejected | failed_before_dispatch | failed_after_dispatch | indeterminate
| retry_scheduled | compensation_requested | compensated
| compensation_failed | manual_repair_required
```

An HTTP 200, a tool-return payload, workflow completion, authoritative external observation, and reconciled domain effect are different facts.

## Plane M — independent verification, claims, evidence, provenance, and receipts

| ID  | Responsibility             | Alternatives                                                                           | Recommended first default                                  | Scale/risk note                                   |
|-----|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| M01 | Claim registry             | One route status, assertion list, requirements traceability, proof obligations         | Atomic claims linked to demand and effects                 | “Verified route” is too broad                     |
| M02 | Oracle registry            | Embedded test, domain validator, reference, external authority, human                  | Named versioned oracle per claim                           | Oracle independence is explicit metadata          |
| M03 | Oracle compiler            | Handwritten, template, property extraction, model proposal, synthesis                  | Deterministic from acceptance predicates; review generated | Reject tautological/self-referential oracles      |
| M04 | Verification planner       | Run all, risk tier, cascade, VOI portfolio, random audit                               | Minimum proof policy plus cheapest independent portfolio   | Reserve execution budget for it                   |
| M05 | Schema validation          | JSON Schema, CUE, Protobuf, SHACL, custom                                              | Native schema validator                                    | Necessary but not sufficient                      |
| M06 | Static analysis            | Types, lint, taint, effect, policy, abstract interpretation                            | Language/domain-native analyzers                           | Scope claims precisely                            |
| M07 | Example/golden tests       | Exact values, snapshots, tolerance, semantic diff                                      | Only stable domains and normalized outputs                 | Snapshots can encode bugs                         |
| M08 | Property-based tests       | Generated cases, invariants, boundary strategies                                       | High-value pure/data primitives                            | Use shrinkable counterexamples                    |
| M09 | Fuzzing                    | Mutation, grammar, coverage-guided, protocol fuzz                                      | Risk-based onboarding/offline                              | Not every execution hot path                      |
| M10 | Metamorphic tests          | Relations under transformed inputs, invariances, monotonicity                          | When exact oracle is unavailable                           | Relation validity itself needs evidence           |
| M11 | Differential validation    | Independent implementation, prior version, alternative route, authority                | Compare different failure domains                          | Common dependencies reduce independence           |
| M12 | Reference-model validation | Simulator, specification interpreter, high-precision slow solver                       | Critical bounded domains                                   | Reference can be incomplete                       |
| M13 | Mutation adequacy          | No check, operator suite, test sensitivity, fault injection                            | Benchmark proof suites, not every run                      | Exposes weak or tautological tests                |
| M14 | Formal checking            | SMT, model checking, proof assistant, PCC, certificate checker                         | Selectively on central/high-risk kernels                   | State exact bounds/assumptions                    |
| M15 | Sandbox probe              | None, dry call, conformance suite, shadow endpoint, canary                             | Unknown contract/effect edges only                         | Probe must not create unauthorized effects        |
| M16 | Human expert oracle        | User approval, domain expert, operator, auditor                                        | Only for subjective/regulatory claims                      | Resolve recipient/role and record evidence        |
| M17 | `ProofDAG`                 | Flat pass list, causal graph, proof tree, shared-premise DAG                           | DAG of claim–evidence dependencies                         | Enables targeted invalidation                     |
| M18 | `WitnessCompiler`          | Logs only, evidence normalizer, proof certificate generator                            | Compile heterogeneous results to typed `WitnessGraph`      | Do not hide verifier-native data                  |
| M19 | Evidence aggregation       | Boolean AND, rules, Bayesian, evidence lattice, confidence interval                    | Rule/lattice based on claim class                          | Scores do not convert empirical evidence to proof |
| M20 | Counterexample store       | Discard, issue tracker, corpus, generalized no-good clause                             | Evidence-linked refutations with scope/TTL                 | Feeds CEGIS and negative retrieval                |
| M21 | Provenance model           | Ad hoc, W3C PROV, OpenLineage, in-toto, custom graph                                   | Small internal causal model with standard exports          | Provenance is about derivation, not just tracing  |
| M22 | Operational trace          | Logs, OpenTelemetry, event log, metrics                                                | OTel-correlated events                                     | Trace IDs link but do not prove claims            |
| M23 | Receipt graph              | Flat JSON, append-only events, causal Merkle DAG, ledger                               | Causal receipt DAG with content digests                    | Exact causal ancestry supports partial replay     |
| M24 | Receipt encoding           | JSON, canonical JSON, CBOR, protobuf, signed envelope                                  | Canonical JSON/CBOR plus typed schemas                     | Canonicalization precedes signing                 |
| M25 | Receipt signing            | None, COSE/JWS, threshold signature, hardware key                                      | Risk-tiered COSE-like signed envelope                      | Key management and role matter                    |
| M26 | Transparency               | Local log, Merkle tree, Rekor, SCITT, external auditor                                 | Optional transparency checkpoint for high-stakes events    | Transparency proves recording, not correctness    |
| M27 | Disclosure views           | Full internal, tenant-redacted, public, selective disclosure                           | Derived signed/redacted views referencing root             | Receipts may contain sensitive inputs             |
| M28 | Replayability class        | Exact, deterministic with seed, environment-rebuildable, live-dependent, nonreplayable | Explicit class and missing dependency report               | No universal exact-replay claim                   |
| M29 | Actual-output binding      | Expected output only, step output hashes, final artifact/effect IDs                    | Bind verification to exact produced artifacts/effects      | Prevent verify-one/return-another errors          |
| M30 | Verification receipt       | Pass flag, per-claim status, evidence bundle, machine proof                            | Claim, oracle, result, evidence, assumptions, versions     | Unknown/refuted are first-class statuses          |

Property-based, metamorphic, differential, mutation, formal, and human verification are not mutually exclusive. They cover different claim classes and failure modes. Proof-carrying code is a useful extreme: an untrusted producer supplies a certificate checked by a small trusted consumer, but only for properties encoded by the policy and proof system ([Necula's proof-carrying code thesis](https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~necula/Papers/thesis.pdf)). COSE Receipts and SCITT provide standards-grounded building blocks for signed receipts and transparent statements ([RFC 9942](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9942), [RFC 9943](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9943)).

## Plane N — lifecycle, invalidation, cache, learning, economics, and governance

| ID  | Responsibility                  | Alternatives                                                              | Recommended first default                                                      | Scale/risk note                                       |
|-----|---------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| N01 | Lifecycle state                 | One active flag, multidimensional axes, state machine                     | Separate availability, trust, freshness, verification, deprecation, revocation | Avoid impossible combined enums                       |
| N02 | Version/lineage                 | SemVer, content DAG, release channel, deployment history                  | Family/contract/artifact/deployment lineage                                    | “Latest” is not an identity                           |
| N03 | Revocation                      | Delete, tombstone, deny overlay, signed kill list, TUF-like metadata      | Immediate deny plus reverse-dependency invalidation                            | Must reach routes, packs, locks, caches, and runs     |
| N04 | Reverse-dependency index        | Full rebuild, direct refs, transitive closure, event-driven cone          | Direct edges plus on-demand transitive traversal                               | Change work proportional to affected cone             |
| N05 | Cache hierarchy                 | Handle, demand, query, candidate, route, compile, artifact, result        | Separate exact caches with explicit epochs                                     | Each level has different validity                     |
| N06 | Semantic cache                  | None, embedding nearest, semantic hash, verified equivalence class        | Conservative candidate-only reuse                                              | Never execute from similarity alone                   |
| N07 | Negative cache                  | Failure tuple, no-route core, incompatibility, revoked item, timeout      | Scoped authoritative no-goods and expiring transient failures                  | Precision is a key SLO                                |
| N08 | Route macro promotion           | Manual, frequency, savings, outcome evidence, bandit                      | Promote recurrent independently successful routes                              | Frequency alone can promote bad policy                |
| N09 | View materialization learning   | Fixed, popularity, uncertainty, marginal utility, active learning         | Allocate expensive views by expected value                                     | Central 50M cost control                              |
| N10 | Retriever learning              | Manual, LambdaMART, hard-negative mining, neural, bandit                  | Offline learning after reliable gold/outcomes                                  | Preserve frozen deterministic baselines               |
| N11 | Solver portfolio learning       | One solver, rules, feature-based selector, parallel race                  | Small frozen portfolio with instance features                                  | Account for timeouts/censoring                        |
| N12 | Selector/model routing learning | Rules, supervised, preferences, bandit, safe RL                           | Shadow cost-aware routing among admissible arms                                | Never explore unsafe routes                           |
| N13 | Propensity/exposure logging     | Winners only, candidate sets, action probabilities, counterfactual shadow | Log full eligible set and controller action probability                        | Required for unbiased offline evaluation              |
| N14 | Delayed outcome learning        | Immediate proxy, authoritative delayed event, user feedback, invoice      | Link all outcome epochs to decision                                            | Proxy optimization can diverge from true value        |
| N15 | Drift detection                 | Global score, demand/catalog/model/cost/policy/oracle-specific tests      | Separate drift monitors by subsystem                                           | Diagnose before retraining everything                 |
| N16 | Active learning queue           | Random labels, high uncertainty, high frequency, high expected savings    | Prioritize recurring costly ambiguities and conflicts                          | Human work should manufacture reusable structure      |
| N17 | Failure clustering              | Raw incidents, taxonomy, embeddings, causal graph, no-good mining         | Typed failures plus semantic clustering                                        | Converts repeated fallback into build backlog         |
| N18 | Outcome ledger                  | Success flag, per-claim results, utility, effects, adoption               | Independent outcomes linked to route and exposure                              | Distinguish selected, executed, accepted, adopted     |
| N19 | Token ledger                    | Provider tokens, cached input, reasoning, output, nested agents           | Stage/model/receipt-level token counts                                         | Token savings alone are insufficient                  |
| N20 | Cost ledger                     | Provider, local compute, storage, network, tool, verification, repair     | Failure-inclusive end-to-end cost                                              | Reconcile estimates to invoices where possible        |
| N21 | Unit economics                  | Per request, per successful execution, per accepted outcome, per user     | Quality-adjusted cost per independently accepted outcome                       | Include abstentions and failures                      |
| N22 | Budget policy                   | Static, tenant tier, risk adjusted, marginal utility, auction             | Request envelope with global ceilings and reserves                             | Controller cannot overspend stage by stage            |
| N23 | Governance                      | Owner approval, peer review, policy-as-code, separation of duties, board  | Risk-tiered review and immutable decisions                                     | Logical plane can use existing repo process initially |
| N24 | Audit/retention                 | Delete, configurable TTL, WORM, legal hold, reconstructible archive       | Retain minimal evidence/receipts by data class                                 | Storage and privacy requirements conflict             |
| N25 | Experiment assignment           | Ad hoc, deterministic hash, randomized blocks, interleaving, bandit       | Predeclared reproducible assignment                                            | Freeze candidate sets for selector experiments        |
| N26 | Release gates                   | Unit tests, benchmark thresholds, canary, shadow, confidence intervals    | Noninferiority quality plus positive savings and safety gates                  | No feature ships on token reduction alone             |
| N27 | Incident response               | Logs, kill switch, rollback, quarantine, repair workflow                  | Rapid deny overlay and dependency-cone report                                  | Revoke before full index rebuild                      |
| N28 | Data deletion                   | Physical delete, cryptographic erasure, tombstone, derived-data traversal | Provenance-driven deletion across views/caches                                 | Required for tenant/privacy obligations               |

End-to-end cost should be reported as:

``` text
C = ingress + retrieval + solver + selector
  + model_input + cached_input + reasoning + model_output
  + tools + execution + verification + retries/repair
  + reconciliation + storage/network amortization
```

The primary metric should be quality-adjusted unit cost:

``` text
total failure-inclusive cost / independently accepted outcomes
```

Token savings are a diagnostic metric under a predeclared noninferiority constraint on correctness, effect safety, and abstention-adjusted coverage.

## Plane O — harness, hooks, agents, skills, protocols, and integration

| ID  | Responsibility            | Alternatives                                                                | Recommended first default                                         | Scale/risk note                                             |
|-----|---------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| O01 | Host adapter              | Separate CLI/IDE/API/MCP, generic JSON, event envelope                      | Canonical invocation event after host boundary                    | Preserve host-native IDs and authority                      |
