| O02 | Project instruction files | None, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, repo config, signed policy bundle           | Versioned project instructions compiled into effective set        | Rules are inputs to PlanLock                                |
| O03 | Instruction registry      | One prompt, layered prompts, skill packs, tenant/project overlays           | Namespaced versioned instruction assets                           | Avoid copy-pasting huge prompt prefixes                     |
| O04 | Precedence resolver       | Closest wins, fixed hierarchy, merge/conflict, policy DAG                   | Deterministic hierarchy plus conflict error                       | Produce effective-instructions digest                       |
| O05 | Skill registry            | Prompts only, procedure+resources, executable package, capability card      | Skill metadata plus lazy resource resolution                      | Skills are reusable controller/compilation knowledge        |
| O06 | Hook/interceptor bus      | None, middleware, before/after/error/finally, event subscribers             | Ordered typed hooks with mutation/failure semantics               | Hooks are not automatically hard policy enforcement         |
| O07 | Tool registry             | Static functions, OpenAPI, MCP, generated wrappers, dynamic discovery       | Typed tool contracts with capability/effect metadata              | Tool schema itself is a primitive view                      |
| O08 | Tool schema cache         | None, prompt every call, schema digest cache, field paging                  | Cache and reference schemas by digest                             | Large tool lists are major token waste                      |
| O09 | Tool argument compiler    | Free JSON, templates, grammar, schema-constrained model, deterministic fill | Templates/exact fields then constrained unresolved slots          | Validate before dispatch                                    |
| O10 | Tool result normalizer    | Raw prose, typed envelope, artifact handle, event stream                    | Typed result/error/artifact/effect envelope                       | Preserve native payload by digest                           |
| O11 | Tool-result cache         | None, exact, semantic, provider cache, materialized view                    | Exact read-only results with freshness/invalidation               | Never cache unsafe effects as results                       |
| O12 | Tool-call coalescer       | No, identical in-flight dedup, batch, fanout aggregation                    | Coalesce pure/read calls by authorization scope                   | A cheap non-LLM token and latency win                       |
| O13 | MCP gateway               | Direct client, transparent proxy, protocol adapter, policy gateway          | Central typed gateway with host-local fast path                   | Keep MCP lifecycle/capability negotiation exact             |
| O14 | Protocol negotiator       | Hard-coded, semver, capabilities, schema downgrade                          | Explicit initialization/version/capability handshake              | Unsupported feature should fail visibly                     |
| O15 | Roots/workspace broker    | Current directory, static roots, snapshots, per-file capabilities           | Read-only scoped roots plus declared outputs                      | Prevent accidental cross-project access                     |
| O16 | Agent topology            | One agent, parent/child, actor model, blackboard, contract-net, peer A2A    | One agent plus deterministic parallel workers initially           | Add agents only for separable work                          |
| O17 | Agent context policy      | Full shared history, task packet, artifact refs, blackboard                 | Minimal typed task packet and immutable shared refs               | Duplicate context multiplies tokens                         |
| O18 | Agent ownership           | Shared writes, file locks, patch queue, task-owned artifacts                | Explicit task/file ownership and merge contract                   | Avoid conflicting speculative edits                         |
| O19 | Agent result contract     | Free prose, JSON, evidence bundle, patch, plan fragment                     | Typed deliverable plus claims/evidence/unknowns                   | Easier deterministic composition                            |
| O20 | Agent supervision         | LLM supervisor, workflow, state machine, budget controller                  | Deterministic lifecycle/budget; model only for semantic dispatch  | Agents should not perform trivial deterministic loops       |
| O21 | Clarification/elicitation | Error, free text, schema form, approval queue                               | Distinct `clarify`, `consent`, `authorize`, `review` actions      | Different legal and product semantics                       |
| O22 | Liveness/cancellation     | Blocking, deadlines, progress tokens, cooperative cancel, queue limits      | Uniform propagation through tools/agents/runtime                  | Receipt partial/indeterminate effects                       |
| O23 | Circuit breaker/fallback  | Blind retry, breaker, alternate tool, degraded mode, human                  | Error-class aware bounded fallback                                | Avoid retry storms                                          |
| O24 | Extension/plugin model    | Source code fork, plugins, skills, MCP servers, marketplace                 | Stable interfaces and signed/versioned packages                   | Admission applies to extensions too                         |
| O25 | Harness test kit          | Manual, recorded fixtures, fake servers, protocol conformance, chaos        | Deterministic protocol/tool fixtures plus failure injection       | Test hooks, cancellation, partial results, version mismatch |
| O26 | Harness observability     | Console logs, trace spans, structured controller decisions                  | One correlation tree across tools, agents, model calls, execution | Attribute cost and failure to exact arm                     |

Claude Code hooks demonstrate useful lifecycle interception points and several hook types, but documented hook behavior should not be confused with a cryptographic or kernel-level policy boundary ([Claude Code hooks](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks)). MCP provides standardized tool/resource interaction and explicit lifecycle/capability negotiation ([MCP specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18)). The OpenAI Agents SDK illustrates a compact set of agent primitives—agents, handoffs, guardrails, sessions, tracing, and human-in-the-loop—that can serve as one harness adapter, not as Taedri's universal internal semantics ([OpenAI Agents SDK](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/)).

## Plane P — product surfaces, federation, marketplace, and human operations

| ID  | Responsibility            | Alternatives                                                                | Recommended first default                                   | Scale/risk note                                    |
|-----|---------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| P01 | Stable control API        | Internal calls, REST, gRPC, MCP, event protocol                             | Typed control API independent of UI                         | Carries handles and receipts                       |
| P02 | SDKs                      | None, generated clients, language-native packages                           | Generate only for active ecosystems                         | Preserve exact schemas and errors                  |
| P03 | CLI                       | Thin API client, local engine, scripting DSL                                | Debuggable thin client with receipt export                  | Useful first operator surface                      |
| P04 | IDE extension             | Search palette, inline suggestions, route debugger, auto execution          | Handles and dry-run first                                   | Host context can eliminate queries                 |
| P05 | Registry/search UI        | Keyword search, faceted explorer, graph browser, marketplace                | Faceted evidence-first catalog                              | Do not expose unverified popularity as trust       |
| P06 | Route debugger            | Text trace, graph, proof DAG, cost waterfall, counterfactuals               | Request-local graph + blockers + receipts                   | Essential for architecture learning                |
| P07 | Pack builder              | YAML, visual builder, record successful run, synthesis                      | Promote a verified run to parameterized pack                | Retain original route/proof lineage                |
| P08 | Primitive foundry UI      | Upload, wrap API, mine repository, generate adapter, test lab               | Guided contract/evidence onboarding                         | Quarantine until verified                          |
| P09 | Receipt explorer          | Raw JSON, timeline, provenance graph, claim matrix                          | Claim/effect/cost views from one ledger                     | Redaction views by audience                        |
| P10 | Benchmark laboratory      | Offline scripts, dashboard, experiment registry, replay service             | Frozen cases, arms, gates, confidence intervals             | Central to self-optimization claims                |
| P11 | Policy console            | Config file, OPA editor, approval workflow, simulation                      | Versioned policy diff and impact preview                    | Show affected routes/tenants before change         |
| P12 | Lifecycle console         | Registry edit, revocation, quarantine, dependency cone                      | Immediate kill plus staged remediation                      | High operational priority                          |
| P13 | Cost/token dashboard      | Provider only, full unit economics, per-arm Pareto views                    | Accepted-outcome cost and avoided calls                     | Avoid vanity token totals                          |
| P14 | Federated hub             | Central copy, metasearch, source agents, hybrid descriptor cache            | Compact central descriptors + lazy native resolution        | Source authorization/freshness remains visible     |
| P15 | Marketplace               | Flat listing, curated packs, trust tiers, paid primitives, private catalogs | Start curated/private with evidence and lifecycle           | Economic incentives can degrade metadata quality   |
| P16 | Recommendation/reputation | Stars, downloads, verified outcomes, environment-specific score             | Evidence/scenario-conditioned reliability                   | Popularity is not applicability                    |
| P17 | Human review queue        | General inbox, claim-specific reviewers, risk-based routing                 | Separate domain quality, safety, legal, and effect approval | One approver cannot certify every claim            |
| P18 | Failure/gap backlog       | Manual tickets, automatic clusters, ROI-ranked foundry queue                | Rank repeated gaps by avoided future cost and user value    | Turns fallback spend into product roadmap          |
| P19 | Standards/export layer    | Proprietary only, OpenAPI/MCP/OCI/SPDX/PROV/OTel exporters                  | Native preservation plus selected standard boundaries       | Avoid standards theater inside hot path            |
| P20 | Deployment modes          | Local single user, team server, edge, managed cloud, federated              | Modular monolith first; explicit security profiles          | Same logical contracts, different trust boundaries |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 5. Recommended physical collapse

The atlas contains hundreds of logical responsibilities. The first implementation should collapse them into roughly eight hot-path modules and four offline/control-plane modules.

## Hot path

1.  **Ingress and context kernel** — request/actor/tenant identity, context references, demand projection, budgets, policy snapshot, risk class, and acceptance claims.
2.  **Catalog and evidence kernel** — identity, aliases, contract facets, lifecycle, evidence, immutable source refs, feature-view registry, and catalog epochs.
3.  **Retrieval broker** — exact/history/pack caches, fielded lexical search, typed filters, optional semantic channels, fusion, adaptive widening, and search receipts.
4.  **Route compiler** — request-local graph, compatibility witnesses, route solver portfolio, route normal form, `PathSkyline`, compact handles, and no-route certificates.
5.  **Controller and selector** — action choice, progressive disclosure, deterministic/non-generative/SLM/hosted arms, calibration, clarification, and budget enforcement.
6.  **Admission and artifact resolver** — static checks, policy, `AdmissionGrant`, `PlanLock`, closure construction, supply-chain validation, and backend lowering.
7.  **Runtime and effect manager** — isolation, identity/secrets, scheduling, retries, idempotency, external-effect state, compensation, reconciliation, and output binding.
8.  **Verifier and receipt ledger** — claims/oracles, verification portfolio, `ProofDAG`, provenance, causal receipts, cost/usage, and outcome records.

## Offline/control plane

9.  **Primitive foundry** — acquisition, extraction, probing, onboarding, adapters, packs, and gap mining.
10. **Index and materialization factory** — channel generation, index builds, tiering, compaction, snapshots, and invalidation.
11. **Learning and benchmark laboratory** — frozen evaluation, shadow arms, calibration, drift, safe policy learning, and release gates.
12. **Governance and operations** — lifecycle, revocation, policy, audit/retention, incidents, deletion, and administrative/product surfaces.

This is still a modular monolith until measured load, security isolation, failure containment, or team ownership makes a split valuable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 6. The full intelligence-removal ladder

The cheapest valid path is chosen per request. “Local” does not automatically mean cheap: local embeddings, rerankers, and SLMs consume latency, energy, memory, and operations. Every stage needs a measured marginal value.

| Tier | Action                                                 |   Model tokens | What must be true to stop                                            | Asset manufactured for the future                            |
|------|--------------------------------------------------------|---------------:|----------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| 0    | Host-supplied exact handle                             |              0 | Handle current, authorized, demand-compatible                        | Handle telemetry and validity rule                           |
| 1    | Exact demand/result replay                             |              0 | Canonical equivalence and all validity keys pass                     | Revalidated exact case                                       |
| 2    | Parameterized `SolutionPack`                           |              0 | Applicability predicates and bindings pass                           | Better pack coverage statistics                              |
| 3    | Queryless event/symbol/error trigger                   |              0 | Deterministic trigger maps to unique safe action                     | Trigger rule                                                 |
| 4    | Rule/grammar intent and slots                          |              0 | Demand fields complete and unambiguous                               | New template coverage                                        |
| 5    | Query-plan prototype retrieval                         |              0 | Prototype applicability and conditionals pass                        | Successful prototype/example                                 |
| 6    | Exact aliases, type bitmaps, fielded lexical retrieval |     0 provider | Route coverage reaches target                                        | Better aliases/field weights                                 |
| 7    | Cached route/subgraph plus typed repair                |     0 provider | Recompiled repaired route is admissible                              | New macro or compatibility witness                           |
| 8    | Deterministic route solving and selector               |     0 provider | One nondominated admissible route or deterministic policy winner     | Route/no-good proof                                          |
| 9    | Non-generative local classifier/ranker                 |     0 provider | Calibrated selective decision meets risk target                      | Labeled contrasts and hard negatives                         |
| 10   | Local embeddings/late interaction                      |     0 provider | Incremental route recall justifies compute and calibrated stop       | Channel attribution                                          |
| 11   | Local constrained SLM                                  |     0 provider | It fills only unresolved typed fields or chooses known handles       | Validated parse/query/decision prototype                     |
| 12   | Deterministic probes/tools                             |  Usually 0 LLM | A fresh fact collapses ambiguity                                     | Evidence, environment fact, or test                          |
| 13   | Cheap hosted general model                             |        Bounded | Small unresolved delta resolved under privacy policy                 | Distillable structured decision                              |
| 14   | Strong hosted model                                    | Bounded higher | High-value residual ambiguity resolved and checked                   | New rule, contrast, adapter specification, or pack candidate |
| 15   | Frontier synthesis/agent portfolio                     |        Highest | Novel query/adapter/plan passes independent compile and verification | Foundry candidate plus tests/evidence                        |
| 16   | Human clarification/review                             |     Human cost | Missing preference/authority/subjective judgment supplied            | Durable field, policy, or benchmark label                    |
| 17   | Safe abstention/no-route certificate                   |        Minimal | No action has positive risk-adjusted value                           | Gap/no-good/clarification backlog item                       |

Two non-obvious consequences:

- Tools and probes can appear before or after local models; ordering is chosen by VOI, not an ideology that “models precede tools.”
- A later tier should receive only unresolved clauses, route deltas, and named evidence handles. It should not reread the whole corpus or conversation merely because it is a stronger model.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 7. Revised first vertical slice

The original slice is preserved as an experiment, but each bundle is made explicit and deletable.

## 7.1 Request and demand

Build one immutable `RequestEnvelope` containing:

- source/actor/tenant/session identities;
- original prompt and turn references;
- typed context references with role, authority, trust, freshness, and scope;
- `DemandProjection` with inputs, outputs, effects, hard constraints, preferences, and uncertainty;
- at least one `AcceptanceClaim`/oracle where execution occurs;
- risk/privacy class and budget envelope; and
- canonical exact fingerprint plus conservative semantic fingerprints.

Keep `ContextManifest` and `DemandIR` as logical projections. Split their storage/services only after independent consumers justify it.

## 7.2 Primitive and catalog

Build:

- `CapabilityFamilyId`, `ImplementationId`, native-source ID, contract digest, artifact digest, and deployment ID;
- `ActionSpec`, `PortContract`, effect/state/failure/resource facets;
- `AlignmentAssertion`, `AdapterCard`, evidence record, and orthogonal lifecycle axes;
- 12–32 cheap/evidence-rich core channels, not hundreds of eager generated descriptions;
- exact aliases, typed bitmap filters, fielded lexical indexes, sparse compatibility witnesses, and a route-macro index; and
- immutable catalog epochs with base-plus-delta updates and immediate revocation overlays.

The verified `PrimitiveCard` becomes one compact presentation/search projection.

## 7.3 Retrieval and graph

Build a typed `QueryPlan` that first tries:

1.  direct handle;
2.  exact/history/pack/prototype caches;
3.  exact aliases and hard field filters;
4.  fielded BM25/trigram;
5.  typed candidate closure and route-macro lookup;
6.  one selected dense channel as an experimental arm;
7.  a non-generative local reranker; and
8.  corrective widening only when a route-coverage certificate says the set is insufficient.

Project a request-local port hypergraph, use forward, backward, and bidirectional typed solver arms, preserve AND requirements and adapters, emit a small `PathSkyline`, and independently recheck every route witness. Do not materialize global pairwise edges.

## 7.4 Presentation and selection

Encode routes with `PlanCodec` and opaque handles. Present the invariant safety core once, a shared route skeleton once, and only decision-changing primitive/edge deltas. Run controlled experiments at:

- `k = 0/1/2/4/8/16` route alternatives;
- 0, only conditional, only decision-changing, and all route-edge exposures;
- 16/64/256/1024-token route-view budgets;
- full cards versus shared-skeleton-plus-delta;
- no selector, deterministic, non-generative ranker, local SLM, cheap hosted, and strong hosted selectors; and
- fixed versus model-requested detail paging.

The production controller later selects the smallest evidence set that meets calibrated risk/coverage and positive marginal VOI.

## 7.5 Compile, execute, and prove

After selection:

- independently compile types, effects, authority, protocols, resources, and oracle completeness;
- create separate demand, candidate, plan, artifact, and effect admission records;
- seal `PlanLock` and compute artifact closure;
- resolve bodies by digest only after the lock;
- execute within the required isolation/durability profile;
- bind every actual output and external effect;
- run claim-specific independent oracles;
- reconcile external effects; and
- emit a causal receipt graph with exact token, tool, compute, execution, verification, and outcome accounting.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 8. Experiment program

## 8.1 Factorial core

Do not vary everything in one giant factorial. Use staged blocked experiments so interactions remain interpretable.

| Experiment family | Arms                                                                  | Primary estimand                                    | Hold fixed                               |
|-------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| Query formation   | raw prompt; rules; template; prototype; local SLM; hosted delta       | Complete-route recall per total cost                | Index snapshot, solver, candidate budget |
| Retrieval         | exact; BM25; trigram; learned sparse; dense; hybrid; route index      | Eligible complete-route recall@budget               | Query plan, corpus, hard filters         |
| Representation    | lexical facts; 3/8/16/32 views; adaptive views; generated views       | Marginal recall/selection gain per byte and compute | Retriever family and index parameters    |
| ANN               | flat; HNSW; IVF-PQ; ScaNN; DiskANN where feasible                     | Recall/latency/RAM/disk/churn frontier              | Same embeddings and filters              |
| Fusion            | union; RRF; calibrated; LambdaMART; Pareto/set-cover                  | Route coverage and diversity regret                 | Per-channel candidates                   |
| Solver            | forward; backward; bidirectional; A\*; CP-SAT/SMT; portfolio          | Sound route found per CPU/latency                   | Same candidate closure                   |
| Route count       | 0/1/2/4/8/16                                                          | Selector accuracy, abstention, prompt tokens        | Route ordering and view budget           |
| Card detail       | 16/64/256/1024 tokens; field paging                                   | Decision loss per token                             | Candidate routes and selector            |
| Edge detail       | none; blockers; decisive; all                                         | Invalid-route choice and token cost                 | Cards and routes                         |
| Selector          | none; rules; LTR; cross-encoder; local SLM; hosted small; strong      | Conditional selection accuracy and cost             | Frozen route set                         |
| Controller        | fixed waterfall; rule DAG; VOI; calibrated early exit; learned shadow | Accepted-outcome cost and coverage                  | Safe action set and hard gates           |
| Verification      | minimum oracle; risk cascade; full portfolio; random audit            | Undetected failure and proof cost                   | Executions and claims                    |

## 8.2 Required catalog-scale ladder

Run frozen gold and temporal test sets at:

``` text
100K → 1M → 5M → 20M → 50M primitives
```

At every scale measure:

- natural growth separately from synthetic distractor inflation;
- exact duplicates, near duplicates, forks, renamed clones, and behaviorally similar but incompatible primitives;
- cold and warm exact/history/route caches;
- static, filtered, out-of-distribution, and streaming insert/delete workloads;
- tenant/policy filtering before and after index lookup;
- single-hop primitive recall, required-capability recall, connector recall, complete-route recall, minimal-route recall, and independently verified execution success;
- P50/P95/P99 latency, QPS, build time, delta-refresh lag, RAM, disk, network, and compute/energy cost;
- query, retrieval, card, selector, tool, execution, verifier, retry, and agent tokens separately;
- negative-cache precision and false permanent blockage;
- identity merge precision and split recall, with a much larger penalty for false merges;
- route regret versus the best verified admissible route in the frozen pool;
- revocation propagation time and stale-route escape rate;
- partial tool/index/model outage and degraded-mode behavior; and
- adversarial descriptions, prompt-bearing artifacts, poisoned history, and misleading popularity.

## 8.3 Primary metrics

The scorecard needs conditional and end-to-end metrics:

1.  demand parse completeness and blocker accuracy;
2.  candidate eligibility precision after authorization/policy;
3.  complete-route recall before selection;
4.  solver soundness and stated bounded completeness;
5.  selector accuracy conditional on the correct route being present;
6.  coverage–risk curve including abstentions;
7.  independently verified end-to-end acceptance;
8.  incorrect external effect versus safe abstention;
9.  reconciled-effect rate and indeterminate-effect rate;
10. closure/materialization and revoked-artifact escape rates;
11. cost and latency per accepted outcome; and
12. lower confidence bound on savings under a predeclared noninferiority margin.

## 8.4 Promotion gates

A new arm is promoted only if:

- it does not reduce independently verified acceptance beyond the declared noninferiority margin;
- it does not increase unauthorized or incorrect effects;
- its savings lower confidence bound is positive on failure-inclusive cost;
- its worst-group/task-family performance meets the risk target;
- route recall and calibration remain valid under temporal/OOD splits;
- every stop/escalation is reproducible from receipts; and
- it has an immediate rollback/revocation path.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 9. Concrete build backlog

## Wave 0 — define claims and build the measuring instrument

- **W0-01** Freeze task-family scope, risk tiers, acceptance claims, and noninferiority margins.
- **W0-02** Define stage-level cost, token, latency, exposure, and outcome events.
- **W0-03** Build a causal receipt/event schema and deterministic replay harness.
- **W0-04** Create gold demands, admissible routes, deliberate no-route cases, and independent oracles.
- **W0-05** Build temporal and out-of-distribution splits; prevent sibling/duplicate leakage.
- **W0-06** Add randomized-block experiment assignment and frozen candidate-set support.
- **W0-07** Implement a baseline: strong-model-from-full-context, measured end to end.
- **W0-08** Implement a no-model exact/direct-handle baseline.
- **W0-09** Create dashboards for route recall, verification, cost, latency, and abstention.
- **W0-10** Establish 100K/1M fixtures and a credible path to 5M–50M without synthetic-only claims.

**Exit:** every architectural claim maps to an estimand and an independent outcome.

## Wave 1 — identity, evidence, request, and invalidation spine

- **W1-01** Implement canonical JSON/typed digests for request, demand, contracts, routes, and receipts.
- **W1-02** Add `CapabilityFamilyId`, `ImplementationId`, contract/artifact/deployment identities, aliases, and lineage.
- **W1-03** Build `RequestEnvelope`, typed context refs, `DemandProjection`, assumptions, and acceptance claims.
- **W1-04** Implement instruction roles, trust/taint, authority, precedence, and conflict records.
- **W1-05** Split primitive identity, native source, contract facets, views, evidence, and lifecycle tables.
- **W1-06** Add content-addressed raw/evidence storage and immutable catalog epochs.
- **W1-07** Implement reverse-dependency invalidation and emergency revocation overlays.
- **W1-08** Create orthogonal status axes for declared/inferred/observed/verified/refuted and active/deprecated/quarantined/revoked.
- **W1-09** Preserve native records and emit a projection loss report.
- **W1-10** Build scoped exact and negative-cache validity keys.

**Exit:** any source or policy change produces a bounded dependency-cone report; no mutable name is mistaken for artifact identity.

## Wave 2 — deterministic catalog and retrieval baseline

- **W2-01** Build exact handle, alias, symbol, package-coordinate, and standard indexes.
- **W2-02** Build tenant/policy/type/license/runtime bitmap filters.
- **W2-03** Build separate fielded lexical indexes for names, contracts, docs, examples, tests, and errors.
- **W2-04** Add identifier-aware tokenization and trigram fallback.
- **W2-05** Implement demand/route/pack/query-prototype exact history.
- **W2-06** Define a typed `QueryPlan` with channel/shard/budget/stop fields.
- **W2-07** Add deterministic clauses, keyphrases, entity linking, and template conditional filling.
- **W2-08** Implement stratified union, hard rechecks, RRF baseline, and per-capability quotas.
- **W2-09** Add explicit no-match/unknown/denied/partial result statuses and full-scan guard.
- **W2-10** Emit exact per-stage search receipts.
- **W2-11** Measure field/channel attribution and candidate/connector recall.
- **W2-12** Add one dense ANN channel and one non-generative reranker strictly as ablation arms.

**Exit:** end-to-end retrieval benchmarks run without any generative query drafting; provider token use is zero through candidate generation.

## Wave 3 — contracts, compatibility witnesses, and request-local routing

- **W3-01** Implement `ActionSpec`, `PortContract`, effects, state, failure, idempotency, compensation, resource, and environment facets.
- **W3-02** Implement `AlignmentAssertion` returning compatible/incompatible/conditional plus witness.
- **W3-03** Build `AdapterCard`; treat adapters as normal governed primitives.
- **W3-04** Add exact identity, structural subtype, cardinality, unit, effect, policy, and environment compatibility rules.
- **W3-05** Store sparse positive proof and negative refutation caches with exact scope and TTL.
- **W3-06** Build type/capability reachability bitmaps and connector expansion.
- **W3-07** Generate request-local port hypergraphs only after retrieval.
- **W3-08** Implement forward, backward, and bidirectional solver arms.
- **W3-09** Preserve AND/hyperedge requirements, conditional/open edges, and missing-capability reports.
- **W3-10** Implement route normal form, stable digest, `LemmaGraph`, `PremiseGraph`, and independent route checker.
- **W3-11** Add scalar, lexicographic, and Pareto/`PathSkyline` objectives with route/failure-domain diversity.
- **W3-12** Emit route proof summaries and minimal no-route certificates.

**Exit:** all returned routes independently recheck; claims about completeness explicitly name candidate closure and solver bounds.

## Wave 4 — compact presentation and selector/controller experiments

- **W4-01** Implement `PrimitiveFrame`, `PrimitiveCodebook`, and 16/64/256/1024-token view levels.
- **W4-02** Implement `PlanCodec` route handles and shared-skeleton-plus-delta presentation.
- **W4-03** Define invariant safety core fields that no detail tier may hide.
- **W4-04** Build the `k=0/1/2/4/8/16` route exposure harness.
- **W4-05** Build none/conditional/decisive/all edge exposure arms.
- **W4-06** Implement no-selector, deterministic, LambdaMART/cross-encoder, local SLM, cheap hosted, and strong hosted arms.
- **W4-07** Grammar-constrain every generative decision to known handles/actions.
- **W4-08** Implement model-requested field/evidence paging under a disclosure budget.
- **W4-09** Calibrate route coverage, selector risk, and explicit abstention.
- **W4-10** Add one-question active clarification and deterministic probe actions.
- **W4-11** Build the finite controller action API and VOI receipt.
- **W4-12** Run sampled counterfactual later tiers to audit early stops.

**Exit:** the smallest evidence/card/route configuration that preserves decision quality is known per task family; stronger arms see only unresolved deltas.

## Wave 5 — compilation, admission, and locked materialization

- **W5-01** Implement tiny PlanAST/GraphIR kernel and native dialect attachments.
- **W5-02** Add canonicalization, schema migration, and independent static type/effect/policy checks.
- **W5-03** Add separate demand, candidate, plan, artifact, and effect admission decisions.
- **W5-04** Implement signed/scoped `AdmissionGrant`.
- **W5-05** Implement full `PlanLock`, typed dynamic slots, validity window, and revalidation triggers.
- **W5-06** Compute fixed-point `ClosureManifest` including code, data, models, prompts, policies, and verifier assets.
- **W5-07** Resolve immutable artifacts by digest and verify trust/license/vulnerability evidence by risk tier.
- **W5-08** Bind runtime/isolation/backend constraints and compile to one real executor.
- **W5-09** Add non-destructive preflight for closure, credentials, quota, and endpoint schema.
- **W5-10** Implement action keys and exact compilation/artifact caching.

**Exit:** no implementation body loads before plan lock; a locked plan either materializes exactly or fails with an actionable closure report.

## Wave 6 — runtime, effects, independent proof, and exact economics

- **W6-01** Implement a deterministic local runtime with explicit input/output artifacts.
- **W6-02** Add isolation profiles, workload identity, secret broker, filesystem roots, and network allowlists.
- **W6-03** Add deadlines, cancellation, resource caps, retries, and error-class semantics.
- **W6-04** Implement effect identities, idempotency registry, and fencing where shared resources exist.
- **W6-05** Add outbox/inbox or durable workflow semantics for cross-system transitions.
- **W6-06** Implement effect state machine, authoritative observation, reconciliation, and indeterminate outcomes.
- **W6-07** Add compensation/manual-repair branches.
- **W6-08** Build claim/oracle registry and schema/property/metamorphic/differential verifier adapters.
- **W6-09** Implement `ProofDAG`, `WitnessCompiler`, counterexample store, and actual-output binding.
- **W6-10** Emit canonical causal receipts and optional signed/transparency views.
- **W6-11** Reconcile estimated tokens/costs to provider usage and invoices.
- **W6-12** Report cost per independently accepted outcome with confidence intervals.

**Exit:** every success is independently checkable and every external effect reaches a reconciled or explicit indeterminate/manual-repair state.

## Wave 7 — scale, federation, and safe self-optimization

- **W7-01** Run 1M/5M/20M/50M natural-growth and distractor-scale benchmarks.
- **W7-02** Compare HNSW/IVF-PQ/ScaNN/DiskANN and hot/warm/cold representation tiers.
- **W7-03** Add base-plus-delta indexes, CDC, tombstones, and high-churn tests.
- **W7-04** Add federated search capability negotiation, predicate pushdown, partial-failure receipts, and watermarks.
- **W7-05** Mine route macros, query prototypes, missing adapters, and frequent ambiguity clusters.
- **W7-06** Allocate expensive representations through measured marginal value.
- **W7-07** Train offline retriever/solver/selector routers only from independently linked outcomes.
- **W7-08** Log propensities and evaluate shadow policies counterfactually.
- **W7-09** Permit bounded randomized exploration only among already admissible near-ties.
- **W7-10** Add subsystem-specific drift monitors and automatic rollback gates.

**Exit:** scale claims are supported at target cardinality and every learned policy can fall back to a frozen deterministic safe baseline.

# 10. High-leverage additional ideation

1.  **Demand microcode.** Compile common demand clauses into tiny reusable opcodes (`must_local`, `output:pdf`, `no_network`, `verify:reconcile`) so repeated language never reaches a model.
2.  **Semantic ABI linker.** Treat compact primitive facets as object-file symbol tables: first link names/types/effects, then resolve bodies after lock.
3.  **Proof-directed retrieval.** Search not only for a route, but for one whose required claims have available independent oracles.
4.  **Verifier-aware route cost.** Include verification cost and oracle availability during route selection, not after selection.
5.  **Failure-domain coloring.** Color primitives, adapters, models, providers, and verifiers by shared failure dependencies; require diversity for high-risk routes.
6.  **Counterexample-indexed retrieval.** When a route fails, index the minimized counterexample against the responsible contract region so similar future demands avoid it.
7.  **Negative-space descriptions.** Generate evidence-backed “not for X / fails when Y / unlike Z” views, often more discriminative than another positive summary.
8.  **Differentiating-predicate index.** Precompute which exact fields separate candidates within common compatibility cells; ask for or retrieve those fields first.
9.  **Ambiguity compilation.** Convert unresolved interpretation branches into a minimal boolean decision diagram; query only variables that can change the winning route.
10. **Queryless contract cells.** Cache eligible regions keyed by typed input/output/effect/environment constraints rather than natural language.
11. **Route quotienting.** Collapse implementations and subgraphs that are observationally equivalent for the active demand; expose one representative plus deltas.
12. **Proof quotienting.** Share common premises across millions of compatibility assertions through a `PremiseGraph` instead of copying evidence.
13. **Description virtual memory.** Treat expensive generated views like virtual pages: materialize on fault, retain by measured reuse, evict safely because source evidence persists.
14. **Information bottleneck cards.** Learn a minimal sufficient selector projection under hard safety-field retention, then verify with ablation and adversarial tests.
15. **Route sketches.** Store compact type/effect/topology sketches to block route candidates before retrieving full macro records.
16. **Graph grammar packs.** Represent recurring subgraphs as typed grammar productions; route solving becomes constrained parsing over reusable motifs.
17. **Adapter bounty market.** Rank repeated missing edges by future avoided cost and let humans/foundry systems submit verified adapters.
18. **No-good generalization ladder.** Generalize a failed exact route only as far as an independent solver/proof permits; retain counterexamples against overgeneralization.
19. **Calibration by difficulty cell.** Calibrate stops separately by demand novelty, route length, effect risk, catalog density, and evidence completeness.
20. **Strong-model tax ledger.** Every strong-model call must identify which missing deterministic asset forced it; aggregate those causes into the backlog.
21. **Prompt-prefix CAS.** Hash effective instructions, schemas, and repeated context; use provider/local prefix caching where available and send deltas where protocols permit.
22. **Schema handles as tools.** Give models a small tool to request a tool/primitive schema by digest rather than injecting thousands of schemas into every prompt.
23. **Argument patching.** Reuse a validated prior tool call AST and ask a model, when necessary, to emit only a typed patch for changed fields.
24. **Result-shape routing.** Route tool outputs directly into compatible primitive ports by schemas and effect receipts; avoid restating results in natural language.
25. **Blackboard-to-ledger commit.** Agents may post hypotheses cheaply, but only a deterministic commit operation can promote them to authoritative evidence.
26. **Speculative compile, not speculative effect.** Parallelize compilation/dry verification for diverse routes while deferring all side effects until one lock wins.
27. **Canary primitive invocation.** For scalable/stateless operations, test a small representative input before full execution and reuse the behavioral evidence.
28. **Reconciliation primitive library.** Treat authoritative status checks and ledger comparisons as reusable primitives paired with effectful actions.
29. **Uncertainty-preserving compiler.** Allow explicit open slots/edges through retrieval and presentation, but make admission fail until each is bound or waived by policy.
30. **Plan leases.** Short-lived locks for volatile catalogs, prices, credentials, or policy; revalidate only changed predicates at renewal.
31. **Outcome-weighted reputation.** Score implementations by environment- and demand-conditioned verified outcomes, never global popularity alone.
32. **Temporal holdout marketplace ranking.** Validate recommendation changes on future catalog epochs to avoid memorizing current winners.
33. **Receipt-driven billing.** Bill or budget by independently accepted outcome and verified effect rather than raw model calls, aligning incentives with the architecture.
34. **Policy impact compiler.** Before a policy change, traverse reverse dependencies to show which packs, locks, users, and future demands become invalid.
35. **Privacy-aware channel routing.** Keep exact, lexical, type, graph, and local embedding branches available even when hosted semantic branches are prohibited.
36. **Evidence freshness auctions.** Spend revalidation budget on high-centrality, high-risk, high-use claims whose evidence is closest to expiry.
37. **Catalog entropy monitor.** Detect regions where aliases, duplicate implementations, conflicting claims, or missing fields cause retrieval branching; target cleanup there.
38. **Centrality-aware formal methods.** Apply expensive proofs to small kernels, adapters, and packs that sit on many routes, maximizing assurance amortization.
39. **Route regret debugger.** For failed or costly runs, compute the best admissible counterfactual route from the frozen candidate pool and attribute regret to retrieval, solver, selector, runtime, or oracle.
40. **Safe capability foundry loop.** `no route → minimal missing contract → adapter/new primitive candidate → sandbox tests → evidence → quarantine → admission → new route macro`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 11. What not to build yet

- A universal ontology covering every primitive domain.
- A universal super-IR that claims lossless OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, WIT, MCP, workflow, stream, agent, and transactional semantics.
- A global all-pairs compatibility or embedding-similarity graph.
- Hundreds of eager model-generated views for every primitive.
- A generative agent in every deterministic stage.
- Unbounded online reinforcement learning over execution decisions.
- A single scalar “verified,” “trust,” “quality,” or “compatibility” score.
- A selector benchmark that changes candidate sets across arms.
- A token-savings claim that excludes local compute, retries, verification, failures, or abstentions.
- Cryptographic receipts that sign estimates but fail to bind actual outputs and external effects.
- A marketplace before revocation, provenance, evidence quality, and lifecycle semantics work.
- Dozens of independently deployed services before the modular monolith proves actual scaling boundaries.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 12. The strongest revised thesis

Taedri is not primarily an LLM query generator. It is a **semantic linker, cost-based planner, evidence compiler, and effect-safe runtime over opaque capabilities**.

Its unit of intelligence reduction is not a shorter prompt. It is a reusable asset:

- a canonical demand clause;
- exact handle;
- typed query prototype;
- feature view;
- compatibility witness;
- refutation/no-good;
- adapter;
- route macro;
- compact `PlanCodec` recipe;
- acceptance oracle;
- `PlanLock`;
- proof witness; or
- reconciled outcome.

The ideal long-run behavior is:

> The common path compiles locally from demand atoms to a previously proved pack or a newly solved typed route with zero provider tokens. Approximate retrieval only nominates candidates. Models see compact handles, invariant safety facts, and decision-changing deltas. Strong models are reserved for the measured unresolved tail, and every successful fallback is distilled into evidence-linked deterministic structure. Bodies load only after admission, real effects are reconciled, and every claim, cost, artifact, and outcome is bound into an exact receipt.

That design can reduce token spend substantially, but the defensible claim is stronger and narrower than “we use fewer tokens”: **lower failure-inclusive cost per independently accepted outcome without inferior quality or unsafe effects**.

## Bottom line

The next valuable experiment is no longer “does a local model draft a cheaper query?” It is:

> Across a frozen demand and catalog epoch, what is the cheapest controller action sequence that preserves complete-route recall, independently verified acceptance, authorization, and effect safety—and which expensive actions can be converted into exact reusable assets after one successful use?

Build the exact/evidence/contract spine first, make every later mechanism an arm, and promote only what lowers failure-inclusive accepted-outcome cost under scale, temporal, and adversarial testing.

# Taedri master plan: deep-research audit and executable build blueprint

> **ANNEX STATUS — HISTORICAL AUDIT AND TARGET BUILD BLUEPRINT.** Its verdicts and
> proposed program remain useful, but source-era “current” claims do not supersede Part
> 0 or establish launch readiness.

**Audit date:** 2026-07-15
**Source audited:** `Pasted text(85).txt`, 1,387 lines
**Scope:** product thesis, evidence boundaries, value economics, 12-stage maturity pipeline, 22 component choices, 38-step prompt-to-proof flow, progressive disclosure, graph proof, 30 benchmark proposals, 170 backlog items, operating metrics, and stop rules.

## Executive verdict

The core thesis is worth building: a system that finds an authorized, contract-compatible, evidence-backed solution unit; keeps its body out of selector context; materializes it deterministically; executes it with least authority; verifies the actual result; and reuses an immutable successful binding can displace generation, integration, review, and maintenance work. The document is strongest when it treats token savings as only one value dimension and requires claim-specific evidence.

It is not yet an executable operating plan. It mixes sound invariants with unproved empirical claims, treats a provider-specific output-limit tactic as a universal rule, conflates several independent notions of status, proposes an editable linear trace as if it were tamper-evident proof, puts replay before the demand contract it needs, filters authorization too late, and labels 71 of 170 tasks P0. Those defects can be fixed without discarding the product thesis.

The recommended product is initially much smaller than the logical architecture in the source: one controller process, one SQLite metadata database, one content-addressed artifact store, one provider adapter boundary, one least-authority execution profile, and one proof/evaluation harness. Keep the 15 logical planes as responsibility boundaries, not services. Prove one demand-backed multi-file SolutionPack and exact same-tenant replay before building distributed scheduling, recursive systems, hosted vector retrieval, or model-mediated composition.

### Decisions to make now

1.  **Replace “omit the cap to get provider maximum” with a provider/model/endpoint capability registry and a request-specific budget policy.** Anthropic's Messages API requires `max_tokens`; Google Vertex documents model-dependent defaults; and Amazon Bedrock initially reserves quota using `max_tokens`, so a maximum can reduce concurrency even though billing uses actual output. A cap hit makes the model attempt transport-incomplete/truncated and ineligible as evidence of provider-complete generation; the resulting artifact may still be accepted only through independent contract/oracle evidence. See [Anthropic Messages](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/api/messages), [Vertex `GenerationConfig`](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/reference/rest/v1beta1/GenerationConfig), [Amazon Bedrock token quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas-token-burndown.html), and [OpenAI reasoning and incomplete responses](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning).
2.  **Replace one overloaded `status` field with orthogonal lifecycle, evidence, deployment, adoption, and security/trust axes.** Verification is scoped to a claim, artifact, environment, policy, and time; deployment and adoption are not stronger kinds of verification.
3.  **Open the evidence trail immediately after cheap envelope/rate/auth checks, build the canonical demand contract before semantic replay, and enforce tenant/ACL scope inside retrieval.** A later authority filter remains defense in depth; it cannot undo existence or score side channels created by cross-tenant retrieval.
4.  **Use canonical event bytes, a causal Merkle-DAG of receipts, signatures, and signed checkpoints.** A `previous_trace_digest` chain does not faithfully represent parallel execution, and append-only JSONL or SQLite is not tamper-evident by itself. Map transparency checkpoints into a registered append-only verifiable-data-structure profile and use independent auditors/witnesses plus gossip or cross-logging when split-view detection matters. RFC 9942 standardizes COSE receipts for verifiable data structures, and RFC 9943 defines the SCITT transparency architecture. See [RFC 9942](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9942) and [RFC 9943](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9943).
5.  **Define compatibility as behavioral refinement, not prose similarity or universal exact equality.** Exact equality is a useful fast path; the authority rule must also cover schema language inclusion, units, cardinality, effects, state, security, failure, temporal/session behavior, and environment. Adapters require endpoint-bound proof.
6.  **Make “minimal disclosure” a proved safety projection plus an empirical selection optimization.** The compact view must preserve the set of valid topologies for its declared purpose. Selection quality is then measured with open-set/no-match tasks, risk–coverage, and field ablations. Titles and summaries are untrusted data and need prompt-injection controls.
7.  **Package evidence using existing standards instead of inventing one monolithic Taedri format.** Use OCI descriptors/layout for content-addressed artifacts; SPDX or CycloneDX for SBOM and licenses; in-toto/SLSA for provenance; Sigstore/COSE plus transparency receipts for signatures; TUF for secure update/rollback protection; W3C PROV/OpenLineage for lineage; and OpenTelemetry for operational traces.
8.  **Turn the 71 P0s into 18 blocker epics and six evidence-gated waves.** P0 should mean “the first truth-serving pilot is unsafe or uninterpretable without this,” not “important eventually.”
9.  **Run a paired, randomized, failure-inclusive benchmark with quality/security non-inferiority gates before any savings claim.** Report task-level paired effects and uncertainty, not only aggregate token percentages. Treat the current v7/v9 numbers as internal observations until raw receipt IDs, denominators, task mix, exact comparators, missingness, and confidence intervals are supplied.
10. **Use one demand-backed pack as the wedge.** The first credible proof is not a universal graph platform; it is exact reconstruction, isolated execution, independent verification, and repeat replay of one valuable multi-file outcome.

## Research method and evidence classification

Every source line is covered by the range ledger below. Propositions were classified as:

- **Keep:** directionally and operationally sound.
- **Revise:** sound intent but the invariant, sequencing, or evidence requirement is incomplete.
- **Reject:** unsafe or factually non-portable as written.
- **Unverified internal observation:** plausible, but this attachment does not include the referenced raw artifacts needed to reproduce it.
- **Add:** a missing control or build item revealed by external standards, failure analysis, or benchmark design.

External sources were selected primarily from official specifications, standards bodies, provider documentation, and primary research. The audit did not treat the document's v7/v9 percentages as externally verified facts because no underlying receipts or executable fixtures were attached.

## Critical red-team findings

| Severity | Finding                                                                      | Why it matters                                                                                                                  | Required fix                                                                                                                              |
|----------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Critical | Output maximum is modeled as omission everywhere                             | APIs differ; some require a value, some default differently, and a high maximum can reserve throughput quota                    | Provider/model/endpoint capability registry; contract-derived budget; record emitted field/value and finish state                         |
| Critical | Retrieval precedes an effective tenant boundary                              | Later filtering can leak existence through candidates, ranks, latency, caches, or counts                                        | Apply authorization and tenant overlay in the query/index plan; add existence-side-channel tests                                          |
| Critical | Linear digest chain is treated as immutable graph proof                      | Parallel events have multiple causal parents; local append-only files remain editable                                           | Canonical parent-linked event DAG, signatures, checkpoints, inclusion/consistency proofs, separate evidence vault                         |
| Critical | “No duplicate paid calls” is promised                                        | A provider may complete and charge after the caller loses the response; exactly-once external effects are generally unavailable | At-least-once state machine, idempotency keys where supported, request-ID reconciliation, uncertain outcome state, invoice reconciliation |
| High     | One `status` field conflates five independent axes                           | It enables invalid promotions such as “deployed therefore verified”                                                             | Orthogonal status records and scoped evidence attestations                                                                                |
| High     | Replay lookup occurs before a demand contract exists                         | Semantic replay cannot safely bind behavior, environment, effects, and oracle                                                   | Limit early replay to safe same-tenant byte-exact keys; do semantic replay after contract construction                                    |
| High     | Route parser rejects cycles while the architecture advertises feedback edges | The grammar, compiler, runtime, and proof model disagree                                                                        | Reject cycles by default; admit only registered strongly connected components with a termination/convergence policy                       |
| High     | “Test every relevant pair” can become quadratic                              | A million candidates make all-pairs comparison infeasible                                                                       | Typed indexes/join keys generate candidate edges; full layered validation only for candidates                                             |
| High     | Compact cards and summaries are implicitly trusted                           | Retrieved text can contain prompt injection or poisoned authority claims                                                        | Strict structured schema, data/instruction separation, source binding, escaping, output grammar, full-graph compiler validation           |
| High     | Internal v7/v9 percentages lack reproducibility material                     | Point percentages can conceal failures, task mix, and missing usage                                                             | Publish raw receipts, paired task table, analysis code, CIs, and exact evidence scope                                                     |
| Medium   | Fifteen planes can be misread as fifteen services                            | It invites premature distributed complexity                                                                                     | Ship as modules in one process until measured isolation/scale triggers are crossed                                                        |
| Medium   | Duplicate section numbers and mixed vocabulary                               | It makes references and implementation contracts ambiguous                                                                      | Give stable IDs to every invariant, schema, stage, claim, experiment, and gate                                                            |

## Recommended operating model

Treat the 15 planes as **logical owners** implemented by a modular monolith until evidence justifies separation. A first deployment needs six durable responsibilities, not 15 services:

``` mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Gateway, identity, policy"] --> B["Demand contract and oracle"]
    B --> C{"Eligible exact reuse?"}
    C -->|yes| D["Compile and bind"]
    C -->|no| E["Scoped retrieval and compatibility"]
    E --> D
    D --> F["Materialize, execute, verify"]
    F --> G["Outcome, lifecycle, replay"]
    H["Evidence ledger and accounting"] -.-> A
    H -.-> D
    H -.-> F
    H -.-> G
```

Suggested first implementation:

- an API/CLI controller with modules for ingress, policy, demand, replay, retrieval, compilation, and lifecycle;
- SQLite in WAL mode for metadata, leases, idempotency state, policy epochs, and indexed body-free cards;
- a content-addressed filesystem/object store for manifests, bodies, proof bundles, and immutable raw receipts;
- one model gateway interface returning a structured result and every physical-attempt receipt;
- a tiered execution adapter with no ambient network, secrets, home directory, or repository;
- an independent verifier that can reconstruct event roots and rerun the pack oracle.

Promote to a hosted database, queue, dedicated worker pool, or separate service only when a named trigger is observed: multi-writer correctness pressure, tenant isolation requirement, queue recovery SLO, throughput saturation, independent scaling, or ownership boundary. Record the metric and threshold that triggered the move.

### Correct request sequence

1.  Apply network-level byte limits, rate limits, and abuse controls.
2.  Parse the minimum envelope, issue a correlation ID, authenticate, resolve tenant, and either record a compact reject event or continue.
3.  Open the request evidence trail; freeze policy, lifecycle, pricing, provider-capability, and environment epochs.
4.  Collect only authorized repository/environment facts, with redaction and provenance.
5.  Build the canonical demand contract: outcome, inputs, outputs, effects, prohibited effects, environment, acceptance/oracle, risk class, and preferences.
6.  Attempt safe same-tenant byte-exact replay; then semantic exact replay or a sealed compiled route using the demand-contract digest.
7.  Query an authorization-scoped index: exact IDs/packs/standards, typed constraints, then lexical/hybrid retrieval as needed.
8.  Build compatible route candidates; prove demand coverage; choose a unique route or abstain. A model/human selector may propose among still-authorized alternatives.
9.  Bind a compiled GraphIR to the snapshot, policy, exact contracts, implementations, artifact closure, sandbox, and oracle.
10. Resolve and verify artifacts, materialize in a fresh tree, execute with least authority, and record every physical attempt and external effect.
11. Run the independent oracle against the exact output/execution root that will be served.
12. Serve a scoped explanation; record adoption/outcome later. Promotion and replay eligibility are separate signed decisions.

The early byte-exact replay path is safe only when the key includes tenant, policy epoch, environment, request bytes, effect/idempotency class, artifact closure, and oracle, and every lifecycle seal remains valid. Any semantic normalization belongs after demand-contract construction.
