## Core contract corrections

### Orthogonal status model

Replace the decision card's single `status` with:

``` yaml
identity:
  logical_id:
  contract_digest:
  implementation_digest:
  artifact_closure_root:
lifecycle:
  state: draft | active | deprecated | superseded | revoked
  effective_at:
  supersedes: []
evidence:
  - claim_id:
    maturity: untested | checked | verified
    subject_digest:
    scope:
    environment_digest:
    verifier:
    receipt_digest:
    expires_at:
deployment:
  state: local | staging | canary | served | disabled
  deployment_profile_digest:
adoption:
  state: unused | trial | adopted | repeat_used | abandoned
trust:
  signature_status: unsigned | signed | verified_signature
  publisher:
  trust_root:
```

“Truth-serving” should be replaced in implementation by **claim-eligible for an exact scope**. A signed asset can still be malicious; a verified signature authenticates an issuer and bytes, not semantic safety. Promotion is a separate attestation by an authorized promoter, and any bound artifact, policy, environment, verifier, standard, or upstream change can invalidate it.

### Provider budget and result contracts

``` yaml
budget_decision:
  provider:
  endpoint:
  requested_model:
  capability_snapshot_digest:
  output_limit:
    policy: contract_derived | provider_max | provider_default | equal_experiment
    transport:
      encoding: omitted | integer
      field_name:
      emitted_value:
    effective_limit:
    provenance:
  reasoning_budget:
  wall_deadline_ms:
  max_attempts:
  max_tool_calls:
  max_loop_iterations:
  max_dollars:
  concurrency_class:
```

For structured selectors, derive the hard output limit from the maximum valid serialized grammar plus safety headroom. For open-ended construction, use the required deliverable size and measured completion distribution, bounded by provider limits. A provider maximum is reasonable when truncation is a greater risk than quota/latency and the endpoint supports it; it is not a moral default. Never use a smaller cap to make a failing output look cheaper.

``` yaml
model_result:
  logical_call_id:
  attempts:
    - attempt_id:
      provider_request_id:
      provider:
      endpoint:
      requested_model:
      returned_model:
      api_version:
      response_status:
      request_digest:
      response_digest:
      raw_request_ref:
      raw_response_ref:
      finish_reason_raw:
      completeness: complete | truncated | cancelled | timed_out | error | unknown
      latency_ms:
      raw_usage_ref:
      normalization_version:
      rate_card_digest:
      pricing_context:
        currency:
        region:
        tier:
      normalized_usage:
        input_uncached:
        input_cache_write:
        input_cache_read:
        output_visible:
        output_reasoning:
        total_processed:
        billable_tokens:
        quota_reserved_tokens:
        dollars:
        completeness: complete | partial | unavailable | inconsistent
        field_provenance: {}
  selected_attempt_id:
  final_text_digest:
```

OpenTelemetry's GenAI semantic conventions provide useful common fields, but they evolve and do not erase provider-specific billing semantics; pin a convention version and preserve raw usage. See the [GenAI attribute registry](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/registry/attributes/gen-ai/), [Anthropic prompt-caching fields](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching), [Gemini usage metadata](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/generate-content/tokens), and [Bedrock `TokenUsage`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/API_runtime_TokenUsage.html).

### Behavioral compatibility

For a required contract and an implementation contract, these are necessary schematic conditions, not a complete compatibility proof:

\[ Pre\_{required} \Rightarrow Pre\_{implementation} \qquad\text{and}\qquad Post\_{implementation} \Rightarrow Post\_{required} \]

For a producer and consumer edge:

\[ L(Output\_{producer}) \subseteq L(Input\_{consumer}) \]

and implementation effects must be a subset of the effects authorized by the request. The complete authority rule must also cover invariants, framing, exceptions, termination/history, schema/refinement, media type/encoding, units, nullability, cardinality, batching/streaming, ordering, error vocabulary, state consistency, security labels, capabilities, resources, version range, and temporal/session protocol. These rules follow behavioral-subtyping principles; see [Liskov and Wing](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~wing/publications/LiskovWing94.pdf). [CUE](https://cuelang.org/docs/reference/spec/) is a useful decidable constraint language for a first implementation, while OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/Protobuf descriptors can be imported into a normalized contract.

Use exact digest/equality as the fast path. Use verified adapters only when an adapter's input contract accepts the exact producer output and its output contract satisfies the exact consumer input, with effects and failures included. Never let embeddings, titles, or prose authorize an edge.

### Progressive-disclosure proof

For purpose (P), full manifest (m), projection (\pi_P), and deterministic decision (\delta_P), the view is decision-sufficient only if:

\[ \forall m_1,m_2:\quad \pi_P(m_1)=\pi_P(m_2) \Rightarrow \delta_P(m_1)=\delta_P(m_2) \]

For route safety, require at minimum:

\[ Routes\_{accepted}(G\_{compact}) \subseteq Routes\_{permitted}(G\_{full}) \]

and require equality when the compact representation is claimed to preserve all valid alternatives. Use SMT/SAT counterexample search for decidable bounded contracts and bounded exhaustive, property-based, metamorphic, and mutation testing otherwise. The full compiler remains the authority even after a projection passes these tests.

Choose disclosed fields as constrained information acquisition, not a fixed D-level prefix:

\[ \min\_{S} Tokens(S) \quad \text{subject to}\quad H(Route\mid Request,S)\le\epsilon ;\land; Risk\_{unsafe}(S)\le\delta \]

In early versions, deterministic ambiguity predicates choose the next authorized facet. Later, a learned value-of-information policy may optimize field choice after its behavior is frozen and evaluated. Every peel binds the policy, snapshot root, ordered handles, prior view, revealed paths/value digests, omitted field classes, and request nonce using canonical bytes. Deterministic CBOR is standardized in [RFC 8949](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc8949); JSON canonicalization is specified by [RFC 8785](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc8785).

The D0–D9 labels are a facet taxonomy, not a trust ranking or a mandatory prefix hierarchy:

| Facet                      | Required correction                                                                                                                               |
|----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| D0 handle                  | Opaque, request/tenant/snapshot/position/expiry bound; never a bearer capability or persistent identity                                           |
| D1 intent                  | Source/issuer, source spans/digest, deterministic vs generated method, template/model version, scope/freshness; all prose `authority: false`      |
| D2 interface               | Schema/profile/version digest, media type/encoding, units, nullability, cardinality, batch/stream/order/refinement, data classification           |
| D3 interface rules         | Compiler-derived predicates where possible; include multi-port/global constraints and ambiguity core, not only handwritten `next` lists           |
| D4 standards/effects       | Exact standards profile; read/write/create/delete and local/external effects; reversibility, transaction, idempotency/deduplication, compensation |
| D5 state/failure/resources | State owner/consistency, clock/random/network/concurrency sources, deadlines, retry ownership, checkpoint, and numeric resource budgets           |
| D6 security/trust/privacy  | Capability and information-flow labels, permitted roots/egress/secret-handle classes, declassification and sandbox class—never secret values      |
| D7 proof/lifecycle         | Exact subject/verifier/suite/environment/scope/limitations/expiry/revocation and contradictory/negative evidence                                  |
| D8 artifact                | OCI-like media type/digest/size/platform, closure, SBOM/license/provenance, materialization recipe; authorized consumers only                     |
| D9 body                    | Node-local least-privilege body access after compilation; audit/repair requires separate time-bound capability and isolated workspace             |

Policy may require D6 before D2; a human auditor is not automatically authorized for D0–D8. Every view is an immutable `ProjectionSpec` with allowed/forbidden field paths, protected normative paths, audience/purpose, sensitivity ceiling, unknown-field behavior, canonical order, schema version, and retention policy.

### Receipt and proof model

Use separate identities:

``` text
logical_graph_digest
  -> selected_graph_digest
  -> compiled_graph_digest
  -> run_id
  -> node_instance_id
  -> attempt_id
  -> actual_execution_graph_root
  -> oracle_receipt_digest
  -> served_result_digest
```

Each authoritative event should include schema/canonicalization version, event ID, causal parent IDs, per-writer sequence, subject IDs, policy/lifecycle epochs, code/artifact/environment/capability digests, input/output/effect digests, state transition, model/resource usage, timestamp source, data classification, signer/key ID, and signature. Compute an event content ID with domain separation, for example:

``` text
event_id = SHA-256(
  "taedri-event-v1" ||
  CanonicalCBOR(event_without_id_or_signature)
)
```

Parallel writers keep local hash chains and causal parents; an aggregator commits periodic Merkle roots. For transparency, map checkpoints into an explicit registered verifiable-data-structure profile—such as an RFC 9162 append-only Merkle log where appropriate—and issue RFC 9942 COSE receipts. A generic event Merkle-DAG is not automatically the RFC 9942 `RFC9162_SHA256` profile. Independent verification checks signatures, parent closure, inclusion, consistency, sequence gaps, and the exact oracle subject; independent auditors/witnesses plus gossip or cross-logging are required to expose split views rather than merely validate one presented history. RFC 9942 and RFC 9943 SCITT provide checkpoint/transparency interoperability under that deployment model. Keep OpenTelemetry as operational observability linked by IDs—not as the immutable proof store. [W3C PROV](https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-dm/) and [OpenLineage](https://openlineage.io/docs/spec/object-model/) can express portable lineage.

Raw prompts, outputs, traces, and repository facts can contain secrets. Put sensitive bodies in an encrypted evidence vault and publish only authorized metadata/commitments in the ledger. Plain hashes of low-entropy secrets are vulnerable to guessing; use encryption or tenant-keyed HMAC/commitments with domain separation, retention controls, redaction, and access audit.

### Edits to the original 38-step execution map

| Original steps | Disposition                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|----------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 01             | Keep receipt of raw ingress bytes, but only after network-level size/rate protection; assign operational correlation separately from semantic identity.                                                                                  |
| 02–06          | Reorder to 03 envelope/auth → minimal trace open → 04 policy/privacy/tenant snapshot → 02 authorized fact collection → 05 canonical intent → full demand contract. Ledger creation cannot wait until step 06.                            |
| 07–09          | Permit an early byte-exact same-scope probe only as a candidate; authoritative replay/compiled-route reuse follows the full demand contract and current lifecycle/environment/oracle seals.                                              |
| 10–13          | Keep classification/decomposition/query/index binding, but treat granularity as an optimization result and bind ontology/analyzer/tenant overlay plus index freshness.                                                                   |
| 14–16          | Push authority/tenant/lifecycle filters into retrieval before candidate generation; retain step 15 as defense in depth. Projection is an allowlisted purpose contract and metadata is untrusted.                                         |
| 17–18          | Replace universal pair testing with typed candidate joins followed by layered behavioral and global route validation. Candidate graph identity includes rejected edges/reasons.                                                          |
| 19–21          | Add demand-satisfaction proof to the decision gate. Selector receives only an authorized projection and emits a proposal/abstention; independent gateway captures exact bytes and attempt usage.                                         |
| 22–25          | Parser rejects prose/unknown/disallowed edges and **ungoverned** cycles. Snapshot binding precedes handle expansion; compiled GraphIR binds ports, policies, assumptions, resources, artifacts, oracle, and any registered feedback SCC. |
| 26–29          | Re-run policy after expansion. Resolve/verify provenance before use. Create the staging sandbox before materialization, then verify the final tree and static security before execution admission.                                       |
| 30–32          | Trace continuously. Scheduler emits state-transition events, per-edge delivery receipts, effect/capability observations, causal parents, and periodic proof roots; step 32 is aggregation, not retroactive collection.                   |
| 33–34          | Oracle evaluates exact served subject and intermediate invariants. Recovery returns through normal acquisition/verification/compilation gates; unknown effect outcomes block blind retry and serving.                                    |
| 35             | Move response to an Egress responsibility; enforce final policy/redaction and bind explanation plus served result digest.                                                                                                                |
| 36–38          | Outcome, replay eligibility, and lifecycle promotion are separate asynchronous decisions. One successful run does not auto-promote; every change emits invalidations through a reverse dependency index.                                 |

## Economic model and decision policy

### Select with constraints, Pareto dominance, and uncertainty

For request (x), eliminate any asset (a) that fails a hard condition:

\[ Eligible(x)={a:\\ Correct(a,x)\land Authorized(a,x)\land Compatible(a,x)\land Risk(a,x)\le R_x} \]

Retain the evidence vector for every eligible alternative. Remove Pareto-dominated choices, then apply the request's declared lexicographic policy—such as safest, standards-first, lowest total cost, or fastest—rather than a global weighted score. Show uncertainty ranges and evidence age. A scalar contextual utility can be used internally when the user has supplied tradeoffs, but it must retain the underlying vector and hard gates.

For tail-sensitive work, compare a risk measure such as expected loss plus CVaR rather than mean cost alone. A fast asset with a small probability of a catastrophic security or maintenance outcome is not equivalent to a slightly slower low-tail-risk asset.

### Routing break-even

For a reuse route with successful-path cost (T_s), failed-route cost before fallback (T_f), routing overhead (T_r), reuse-success probability (p), and from-scratch cost (T_b):

\[ E\[T\_{reuse}\] = T_r + pT_s + (1-p)(T_f+T_b) \]

Reuse breaks even only when (E\[T\_{reuse}\]\<T_b). When successful reuse itself is nearly free, this becomes approximately:

\[ p \> \frac{T_r+T_f}{T_b+T_f} \]

This explains why a small leaf can lose even when it is correct: routing, card, glue, and verification overhead can exceed the displaced body. It also explains why exact replay and large packs are the promising regions. Estimate these terms by task family and path; do not turn “small/medium/large/frontier” into hardcoded rules.

### Asset lifetime value

For a pack with fixed acquisition/verification/package cost (F), maintenance (M_t), expected uses (N_t), probability it remains valid and passes (p\_{valid,t}), per-use baseline and reuse costs (C\_{b,t},C\_{r,t}), and discount rate (r):

\[ NPV\_{pack}=-F+\sum_t \frac{p\_{valid,t}N_t(C\_{b,t}-C\_{r,t})-M_t}{(1+r)^t} \]

A simple break-even use count (N^\*=F/E\[C_b-C_r\]) is meaningful only when the denominator is positive and validity, maintenance, failures, and opportunity cost have not been omitted. Report both marginal serving economics and fully loaded portfolio economics.

### Complete per-task cost

\[ C\_{task}=C\_{model}+C\_{retrieval}+C\_{storage/network}+C\_{materialize/execute}+C\_{verify}+t\_{human}w+E\[C\_{defect/rework/maintenance}\] \]

Keep native provider usage and prices by model/rate-card version. Tokens across providers are not a universal work unit. Report input, cache write/read, visible output, reasoning output, retries, failures, dollars, latency, human time, oracle result, and long-term maintenance independently.

Developer productivity also cannot be inferred from token savings, generated lines, or time-to-first-answer. Use a multidimensional model such as [SPACE](https://queue.acm.org/detail.cfm?id=3454124) and delivery outcomes such as [DORA](https://dora.dev/research/). The GitHub Copilot controlled experiment on a bounded task reported a speed improvement, while METR's randomized study of experienced developers working in familiar repositories found a slowdown in its setting; that contrast is exactly why Taedri must segment expertise, task familiarity, repository complexity, and workflow. See the [Copilot experiment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.06590) and [METR developer study](https://metr.org/blog/2025-07-10-early-2025-ai-experienced-os-dev-study/).

## Artifact, provenance, update, and lineage stack

| Concern                | Recommended standard                                                                                                                                                     | Taedri use                                                                                                                   |
|------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Content reference      | [OCI descriptor](https://github.com/opencontainers/image-spec/blob/main/descriptor.md) and [OCI image layout](https://specs.opencontainers.org/image-spec/image-layout/) | Algorithm-tagged digest, media type, byte size, platform, manifest/index; transportable pack and attachment graph            |
| Build/test provenance  | [in-toto Attestation Framework](https://github.com/in-toto/attestation/blob/main/spec/README.md) and [SLSA v1.2](https://slsa.dev/spec/v1.2/)                            | Subject + typed predicate + authenticated builder/test evidence; provenance level remains distinct from semantic correctness |
| SBOM/license           | [SPDX 3.0.1](https://spdx.github.io/spdx-spec/v3.0.1/) or [CycloneDX](https://cyclonedx.org/specification/overview/)                                                     | Dependency closure, licenses, known relationships, vulnerability scanning input                                              |
| Signing/transparency   | Sigstore/COSE plus [RFC 9942](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9942) and [RFC 9943](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9943)                                           | Artifact/attestation signatures, checkpoint receipts, inclusion/consistency/non-equivocation evidence                        |
| Secure distribution    | [The Update Framework](https://theupdateframework.io/docs/security/)                                                                                                     | Root/targets roles, key rotation, rollback/freeze/mix-and-match protection, expiry                                           |
| Reproducibility        | [Reproducible Builds definition](https://reproducible-builds.org/docs/definition/)                                                                                       | Exact source/build environment and independent output comparison; reproducible does not mean correct                         |
| Provenance interchange | [W3C PROV-DM](https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-dm/) and [OpenLineage](https://openlineage.io/docs/spec/object-model/)                                                          | Entity/activity/agent lineage and job/run/dataset projections                                                                |
| Operational telemetry  | [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/overview/)                                                                                                      | Unsigned/sampled operational traces and metrics linked to, but not replacing, proof receipts                                 |

Use typed, domain-separated hashes and canonical encodings. A CAS proves retrieval integrity of bytes addressed by a digest; it does not prove publisher identity, authorization, safety, availability, or freshness. Pin roots while a route/replay is eligible, walk reachability for GC, scrub integrity, enforce tenant quotas/encryption, and test backup/restore and deliberate corruption.

### Safe materialization acceptance suite

The first materializer must reject:

- absolute paths, `..` traversal, alternate separators, encoded traversal, and path normalization surprises;
- symlink and hardlink escapes, link swaps/TOCTOU, special/device files, sockets, and setuid/setgid bits;
- case-folding and Unicode-normalization collisions across supported filesystems;
- undeclared or duplicate files, manifest/blob media-type/size mismatch, hash-algorithm confusion, and platform mismatch;
- archive recursion, decompression ratio bombs, excessive file count/depth/size, sparse-file disk exhaustion, and oversized metadata;
- untyped templating, command substitution, configuration escaping, dependency confusion, and unexpected network installs.

Materialize into a fresh root using safe descriptor-relative filesystem operations, enforce quotas before and during extraction, verify every object before decoding, make the tree read-only before execution, and compute an output-tree digest. Exact-replay claims require the same digest on at least two independent clean workers. For inherently nondeterministic artifacts, define observational equivalence instead of claiming byte-identical replay.

### Execution isolation tiers

| Risk/profile                           | Preferred isolation                                              | Minimum controls                                                                          |
|----------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Pure portable typed transform          | WebAssembly Component Model/WASI                                 | Explicit imports/capabilities, memory/time limits, no ambient filesystem/network          |
| Trusted local conventional tool        | Linux namespaces + cgroups + seccomp + Landlock + `no_new_privs` | Read-only base, declared mounts, process/FD/disk/output limits, network denied by default |
| Untrusted multi-tenant Linux workload  | gVisor-style userspace kernel                                    | Isolated filesystem/network, capability broker, dedicated identity, egress proxy          |
| Hostile native or high-impact workload | Firecracker-style microVM or equivalent VM boundary              | Dedicated kernel, short-lived image, no host devices/sockets, brokered secrets/egress     |

WASI is designed around capability-based interfaces ([WASI design principles](https://github.com/WebAssembly/WASI/blob/master/docs/DesignPrinciples.md)); [Landlock](https://docs.kernel.org/userspace-api/landlock.html), [gVisor](https://gvisor.dev/docs/architecture_guide/intro/), and [Firecracker](https://www.usenix.org/system/files/nsdi20-paper-agache.pdf) provide progressively stronger building blocks. A container alone is not a hostile-code proof. Unsupported authority should cause abstention, not silent sandbox downgrade.

Secrets should be referenced by audience-bound short-lived handles and injected directly by a broker only to the admitted node. Network should be denied by default and mediated by an egress proxy enforcing destination, DNS/redirect/IP range, method/port, TLS, payload size, data classification, and logging. Selector-visible metadata never receives secrets or capability-bearing tokens.

## Retrieval, routing, and selection blueprint

### Retrieval stack

Start with the cheapest auditable stack:

1.  same-tenant exact replay, exact pack/implementation ID, exact standard/profile, and sealed compiled route;
2.  hard tenant, lifecycle, trust, environment, effects, security, and proof filters executed before ranking;
3.  typed contract indexes and schema/profile join keys;
4.  SQLite FTS/BM25 over non-authoritative body-free facets;
5.  optional dense or learned-sparse retrieval only after an ablation shows incremental eligible recall;
6.  simple rank fusion such as [Reciprocal Rank Fusion](https://research.google/pubs/reciprocal-rank-fusion-outperforms-condorcet-and-individual-rank-learning-methods/);
7.  optional late-interaction reranking such as [ColBERTv2](https://aclanthology.org/2022.naacl-main.272/) when its recall gain exceeds latency/index cost;
8.  layered deterministic compatibility, route construction, demand-coverage proof, and calibrated abstention;
9.  human/model selection only among the remaining eligible routes.

BM25 is a necessary baseline, not an embarrassment. A model-generated query is an evaluated fallback for unresolved misses, not a default turn and not permanently forbidden. Learned sparse retrieval such as [SPLADE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.10086) can be tested later. Never authorize through similarity.

### Retrieval evaluation

Set the no-match/adversarial prevalence from the declared production population and risk objective. If no production estimate exists, 20–30% is an illustrative stress-test starting range, not a routing constant. Include wrong versions, expired/revoked assets, tenant-private assets, aliases, standards/profile mismatches, effect/security mismatches, stale summaries, and poisoned metadata. Report:

- eligible candidate recall@k and constraint-aware recall;
- MRR/nDCG only as secondary ranking measures;
- high-confidence false-reuse rate and severity;
- no-match abstention, selective risk at fixed coverage, and full risk–coverage curves;
- cross-tenant existence leakage and cache/index contamination;
- index freshness/lag, corpus churn, p50/p95/p99 latency, CPU, memory, and dollars;
- cold, warm, cached, and replay paths separately.

Pairwise compatibility is not an all-pairs operation. Index output and input ports by normalized schema/profile/media type/security class, use those joins to produce a small candidate edge set, then run full refinement checks. For multi-port nodes and global constraints, validate entire candidate routes; pairwise edges alone cannot prove join completeness, transaction compatibility, or global effect budgets.

### Metadata prompt-injection defense

All titles, aliases, summaries, descriptions, imported docs, tool outputs, and model-generated facets are untrusted data. Store normative fields in typed paths, keep natural-language metadata out of system/developer instructions, escape/delimit it, apply strict input schemas and output grammar, and independently audit the exact bytes that reach the selector. The selector output cannot grant capabilities, reveal bodies, alter policies, or introduce graph elements. The full compiler validates every proposal against the hidden authorized graph.

Each facet records kind (deterministic/extractive/model/human/imported), source digest/spans, generator/template identity, contradictions, scope, freshness, and `authority: false`. A generated summary can improve retrieval; it cannot expand what the underlying contract authorizes.

## Benchmark and proof program

### Claims and estimands

Pre-register separate estimands instead of one “Taedri wins” result:

1.  **Intention-to-treat quality:** paired difference in oracle pass rate for every assigned task, counting truncation, timeout, refusal, retrieval miss, materialization failure, and fallback according to the frozen failure policy.
2.  **Quality-gated economic effect:** paired difference in fully loaded and marginal cost, conditional only on the predeclared analysis rule—not on post-hoc removal of failures.
3.  **Coverage/risk:** probability of a wrong served reuse at each coverage level, including no-match tasks.
4.  **Exact-path effect:** model calls, time, and cost for exact replay/direct pack lookup versus the same task's baseline.
5.  **Longitudinal effect:** change-task time, regressions, rollback, dependency churn, and retained reuse at 7/30/90 days.

The confirmatory claim should be narrow:

> For task family X, environment Y, model/provider policy Z, and evidence profile P, exact pack reuse produces quality/security-noninferior outcomes and a positive failure-inclusive paired total-cost difference, with the stated confidence interval.

### Arms

Use the same frozen task, environment, tool access, deliverable contract, and independent hidden oracle:

- A: from-scratch baseline;
- B: exact SolutionPack/direct deterministic route;
- C: verified leaf assembly, when feasible;
- D: exact replay or sealed-plan re-execution for repeated tasks;
- E: explicit no-reuse/bypass arm for task families where routing is expected to lose.

Run the small leaf as an expected negative economic control rather than presenting it as a co-equal product thesis. Keep cached-result reuse, deterministic re-execution, compiled-plan reuse, and artifact reuse as separate path labels.

### Execution design

1.  Run a small instrumented calibration batch to validate the harness and estimate paired variance; 20–30 tasks is an illustrative starting range, with the stopping point driven by variance-estimate stability and planned precision. Do not use calibration tasks for the confirmatory headline.
2.  Use those estimates, the preregistered quality non-inferiority margin, desired precision/power, task/repository clustering, and expected missingness to choose the confirmatory sample. Do not substitute a large provider/model grid for statistical power at the task level.
3.  Block on task/repository/family, provider/model, and relevant experience/familiarity. Randomize or counterbalance arm order within blocks; preserve every assigned cell.
4.  Reserve a hidden holdout and separate adversarial/no-match set. Freeze tasks, code, index, artifacts, policy, prices, provider/model, environment, oracle, and analysis code before calls.
5.  Include all physical attempts, fallbacks, repairs, cancellations, and uncertain outcomes. Missing provider usage remains null; the cell cannot support a token headline, but the failure remains in ITT.
6.  Run cold first use, warm artifact/index, compiled route, and exact replay separately. Never average them without weights matching a declared production mix.
7.  Publish a task-level paired table, raw receipt roots, exclusions fixed in advance, effect sizes, intervals, and negative findings.

NIST recommends blocking when nuisance variation can be controlled; see [randomized block designs](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/pri/section3/pri332.htm). For repeated monitoring, use a declared sequential/always-valid method instead of repeatedly peeking at fixed-horizon p-values.

### Statistical analysis

- Paired binary pass/fail: exact McNemar analysis and a confidence interval for the paired difference.
- Tokens, cost, latency, human time: paired differences and ratios with task/repository-clustered or hierarchical bootstrap; report median, mean, p90/p95/p99, and tail regressions.
- Interchangeability: equivalence or non-inferiority test with a product-risk-derived margin. “Not statistically significant” is not equivalence.
- Abstention: full risk–coverage curve, area under risk–coverage, and selective risk at fixed production coverage.
- Multiple claims: preregister a primary outcome and apply Holm or hierarchical gatekeeping to secondary families.
- Factor interactions: use screening/covering-array designs, then focused factorial experiments. Independent one-factor sweeps miss reader×compression, pack-size×cold-cache, and graph-shape×failure interactions.
- LLM judges: secondary only; blind arm/provider, randomize and swap order, calibrate against anchored human cases, repeat, use cross-family judges, and report agreement/uncertainty. The original LLM-as-judge research documents position, verbosity, and self-enhancement biases ([Zheng et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.05685)).

Remove self-declared `serves_truth` from the bundle. Promotion is a separately signed authorization over exact claim IDs, subject, scope, environment constraints, expiry, and revocation reference.

### Expanded fault matrix

Generate faults across `location × type × timing × duration × correlation × recovery`. Add disk-full/bit-rot, OOM, `kill -9`, network partition, partial commit, clock skew, split brain, duplicate/late provider responses, 429/5xx, cancellation, DNS rebinding/redirect, malicious cards, Unicode/confusable handles, duplicate JSON/CBOR keys, ACL side channels, index poisoning, logger/exporter loss, stale keys, proof-log fork, output served before receipt commit, external effect before crash, double compensation, and oracle reading a different output from the served one.

Use deterministic simulation for scheduler/retry/lifecycle state machines, property-based state-machine testing, coverage-guided fuzzing for parsers/canonicalizers/materializers, mutation testing for compiler/oracle rules, and bounded TLA+ models for safety/liveness of feedback, leases, invalidation, and reconciliation. Runtime watchdogs remain necessary even after model checking.

### Proposed launch gates

These are starting defaults to preregister and adjust by risk—not universal constants:

| Gate                | Blocking condition                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|---------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Accounting          | Every physical attempt has provider/model/request/finish/raw receipt; no missing required usage in a headline cell; raw-to-normalized reconciliation passes                                                                                |
| Canonicalization    | Byte-identical golden digests across a preregistered independent implementation/language set; three is an initial high-assurance target, not a universal constant; every declared ambiguous/unsupported negative vector rejects            |
| Pack reconstruction | Repeated output-tree digest match across the declared independent clean-worker set; two is the initial minimum for an independence claim; no ambient repository/secrets; zero observed violations in the declared extraction-attack corpus |
| Assurance           | Hidden oracle passes; known wrongs and critical mutants fail; zero unresolved critical security/license/provenance finding                                                                                                                 |
| Projection          | Zero forbidden field paths in independent gateway captures; no bounded counterexample to the declared safety projection                                                                                                                    |
| Handle binding      | Reorder/insert/delete/substitute/cross-request/cross-tenant/expiry/stale-snapshot controls all reject                                                                                                                                      |
| Retrieval           | Production-derived recall and abstention gates are met; confident wrong-route and tenant leakage remain below the predeclared risk limit                                                                                                   |
| Compiler            | Zero false accepts in bounded fixtures; every critical compiler mutant killed; all served runs satisfy compiled semantics                                                                                                                  |
| Sandbox             | No unexpected filesystem/network/secret/process authority in the adversarial corpus; all declared capabilities still work                                                                                                                  |
| Lifecycle           | Every stale route/replay rejects after revocation within the declared propagation SLO                                                                                                                                                      |
| Quality             | One-sided 95% interval establishes non-inferiority with the risk-derived margin; severe security regressions have zero allowance                                                                                                           |
| Savings             | Lower 95% bound of paired failure-inclusive total-cost improvement is positive for the declared production mix                                                                                                                             |
| Adoption            | Repeat successful external use is observed; a one-time demo does not promote the product thesis                                                                                                                                            |

Zero observed failures is not proof of zero risk. With zero approximately independent failures in (n) trials, the one-sided 95% upper bound is roughly (3/n); correlated adversarial cases make the effective evidence weaker. Structural controls and formal reasoning remain necessary.

### Six evidence-gated waves

| Wave                      |     Timebox | Build                                                                                                                  | Exit/kill decision                                                                                                                    |
|---------------------------|------------:|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 0 — demand                |    Days 0–3 | B0-01; freeze demand, baseline, oracle, risks, buyer, and kill matrix                                                  | Stop if no repeat task, no executable acceptance criterion, no measurable pain, or no plausible second use                            |
| 1 — evidence kernel       |   Weeks 1–2 | B0-02–05 and the local event/CAS foundations                                                                           | Fixtures plus live smoke calls produce complete, internally consistent, independently verifiable receipts; otherwise do not benchmark |
| 2 — one trustworthy pack  |   Weeks 2–4 | B0-06–10, B0-13–14, B0-18                                                                                              | Clean-room deterministic reconstruction, provenance/license/signature, sandbox, oracle, revoke/rollback all pass                      |
| 3 — deterministic reuse   |   Weeks 4–6 | B0-11–12 and B0-15 in shadow mode                                                                                      | Exact route is zero-model and snapshot-stable; retrieval meets preregistered recall/risk/ACL gates; selector remains off              |
| 4 — causal/economic pilot |   Weeks 6–8 | B0-16–17 with 3–5 design partners where possible                                                                       | Quality/security non-inferiority and positive cost interval; evidence of adoption/repeat use. Kill or redesign failing families       |
| 5 — conditional expansion | Weeks 9–12+ | Progressive disclosure/selector only if ambiguity persists; more same-family packs; deployment parity; platform matrix | Each addition has a decision-changing experiment. Defer distributed graph/runtime features until actual tasks require them            |

Do not build a proprietary durable scheduler, recursive blueprint runtime, governed cycles, hosted vector database, or broad provider/model matrix in these 12 weeks unless the chosen workflow cannot be delivered without it. If durable orchestration becomes necessary, first run a build-versus-buy evaluation against an existing engine.

## High-leverage product and research ideas

- **Shadow router:** compute what Taedri would have selected while the customer's original path remains authoritative. This builds demand, recall, abstention, and cost evidence without workflow risk.
- **Counterfactual reuse-regret sampler:** on a small randomized subset, run one alternate eligible route or from-scratch arm to estimate how often the chosen route was economically wrong. Budget it explicitly; never do this on effectful production work without isolation.
- **Verify on demand:** store thin candidates/references cheaply; pay full verification/package/maintenance cost only after repeated demand or a risk/standard requirement crosses a threshold.
- **Active-learning curation queue:** prioritize abstentions, near-miss false routes, repairs, user modifications, and repeated misses rather than generating more generic inventory.
- **Rate–distortion views:** minimize selector-visible bytes subject to an empirical upper bound on selection loss and a formal no-false-authorization condition.
- **Constraint-coverage knapsack:** choose context by mandatory demand constraints discharged per byte/token, not generic semantic relevance.
- **Near-neighbor poison corpus:** deliberately create convincing but incompatible versions, licenses, effects, standards profiles, tenants, and summaries; make confident selection of one a blocking failure.
- **Nightly canary replay:** rerun a small high-value portfolio when an upstream, policy, index, materializer, oracle, model, or provider changes. Update evidence rather than assuming permanence.
- **OCI referrer evidence graph:** attach SBOM, provenance, signature, test, vulnerability, conformance, and promotion statements to a pack without bloating its runtime manifest.
- **Thin verified upstream reference:** prefer a pinned, verified installation/configuration/adapter around a maintained upstream package when copying its body would create ownership and update debt.
- **Private policy overlays:** let an organization refine eligibility, preferred standards, approved publishers, and local packs without mutating public/global evidence.
- **Bypass champion:** every task family keeps an explicit direct/no-reuse option. If it wins on risk-adjusted total cost, the system explains and uses it.
- **Asset survival curves:** estimate how long evidence remains valid by dependency churn, task family, owner, and environment; use that probability in pack NPV and maintenance scheduling.
- **Proof debt budget:** track assets whose use outpaces evidence freshness or maintenance. Stop new promotion when proof debt exceeds an owner-set ceiling.

An experiment is worth running only if its plausible outcomes lead to different actions. Freeze the action table before collecting data.

## Definitions of done by claim

### Savings or efficiency

- Same assigned task population, deliverable class, tools/access, and independent oracle.
- All failures, retries, repairs, fallbacks, truncations, and uncertain calls included.
- Every headline cell has complete provider identity and required usage; prices and shared-cost allocation are versioned.
- Quality/security passes preregistered non-inferiority before cost superiority is considered.
- Paired effect distribution and confidence interval, with cold/warm/replay scope and production mix.
- Fully loaded and marginal economics reported separately.

### Correctness, security, or reliability

- Exact subject, environment, threat/risk profile, protocol, verifier, negative/mutation/fault cases, result, uncertainty/coverage, expiry, and known limitations.
- Signatures and provenance authenticate the evidence producer and bytes; they are not substituted for semantic testing.
- The oracle and security checks evaluate the actual execution/served subject.
- Revocation and upstream-change invalidation are tested.

### Standards or “best practice”

- Exact document/edition/profile and licensed/private digest where applicable.
- Executable conformance and interoperability with independent peers, including negative/version-skew vectors.
- Deviations and unsupported options visible.
- Replace “best practice” with “profile shown superior or required for this comparator and scope.”

### Maintainability and anti-debt

- Named owner, upstream/support concentration, dependency closure, lifecycle and replacement plan.
- Upgrade, vulnerability patch, schema/API migration, platform replacement, rollback, and new-environment tasks at 7/30/90 days.
- Time, changed surface, review, regressions, rework, change-failure/recovery, cognitive load, and abandonment/repeat reuse.

### Developer productivity

- Segment by expertise, task/repository familiarity, task family, and workflow.
- Use time-to-green and review alongside quality, rework, incidents, satisfaction/cognitive load, and maintainability.
- Do not publish token, generated-line, or completion-time measures alone as productivity.

## Dashboard that can drive decisions

**North star:** verified repeat successful reuse per active team per week, segmented by task family and risk profile. It must mean an oracle-passing result that was adopted and later succeeded again; it is not a search hit or materialization count.

| Area                 | Decision metrics                                                                                                                                                                         |
|----------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Demand               | repeated task families, frequency, current fully loaded cost, failure severity, buyer/WTP, abstentions/misses, unserved high-pain demand                                                 |
| Supply               | candidates and claim-eligible assets by granularity; unique behavioral fingerprints; evidence age/expiry; owner/bus factor; maintenance due; revocations                                 |
| Funnel               | eligible → retrieved → dry-run → compiled → materialized → oracle pass → accepted → modified/unmodified → repeated → retained/abandoned                                                  |
| Retrieval/selection  | eligible recall@k, hard-negative false reuse, no-match abstention, risk–coverage, ambiguity locus, peels/tokens, unauthorized-field and tenant-leak count                                |
| Execution/proof      | served runs conforming to compiled semantics, unreconciled dispatches, effect/compensation outcomes, proof gaps, signature/log inconsistencies, sandbox denials and unexpected authority |
| Economics            | failure-inclusive paired total cost, marginal vs fully loaded, input/cache/output/reasoning usage, quota reservation, p50/p95/p99 latency, human time, defects/rework/maintenance        |
| Quality/security     | oracle pass, mutation score, severe findings, conformance/interoperability, fault recovery, stale route/replay rejection, incident rate                                                  |
| Customer/maintenance | time-to-first-green, review, modification, repeat use, retention, 7/30/90-day upgrade/patch/rollback results, WTP/paid continuation                                                      |
| Evidence health      | claim-eligible denominator, incomplete usage, expired/contradicted evidence, invalidation lag, proof-debt budget, independent-verifier failures                                          |

Never optimize primitive count, token savings, model-call suppression, or raw adoption as a standalone north star. A high reuse rate produced by forced unsafe routing is a failure.

## Automated stop, bypass, and incident rules

Immediate global stop/containment:

- any cross-tenant disclosure or unauthorized body/capability;
- critical sandbox escape, secret exfiltration, or unbrokered external effect;
- served output whose digest differs from the oracle subject;
- compromised trust root/signing key or inconsistent transparency checkpoint;
- unreconciled effectful dispatch being treated as success;
- critical provenance/license violation in a served artifact.

Family/path kill or redesign:

- quality/security lower bound fails the preregistered margin;
- lower confidence bound of fully loaded cost improvement is non-positive and no separately proven value dimension compensates;
- confident false-reuse risk exceeds the risk-profile limit;
- exact/replay path still invokes a model without a recorded reason;
- most users materially rewrite or abandon the pack, repeat use does not appear within the decision window, or no buyer will continue;
- selector resolves too little ambiguity to repay its incremental cost/latency/error; keep deterministic/human/no-reuse path;
- evidence expires faster than it can be maintained or owner/support concentration exceeds policy;
- complexity adds services/runtime semantics without an observed SLO, isolation, reliability, or customer need.

Every automated rule needs metric, numerator/denominator, threshold, observation window, severity, owner, action, rollback, and re-enable condition. Suggested numbers in the benchmark section are starting hypotheses, not silent architectural constants.

## First 12-week deliverables

Recommended repository/module boundaries for implementation:

``` text
schemas/          canonical contracts, identities, status, claims
policy/           provider capabilities, resource and authorization decisions
ledger/           canonical events, Merkle roots, signatures, verification
cas/              descriptors, manifests, pin/lease/GC, integrity
materializer/     safe tree construction and typed overlays
sandbox/          execution profiles, capability/secret/egress brokers
oracle/           independent task and security assurance
replay/           exact keys, seals, invalidation
retrieval/        scoped exact/typed/FTS shadow pipeline
compiler/         compatibility, demand coverage, GraphIR binding
bench/            frozen tasks, arms, fault injection, analysis
cli/              inspect, dry-run, materialize, verify, run, export/import
```

By day 3: one signed-off demand contract, oracle, baseline, customer/buyer, and kill matrix.
By week 2: provider/cost receipts and canonical proof events verify independently.
By week 4: one pack reconstructs identically across the declared independent clean-worker set (two is the initial minimum), passes security/oracle/provenance/license gates, and can be revoked/rolled back.
By week 6: exact replay/direct route is zero-model; scoped retrieval runs in shadow with calibrated abstention.
By week 8: paired pilot result and raw proof roots exist, including negative results.
By week 12: repeat-use and a first maintenance/change task decide whether to expand packs, add a selector, or stop.

## Final operating principle

> For a fully bound demand and policy scope, choose the largest eligible verified closure that minimizes risk-adjusted expected total cost; keep non-authoritative descriptions and full bodies out of authority decisions; compile, materialize, execute, and verify with least authority; record every physical attempt and effect in independently verifiable receipts; promote only scoped claims; and prefer bypass whenever reuse does not win.

The narrow claim to prove first is valuable and defensible:

> For one declared task family and environment, Taedri can select or exactly replay a demand-matching SolutionPack, produce a quality- and security-noninferior result, reduce failure-inclusive total cost with uncertainty reported, and emit an independently verifiable chain from demand through artifacts, execution, oracle, and outcome.

Prove that before proving “Taedri supports every graph.”
