# Existing-Code Architecture Notes for the Taedri Specification

> **ANNEX STATUS — TARGET ARCHITECTURE NOTES.** Names, schemas, analyzers, services,
> and rollout steps here are design proposals unless the controlling empirical state in
> Part 0 identifies matching current evidence.

## Recommended project and repository name

**Project:** Taedri CodeLattice
**Repository:** `taedri-code-lattice`

The name fits the actual architecture: exact source occurrences, revision-bound symbols, logical lineages, groups, builds, runtime observations, and retrieval projections form a lattice of related identities and abstractions rather than one flat “code graph.” It is also broad enough to cover repositories, PyPI distributions, monorepos, generated code, binaries, notebooks, schemas, and future ecosystems. Treat the name as a working name; GitHub, package, domain, and trademark availability have not been formally cleared.

Useful alternatives are `taedri-symbol-mesh`, `taedri-code-weave`, `taedri-code-cortex`, and `taedri-code-catalog`, but `taedri-code-lattice` is the clearest description of the distinctive identity model.

## One-sentence mission

Taedri CodeLattice deterministically turns code that already exists into an evidence-bearing, language-neutral, incrementally maintained entity-and-relation fabric that lets tools and models find, understand, compose, modify, and verify code without repeatedly reading whole repositories or inventing free-form queries.

## The decisive architectural correction

Do **not** try to invent one universal AST, globally rename source variables, or make LLM-generated summaries the source of truth. Build a thin universal envelope over precise native representations:

``` text
existing source, packages, builds, docs, tests, traces
    -> immutable artifacts and workspace snapshots
    -> language-native syntax/symbol/type/flow facts
    -> evidence-bearing normalized entities and relations
    -> exact, lexical, structural, graph, clone, and semantic projections
    -> budgeted task-specific CodeSlices and CodeCapsules
    -> typed ChangeIR lowered by language-specific refactoring engines
    -> independent verification and exact receipts
    -> incremental graph epoch and measured learning
```

The normalized layer is a bridge and control plane. Native analyzer output remains attached so no language-specific precision is destroyed. [SCIP](https://github.com/scip-code/scip) already supplies a language-agnostic Protobuf format for definitions, references, and implementations across a useful set of languages; [Kythe](https://kythe.io/docs/schema/) provides typed code-node/edge and byte-anchor precedents; [Glean](https://github.com/facebookincubator/Glean) demonstrates scalable storage and derivation of source-code facts. None of them alone supplies package/build identity, evidence modality, behavior, safe transformation, retrieval projections, and LLM receipts, so CodeLattice should compose them rather than replace them.

## Five planes, kept separate

1.  **Immutable fact plane:** exact source/artifact bytes, native analyzer bundles, occurrences, extracted assertions, runtime observations, hashes, and provenance.
2.  **Logical overlay plane:** revisable lineage, equivalence, deprecation, ownership, policy, semantic roles, human annotations, and inferred claims. Nothing here silently rewrites immutable facts.
3.  **Serving projection plane:** fielded lexical indexes, exact maps, compressed adjacency, embeddings, clone fingerprints, entity cards, group capsules, and task-specific materialized views. These are disposable and reproducible.
4.  **Transactional change plane:** workspace snapshot locks, typed edits, language-specific lowering, patch preconditions, graph deltas, verification, rollback, and receipts.
5.  **Evidence and learning plane:** which facts, slices, routes, models, transformations, and tests produced a result; whether it was accepted; and what cheaper deterministic route can be manufactured for the next similar task.

This separation prevents a generated description, stale embedding, guessed rename lineage, or failed patch from corrupting canonical code identity.

## Full existing-code processing stack

### 1. Acquisition and authority

Acquire repositories, registry releases, wheels, sdists, archives, OCI images, generated sources, SBOMs, build manifests, docs, examples, tests, and optional runtime traces. Every acquisition records origin, registry authority, retrieval time, declared license, cryptographic digest, tenant/ACL, and takedown status. Do not equate a registry package with a repository: the published artifact is authoritative for what users installed, while a linked repository is a separately validated source claim.

For PyPI, consume the JSON Simple Repository API, verify advertised hashes, retain `X-PyPI-Last-Serial` for incremental discovery, and ingest every relevant distribution as its own artifact variant. PyPI explicitly recommends the JSON form for new integrations and provides hashes, core metadata links, Python-version constraints, yanked status, file size, and upload time in its index surface. [PyPI Index API](https://docs.pypi.org/api/index-api/)

### 2. Exact snapshot and artifact layer

Create content-addressed IDs for repository trees, commits, dirty worktrees, files, distributions, build outputs, generated files, and dependency closures. A Git commit is insufficient: untracked files, local modifications, submodules, generated content, symlinks, LFS objects, case sensitivity, and build flags can change the analyzed program. Define a `WorkspaceSnapshotID` as a Merkle root over the selected source boundary plus relevant configuration and dirty changes.

### 3. Source-boundary and polyglot discovery

Discover nested packages, monorepo workspaces, source roots, test roots, generated/vendor/minified regions, notebooks, embedded SQL/GraphQL/templates, FFI boundaries, build systems, language versions, and target variants. Detection emits confidence and evidence; an extension is a hint, not ground truth. Preserve host/embedded language mappings so a SQL query inside Python or JavaScript is an addressable subdocument with a projection back to its host span.

### 4. Build-universe recovery

Resolve manifests, lockfiles, interpreter/compiler versions, feature flags, extras, conditional dependencies, macros, target triples, environment variables, generated-source steps, and compile databases. The same file can denote different programs under different build universes, so semantic facts bind to a `BuildUniverseID`. Indexing must still produce syntax-only coverage when a build cannot be recovered.

### 5. Native parsing and indexing

Use an adapter portfolio, not a single parser:

- broad cheap coverage: Tree-sitter, Universal Ctags, archive/file metadata;
- precise navigation: SCIP indexers, compiler APIs, language servers;
- deep semantics: CodeQL, compiler CFG/data-flow, Code Property Graph/Joern, language-specific analyzers;
- lossless edits: LibCST for Python, TypeScript compiler/Babel/ts-morph or jscodeshift for JS/TS, OpenRewrite/Spoon/JDT for JVM, Roslyn for .NET, Clang tooling for C/C++, and language-native rewrite APIs elsewhere;
- structural fallback: ast-grep or equivalent tree patterns for broad search and conservative rewrites.

SCIP’s current official indexer list spans Java/Scala/Kotlin, TypeScript/JavaScript, Rust, C/C++, Ruby, Python, .NET, Dart, PHP, and Debian files. [SCIP](https://github.com/scip-code/scip) For modification, lossless trees matter: Python’s AST drops comments and formatting, while LibCST retains enough syntax to reproduce the input and exposes typed semantic nodes. [LibCST](https://libcst.readthedocs.io/en/latest/why_libcst.html) OpenRewrite similarly uses lossless semantic trees and recipes to make minimally invasive, format-preserving changes. [OpenRewrite](https://docs.openrewrite.org/)

### 6. Native fact preservation

Every normalized assertion points to a native fact bundle, extractor version, configuration digest, build universe, and source snapshot. Preserve overload resolution, inferred types, macro expansion, may/must semantics, alias/points-to sets, path conditions, implicit/generated entities, and analyzer diagnostics. Normalization must not collapse these into a lowest-common-denominator graph.

### 7. Identity and lineage

Use globally unique **sidecar** IDs, never global source renaming. Native names remain in source, APIs, stack traces, serialization, reflection, and developer workflows.

The minimum identity lattice is:

``` text
RegistryAuthority
  -> PackageLineageID
  -> ReleaseID
  -> DistributionID
  -> SourceSnapshotID / WorkspaceSnapshotID
  -> BuildUniverseID / BuildID
  -> FileContentID
  -> OccurrenceID
  -> RevisionEntityID
  -> optional ConceptID (revisable lineage claim)
  -> BehaviorID (build + environment + input domain + oracle)
```

Exact IDs are content/context bound and never reassigned. A `ConceptID` is not a hash and never justifies destructive merging; it is a versioned assertion supported by `renamed_from`, `copied_from`, `split_into`, `merged_from`, `forked_from`, or `same_concept_as` evidence. For locals, lambdas, anonymous types, generated names, and macros, exact occurrence identity may be all that can be defended.

For a local variable, a safe key is snapshot/build + language + enclosing revision entity + declaration occurrence + structured local discriminator. For a public method, add package/release, fully qualified native descriptors, overload/signature, and native indexer symbol. Store the full canonical identity key in addition to its hash.

### 8. Extensible entity-aspect model

Avoid one enormous nullable `CodeEntity` record. Use a small universal envelope plus typed aspects:

``` yaml
EntityEnvelope:
  revision_entity_id: ceg:v1:entity:...
  artifact_id: ceg:v1:artifact:...
  kind: function|class|variable|module|endpoint|test|runtime_object|...
  native_names: []
  occurrence_ids: []
  aspect_refs: []
  native_fact_bundle_refs: []
  schema_version: 1
```

Aspects include `CallableAspect`, `TypeAspect`, `StorageAspect`, `ValueAspect`, `ModuleAspect`, `ClassAspect`, `ResourceAspect`, `EndpointAspect`, `TestAspect`, `BuildAspect`, `DocumentationAspect`, `RuntimeAspect`, `PolicyAspect`, and `RetrievalAspect`. This permits a Python function, Rust trait, SQL view, protobuf field, HTTP endpoint, configuration key, notebook cell, and runtime allocation to share identity/evidence machinery without pretending they have identical semantics.

### 9. Occurrence, anchor, and source-map layer

An entity is not a source range. Store definitions, declarations, references, reads, writes, calls, imports, doc mentions, generated anchors, and implicit occurrences independently. Canonical source anchors use byte ranges against exact file bytes; line/column is only a convenience projection because Unicode encodings and newline normalization vary. A generated entity retains a source-map chain back through code generators, templates, macros, notebooks, and build steps.

### 10. Evidence-bearing relation hypergraph

Binary edges are insufficient for calls, argument binding, data flow, builds, effects, tests, and runtime observations. Use relation nodes with participants/roles:

``` yaml
RelationAssertion:
  relation_id: ceg:v1:relation:...
  predicate: call|flow|build|test|effect|lineage|...
  participants:
    - {role: caller, entity_id: ...}
    - {role: callsite, occurrence_id: ...}
    - {role: candidate_callee, entity_id: ...}
  modality: asserted|extracted|inferred|observed|verified
  quantifier: may|must|observed
  polarity: positive|negative|unknown
  scope_snapshot_id: ...
  scope_build_universe_id: ...
  producer: {id: ..., version: ..., config_digest: ...}
  evidence_refs: []
  confidence: optional
  calibration_version: optional
```

Absence is not false. A negative conclusion is publishable only when an analyzer’s declared coverage makes the absence meaningful. Conflicting analyzers remain parallel assertions and are reconciled in a projection, never erased.

### 11. Semantic ports and boundary contracts

Represent parameters, return/yield values, errors, callbacks/events, reads/writes, capabilities, resources, state transitions, serialization forms, and effects as ports. A port records direction, ordinal/name, type claims, constraints, cardinality, ownership/mutability, semantic roles, and evidence.

This generalizes the primitive idea to any existing code region. For an entity set `S`, derive:

- inbound boundary `delta-(S)`: types, values, calls, events, resources, and capabilities entering `S`;
- outbound boundary `delta+(S)`: outputs, mutations, calls, events, and resources leaving `S`;
- internal invariants and state;
- may/must effects and failure modes;
- tests/oracles that cover the boundary;
- decisive internal edges needed to understand or safely alter it;
- coverage and abstraction-loss estimates.

The resulting `CodeCapsule(S)` is the black-box description the user is aiming for. It lets an LLM compose or modify a class, module, package, subsystem, or library without reading every body, while retaining handles that resolve progressively to selected internals. It is an evidence-backed abstraction, not a claim of total behavioral equivalence.

### 12. Hierarchical groups rather than arbitrary merging

Support groups at occurrence, callable, type, class, module, package, service, repository, workspace, and ecosystem scales. Groups can be native containment sets or derived sets based on strongly connected components, call/data-flow communities, co-change history, tests, clone families, ownership, domain tags, or minimum-boundary graph cuts.

``` yaml
EntitySetDefinition:
  set_id: ceg:v1:set:...
  graph_epoch: ...
  definition_kind: explicit|query|algorithmic|historical
  definition_ref: ...
  frozen_membership_digest: ...
  membership_evidence_refs: []
  boundary_capsule_ref: ...
```

A derived group records its algorithm/version/parameters. Never pretend community detection or an embedding cluster is an architectural truth.

### 13. Documentation and multi-description layer

Keep original docstrings, comments, README fragments, examples, API references, issue explanations, generated summaries, search aliases, and negative constraints as separate `DescriptionAssertion`s. Each records author/model, prompt/model version where applicable, source spans, intended audience, freshness, modality, and evidence. A human docstring is an assertion; an LLM summary is an inferred projection; neither replaces code or test evidence.

Generate multiple retrieval views when useful: exact API synopsis, behavior, input/output examples, effects, risks, common intents, error vocabulary, standards, and “not suitable for” descriptions. Embeddings are derived records with model, dimension, preprocessing, input refs, and version; they are never identity.

### 14. Behavior and runtime evidence

Static facts cannot fully resolve reflection, monkey patching, dependency injection, dynamic imports, native extensions, RPC, plugins, or environment-dependent behavior. Add opt-in sandboxed test/example/property probes and runtime instrumentation. A runtime object receives a trace-scoped ID, allocation site, type claim, lifetime, and environment; do not assign every ephemeral object a global logical identity.

Bind every observation to build, dependency closure, environment, input domain, sample size, timestamp, and oracle. “Test passed once” is evidence, not a universal behavior contract.

### 15. Storage and publication

Use several purpose-built projections:

1.  content-addressed object storage for source, artifacts, native bundles, and evidence;
2.  immutable Protobuf or Arrow/Parquet fact shards;
3.  exact ID key/value mapping;
4.  fielded lexical index for names, signatures, docs, effects, errors, packages, and standards;
5.  compressed forward/reverse adjacency and bitmap indexes;
6.  columnar analytical view for corpus-wide scoring and evaluation;
7.  optional sparse/dense/multivector indexes;
8.  an interactive graph database only where it materially helps, not as the canonical store.

Publish candidate graph epochs atomically after schema validation, referential-integrity checks, collision checks, coverage accounting, and signed manifest generation. Queries, slices, plans, and receipts pin an epoch. Tenant/workspace overlays sit above a shared immutable public-package base and are authorization-filtered **before** retrieval/ranking.

### 16. Existing-code retrieval waterfall

The cheapest route should dominate:

1.  explicit entity/package/file handle, cursor, diagnostic, stack frame, or changed line;
2.  exact name, qualified symbol, import, path, signature, error code, standard, or prior successful route;
3.  deterministic task template with typed slots;
4.  fielded BM25 and character/trigram/edit-distance search;
5.  AST/structural pattern search;
6.  type/port/effect constraint solving and bidirectional graph routes;
7.  clone fingerprints, MinHash/SimHash/LSH, co-change and test-neighborhood retrieval;
8.  local sparse/dense retrieval and graph-aware fusion;
9.  local cross-encoder/ranker or constrained SLM;
10. cheap hosted structured-query/selector model;
11. strong-model custom query or graph exploration only for unresolved novelty.

Useful existing-code routes include `definition`, `references`, `implementation`, `call_path`, `dataflow_path`, `impact`, `test_oracle`, `change_surface`, `equivalent_existing_implementation`, `adapter_path`, and `package_usage_example`. A typed route solver can search forward from known inputs and backward from required output/effect/oracle until compatible boundaries meet.

### 17. Context projection instead of repository dumping

Compile a task-specific connected slice:

``` yaml
ContextSlice:
  slice_id: ...
  graph_epoch: ...
  workspace_snapshot_id: ...
  demand_ir_ref: ...
  seed_entity_ids: []
  included_entity_cards: []
  included_source_spans: []
  included_relation_assertions: []
  included_evidence_refs: []
  omitted_frontier_handles: []
  coverage: {}
  token_estimate: ...
  integrity_digest: ...
```

Select candidates under a token/latency budget using relevance, path connectivity, evidence strength, novelty, expected information gain, and verification value, penalized by token cost, redundancy, staleness, uncertainty, and policy risk. This is a prize-collecting connected-subgraph/knapsack problem, not simply top-k vector similarity.

Start with signature, boundary contract, decisive effects, tests, and one or two strongest paths. Expand 1/2/4/8 alternatives and detail levels only when ambiguity or verification risk justifies it. Return frontier handles so an agent can resolve another body or neighborhood without resending the slice.

### 18. LLM traceability

The model receives native source names plus out-of-band stable entity/occurrence IDs. Never inject global IDs into real source identifiers. Every model call records:

- demand and context-slice digest;
- graph epoch and workspace snapshot;
- included entity/occurrence/edge/evidence IDs;
- model/provider/router policy and parameters;
- tool calls and resolved bodies;
- claims and proposed operations tied to IDs;
- token, latency, cache, and cost accounting;
- verifier outcomes and adoption status.

This makes “why did the model change this?” answerable and lets successful paths become deterministic templates or reusable change recipes.

### 19. Typed modification pipeline

Separate read/search from write authority. Prefer a model-produced `ChangeIR` over unrestricted full-file generation:

``` yaml
ChangePlan:
  plan_id: ...
  base_workspace_snapshot_id: ...
  graph_epoch: ...
  target_entity_ids: []
  intent: ...
  impact_slice_ref: ...
  operations:
    - op: rename_entity|change_signature|replace_body|add_member|move_entity|edit_docs|edit_config|raw_patch
      target: ceg:v1:entity:...
      preconditions:
        entity_digest: ...
        expected_occurrences_digest: ...
        expected_text_digest: ...
      payload: {}
  required_verifiers: []
  effect_budget: {}
```

The compiler resolves exact occurrences, lowers semantic operations through language-specific lossless codemods, emits a patch, reparses changed files, computes a semantic graph diff, and rejects unresolved or stale anchors. A raw textual patch remains an explicit lower-confidence escape hatch.

Never silently fuzzy-apply against a changed worktree. If the snapshot precondition fails, re-resolve/replan or request intervention. For renames and API changes, static references are not enough: inspect reflection strings, serialization fields, config keys, database schemas, templates, FFI/ABI, CLI flags, docs/examples, and external consumers, then label unresolved dynamic surfaces.

### 20. Verification and exact receipts

Verification escalates with risk:

1.  source digest and patch preconditions;
2.  parser/CST round trip;
3.  syntax/format/lint;
4.  symbol resolution and type checking;
5.  graph invariant and public-API diff;
6.  targeted tests selected from graph coverage;
7.  broader tests/builds;
8.  property, differential, security, performance, and compatibility checks as demanded;
9.  independent model judge only for semantic criteria lacking deterministic oracles.

The final `ChangeReceipt` contains before/after snapshots, exact diff digest, changed entities/edges/ports/effects, verifier commands/configs/results, unresolved risks, model/tool lineage, and rollback handle. “Agent said complete” is never proof.

### 21. Incremental updates

Use content-addressed reuse and fact-family-specific invalidation:

- syntax facts: file digest + grammar/parser version;
- symbol/type facts: source digest + language/tool version + build universe + dependency interfaces;
- call/data-flow facts: semantic dependency closure and analyzer configuration;
- build facts: recipe + toolchain + inputs + target;
- behavior observations: retained historically but marked non-current when build/environment changes;
- embeddings/cards: source fact IDs + projection generator/model version;
- lineage: recomputed separately from exact identity.

Maintain an immutable base epoch plus a cheap dirty-workspace overlay. A save or Git event updates only affected file facts, then follows reverse invalidation dependencies. When dependency knowledge is incomplete, invalidate conservatively and expose that broader scope in coverage metadata. Parallel branches get parallel overlays; merge creates a new snapshot rather than mutating past truth.

## Concrete contracts to define first

1.  `CorpusManifest` — acquisition boundary, tenant, origins, registry authority, inclusions/exclusions, policy.
2.  `ArtifactEnvelope` — source/distribution/build bytes, hashes, provenance, license evidence.
3.  `WorkspaceSnapshot` — exact dirty-worktree Merkle identity and configuration roots.
4.  `BuildUniverse` — language/tool versions, target, dependencies, flags, generators, environment inputs.
5.  `LanguageAdapterManifest` — supported languages/fact families, precision, requirements, producer version.
6.  `NativeFactBundle` — immutable analyzer output plus schema/config/source references.
7.  `EntityEnvelope` and typed aspect schemas.
8.  `Occurrence` and `SourceMapChain`.
9.  `Port` and `BoundaryContract`.
10. `RelationAssertion` and n-ary participant roles.
11. `EvidenceRecord` — origin, modality, producer, confidence/calibration, scope, timestamp.
12. `AnalysisCoverageManifest` — what was attempted, supported, skipped, failed, and therefore unknown.
13. `IdentityMap` and `LineageAssertion`.
14. `EntitySetDefinition` and `CodeCapsule`.
15. `DescriptionAssertion` and `EmbeddingRecord`.
16. `GraphEpochManifest` and `DeltaPack`.
17. `CodeSearchRequest`, `CodeSearchHit`, and score/explanation channels.
18. `ContextDemand` and `ContextSlice`.
19. `ChangePlan`, `ChangeOperation`, and `PatchAnchor`.
20. `VerificationPlan`, `VerificationResult`, and `ChangeReceipt`.
21. `ModelCallTrace` and `ToolExecutionTrace`.

`AnalysisCoverageManifest` is especially important. Without it, “no edge found” will be misread as “no relation exists,” which is fatal in dynamic languages and partial builds.

## Language adapter contract

``` yaml
LanguageAdapter:
  adapter_id: python.v1
  detects: [python, stub, notebook-python]
  consumes: [artifact, workspace_snapshot, build_universe]
  emits_fact_families:
    syntax: precise
    declarations: precise
    references: conditional
    types: conditional
    calls: may
    dataflow: optional
    lossless_tree: true
  supports_operations: [rename, add_import, change_signature, replace_body]
  requirements: [python_version, source_roots]
  sandbox_profile: no-network-no-exec
  coverage_schema_version: 1
```

Adapters are capability-described and independently versioned. Cross-language parity is not assumed; the query/change planner filters by actual adapter coverage.

## Python/PyPI first vertical slice

### Scope

- latest stable release of 1,000 representative PyPI projects, stratified by popularity, size, packaging style, typing level, pure/native code, frameworks, CLIs, and data libraries;
- sdist plus pure-Python wheels initially; record platform wheels and native boundaries without executing them;
- one tenant/workspace overlay containing a real multi-package Python repository;
- I0–I4 facts by default, targeted I5–I8 for an evaluation subset.

### Safe acquisition

1.  Read the PyPI JSON Simple API incrementally and verify file hashes.
2.  Store wheel/sdist bytes in CAS; parse archive members without import or install.
3.  Parse `METADATA`, `WHEEL`, `RECORD`, entry points, dependencies/extras, Python constraints, project URLs, and license evidence.
4.  Treat every wheel/sdist as a distinct `DistributionID`; one release can have materially different platform contents.
5.  Validate, rather than assume, any mapping from distribution name to import package and any link from release to source repository.
6.  Only build or execute packages in a locked, disposable, no-secret, resource-limited sandbox after explicit escalation to the behavioral tier.

### Python extraction portfolio

- `ast` for fast semantic syntax;
- LibCST for lossless spans and codemods;
- Tree-sitter/Ctags as broad comparison/fallback;
- SCIP-Python for persistent symbols/occurrences;
- Pyright or another type resolver for typed subset coverage;
- import graph and `__all__`/entry-point analysis without importing;
- optional CodeQL/data-flow and sandboxed tests for selected packages.

Explicitly distinguish distribution name, import module, namespace package, module, attribute, entry point, generated member, monkey-patched member, and native-extension export. `__all__`, docs, syntax, static resolver, and runtime observations are parallel assertions, not automatically reconciled truth.

### First query/change surfaces

``` text
code.search
code.resolve
code.show_card
code.slice
code.impact
code.find_tests
code.compare_versions
code.plan_change
code.compile_change
code.verify_change
code.receipt
```

Expose these as CLI, local SDK, HTTP/gRPC, and a compact MCP server. Do not expose one tool per function/class/variable; entity handles and the meta-tools scale to hundreds of millions of entities.

### Initial end-to-end demonstrations

1.  Find the existing implementation of an intent across installed/public packages without an LLM-authored query.
2.  Given a stack trace, resolve exact release/build symbols and return the smallest connected explanation slice.
3.  Given a function, show callers, data/effect boundaries, tests, public exposure, and likely blast radius.
4.  Rename a Python public method through typed ChangeIR, preserve formatting, flag unresolved reflective strings, run selected tests, and issue a receipt.
5.  Compare two PyPI releases and distinguish exact API/behavior/effect changes from guessed lineage.
6.  Summarize a package/module as a `CodeCapsule` and progressively disclose only the bodies needed to compose it with another package.

## Failure modes and required defenses

| Failure                                           | Why it happens                               | Required defense                                                         |
|---------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Package name mistaken for import name             | Distribution and Python namespace differ     | File/module inventory plus evidence-backed mapping                       |
| Registry package mistaken for repository          | Metadata missing, stale, or wrong            | Separate IDs; validate content/revision correspondence                   |
| Sdist assumed equal to wheel                      | Generated/native/platform files differ       | Distinct distribution/build identities and diffs                         |
| Indexer executes malicious build code             | Package metadata/build hooks are executable  | Static-first archive parsing; disposable sandbox for build/runtime tiers |
| One AST treated as universal                      | Language semantics and build variants differ | Universal envelope plus native facts/adapters                            |
| Source renamed to global identifiers              | Breaks API, ABI, reflection, serialization   | Sidecar IDs only                                                         |
| Local symbol IDs drift after edits                | Line/ordinal anchors are unstable            | Exact occurrence IDs plus revisable lineage; re-resolve against snapshot |
| False cross-version equivalence                   | Rename/copy/split heuristics overreach       | Parallel lineage assertions with evidence; no destructive merge          |
| Missing edge read as negative                     | Partial parse/build/analyzer coverage        | Coverage manifest and explicit unknown/negative polarity                 |
| Static call graph overclaims dynamic dispatch     | Reflection, plugins, DI, monkey patches      | May/must/candidate sets plus runtime evidence and unresolved flags       |
| Docs or LLM summary becomes “truth”               | Convenient prose outranks code               | Description assertions with modality; executable evidence ranking        |
| Generated code edited directly                    | Source of truth is generator/template        | Source-map chain; edit highest authoritative source or flag regeneration |
| Text patch hits wrong overload/copy               | Names and text repeat                        | Entity/occurrence anchors, snapshot preconditions, semantic lowerer      |
| Worktree changes during agent edit                | Concurrent human/tool actions                | Snapshot lock, compare-and-swap, replan/rebase; no silent fuzzy apply    |
| Index becomes stale after a small edit            | Semantic dependents not invalidated          | Fact-family dependency graph and conservative fallback invalidation      |
| Context slice omits decisive edge                 | Top-k retrieval ignores connectivity/risk    | Task-specific connected slicing, frontier handles, coverage report       |
| Too much duplicate context                        | Bodies/docs/cards overlap                    | content/span deduplication and marginal information scoring              |
| Graph database becomes bottleneck                 | Billions of occurrences/edges                | Immutable shards + exact/lexical/adjacency/columnar projections          |
| Embedding upgrade changes identity                | Derived vector confused with entity          | Versioned disposable EmbeddingRecord, never canonical ID                 |
| Cross-tenant search leaks names/graph             | Authorization applied after ranking          | ACL filter before candidate generation and neighborhood expansion        |
| Runtime observation overgeneralized               | One env/input/test is narrow                 | Bind observation to build/env/domain/oracle/sample and uncertainty       |
| Binary/native boundary disappears                 | Source analyzer cannot inspect it            | Opaque entity/capability boundary, exported symbols/stubs, coverage gap  |
| Public rename passes local tests but breaks users | External/reflective consumers absent         | API/ABI/serialization/config impact scan and compatibility policy        |
| Model claims success without executing            | Language model is not an oracle              | Independent verification plan and immutable receipt                      |

## Non-negotiable invariants

1.  Native source names are never changed merely to create identity.
2.  Exact IDs never change meaning or get reassigned.
3.  Every published relation has producer, scope, modality, and evidence.
4.  Unknown is distinct from false; absence is negative only under declared coverage.
5.  Every behavior claim is bound to build, environment, input domain, and oracle.
6.  Every query/slice is pinned to a graph epoch and authorization context.
7.  Every change is pinned to an exact workspace snapshot and explicit preconditions.
8.  No model output mutates source or canonical facts without deterministic lowering and a receipt.
9.  Native analyzer detail remains resolvable from normalized facts.
10. Derived cards, summaries, clusters, embeddings, and logical lineages are versioned and reproducible or retractable.
11. A public-package base and private overlays never mix before policy filtering.
12. An expensive model fallback must create labeled evidence, a template, a route, or a new verifier that can make the next equivalent request cheaper.

## First build sequence

1.  Lock identity canonicalization, evidence, coverage, snapshot, graph-epoch, and receipt contracts before indexing scale.
2.  Build the no-execution PyPI acquisition and artifact layer.
3.  Implement Python AST + LibCST + SCIP normalization and a differential fixture suite.
4.  Publish exact-ID, fielded BM25, and typed forward/reverse adjacency projections.
5.  Ship `search`, `resolve`, `slice`, `impact`, and `find_tests` through CLI/MCP.
6.  Add `CodeCapsule` boundary derivation for function/class/module/package groups.
7.  Implement Python ChangeIR lowering through LibCST with snapshot preconditions.
8.  Add parser/type/test verification and exact change receipts.
9.  Benchmark 1/2/4/8 candidates and progressive detail against raw repository-context baselines.
10. Add PyPI scale, local ranking, clone/LSH, dynamic evidence, and more languages only after the contracts and first end-to-end transaction are correct.

## Success metrics

- cost and latency per package/release/file/entity indexed by pass;
- deterministic ID reproducibility and graph referential-integrity error rate;
- parse, symbol, type, call, flow, test, and build coverage, reported separately;
- exact symbol/reference precision and recall on language fixtures;
- search top-k recall, complete-route recall, and no-match abstention;
- tokens per verified task and percentage stopped before any hosted LLM;
- context compression versus whole-repository prompting at equal verification success;
- change compilation rate, stale-anchor rejection, semantic-edit correctness, and patch adoption;
- incremental invalidation precision/recall and time-to-fresh-overlay;
- wrong-confident impact/lineage/behavior claim rate;
- verifier pass rate, post-merge defect/rollback rate, and reproducible-receipt rate.

The primary economic metric should be **total cost per independently verified successful existing-code task**, including indexing amortization, local compute, model tokens, failed attempts, verification, and human correction—not token reduction alone.
